intro: IELTS 7.0 kursida biz savol turlarini alohida emas, IMTIHONDAGIDEK — bitta passage'da kombinatsiyada ishlaymiz. Unit 1 dagi Passage 1 kombinatsiyasi: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN (1–5) + Note completion (6–9) + Short-answer questions (10–13). Passage 1 eng oson bo'lim, matni tasviriy va faktik; unga 20 daqiqadan ko'p sarflamang.

1-QADAM — XARITA (1 daqiqa). Uchala guruhni ko'zdan kechiring va har biri matnning qaysi qismiga tegishli ekanini belgilang. SB da: 1–5 matnning birinchi yarmi (campus, Harvard, motto, logo, Silicon Valley); 6–9 bitta odam haqida ("Christopher Merrill — student at MIT" — sarlavha joyni ko'rsatadi); 10–13 matn oxiri (Silicon Valley, Energy Initiative, viruses, Tim Berners-Lee).

T/F/NG: savolda joy topish uchun kalit so'zni (MIT campus, Harvard, motto, logo, Silicon Valley) tagiga chizing, keyin shu joy ATROFINI diqqat bilan o'qing. Band 7 darajasida savol matndagi so'zlarni takrorlamaydi — paraphrase qiladi: "shared a similar approach" ↔ "While Harvard stuck to ... MIT looked to ...". Ma'no bir xil — TRUE; qarshi — FALSE; da'vo haqida ma'lumot yo'q — NOT GIVEN.

NOT GIVEN tuzog'i: mavzu matnda bor, lekin savoldagi aniq da'vo yo'q. Motto matnda bor, lekin uni KIM taklif qilgani — yo'q (Q3). Silicon Valley matnda bor, lekin maosh haqida — yo'q (Q5). Qoida: isbot gapni ko'rsata olmasangiz, FALSE yozmang.

NOTE COMPLETION: notes sarlavhasi (odam, joy, jarayon) matnning qaysi qismini o'qish kerakligini aytadi. Har bo'shliq uchun so'z turini aniqlang: "to (7) ___ the automated construction" — fe'l; "the (8) ___ of robots" — ot. DIQQAT: notes'dagi ma'lumot matn tartibidan boshqacha bo'lishi mumkin (Exam advice). Javob matndan AYNAN ko'chiriladi.

SHORT-ANSWER QUESTIONS: savollar matn tartibida keladi. Savol so'ziga e'tibor bering — u javob turini belgilaydi: "What proportion" — ulush (a quarter), raqam emas (25,800 emas!); "Which 'green' innovation" — ixtiro nomi (electric cars), jarayon emas; "In which part of the university" — joy (the corridors).

Band 7 dagi 0-ball xatolar: 1) so'z chegarasini buzish ("a new contact lens" — 4 so'z); 2) qiyin so'zni noto'g'ri ko'chirish (adaptibility, computer sciense); 3) ikki so'zli javobdan birini tashlab ketish ("science"); 4) savolni noto'g'ri tushunish. Vaqt: xarita 1 + T/F/NG 6 + notes 5 + short answers 5 + tekshirish 2 daqiqa.
formulas: Xarita: uch guruhni 1 daqiqa ko'zdan kechiring
T/F/NG kalit so'zlarini belgilang va skanerlang
Short answer: savol so'zi → javob turi
presentation: Uch guruhni qaysi tartibda ishlayman?
Odatda tartib bilan: 1–5, 6–9, 10–13. Lekin boshlashdan oldin xaritani qiling — notes bitta odam haqida bo'lsa, u qism matnning qayerida ekanini bilasiz.
Notes javoblari matn tartibidami?
Har doim emas. Notes'dagi ma'lumot boshqa tartibda berilishi mumkin — shuning uchun sarlavha va kalit so'z bo'yicha qidiring.
Short answer va notes farqi nima?
Notes — gap bo'lagini to'ldirish (grammatika mos bo'lishi kerak). Short answer — savolga javob; savol so'zi (what proportion, which, where) javob turini belgilaydi.
"a quarter" yoki "one quarter"?
Ikkalasi ham to'g'ri. Lekin "about a quarter of the workforce" — 5 so'z, 0 ball.
Matnda "program" deb yozilgan. "programme" yozsam bo'ladimi?
Xavf qilmang — matndagi shaklni aynan ko'chiring. Bu yerda "program" — fe'l (robotni dasturlamoq); kompyuter ma'nosida British English'da ham "program" yoziladi.
T/F/NG da savoldagi so'z matnda bor edi, lekin javob NOT GIVEN chiqdi. Nega?
So'z bir xil bo'lishi ma'no bir xil degani emas. "motto" bor, "suggested by a former student" — yo'q.
notes: Bu kursning asosiy g'oyasi — imtihondagi kombinatsiya. Aynan shu uchlikni (T/F/NG + notes + short answers) 6.0 ning 7-darsida ko'rgan edik; 7.0 da talab kuchayadi: paraphrase chuqurroq, so'z chegarasi qat'iy, Passage 1 ga 20 daqiqadan ko'p sarflanmaydi.
Har javobdan keyin ikki savol bering: "isbot qaysi gapda?" va "savoldagi so'z matnda qanday aytilgan?" — SB kalitida isbot gaplar bor.

Kuchli o'quvchilarga: SB 4-mashqdagi referencing iboralarini (This unusual community, As such, You can see that) topib, nimaga ishora qilishini aytish — bu T/F/NG da paraphrase'ni tushunishga yordam beradi.
mistakes: Q1 ga TRUE ("like those at any other university")
FALSE — "precious little going on that you would normally see"
NOT GIVEN — kim taklif qilgani aytilmagan
Q9: "a contact lens" yoki "original version of a contact lens"
So'z chegarasi: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS
Savol "green innovation" so'rayapti — batareya vosita, innovatsiya emas

how: CORE — universitet va malaka mavzusidagi asosiy so'zlar; STRONG — SB/WB matnlaridagi Band 7 so'zlari; SUPER — akademik iboralar.
Har o'quvchi o'z rejasidan bitta gap tuzsin: "I'd like to enrol on a vocational course before university."

class_ex.title: Skimming va referencing (SB, 3–4-mashq)
class_ex.instr: Avval 2 daqiqada matnni skim qiling va muallif maqsadini tanlang (a, b, c). Keyin iboralar nimaga ishora qilishini qisqa ayting.
items: Muallif maqsadi: a) to review the courses at MIT b) to explain why MIT has been so successful c) to describe the history of MIT
This unusual community
that single unifying ambition
This down-to-earth quality
That symbiosis of intellect and craftsmanship
As such
answers: to leap into the dark and reach for the unknown
bilim foydali bo'lishi kerakligi (German system, hands-on)
motto (Mind and hand) va logo (olim + temirchi)
Merrill g'oyasi bozorga kech qolishi mumkinligi
why: Matn tarixni ham, kurslarni ham qisman eslatadi, lekin hammasi bitta savolga javob: MIT nega shunchalik muvaffaqiyatli. Tarix (1861) faqat bitta xatboshida.
Oldingi gap: "... is not a bad description of MIT as a whole".
"united by a common desire: to leap into the dark..." — "single unifying ambition" = "common desire".
"Knowledge was at a premium, but it had to be useful" — amaliy yondashuv.
Oldingi gapdagi motto va logo — aql (scholar) va hunar (ironmonger) birligi.
"He is fearful that he might be just too late..." — shuning uchun (as such) u muvaffaqiyatsiz kompaniyalar qatoriga qo'shilishi mumkin.
class_ex.note: Referencing — Band 7 paraphrase'ning kaliti: T/F/NG isbot gapi ko'pincha "this/that/such" bilan oldingi gapga bog'lanadi.

class_ex.title: Nega 0 ball? (SB, 9-mashq asosida)
class_ex.instr: Bu javoblar SB Q6–13 ga yozilgan va 0 ball olgan. Har biri uchun sababni ayting: so'z chegarasi, imlo, bitta so'z tushib qolgan yoki savol noto'g'ri tushunilgan.
items: 6 — computer sciense
6 — science
8 — adaptibility
9 — a new type of contact lens
12 — batteries
why: To'g'ri: computer science. Qiyin so'zni harfma-harf solishtiring.
Fan nomi — "computer science"; faqat "science" boshqa ma'no.
To'g'ri: adaptability (-ability).
Notes'da "new type of" allaqachon bor; javob faqat "contact lens".
25,800 — kompaniyalar soni. Savol "what proportion" — ulush: a quarter.
Batareyalar — vosita. Savol "green innovation" ni so'raydi: electric cars.
class_ex.note: Doskada uch ustun: IMLO | SO'Z CHEGARASI | SAVOL TURI. Har xato javobni o'quvchilar bir ustunga joylashtiradi.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: TRUE — matn xuddi shu ma'noni aytadi; FALSE — matn qarshisini aytadi; NOT GIVEN — matnda bu da'vo haqida ma'lumot yo'q. Tagiga chiziladigan so'zlar: MIT campus, Harvard, motto, logo, Silicon Valley.
items: The activities going on at the MIT campus are like those at any other university.
Harvard and MIT shared a similar approach to education when they were founded.
The school motto was suggested by a former MIT student.
MIT's logo reflects the belief that intellect and craftsmanship go together.
Silicon Valley companies pay higher salaries to graduates from MIT.
why: "There's precious little going on that you would normally see on a university campus". "Precious little" = deyarli yo'q — savol teskarisini aytadi.
"While Harvard stuck to the English model ... MIT looked to the German system". "While" — qarama-qarshilik belgisi.
Motto (Mens et manus) matnda bor, lekin uni kim taklif qilgani aytilmagan. Mavzu bor — da'vo yo'q.
Logo olim va temirchini ko'rsatadi; keyingi gap: "That symbiosis of intellect and craftsmanship". Symbiosis = go together.
Silicon Valley ishchi kuchining chorak qismi haqida gap bor, maosh haqida — hech narsa.
tasks.note: Q1 va Q2 — ikkalasi FALSE, lekin isbot usuli har xil: Q1 da inkor ibora (precious little), Q2 da qarama-qarshilik bog'lovchisi (while). Q3 va Q5 — darsning asosiy NOT GIVEN namunalari.

"Which student can most effectively program a robot to build a house". "to ___ the automated construction" — fe'l kerak; matndagi shakl (program) harfma-harf ko'chiriladi.
"An area of robotics that remains unconquered – adaptability". "the ___ of robots" — ot.
"An original version of a contact lens". Notes'da "new type of" bor — faqat "contact lens".
tasks.note: Kalitdagi savol: "Did you copy your answers for Questions 6, 8 and 9 correctly?" — imloni harfma-harf tekshirtiring.

11 What problem does MIT's Energy Initiative aim to solve?

"Batteries that could prove crucial in the advancement of electric cars". Batteries — vosita, innovatsiya — electric cars.
"When I do walk the corridors, I bump into people...". Tuzoq: David Koch Institute — boshqa xatbosh.

tasks.title: 1-mashq: muallif maqsadi
tasks.type: Choose A, B or C
tasks.instr: Matnni 2 daqiqada skim qiling.
items: 1 Which best describes the writer's purpose? A) To summarise the main reasons why students take a gap year. B) To explain why some gap year programmes are so successful. C) To illustrate, with examples, one particular advantage of a gap year.
why: Matn ikki misol (Christine va Agnes) orqali bitta foydani ko'rsatadi: gap year yangi maqsad va yo'nalish beradi ("a new sense of purpose"). A — sabablar ro'yxati yo'q; B — dasturlar muvaffaqiyati mavzu emas.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: TRUE — matn xuddi shu ma'noni aytadi; FALSE — matn qarshisini aytadi; NOT GIVEN — matnda bu da'vo haqida ma'lumot yo'q.
items: The majority of young people who go travelling during their gap year must work in order to finance their trip.
Taking a gap year can give young people time to consider whether or not they want to continue with their studies.
The number of university students has increased in the last few years.
Christine Samways lacks the right qualities to be a good student.
Christine Samways believes that if you lack educational qualifications, your career options are reduced.
why: Matnda "often supplementing their limited funds by taking on casual work" — "often" bor, lekin ko'pchilik "majbur" ekani aytilmagan.
"Offering a chance to think about why you should study, or if you need to study at all".
Faqat 19 va 20 yoshlilar soni o'sgani aytilgan ("in this age group"). Umumiy talabalar soni haqida ma'lumot yo'q — tor guruhdan umumiy xulosa chiqarmang.
"Despite having all the attributes of a good student" — sifatlari bor edi, u faqat qiyin bo'lishidan qo'rqqan.
"If you don't have qualifications, or the right qualifications, you have fewer work choices".
tasks.note: Q3 — Band 7 tuzog'i: matndagi raqamlar o'sishni ko'rsatadi, lekin faqat ma'lum yosh guruhida. Savol umumiy — shuning uchun NOT GIVEN (kalit bo'yicha).

readings.title: Practice 1: Earning while learning — the degree apprenticeship
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 1 darajasi, Band 7)
text: For most of the twentieth century, the route into a professional career in Britain appeared straightforward. School leavers with strong grades went to university and studied full-time for three or four years, while those who preferred practical work took an apprenticeship and learned a trade on the job. The two routes rarely met, and they carried very different levels of prestige. Since 2015, however, a hybrid known as the degree apprenticeship has begun to blur this boundary. Participants are employed by a company and receive a salary, yet they also study part-time for a full bachelor's or even master's degree, with the cost of tuition met by the employer and the government rather than by the student.

The appeal for young people is easy to understand. Graduates of conventional degrees in England typically leave university with considerable debt, whereas apprentices finish with a recognised qualification, several years of relevant work experience and, in most cases, no loans to repay. Many also choose to remain with the employer that trained them, which spares them the uncertainty of searching for a first job. Supporters argue that the model also addresses a long-standing complaint from business: that new graduates, however intellectually able, arrive in the workplace without the practical skills needed to be productive from their first day. For many families, too, the absence of tuition fees makes the option attractive, particularly where nobody in the family has previously attended university.

The structure of the programmes varies between providers. A common model involves four days a week at the workplace and one day at the university, although some programmes prefer block release, in which apprentices spend several weeks at a time on campus before returning to their jobs. Assessment is also distinctive. Alongside conventional examinations and essays, apprentices must pass an 'end-point assessment', in which an independent assessor judges whether they can actually perform the job to the standard the industry expects. Academic success on its own is therefore not sufficient: an apprentice who writes excellent essays but cannot apply that knowledge at work will not complete the programme. Apprentices are also expected to keep a portfolio of evidence showing how their studies relate to the tasks they carry out at work, and their line manager usually meets a university tutor several times a year to review their progress.

Early fears that the scheme would be dismissed as a second-class alternative to university have largely proved unfounded. Well-known employers in engineering, law and accountancy now recruit a significant share of their entry-level staff in this way, and competition for places can be as fierce as it is for the most selective universities. Some large firms report receiving dozens of applications for every place they advertise, and the selection process, which may include online tests, interviews and assessment days, is often more demanding than a university admission.

Not everyone is convinced, however. Critics point out that degree apprenticeships are concentrated in a narrow range of sectors, notably digital technology, management and engineering, and are far less common in the arts and humanities. Others are concerned that the benefits are going disproportionately to candidates who would have gone to university anyway, rather than to the young people from disadvantaged backgrounds for whom the scheme was partly designed. There is also the question of workload. Combining a demanding job with degree-level study leaves little time for the social side of student life, and some apprentices describe feeling isolated from the full-time students they meet on campus.

Employers face challenges of their own. Releasing staff for study reduces productivity in the short term, and smaller companies in particular may lack the experienced managers needed to mentor apprentices properly. For this reason, the majority of places are currently offered by large organisations, which can spread the cost across many departments. Nonetheless, many of those who have completed the programmes are enthusiastic about them. As one former apprentice, now working as a software engineer, put it: 'I never had to choose between a degree and a career. I got both, and I was paid while I was doing it.'
glossary: block release — o'qish uchun bir necha haftalik ta'til (ishdan)

readings.title: Practice 2: Why the lecture refuses to die
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 1 darajasi, Band 7)
text: The lecture is one of the oldest teaching methods still in use. In the universities of medieval Europe, books were copied by hand and were so expensive that few students could afford to own them. A lecturer, whose title comes from the Latin legere, 'to read', would read aloud from a text while students wrote it down, often word for word. In effect, the lecture was a way of producing books as much as a way of explaining ideas.

The invention of printing removed that justification centuries ago, yet the format survived and eventually spread to universities all over the world. Today a first-year student at a large university may spend ten or more hours a week in lecture halls, some of which hold several hundred people. Institutions favour the lecture partly for economic reasons: a single academic can teach an almost unlimited number of students at the same time, and the cost per student falls as the audience grows. Lecture theatres are also relatively cheap to run and simple to timetable, which makes them attractive to administrators planning courses for thousands of students.

Critics have long argued that this efficiency is largely an illusion. Attention, they claim, declines noticeably after the first quarter of an hour, and much of what is heard is forgotten within days unless it is actively used. In 2014, a widely cited analysis of more than two hundred studies of science and engineering courses compared traditional lectures with 'active learning', in which students solve problems, discuss questions in small groups or respond to questions during class. Students in traditional lectures were found to be about one and a half times more likely to fail than those who were taught actively.

Findings of this kind have encouraged a number of alternatives. The best known is the 'flipped classroom', in which students watch recorded lectures at home and use class time for exercises and discussion while the tutor is present to help. Another approach, known as peer instruction, interrupts the lecture every few minutes with a question. Students vote on the answer individually, then try to persuade their neighbours before voting a second time. Teachers who use the method report that the second vote is almost always more accurate than the first.

Yet the lecture still has its defenders. A skilled speaker, they argue, can do things that a textbook cannot: show how an expert reasons through a problem, convey enthusiasm for a subject and adjust an explanation in response to the reactions of the audience. Some students also prefer lectures because they are predictable and easy to plan around. Moreover, teachers who have tried the flipped classroom often report that it only succeeds if students actually prepare in advance, which a considerable number do not. A well-organised lecture series can also give a course a clear structure, signalling which topics matter most and how they connect to one another.

Recorded lectures have added a further complication. Many universities now make recordings available online, and some have seen attendance at live sessions fall as a result. Lecturers are divided on whether this matters. Some regard recordings as a valuable resource for revision, particularly for students who are studying in a second language and may need to hear a difficult passage more than once. Others fear that students who rely on recordings fall behind, because they tend to postpone watching them until shortly before examinations. Some institutions have responded by asking lecturers to include activities that can only be done in the room.

What seems likely is that the lecture will evolve rather than disappear. Many lecturers now break their sessions into short segments separated by brief activities, such as a question to discuss with a neighbour. The most effective seem to treat the lecture not as a means of transmitting information, which can be done more cheaply in other ways, but as an opportunity to demonstrate how knowledge is actually used. Seen in this light, the survival of the lecture is less surprising than it first appears.

readings.title: Practice 3 (uyga): Houses of learning — the first universities
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 1 darajasi, Band 7), uy vazifasi
text: Few institutions have proved as durable as the university. Several of the world's oldest organisations still in operation are places of learning, and some have existed for longer than the countries in which they now stand. Among them are institutions that have survived wars, revolutions and changes of language and government. Yet the word 'university' did not originally refer to a building, a set of courses or even a place. In medieval Latin, universitas simply meant a community or corporation: a group of people with shared interests who organised themselves in order to protect those interests.

The institution most often described as the oldest still operating is al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco. It was founded in 859 as a mosque by Fatima al-Fihri, the daughter of a wealthy merchant, and it gradually developed into a major centre of learning in which subjects such as grammar, law, mathematics and astronomy were taught alongside religious studies. Scholars travelled considerable distances to study and teach there, and its library, one of the oldest in the world, still holds manuscripts that are many centuries old. It was formally incorporated into Morocco's modern state university system in 1963.

In Europe, the University of Bologna, which traditionally dates its foundation to 1088, grew up around the study of law. Its most unusual feature was that it was controlled by its students. Students from other cities, who had few legal rights in Bologna, formed associations to protect themselves, and these associations became powerful enough to hire teachers and to set rules for them. The students even elected the rector, the head of the university, from among their own number. Lecturers could be fined for starting late, for finishing early or for skipping difficult sections of a text.

Paris developed along different lines. There, it was the teachers rather than the students who formed the governing corporation, and the university became famous for theology and philosophy. The Paris model was later adopted in northern Europe, including at Oxford, where teaching was taking place by the end of the eleventh century; its colleges, which today give the town much of its character, were founded later, from the thirteenth century onwards. Oxford expanded rapidly after 1167, when English students were prevented from attending the University of Paris. Cambridge, in turn, was established in 1209 by scholars who had left Oxford following a dispute with the local townspeople.

Central Asia has its own long tradition of higher learning. In the fifteenth century, the ruler and astronomer Ulugh Beg built madrasas in Bukhara and Samarkand. Unlike many institutions of the period, which concentrated mainly on religious subjects, these gave an important place to the exact sciences. The Samarkand madrasa, completed around 1420, attracted some of the leading mathematicians and astronomers of the age, and Ulugh Beg is said to have lectured there himself. Nearby he built an observatory whose measurements of the positions of the stars were remarkably accurate for a period long before the invention of the telescope.

What did these early institutions have in common? Most began not with a grand plan but with a concentration of respected scholars in one place, followed by students who came to hear them. Degrees developed as a kind of licence: a graduate of a medieval university had, in principle, the right to teach elsewhere. There were no entrance examinations in the modern sense, and students were often very young by today's standards, some beginning their studies at fourteen or fifteen. Teaching was in Latin in European universities and in Arabic in much of the Islamic world, which allowed students and teachers to move freely between cities and even between countries.

Much has changed since then, but a surprising amount remains. Academic gowns, the division of universities into faculties, the tradition of public examinations and the title 'master' all have medieval origins. So does an idea that is still central to many universities today: that a community of scholars should, as far as possible, govern itself. Even the practice of dividing the academic year into terms can be traced back to this period.

intro: Section 1 — ikki kishi o'rtasidagi kundalik yoki ijtimoiy mavzudagi suhbat (ro'yxatdan o'tish, ariza, bron). Bu Listening testining eng oson qismi va faqat shu yerda boshida misol (Example) beriladi. Band 7 uchun bu section'da deyarli xato qilmaslik kerak: 10 dan 9–10.

TAYYORLANISH: har bo'shliq uchun ma'lumot turini chetiga yozing. SB kalitidagi namunaviy javob: 1 — harflab aytiladigan familiya, 2 — millat, 3 — harflab aytilishi mumkin bo'lgan email, 4 — BA turi, 5 — sana, 6 — pul yig'ish tadbiri, 7 — qiziqishlar, 8 — ish nomlari, 9 — lavozim, 10 — fair haqida qayerdan eshitgani.

HARFLASH va RAQAMLAR: uzun nomni guruhlab yozing (A-L-E-X / A-N-D / R-O-V-N-A). Email'da "at" = @, "dot" = nuqta, "all one word" — bo'sh joysiz. Raqamni son bilan yozing; telefon raqami guruhlab aytiladi, guruhlar har xil bo'ladi (0771 429 3360 — 4 + 3 + 4; 77 276 97 77 — 2 + 3 + 2 + 2) — eshitganingizdek guruhlab yozing va har guruhni tekshiring.

TUZATISH (correction) — 7.0 darajadagi eng ko'p uchraydigan tuzoq: gapiruvchi yoki eshituvchi xato qiladi, keyin tuzatiladi. WB: "0878 643 9844" — "No, that's 884 at the end"; "Taylor with a y?" — "No, an i"; "Tuesday 9th?" — "Would Wednesday be possible?". Qoida: birinchi eshitganni yozing, lekin gap oxirigacha tinglang va kerak bo'lsa ustidan yozing.

TUZOQ (distractor): javob yaqinida boshqa mos ko'rinadigan ma'lumot aytiladi. "Born in Poland ... my mum's Polish, but I'm Russian" — millat: Russian. "Is that part time?" — "No, I'm a full-time student". "I'm taking a holiday on the 12th" — mavjud sana: 21st July.

IKKI JAVOBLI BO'SHLIQ va CHEKLOVLAR: "Interests: (7) ___ and ___" — ikkalasi ham kerak (cooking and swimming); bittasi — 0 ball. "Up to (6) ___ per week" — eng ko'p son: "a couple ... or maybe three. But no more" → three evenings.

GRAMMATIK MOSLIK va SO'Z CHEGARASI: javob formadagi so'zlar bilan birga to'g'ri gap bo'lishi kerak ("Would like (7) some work experience"). NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER: "challenging but rewarding" — 3 so'z, to'g'ri; formada bor so'zni ("@qmail.com", "BA", "Course") takrorlamang.
formulas: Birinchi eshitgan har doim javob emas
cooking and swimming; up to three
Q7 ni yozayotib Q8 ni ko'ring
presentation: Harflashda bitta harfni o'tkazib yubordim. Nima qilaman?
Eshitganingizni yozing va davom eting. Ko'pincha eshituvchi nomni qaytaradi — shu paytda tekshirasiz.
Sanani qanday yozaman?
21st July, 21 July yoki 21/7 — hammasi qabul qilinadi. Faqat oyni harf bilan yozish xavfsizroq: 7/21 chalkashlik tug'diradi.
"(a) full-time" — artiklni yozishim kerakmi?
Qavs ichidagi so'z ixtiyoriy. Lekin formada "___ BA" bor — "full-time" yetarli va chegarada.
Bo'shliqda "and" bor. Ikki so'z yozamanmi?
Ha, ikkala qiziqishni ham: "cooking" va "swimming". Kalit: "must have both".
Email'ni qanday yozaman?
Faqat "@" gacha bo'lgan qism: dom54, flipt14. Formada domen (@qmail.com) allaqachon bor.
WB da 12 ta savol. Imtihonda ham shundaymi?
Imtihonda Section 1 da 10 savol. WB 12 savol bilan tezlikni mashq qildiradi: oldinga o'qish ko'nikmasi.
notes: 6.0 da forma + MCQ kombinatsiyasini ishlagan edik. 7.0 da Section 1 ning o'zi oson, lekin Band 7 uchun ball faqat aniqlikda: harflash, tuzatish, ikki javob va grammatik moslik.
Tekshiruvda har javobdan keyin skriptdan javob gapini va tuzoq gapni ekranga chiqaring (skript rasmida javoblar tagiga chizilgan — WB).

listenings.title: Jony Academy mashqi: Graduate Skills Programme — registration (Q1–10)
intro: Ustoz skriptni bir marta, tabiiy tezlikda o'qiydi (ikki ovoz: ADVISER va MADINA); javob so'zlarini urg'u yoki pauza bilan ajratib ko'rsatmang. O'quvchilar avval 30 soniya formani o'qiydi va har bo'shliq turini belgilaydi. Ko'rsatma: NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER.

1 va 4-savollardan tashqari har savolda kamida bitta tuzoq bor (5 va 9-savollarda — ikkitadan), masalan: tuzatilgan raqam, band qilingan variant, "normally", rad etilgan so'z yoki keyingi manba. 1 va 4-savollarda qiyinchilik — harflash (K-H; email nuqta va bo'sh joysiz). Tekshiruvda o'quvchi tuzoqni ham aytishi kerak.
transcript: ADVISER: Good afternoon, Careers Centre. How can I help?
MADINA: Hi. I'd like to sign up for the Graduate Skills Programme, if there are still places.
ADVISER: There are. I'll fill in the registration form on screen. You're a postgraduate student, I take it?
MADINA: Yes, that's right.
ADVISER: And your name?
MADINA: Madina Rakhimova.
ADVISER: Could you spell your surname for me?
MADINA: Of course. R-A-K-H-I-M-O-V-A.
ADVISER: R-A-K-H ... I-M-O-V-A. Thanks. And what are you studying at the moment?
MADINA: Well, my first degree was in chemistry, but I'm now doing a master's — an MSc in Environmental Engineering.
ADVISER: Environmental Engineering. Could I have your student number?
MADINA: It's four-oh-seven-one, eight-two-five-six. Oh, hang on — I always get the last two the wrong way round. It's eight-two-six-five at the end.
ADVISER: So that's 4071 8265.
MADINA: Yes, that's it.
ADVISER: We send all the details by email. Is your university address best?
MADINA: Yes. It's M-R-A-K-H, then the number twenty-two, at northfield dot ac dot uk. No dots or spaces before the 'at'.
ADVISER: mrakh22. Lovely. Now, there are three workshops this term, and you can choose one: CV writing, presentation skills and interview skills.
MADINA: I was hoping to do CV writing, actually.
ADVISER: I'm afraid that one's already fully booked.
MADINA: Oh, what a pity. Presentation skills clashes with my lab sessions, so ... I'll go for interview skills. I've got a few applications coming up anyway.
ADVISER: Fine. Sessions run on Tuesdays and Thursdays from six o'clock. Which would you prefer?
MADINA: Tuesdays would normally be easier, but this term I'm in the lab until seven on Tuesdays, so it'll have to be Thursdays.
ADVISER: Thursdays, then. It also helps the trainers to know about any work experience you have.
MADINA: Last summer I worked for a water company. I applied for an internship in their laboratory, but in the end they took me on as a research assistant on a project about river pollution.
ADVISER: So I'll put 'research assistant'. At the end of the programme there's a networking lunch with local employers. Do you have any dietary requirements?
MADINA: Yes, I'm vegetarian. Not vegan — I do eat eggs and cheese.
ADVISER: Noted. Each participant is also paired with a mentor from industry. Which field would you like your mentor to come from?
MADINA: Ideally water treatment, because that's my dissertation topic.
ADVISER: Let me check ... Unfortunately, we don't have anyone in water treatment this year. We do have mentors in waste management and in renewable energy.
MADINA: Renewable energy, please. I'd like to keep that option open for after I graduate.
ADVISER: Renewable energy. And finally, how did you find out about the programme? Was it the website?
MADINA: I did look at the website later, but it was my supervisor who first told me about it. She did the programme herself years ago.
ADVISER: Great. You'll get an email confirmation within twenty-four hours. Good luck, Madina!

intro: Band 6.5–7.5 darajasida Passage 2 odatda uch savol turidan iborat. Bu unitda ikki kitobda ham bir xil uchlik: Matching headings, Summary completion (so'z matndan olinadi) va Choose TWO letters. 6.0 da headings va TWO letters ni birga yechgan edik; endi ularga summary qo'shiladi va sarlavhalar ancha abstrakt bo'ladi.

Birinchi qadam — sarlavhalar. Headings savollari passage'dan OLDIN beriladi va butun matnning xaritasini beradi. Har section'ni o'qib, 5–7 so'zli asosiy g'oyani chetga yozing, keyin ro'yxatdan mos sarlavhani tanlang. Bu xarita keyingi ikki savol turi uchun ham kerak bo'ladi: summary va TWO letters ning javobi qaysi section'da ekanini darhol ko'rasiz.

Band 7 sarlavhalari mavzuni emas, xatboshining VAZIFASINI aytadi: "A curious state of affairs" — g'alati, tushunarsiz holat (muammo qo'yiladi); "A possible explanation" — gipoteza; "Checking out the theory" — tajriba; "Some unsurprising data" — kutilgan natija ("As predicted"). Shuning uchun xatboshining birinchi va oxirgi gapiga, ayniqsa bog'lovchilarga (however, to explore this further, as predicted) e'tibor bering.

Tafsilot tuzog'i: sarlavhadagi so'z xatboshining bitta gapida uchraydi, lekin butun xatbosh boshqa narsa haqida. Workbook D section'da Qirolicha Viktoriya bor, lekin "Seeking royal support" to'g'ri emas — Perkin yordamni izlamagan, xatbosh esa laboratoriyadan do'konlargacha bo'lgan yo'l haqida.

Summary completion: sarlavha ("The Hypothesis") va birinchi gap kerakli section'ni ko'rsatadi. Summary ko'pincha matn tartibida boradi, lekin paraphrase juda kuchli: "despite ___" = "even after hundreds of training trials". Bo'shliqdan oldin va keyingi so'zlarga qarab so'z turini aniqlang (a/the + ot, may be + sifat), javobni matndan AYNAN ko'chiring va so'z chegarasini tekshiring.

Choose TWO letters: beshta variantdan ikkitasi to'g'ri. Qolgan uchtasi uch xil tuzoq: matnga zid (FALSE), matnda yo'q (NOT GIVEN) yoki matnda bor, lekin savolga javob emas. Har variant yoniga ✔ / ✘ / ? belgisi qo'ying va faqat isbot gapi bor ikkitasini yozing.

Vaqt: Passage 2 ga 20 daqiqa — sarlavhalarga 8, summary'ga 5, TWO letters ga 5, tekshirishga 2 daqiqa. Bitta sarlavhada qotib qolsangiz, uni oxiriga qoldiring: boshqa section'lar tanlangach, variantlar kamayadi.
formulas: Sarlavhalar ro'yxatini o'qing, kalit so'zlarni belgilang
Har section: asosiy g'oyani 5–7 so'zda yozing
Bo'shliq turini aniqlab, so'zni aynan ko'chiring
presentation: Sarlavhalarni oxirida yechsam bo'ladimi?
Yo'q. Ular matn xaritasini beradi — summary va TWO letters uchun qaysi section kerakligini aynan sarlavhalar orqali bilasiz.
Sarlavhadagi so'z matnda bor. Demak to'g'rimi?
Shart emas. Band 7 da aksincha: to'g'ri sarlavha ko'pincha matndagi so'zlarni takrorlamaydi, tuzoq sarlavha esa takrorlaydi.
Summary javoblari tartib bilan keladimi?
Odatda ha, lekin summary ikki section'ni qamrashi mumkin (SB: A va B). Sarlavha qaysi qismni aytayotganini tekshiring.
"(pre-nominal) position" — qavs nima degani?
Qavsdagi so'z ixtiyoriy: "position" ham, "pre-nominal position" ham to'g'ri — ikkalasi ham ikki so'z chegarasida.
TWO letters da bittasiga ishonchim komil. Ikkinchisi-chi?
Qolgan to'rttasini ✘ bilan chiqarib tashlang. Baribir ikkita harf yozing — har harf alohida ball.
Variant to'g'ri, lekin boshqa section haqida. Javobmi?
Yo'q. SB 10–11 "about the experiment" — faqat tajriba (C section) haqidagi variantlar hisoblanadi.
notes: 5.0 da headings, summary va multiple choice alohida o'rganilgan; 6.0 da headings + TWO letters juftligi bo'lgan. Bugungi yangilik — uchinchi tur (summary) va Band 7 dagi abstrakt sarlavhalar.
Har sarlavha javobidan keyin o'quvchidan so'rang: "Bu section'ning vazifasi nima — muammo, gipoteza, tajriba yoki natija?" Shu savol Band 7 sarlavhalarining kaliti.
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: SB ro'yxatidagi ishlatilmagan sarlavhalar (ii, v, vi) uchun matnda qaysi gap ularni "tuzoq" qilganini topish.
mistakes: Sarlavhani bitta so'z mosligi bilan tanlash ("royal" → Seeking royal support)
Summary'ga uch so'z yozish: "alternative medical practice"
TWO letters da uchta harf yozish
Matnda bor, lekin savolga tegishli bo'lmagan variantni tanlash

Har so'z bilan o'quvchi rang yoki o'qish haqida bitta gap tuzsin: "It took me years to distinguish between 'teal' and 'turquoise'."

class_ex.title: Abstrakt sarlavhani "tarjima qilish" (SB, 3-mashq asosida)
class_ex.instr: Matnni ochmasdan: har sarlavha qanday xatboshiga mos kelishini o'zbekcha ayting — muammo, gipoteza, tajriba yoki natija? Qaysi bog'lovchi so'z shunga ishora qiladi?
items: A curious state of affairs
A possible explanation
Checking out the theory
Some unsurprising data
Standing out from the crowd
An unexpected but fortunate side result
why: Signal so'zlar: "for some reason, however", "surprisingly", "it turns out". SB A section: bolalar yuzlab so'zni o'rganadi, lekin rang so'zlarida "perform very badly".
Signal: "hypothesized", "may be linked to", "it seems". SB B section.
Signal: "to explore this idea further", "recruited", "experiment". SB C section.
Signal: "as predicted", "confirmed". SB D section — natija gipotezaga mos, shuning uchun "unsurprising".
Signal: "mark themselves out as better than those around them". WB A section — binafsha rang mavqe belgisi.
Signal: "to his surprise", "turned out to be". WB C section — Perkin dori o'rniga bo'yoq topdi.
class_ex.note: Mashqdan keyin doskaga yozing: Band 7 sarlavhasi ko'pincha xatboshining MAZMUNINI emas, VAZIFASINI aytadi.

class_ex.title: Summary bo'shlig'ini bashorat qilish (SB, 5-mashq)
class_ex.instr: SB Questions 5–9 ni javob bermasdan o'qing. Har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z turi kerak va u matnning qaysi section'ida bo'lishi mumkin?
items: 5 — "despite ___, many four-year-olds still struggle"
6 — "this is due to the ___ of the adjectives in a phrase"
7 — "objects consist of a number of ___ that can be used to recognise other similar objects"
8 — "the ___ of a colour cannot be developed using the same approach"
9 — "the way colour words tend to be used may be ___ to children"
answers: ot (ko'plik) — urinish yoki mashq; A section
ko'plikdagi ot — qismlar, belgilar; B section
sifat — foydali / foydasiz; B section oxiri
why: "Despite" dan keyin ot keladi; to'rt yoshli bolalar hali ham qiynalishi — ko'p harakatga qaramay. A section oxiri.
"The ___ of the adjectives" — sifatning gapdagi o'rni. Sarlavha "The Hypothesis" — B section.
"A number of" + ko'plik ot. Stul misoli (arms, legs, backs).
"The ___ of a colour" — rang so'zining ma'nosi; "developed" — o'quvchi uni o'zida shakllantiradi.
"May be ___ to children" — sifat. Mantiqan salbiy, chunki bolalar rang so'zlarini sekin o'rganadi.

tasks.title: Questions 1–4
tasks.type: Matching headings — uchta sarlavha ortiqcha
tasks.instr: Har section uchun bitta sarlavha. Ro'yxatda sarlavhalar section'lardan ko'p — ortiqchalari ataylab qo'yilgan tuzoq. Sarlavha section'ning ASOSIY g'oyasiga mos kelsin, bitta gapdagi so'zga emas. Kitobdagi 3-mashq: avval har section'ning asosiy mavzusini yozib, keyin ro'yxat bilan solishtiring.
items: Section A
Section B
Section C
Section D
answers: iv A curious state of affairs
why: "For some reason, however, when it comes to learning color words, the same children perform very badly." Hamma so'zni tez o'rganadigan bola rang so'zlarida qiynaladi — g'alati holat. Tuzoq vi (age): yosh raqamlari (4 oy, 2 yosh, 4 yosh) bor, lekin xatbosh yoshning ta'siri haqida emas.

"Scientists ... hypothesized that children's incompetence at color-word learning may be directly linked to the way these words are used." Tuzoq ii (names of objects): stul misoli bor, lekin buyum nomlari foydasiz deyilmaydi — foydasizi rang sifatlarining joylashuvi.
"To explore this idea further, the research team recruited 41 English children ... and carried out a three-phase experiment." Tajriba — nazariyani tekshirish.

"As predicted, when children are exposed to color adjectives in post-nominal position, they learn them rapidly." "As predicted" = unsurprising. Tuzoq v (how words are formed): so'z yasalishi emas, so'z tartibi haqida.
tasks.note: Ishlatilmagan sarlavhalar: ii, v, vi. Har biri matndagi bitta tafsilotga "yopishadi" — sinfda qaysi gap tuzoq bo'lganini so'rang.

iv A curious state of affairs
v The need to look at how words are formed

tasks.title: Questions 5–9 — The Hypothesis
tasks.type: Complete the summary below. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.
tasks.instr: Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage. Summary sarlavhasi va birinchi gapi matnning qaysi qismini o'qishni aytadi. So'z matndan aynan ko'chiriladi va gap grammatik jihatdan to'g'ri chiqishi kerak. Kalitga ko'ra javoblar A va B section'larda.
items: 5 In fact, despite (5) ..., many four-year-olds still struggle to arrange objects into colour categories.
6 Scientists have hypothesised that this is due to the (6) ... of the adjectives in a phrase or sentence.
7 While objects consist of a number of (7) ... that can be used to recognise other similar objects, ...
8 ... the (8) ... of a colour cannot be developed using the same approach.
9 As a consequence, the way colour words tend to be used in English may be (9) ... to children.
why: "Even after hundreds of training trials, children as old as four may still end up being unable to accurately sort objects by color." Despite = even after; arrange into categories = sort by color.
"They are used overwhelmingly in pre-nominal position." "Position" yoki "pre-nominal position" — ikkalasi ham ikki so'z chegarasida.
"Chairs have features, such as arms and legs and backs" / "narrow down the set of cues that make up a chair". Kalit ikkala so'zni ham qabul qiladi.
"In this way they learn the concept associated with that word" / "nothing systematic about color words to help cue their meaning".
"Most of what children hear from adults will, in fact, be unhelpful in learning what color words refer to." Sifat, matndagidek aynan.
tasks.note: 6-savolda "order" yoki "word order" yozganlar ko'p bo'ladi — mantiqan yaqin, lekin matndan olinmagan. Summary javobi FAQAT matndagi so'z.

tasks.title: Questions 10–13
tasks.type: Choose TWO letters, A–E
tasks.instr: Har juftlikda ikkita javob; tartib ahamiyatsiz ("A, C" = "C, A"), imtihonda har harf alohida 1 ball. Variant matnga to'g'ri kelishi yetarli emas — u aynan savoldagi shartga (10–11: "about the experiment"; 12–13: "outcomes reported in the passage") javob bersin. Kalit: 10–11 → C section, 12–13 → D section.
items: 10–11 Which TWO of the following statements about the experiment are true? A) The children were unfamiliar with the objects used in the pre- and post-test. B) The children had to place the pre- and post-test objects onto coloured trays. C) The training was conducted by dividing the children into two groups. D) Pre-nominal questions were used less frequently than post-nominal questions in the training. E) The researchers were looking for inconsistencies in children's knowledge of word order.

12–13 Which TWO of the following outcomes are reported in the passage? A) Average results contradicted parental assessment of children's knowledge. B) Children who were post-tested using post-nominal adjectives performed well, regardless of the type of training. C) Greatest levels of improvement were achieved by children who were trained and post-tested using post-nominal adjectives. D) Some children performed less well in the post-test than in the pre-test. E) Some children were unable to accurately name any of the colours in the pre- and post-tests.
why: A — "six objects that were novel to the children" (novel = unfamiliar). C — "half the children were presented with the items ... pre-nominally, while the other half ... post-nominal". Tuzoqlar: B — buyumlar "presented on trays", bolalar ularni patnisga qo'ymagan va patnis rangli emas; D — mashg'ulotda ikki guruh teng bo'lingan, "less frequently" yo'q; E — teskari: "correct choices on items that were consistent" o'lchangan.

C — "Only children who had been trained with post-nominal ... and then tested with post-nominal question types were significantly more accurate than chance." D — "a significant decline in performance when children were both pre- and post-tested with ... pre-nominally". Tuzoqlar: A — teskari: natijalar ota-onalar hisobotini "confirmed"; B — "regardless of training" noto'g'ri, eng yomon natija pre-nominal o'qitilib post-nominal sinalganda; E — teskari: "at least some knowledge of the three colour words".
tasks.note: 12–13 da B variant eng kuchli tuzoq: post-nominal test haqida gap bor, lekin "regardless of training" D section'dagi "worst when trained on pre-nominal ... tested on post-nominal" ga zid.

readings.title: Practice 1: Naming the rainbow
readings.qtype: Matching headings (1–5) + Summary completion (6–9) + Choose TWO letters (10–13)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2, Band 7 darajasi)
text: A  Look at a rainbow and you will see a smooth band of light in which one shade melts gradually into the next. Nothing in the physics of light tells us where 'red' ends and 'orange' begins; the spectrum is a continuum, not a set of boxes. Yet every human language slices this continuum into named categories, and the striking thing is how differently they do it. Some languages manage with only a handful of basic colour words, while English has eleven, and Russian arguably has twelve. Even familiar terms have surprising histories: in English, 'orange' was the name of a fruit long before it became the name of a colour, and English speakers treat pink as a separate category rather than as a pale shade of red, which many other languages do not. For linguists, this raises an awkward question: if human eyes are built in roughly the same way everywhere, why do vocabularies disagree so sharply?

B  For much of the twentieth century, the dominant answer was that colour naming is essentially arbitrary. Each culture, it was argued, draws its boundaries wherever convention happens to place them, and children simply absorb those conventions along with the rest of their mother tongue. Some scholars went further, suggesting that people whose language lacked a word for a colour might struggle even to notice it. This view fitted neatly with a broader belief, popular among anthropologists at the time, that languages could vary almost without limit. Evidence seemed plentiful, because anthropologists returning from fieldwork regularly described languages with apparently strange colour systems. Colour seemed an ideal illustration: the same physical stimulus, carved up in countless unpredictable ways.

C  That consensus was shaken in 1969, when two researchers at the University of California, Berkeley, Brent Berlin and Paul Kay, published a comparison of the basic colour terms of 20 languages. They asked speakers to pick out, from a chart of several hundred coloured chips, the best example of each of their colour words. Although the boundaries between categories varied considerably, the best examples clustered remarkably tightly: one speaker's ideal red was very close to another speaker's ideal red, whatever language they spoke. Berlin and Kay also proposed that colour vocabularies grow in a predictable order. A language with only two terms distinguishes dark and cool shades from light and warm ones; if it has three, the third is always red; green and yellow come next, followed by blue, and only then terms such as brown, purple, pink, orange and grey.

D  Their claims have since been refined rather than overturned. Later surveys found exceptions to the strict sequence, and critics pointed out that most of the original participants lived in the San Francisco area and were bilingual in English, which may have influenced their choices. Nevertheless, a much larger project, which collected colour names from speakers of 110 unwritten languages in their own communities, confirmed that the best examples of categories tend to fall in the same regions of colour space. Most researchers now accept a compromise: human vision provides certain natural anchor points, but each language decides how many categories to create and exactly where to draw the lines between them.

E  Whether these linguistic differences affect what people actually see is a separate and more contentious matter. In one frequently cited experiment, Russian speakers, whose language obliges them to choose between separate words for light blue (goluboy) and dark blue (siniy), were quicker to tell apart two shades of blue when the shades fell on opposite sides of that boundary. English speakers, who call both shades 'blue', showed no such advantage. Crucially, the Russian speakers lost their advantage when they were asked to repeat a string of numbers silently during the task, which suggests that language was helping them in the moment rather than permanently reshaping their eyesight. Words, in other words, seem to act as a shortcut the brain calls upon when a decision has to be made quickly. The effect is real but modest: nobody who lacks a separate word for light blue is blind to the difference.

readings.title: Practice 2: Colour on the plate
readings.qtype: Matching headings (1–6) + Choose TWO letters (7–10) + Summary completion (11–14)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2, Band 7 darajasi; Workbook tartibida)
text: A  Ask most people how they judge the flavour of a meal and they will talk about the tongue and perhaps the nose. Few would mention the eyes. Yet a growing body of research suggests that what we see on the plate begins shaping our expectations of taste before the first mouthful, and that colour is one of the most powerful visual cues of all. Chefs have long known this instinctively; scientists are only now beginning to measure it. Restaurants, advertisers and packaging designers make decisions about colour every day, often without being able to explain exactly why one shade works better than another.

B  In one well-known experiment, students of wine-tasting at a French university were asked to describe a white wine and then the same wine dyed red with a colouring that had no smell or taste of its own. The students were not told that anything had been altered, and few, if any, commented on the change. Many of them described the coloured sample using words normally reserved for red wines, such as references to dark berries. Since the dye itself added nothing to the flavour, the change in their descriptions could only have come from what they saw. Similar effects have been reported with fruit drinks: when a cherry-flavoured drink is coloured orange, many people confidently report that they can taste orange.

C  Why should the eyes overrule the tongue in this way? The most widely accepted explanation is that the brain is constantly making predictions. Over a lifetime, we learn that red fruit is usually ripe and sweet, while green fruit is often sour. When a food's colour triggers one of these learned associations, the brain prepares for a particular taste, and the actual signal from the tongue is interpreted in the light of that expectation. Because taste signals are frequently weak or ambiguous, the prediction can win. This is not a sign of foolishness. In everyday life, predictions of this kind are usually correct and save the brain a great deal of effort; it is only when scientists deliberately break the link between colour and flavour that the system is exposed.

D  Food manufacturers have been exploiting this for well over a century. Margarine, which is naturally pale, was coloured yellow to resemble butter, a practice so effective that dairy farmers campaigned against it, and in several American states margarine at one time had to be sold uncoloured. Today, colour is managed in products ranging from farmed salmon, whose pink flesh is controlled through what the fish are fed, to soft drinks, where even a slight change of shade can alter how sweet the product is judged to be. Consumers can react strongly when familiar colours change: when manufacturers have removed artificial colourings from well-known sweets, the paler versions have sometimes been criticised as less tasty, even when the recipe was otherwise unchanged.

E  The influence of colour extends beyond the food itself. Researchers have found that the same dessert is rated sweeter when it is served on a white plate than on a black one, and that the colour of a cup can change how people rate a hot drink: in one study, hot chocolate was judged most chocolatey when served in an orange or cream-coloured cup. Findings like these have encouraged some hospitals to experiment with brightly coloured plates for elderly patients, who often lose their appetite, although the evidence that this makes people eat more remains limited. Even the colour of a room has been claimed to affect how food tastes, but these effects are smaller and much harder to measure.

F  Not everyone is equally affected. Experienced tasters are generally harder to mislead than beginners, although, as the wine study showed, expertise offers no complete protection. There are also cultural differences: a colour associated with sweetness in one country may signal something quite different elsewhere, which is why companies that sell internationally often test packaging and product colours separately in each market. For the rest of us, the lesson is a simple one. If you want to know what something really tastes like, try it with your eyes closed.

readings.title: Practice 3 (uyga): Seeing the world in other colours
readings.qtype: Matching headings (1–5) + Summary completion (6–9) + Choose TWO letters (10–13)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2, Band 7 darajasi), uy vazifasi
text: A  Humans tend to assume that the world simply is the way it looks to us: grass is green, poppies are red and the sky is blue. But colour is not a property of objects alone. Light itself has no colour; it simply consists of waves of different lengths. Colour is constructed by a nervous system from the light that objects reflect, and different nervous systems construct it differently. Most people have three types of colour-sensitive cell, known as cones, in the retina, each tuned to a different band of wavelengths. The brain compares the signals from these three types, and it is this comparison, rather than any single signal, that produces the sensation of colour. Asking what an animal 'really' sees is therefore a question about its eyes and brain, not about the world.

B  Many mammals make do with less. Dogs, cats and most other mammals have only two types of cone, a condition known as dichromacy. A dog can readily distinguish blue from yellow, but reds, oranges and greens all fall into a narrow range of yellowish or greyish tones. This is why a red ball lying on green grass, so obvious to its owner, may be surprisingly hard for a dog to find by sight; it is far more likely to locate it by smell. Contrary to a popular myth, however, dogs do not see the world in black and white. Biologists believe that early mammals, which were small and active mainly at night, lost two of the four cone types their ancestors possessed, since colour vision was of little use in the dark.

C  Primates, including humans, later regained a third cone type. One influential theory links this to diet: the ability to separate red and orange from green would have helped fruit-eating primates to spot ripe fruit, and perhaps young, protein-rich leaves, against a background of mature foliage. Some researchers suggest that the ability to detect the reddening of skin, which can signal emotion or health in other members of a group, may also have played a part. Birds, reptiles and many fish, whose ancestors never went through a nocturnal phase, kept all four cone types. Many birds can also detect ultraviolet light, and in some species the feathers carry ultraviolet patterns that are invisible to us but act as signals to potential mates.

D  Insects illustrate another variation. Honeybees have three types of photoreceptor, but their range is shifted towards shorter wavelengths: they see ultraviolet, blue and green, but are largely insensitive to red. To a bee, a red flower among green leaves may look much like the leaves themselves. Many flowers that look plain to human observers carry ultraviolet 'nectar guides', lines or patches that lead the bee towards the centre of the flower. Plant species that depend on birds for pollination, by contrast, frequently have red flowers, which birds see clearly and bees tend to overlook. Some flowers even change colour once they have been pollinated, telling insects that there is no longer any reward to be collected.

E  The most extraordinary visual system may belong to the mantis shrimp, a marine animal with somewhere between 12 and 16 types of photoreceptor. It was once assumed that this must give it an almost unimaginable richness of colour experience. However, when researchers trained the animals to choose between pairs of colours, the shrimp performed poorly whenever the two wavelengths were close together – far worse than humans. The leading explanation is that the shrimp does not compare signals in the way our brains do; instead, it may recognise colours directly, rather like a shop scanner reading a barcode. This would make identification very fast, a valuable advantage for a predator that strikes in a fraction of a second, but at the cost of fine discrimination. Its eyes can also detect polarised light, a property of light that humans can hardly perceive without special equipment. Whatever the final explanation, the shrimp is a reminder that more receptors do not automatically mean better colour vision.

tasks.title: Questions 6–9 — Mammals and colour
tasks.type: Complete the summary below. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.
tasks.instr: Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage. Summary sarlavhasi va birinchi gapi matnning qaysi qismini o'qishni aytadi. So'z matndan aynan ko'chiriladi va gap grammatik jihatdan to'g'ri chiqishi kerak. Summary B va C section'larga tegishli.
items: 6 Most mammals have only two kinds of cone, a condition called (6) ... .
7 A red ball on grass may be hard for a dog to see, so it is more likely to find it using (7) ... .
8 Scientists think early mammals lost some cone types because they were active mostly (8) ... .
9 Primates later gained a third type, possibly because it helped them to spot (9) ..., and perhaps young leaves, among older foliage.
why: "Only two types of cone, a condition known as dichromacy".
"It is far more likely to locate it by smell".
"Small and active mainly at night". Mostly = mainly; "at night" — ikki so'z.
"To spot ripe fruit, and perhaps young, protein-rich leaves". "Young leaves" summary'da allaqachon bor.

tasks.title: Questions 10–13
tasks.type: Choose TWO letters, A–E
tasks.instr: Har juftlikda ikkita javob; tartib ahamiyatsiz ("A, C" = "C, A"), imtihonda har harf alohida 1 ball. Variant matnga to'g'ri kelishi yetarli emas — u aynan savoldagi shartga (10–11: "honeybees"; 12–13: "the mantis shrimp") javob bersin.
items: 10–11 Which TWO statements about honeybees are made in the passage? A) They can see ultraviolet light. B) They have more types of photoreceptor than birds. C) They are attracted mainly by the scent of flowers. D) They see red poorly. E) They pollinate most red flowers.

12–13 Which TWO points does the writer make about the mantis shrimp? A) It lives mainly in fresh water. B) Its colour experience has been shown to be richer than ours. C) It was worse than humans at telling similar colours apart. D) It was trained to hunt using coloured targets. E) Its way of processing colour may allow very rapid identification.
why: A — "they see ultraviolet, blue and green". D — "largely insensitive to red". Tuzoqlar: B — asalarida uch tur, qushlarda to'rt — teskari; C — hid haqida gap yo'q; E — teskari: qizil gullarni qushlar changlatadi, asalarilar "tend to overlook".

C — "performed poorly whenever the two wavelengths were close together – far worse than humans". E — "This would make identification very fast". Tuzoqlar: A — "a marine animal" (dengiz); B — bu faqat eski taxmin ("it was once assumed"), tajriba uni tasdiqlamagan; D — ranglarni tanlashga o'rgatilgan, ov qilishga emas.

homework_intro: Bugun Passage 2 dagi uch savol turini bitta tartibda yechdik: avval sarlavhalar (matn xaritasi), keyin summary, keyin TWO letters. Uyda xuddi shu tartibda yolg'iz ishlaysiz.

Birinchi vazifa — Practice 3 "Seeing the world in other colours": 20 daqiqa vaqt oling, 13 savolga javob bering. Har sarlavha yoniga section'ning asosiy g'oyasini 5–7 so'zda yozing, har TWO letters variantiga ✔ / ✘ / ? belgisini qo'ying.

Ikkinchi vazifa — kitobdagi qo'shimcha mashq: Student's Book 22-bet, Vocabulary "Phrasal verbs" 1–2-mashqlar (passage'dagi phrasal verb'lar) va Workbook 15-bet, Vocabulary 1-mashq (Janice haqidagi matn, 14 bo'shliq). Javoblar kitob kalitida.
Uchinchi vazifa — xatolar daftari: bugungi barcha xato javoblarni yozing — savol, to'g'ri javob va sabab ("tafsilot tuzog'i", "so'z chegarasi", "boshqa section haqidagi variant" va h.k.).

kahoot.q: Matching headings: what should the heading match?
options: The main idea of the whole section
A word repeated in the section
Only the first sentence of the section
The most specific detail in the section
kahoot.explain: Sarlavha butun section'ning asosiy g'oyasiga mos keladi. Bitta so'z yoki tafsilotga moslash — eng ko'p uchraydigan tuzoq.

kahoot.q: Which phrase in a section best signals the heading 'Some unsurprising data'?
kahoot.explain: "As predicted" — natija kutilganidek chiqdi, ya'ni unsurprising. Qolganlari: muammo, tajriba, gipoteza.

kahoot.q: Heading 'A curious state of affairs' usually describes a section that...
options: describes how an experiment was carried out
gives the final results of the research
offers a solution to the problem
kahoot.explain: Curious = g'alati. SB A section: bolalar yuzlab so'zni o'rganadi, lekin rang so'zlarida qiynaladi — tushunarsiz holat.

kahoot.q: Why is 'Seeking royal support' wrong for WB Section D?
options: Perkin received help; he did not seek it
The Queen is not mentioned anywhere in Section D
Section D is mainly about colour therapy
Royal support came before the dye was invented
kahoot.explain: Qirolicha D da bor, lekin "receive a helping hand" — izlamagan. Asosiy g'oya: laboratoriyadan do'konlargacha (i).

kahoot.q: What is the best order for Headings + Summary + TWO letters?
options: Headings first, then use them as a map
TWO letters first, because they are easiest
Summary first, and ignore the headings
Read the whole passage twice first
kahoot.explain: Sarlavhalar matn xaritasini beradi: summary va TWO letters javobi qaysi section'da ekanini darhol bilasiz.

kahoot.q: A summary is titled 'The Hypothesis'. Where do you look first?
options: The section that explains the theory
The section that reports the final results
Only the last paragraph of the passage
The section that describes the experiment
kahoot.explain: Summary sarlavhasi kerakli qismni ko'rsatadi: gipoteza B section'da; summary A section oxiridan boshlanadi.

kahoot.q: Summary: 'despite ___, many four-year-olds still struggle'. Which text phrase matches?
options: even after hundreds of training trials
in an effort to work out why
kahoot.explain: Despite = even after. Javob: training trials — matndan aynan, ikki so'z.

kahoot.q: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS. Text: 'the alternative medical practice'. Gap: 'a form of ___'.
kahoot.explain: Uch so'z chegaradan oshadi; "alternative practice" matnda yonma-yon kelmaydi. Kalit: medical practice.

kahoot.q: 'The way colour words are used may be ___ to children.' Which word class fits?
kahoot.explain: "may be ___ to" — sifat kerak. Kalit: unhelpful.

kahoot.q: Choose TWO letters (Questions 10–11). How are marks given?
options: One mark for each correct letter
One mark only if both are correct
Marks only if the order is A–E
No mark if one letter is wrong
kahoot.explain: Har savol raqamiga bitta harf — har to'g'ri harf alohida ball. Tartib ahamiyatsiz.

kahoot.q: An option is true in the passage but not about the thing asked. Is it an answer?
options: No — it must answer the question asked
Yes — every true statement in the passage counts
Only if it is option A
Yes, if it uses the same words as the passage
kahoot.explain: Savoldagi shart muhim: "about the experiment", "before Perkin's creation". Boshqa qism haqidagi fakt javob emas.

kahoot.q: WB 7–8: 'It was only used to colour clothes.' Why reject it?
options: It contradicts the title of the passage
It is about Perkin, not before him
kahoot.explain: "Only" matnda yo'q — cheklovchi so'zlar ko'pincha tuzoq.

kahoot.q: The toddler's colour choices were random, completely ___.
kahoot.explain: Haphazard — tartibsiz, tasodifiy. SB: "mapping of objects to individual colors is haphazard".

kahoot.q: Perkin quickly ___ his discovery by patenting it.
kahoot.explain: Capitalise on — imkoniyatdan foydalanib qolmoq.

kahoot.q: Purple was such a ___ colour in Rome that only the emperor could wear it.
kahoot.explain: Revered — e'zozlangan, juda hurmat qilingan.

kahoot.q: The objects were ___ to the children: they had never seen them before.
kahoot.explain: Novel (sifat) — yangi, notanish. SB 10–11 A: novel = unfamiliar.

kahoot.q: In the end, the problem may simply ___ the way adjectives are used.
kahoot.explain: Come down to — oxir-oqibat ...ga borib taqalmoq.

kahoot.q: At four months, babies can ___ between basic colour categories.
kahoot.explain: Distinguish between — farqlamoq.

kahoot.q: Perkin's work helped ___ between pure chemistry and industry.
kahoot.explain: Bridge the gap between A and B — A va B orasidagi bo'shliqni to'ldirmoq.

kahoot.q: About 70% of the time, colour adjectives are ___ used before the noun.
kahoot.explain: Overwhelmingly — juda katta ko'pchilikda, asosan.

lessons.title: Unit 2 Listening — Section 2: Table completion + Multiple choice (TWO letters)
lessons.grammar_topic: Section 2 kombinatsiyasi: Table completion (ONE WORD) + Choose TWO letters, A–E
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 2 (Colour my world) — rang ko'rgazmasi, ranglar va xarid psixologiyasi
lessons.book_ref: Complete IELTS Bands 6.5–7.5: Student's Book, Unit 2, 23-bet (Listening Section 2, CD1 Track 8–9), recording script 150–151-betlar; Workbook, Unit 2, 14–15-betlar (Listening Section 2, Track 3–4), recording script 55-bet.
objectives: Section 2 da (bitta so'zlovchi, ijtimoiy mavzu) jadval va TWO letters birga kelganda tayyorlanish vaqtini bo'lish: jadval qatorlari bo'yicha "yo'l xaritasi" + TWO letters kalit g'oyasi.
Jadvalda ustun va qator sarlavhalaridan foydalanib, gapiruvchi hozir qaysi qatorda ekanini kuzatib borish.
Jadval bo'shlig'iga paraphrase orqali kelgan so'zni tanib olish (huge → giant, connect → links between) va ONE WORD chegarasiga rioya qilish.
"Choose TWO letters" da beshala variant eshitilganda to'g'ri ikkitasini savoldagi shart bo'yicha ajratish (children vs adults, most popular vs expected).
So'z tuzog'ini tanish: variantdagi so'z audioda boshqa ma'noda keladi ("enthusiastically" → enthusiastic emas).

Workbook, Unit 2, 14–15-betlar — savollar (rasm) va Track 3–4 audiosi (imtihon rejimi, bir marta).
Recording script rasmlari — faqat ustozda; tekshiruvdan keyin ekranga chiqariladi.
Kolonka yoki quloqchin; audio platformadan ochiladi (internetni oldindan tekshiring).
Doskada ikki ustun: "Jadval: qator → kalit so'z" va "TWO letters: ✔ / ✘".

intro: Section 2 — bitta so'zlovchining ijtimoiy yoki umumiy mavzudagi nutqi: radio dasturi, ekskursiya, e'lon. Section 1 dan biroz qiyinroq: suhbatdosh savol berib, ma'lumotni qaytarmaydi, shuning uchun har javob bir marta eshitiladi.

Bu unitda ikki kitobda ham bir xil kombinatsiya: avval jadval (Table completion, ONE WORD), keyin "Choose TWO letters" (A–E dan ikkitasi). Tayyorlanish vaqtini ikkiga bo'ling: jadvalga ko'proq (qatorlar tartibini ko'rish), TWO letters ga — kalit g'oyani tagiga chizish.

Jadvalni "o'qish": qator sarlavhalari (bo'lim nomlari: 'Seeing colour', 'Colour in culture' ...) gapiruvchining yo'l xaritasi. U yangi qatorga o'tganda odatda nomini aytadi: "Another section that's very interesting is called ...". Adashib qolsangiz, keyingi qator nomini kuting va o'sha yerdan davom eting.

Bo'shliq atrofidagi so'zlar javobni paraphrase bilan kutadi: "a huge ___" → "a giant eyeball"; "to connect colour and ___" → "links between colour and certain aspects of our lifestyle". Ustun sarlavhasi (Aim / Examples / Features) bo'shliqning turini aytadi.

ONE WORD — bitta so'z. Artikl, sifat yoki jadvalda bor so'zni qo'shsangiz, javob 0 ball: "giant eyeball", "the lighting", "personality test" — xato. Ba'zan ikki xil so'z ham to'g'ri bo'lishi mumkin (lighting / atmosphere) — kalit ikkalasini qabul qiladi, lekin siz bittasini yozasiz.

Choose TWO letters: Band 7 darajasida beshala variant deyarli har doim audioda tilga olinadi. To'g'ri ikkitasi savoldagi shartga mos keladi, qolganlari: (1) boshqa guruh haqida (bolalar emas, kattalar), (2) kutilgan, lekin bo'lmagan narsa ("purple, which I would have expected to be a high scorer"), (3) so'z tuzog'i ("enthusiastically"). Javoblar variantlar tartibida kelmasligi mumkin.
Transfer: imlo (eyeball, disability, preferences), ko'plik "-s" (experiments), bitta so'z. TWO letters uchun ikkita harf — ishonchingiz komil bo'lmasa ham, ikkinchi harfni yozing.
formulas: a huge + ot; colour and + ot
Transfer: bitta so'z, imlo, ikki harf
presentation: Jadvalda qaysi yo'nalishda o'qiyman — qator yoki ustun?
Odatda chapdan o'ngga, qatorma-qator: gapiruvchi bitta bo'lim haqida gapirib, keyingisiga o'tadi.
"Giant eyeball" eshitdim. Ikkalasini yozsam-chi?
Yo'q. Jadvalda "huge" bor — u "giant" ning o'rnida. Faqat "eyeball".
Kalitda "lighting/atmosphere" — qaysi birini yozaman?
Bittasini. Ikkalasi ham to'g'ri, lekin "lighting and atmosphere" — uch so'z, ONE WORD chegarasidan oshadi.
TWO letters da beshala variant eshitildi. Qanday tanlayman?
Savoldagi shartni qayta o'qing: "most popular", "children", "limited amount of money". Shartga javob beradigan ikkitasi — to'g'ri.
Javoblar variantlar tartibida keladimi?
Shart emas. SB 7–8 da variantlar A, D, B, C, E tartibida tilga olinadi (blue → purple → deep pink → lime green → red). Shuning uchun beshala variantni birdaniga kuzatib boring.
Variantdagi so'zni aynan eshitdim. Demak to'g'rimi?
Ehtiyot bo'ling: WB 7–8 da "enthusiastically" eshitiladi, lekin "feel enthusiastic" — javob emas. Aynan so'z ko'pincha tuzoq.
notes: 5.0 da jadval va MCQ alohida o'rganilgan; 6.0 da Section 2 da MCQ + xarita bo'lgan. Endi Section 2 da jadval + TWO letters — Band 7 uchun asosiy qiyinchilik: beshala variant ham eshitiladi.
Tekshiruvda har TWO letters savoli uchun beshala variantning "taqdirini" so'rang: qaysi gapda eshitildi va nega javob emas?

Kuchli o'quvchilarga: Workbook Track 4 ni skriptsiz tinglab, to'rt xil xaridor turi va ularga mos ranglarni jadval qilib yozish (impulse → red, restricted budget → light blue, low income → pink, plenty of money → purple).
mistakes: Jadvalda "huge" bor; kamera — ko'z ichidagi qurilma

how: CORE — ko'rgazma va xarid mavzusidagi asosiy so'zlar; STRONG — rangni tasvirlash; SUPER — Section 2 dagi so'zlashuv iboralari.
Har o'quvchi o'zi borgan ko'rgazma yoki do'kon haqida 3 gap aytadi va kamida ikkita yangi so'zni ishlatadi.
Takror so'zlar: hands-on (1-dars) va perceive (3-dars) — yangi so'z sifatida sanalmaydi; ularni gapda faol ishlatishga e'tibor bering.
core: The colour exhibition runs until the end of May.
Rang ko'rgazmasi may oxirigacha davom etadi.
Each display explains how colour shapes our world.
Har bir eksponat rang dunyomizni qanday shakllantirishini tushuntiradi.
Many animals use camouflage to hide from predators.
Ko'p hayvonlar yirtqichlardan yashirinish uchun niqoblanadi.
We all perceive light blue in the same way.
Biz hammamiz och ko'k rangni bir xil idrok etamiz.
Red is the predominant colour in many fast food outlets.
Ko'p fastfud do'konlarida qizil — asosiy rang.
Colour preferences often depend on personality.
Rangni afzal ko'rish ko'pincha shaxsiyatga bog'liq.
Warm colours can stimulate your appetite.
Bright plates may help patients who have lost their appetite.
Yorqin likoplar ishtahasi yo'qolgan bemorlarga yordam berishi mumkin.
Shoppers on a tight budget respond well to light blue.
Mablag'i cheklangan xaridorlar och ko'k rangga yaxshi ta'sirlanadi.
strong: It's a very vibrant exhibition, full of bright colours.
Bu yorqin ranglarga to'la juda jo'shqin ko'rgazma.
Children usually prefer bold colours to pale ones.
Bolalar odatda och ranglardan ko'ra yorqin, keskin ranglarni afzal ko'radi.
The chapter was striking because of its photography.
Its colour helps the animal conceal itself in the jungle.
Rangi hayvonga o'rmonda yashirinishga yordam beradi.
As an impulse shopper, I buy things the moment I like them.
O'ylamay xarid qiluvchi sifatida yoqqan narsani darhol olaman.
Fast food outlets want a quick turnover of customers.
Fastfud do'konlari mijozlar tez almashinishini xohlaydi.
super: qo'l bilan ushlab, amalda sinab ko'riladigan
The museum is packed with hands-on exhibits.
Muzey qo'l bilan sinab ko'riladigan eksponatlarga to'la.
In the camouflage suit, you disappear to all intents and purposes.
People on low incomes find it hard to part with their cash.
Kam daromadli odamlar pul sarflashga qiynaladi.
Children pick out bright colours over and above the rest.
Bolalar yorqin ranglarni boshqalardan ustun qo'yib tanlaydi.

class_ex.title: Jadval bo'shlig'ini bashorat qilish (SB, 2-mashq)
class_ex.instr: SB Questions 1–6 ni tinglamasdan o'qing. Har bo'shliq atrofidagi kalit g'oyani ayting va qanday so'z kerakligini taxmin qiling.
items: 1 — "view the gallery through a huge ___"
2 — "to connect colour and ___"
3 — "learn how a ___ affects sight"
4 — "put on a camouflage suit and pick a suitable ___"
5 — "The ___ room" ("to show how colours make us feel")
6 — "listen to music as the colours and ___ change"
answers: birlik ot — ko'rishga ta'sir qiladigan narsa
birlik ot — hayvon / tabiat, yashirinish joyi
why: "a huge" — sifat + birlik ot; "through" — oyna, teshik, ko'z kabi narsa.
Bo'lim nomi "Colour in culture" — lekin "culture" ni yozmang, u allaqachon jadvalda.
"a ___ affects sight" — kasallik, nuqson yoki holat.
Kamuflyaj — fon (orqa ko'rinish) tanlash kerak, unda ko'rinmay qolasiz.
Maqsad ustuni: "how colours make us feel" — kayfiyat.
"colours and ___ change" — rang bilan birga o'zgaradigan: yorug'lik yoki muhit.
class_ex.note: Bu mashq SB kalitidagi "suggested answers" ga mos keladi. Tinglagandan keyin taxminlarni haqiqiy javoblar bilan solishtiring.

class_ex.title: "Qaysi ikkitasi?" — TWO letters tuzoq mashqi
class_ex.instr: Ustoz gapni o'qiydi. O'quvchilar savolga IKKITA javob beradi va qaysi so'z tuzoq ekanini aytadi.
items: "White was only moderately popular. I expected green to win, but it was yellow and orange that came out on top." — Which TWO colours were most popular?

"Parents told us they choose dark school bags because they don't show the dirt. The children, though, wanted bags in the colours of their favourite cartoon characters, or ones that are easy to spot in a crowded cloakroom." — Which TWO reasons did the children give?
"Pale colours make a small room look bigger, but dark walls make a bedroom feel cosy and can even help you sleep." — Which TWO effects do dark walls have?

"Passengers in a hurry follow the red signs to the gates, while those with time to spare follow the green and blue signs to the shops. The grey doors are for staff only." — Which TWO colours do passengers with plenty of time follow?
why: White — "only moderately popular"; green — "I expected", bo'lmagan narsa.
"Don't show the dirt" — ota-onalar sababi, bolalar emas (guruh tuzog'i).
"Look bigger" — och ranglar haqida, to'q ranglar emas.
Red — shoshayotgan yo'lovchilar, ya'ni teskari guruh; grey — xodimlar uchun. "Time to spare" = plenty of time (paraphrase).
class_ex.note: Har gapda uch-to'rt variant eshitiladi, lekin savol shartiga faqat ikkitasi mos. Bu — Band 7 dagi TWO letters ning mohiyati.

listenings.title: Student's Book, Track 8: 'Eye for Colour' exhibition (Q1–6)
intro: Radio dasturi: Darren Whitlock "Eye for Colour" ko'rgazmasining to'rt bo'limi haqida gapiradi. Tinglashdan oldin 30 soniya: jadvaldagi to'rt bo'lim nomini va har bo'shliq turini belgilang (SB 2-mashq).

tasks.title: Questions 1–6 — Eye for Colour Exhibition
tasks.type: Complete the table below. Write ONE WORD for each answer.
tasks.instr: Write ONE WORD for each answer. Tinglashdan oldin har bo'shliq atrofidagi kalit so'zlarni belgilang va qanday so'z kerakligini (ot / sifat / ko'plik) taxmin qiling. Jadval qatorlari = gapiruvchining tartibi.
why: "You look at the museum gallery through a giant eyeball". Huge = giant. Tuzoq: "a 32" camera and screen" — ko'z ichidagi qurilma.
"The powerful links that exist between colour and certain aspects of our lifestyle". Connect = links between. Tuzoq: "culture" — bo'lim nomi.

"A projector subtly alters the lighting in the room and with it, the atmosphere". Change = alters. Ikkalasi ham to'g'ri, lekin bittasi yoziladi.
tasks.note: 6-savol: "lighting and atmosphere" yozgan o'quvchi ONE WORD qoidasini buzadi. Kalit ikki variantni qabul qiladi — lekin bitta so'z.

tasks.title: Questions 7–10
tasks.type: Choose TWO letters, A–E
tasks.instr: Ikkita harf; tartib ahamiyatsiz ("B, E" = "E, B"), har harf alohida 1 ball. Beshala variant ham ko'pincha eshitiladi — tinglayotganda har variantga ✔ / ✘ qo'yib boring. To'g'ri javob odatda paraphrase bilan keladi.
items: 7–8 Which TWO colours were most popular among visitors? A) blue B) deep pink C) lime green D) purple E) red

9–10 Which TWO reasons did the children give for selecting their favourite colour? A) They like wearing it. B) They notice it more than other colours. C) It makes them feel relaxed. D) It has a connection with a sport. E) Someone they admire wears it.
why: B — "unlike deep pink, which came next to top". E — "red ... was more popular with children than anything else". Tuzoqlar: A — "of average popularity"; D — "which I would have expected to be a high scorer, had just 1.73%"; C — "in the middle ground".

B — "they go for colours that hit them ... that they pick out over and above the rest". D — "there are associations with football that led a lot of both boys and girls to go for particular colours". Tuzoqlar: A — "As adults, it's all about clothes"; C — "It's less to do with how they feel – whether it calms them down"; E — "adults would be more likely to go for something worn by someone they really like".
tasks.note: 9–10 — darsning eng yaxshi misoli: A va E kattalar haqida, C inkor bilan keladi ("less to do with"). Uchala tuzoq ham audioda aniq eshitiladi.

tasks.instr: Ikkita harf; tartib ahamiyatsiz ("B, E" = "E, B"), har harf alohida 1 ball. Beshala variant ham ko'pincha eshitiladi — tinglayotganda har variantga ✔ / ✘ qo'yib boring. To'g'ri javob odatda paraphrase bilan keladi.
items: 7–8 According to the book, which of these TWO effects are red and orange believed to have on shoppers? A) They calm you down. B) They make you feel energetic. C) They give you an appetite. D) They make you feel enthusiastic. E) They encourage you to spend more.
9–10 Which of these TWO colours do people with a limited amount of money respond to the best? A) light blue B) purple C) orange D) pink E) red
why: B — "Warm colours not only give you more energy". C — "they can also stimulate or bring on hunger". Tuzoqlar: A — "calming cool colours such as blue and green"; D — "used so enthusiastically by fast food companies" (so'z tuzog'i); E — teskari: juda yorqin bo'lsa "a hurrying effect", ko'proq sarflash uchun "best avoided".

A — "Those on a restricted budget tend to respond well to light blue". D — "for those on a really low income ... appears to be pink". Tuzoqlar: E — impulse shoppers; C — "a similar, although less pronounced, effect" (qizilga o'xshash); B — "Consumers with plenty of money".
