listenings.title: Jony Academy mashqi: Colour Week at the Harbour Arts Centre (Q1–10)
listenings.qtype: Table completion (ONE WORD) + Choose TWO letters — Section 2
intro: Ustoz skriptni bir marta, tabiiy tezlikda o'qiydi (bitta ovoz — radio boshlovchisi); javob so'zlarini urg'u yoki pauza bilan ajratib ko'rsatmang. O'quvchilar avval 45 soniya jadvalni va Q7–10 ni o'qiydi.

1-, 2-, 4- va 5-bo'shliqlarda tuzoq bor: javobdan oldin boshqa so'z eshitiladi, lekin u rad etiladi yoki boshqa narsaga tegishli bo'lib chiqadi; 3- va 6-javoblar to'g'ridan-to'g'ri yoki paraphrase bilan keladi. TWO letters da beshala variant eshitiladi. Tekshiruvda o'quvchi tuzoq gapni ham aytishi kerak.
transcript: PRESENTER: Good morning, and welcome back to 'Out and About'. Today I'm going to tell you about Colour Week, which starts at the Harbour Arts Centre next Monday and runs for six days. There's far too much on the programme to cover everything, so I'll focus on three events for adults, and then say a few words about what's on offer for families.

PRESENTER: The week opens on Monday evening with a talk called 'Dyes of the Silk Road'. The speaker is a textile historian who has spent many years studying traditional dyeing in Central Asia. People often assume that most natural dyes came from minerals, but she'll be explaining that the richest reds were, in fact, produced from insects – tiny creatures that were dried and crushed in their millions. And at the end of the talk, rather than the usual slideshow, she's bringing a collection of antique fabrics, and the audience will be able to handle some of them, which I think is a real treat.

PRESENTER: On Wednesday afternoon, there's a practical workshop, 'Mixing your palette', run by the landscape painter Nadia Brooks. It's designed for complete beginners, and the aim is to show you how to create almost any colour from just three tubes of paint. All the materials are supplied – paints, brushes, even aprons – but you're asked to bring a photograph of a place you love, because that's what you'll be painting. The printed programme says the workshop lasts two hours, but I've checked with the centre and it's actually been extended to three, so you'll get plenty of practice.

PRESENTER: On Thursday morning there's a guided walk called 'Colour and the City', led by a local architect. Please note that it doesn't start at the Arts Centre itself – you meet at ten o'clock outside the old harbour station. The walk takes you through the old town, where you'll learn why so many of the buildings are painted in such bright shades. Apparently it wasn't just decoration: fishermen painted their houses in strong colours so that they could recognise them from the sea. The walk lasts about ninety minutes and finishes at the market.

PRESENTER: Now, for families. On Saturday the whole ground floor is given over to children. There's a 'colour lab' where kids can do simple experiments – separating the colours in felt-tip ink, that kind of thing. Some parents have asked whether there's an age limit. There isn't, although the organisers say the activities are best suited to children over five. And unlike the rest of the festival, the family day is completely free. There was talk of a face-painting stall, but sadly that's been cancelled because there weren't enough volunteers.

PRESENTER: A couple of final tips. Places on the Wednesday workshop are limited to fifteen, so I'd strongly advise booking online as soon as you can. For the talk, you can pay on the door, and there's usually plenty of space, so there's no need to turn up early. Parking near the Arts Centre is very limited during the week, so if you can, take the bus – the number 12 stops right outside. The walk only goes ahead if it's dry; if it's cancelled, you'll get your money back automatically. And there's no combined ticket for all the events this year, unfortunately. Right, that's all from me – enjoy Colour Week!

kahoot.q: IELTS Listening Section 2 is usually...
options: one speaker on a social or general topic
two students and a tutor discussing an assignment
a phone booking between two people
kahoot.explain: Section 2 — bitta so'zlovchi, ijtimoiy mavzu (radio, ekskursiya, e'lon). Section 1 dan biroz qiyinroq.

kahoot.q: Table: 'view the gallery through a huge ___'. You hear 'a giant eyeball'. You write...
kahoot.explain: Jadvalda "huge" bor — u "giant" o'rnida. ONE WORD: faqat eyeball.

kahoot.q: ONE WORD only. Which answer is acceptable for SB Question 6?
kahoot.explain: Kalit: lighting / atmosphere. Artikl qo'shilsa ikki so'z bo'ladi; projector — boshqa narsa.

kahoot.q: How do the correct options in a TWO-letter question usually come?
options: With the exact words of the option
kahoot.explain: Javoblar variantlar tartibida kelmasligi mumkin va ko'pincha paraphrase bilan keladi.

kahoot.q: 'Purple, which I would have expected to be a high scorer, had just 1.73%.' Purple is...
kahoot.explain: "Would have expected" — kutilgan, lekin bo'lmagan narsa. Eng mashhurlar: deep pink va red.

kahoot.q: 'They pick out colours over and above the rest.' Which option does this paraphrase?
options: They notice it more than other colours.
kahoot.explain: Pick out over and above the rest = notice more than others. SB 9–10 B.

kahoot.q: 'As adults, it's all about clothes.' Why is 'They like wearing it' wrong for children?
options: Clothes are never mentioned in the recording
It is a paraphrase of football
kahoot.explain: Savol bolalar haqida. Kiyim va yoqtirgan odam kiyadigan rang — kattalar sabablari.

kahoot.q: WB: warm colours are used 'enthusiastically' by fast food firms. Is 'feel enthusiastic' correct?
options: No — the effects are energy and hunger
Yes — the same word is heard in the recording
kahoot.explain: So'z bir xil, ma'no boshqa: kompaniyalar ranglarni ishtiyoq bilan ishlatadi. Javob: B (energy) va C (appetite).

kahoot.q: What is the best use of preparation time for a table task?
options: Read around each gap and predict the word type
Read only the column headings and the title
Look at Questions 7–10 only and ignore the table
kahoot.explain: Har bo'shliq atrofidagi kalit so'zlar va so'z turi — tinglashda nimani kutishni aytadi.

kahoot.q: WB table says 'A ___ test'. You write 'personality test'. Result?
options: Wrong: two words, 'test' is already given
Correct: both words are heard in the recording
Half a mark, because one word is right
kahoot.explain: Jadvaldagi so'zni takrorlamang. ONE WORD: personality.

kahoot.q: 'Those on a restricted budget respond well to light blue.' A restricted budget means...
kahoot.explain: Restricted budget = limited amount of money. WB 9–10: light blue (A) va pink (D).

kahoot.q: In a TWO-letter question you are sure of only one answer. What do you do?
options: Write it and guess the second
Write three letters to be safe
kahoot.explain: Har harf alohida ball: ishonchlisini yozing, ikkinchisini tuzoqlarni chiqarib tashlab tanlang.

kahoot.q: The exhibition is packed with ___ exhibits that you can touch and try.
kahoot.explain: Hands-on — qo'l bilan sinab ko'riladigan, amaliy.

kahoot.q: Many animals use ___ to hide from predators.
kahoot.explain: Camouflage — niqoblanish: rang, shakl va naqsh orqali yashirinish.

kahoot.q: Red is the ___ colour in many fast food restaurants.
kahoot.explain: Predominant — asosiy, ustun.

kahoot.q: Warm colours can ___ hunger.
kahoot.explain: Stimulate — qo'zg'atmoq. WB: "stimulate or bring on hunger".

kahoot.q: Children tend to choose bright, eye-catching, ___ colours.
kahoot.explain: Bold colours — yorqin, keskin, ko'zga tashlanadigan ranglar. SB: "the bold colours were the winners".

kahoot.q: People on a very low income find it hard to ___ their cash.
kahoot.explain: Part with one's cash — puldan ajralmoq, sarflamoq.

kahoot.q: Our eyes differ, yet we all ___ colour in the same way.
kahoot.explain: Perceive — idrok etmoq. WB: "we all perceive colour in the same way".

kahoot.q: Fast food outlets want a quick ___ of customers.
kahoot.explain: Turnover — mijozlarning tez almashinishi.

lessons.title: Unit 3 Reading — Passage 3: Yes / No / Not Given + Summary completion (word box) + Multiple choice
lessons.grammar_topic: Passage 3 kombinatsiyasi: YES / NO / NOT GIVEN + Summary (so'zlar ro'yxati A–I) + Multiple choice (A–D)
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 3 (A healthy life) — dori sinovlari, platsebo effekti, jismoniy faollik va miya
lessons.book_ref: Complete IELTS Bands 6.5–7.5: Student's Book, Unit 3, 32–34-betlar (Reading Section 3: "Examining the placebo effect"); Workbook, Unit 3, 20–22-betlar (Reading Section 3: exercise and the brain). Kalit: SB 169–170-betlar, WB 64-bet. Practice 1–3 — Jony Academy matnlari.
objectives: Passage 3 dagi uch savol turini (Y/N/NG, summary with a box, MCQ A–D) matnning qaysi qismiga tegishli ekanini 2 daqiqada aniqlash (xarita usuli).
YES / NO / NOT GIVEN ni T/F/NG dan farqlash: savol faktni emas, yozuvchining da'vosi va bahosini (in my view, alarmingly, not surprisingly) tekshiradi.
Summary'da bo'shliq atrofidagi so'zlardan grammatik turni aniqlash va A–I ro'yxatidan grammatik jihatdan mos, lekin ma'nosi noto'g'ri variantlarni chiqarib tashlash.
MCQ (A–D) da ism, raqam va iqtibos ("line 80") orqali joyni topish, keyin yuqori va quyi gaplarni o'qib, uchta tuzoqni isbot bilan rad etish.
Band 7 darajasidagi so'z birikmalari (gauge the effectiveness, overlook a factor, yield results, challenge an assumption) bilan passage'ni tez paraphrase qilish.
materials: Student's Book, Unit 3, 32–34-betlar ("Examining the placebo effect") — sinfda birga ishlanadi (quyida rasm).
Workbook, Unit 3, 20–22-betlar ("Scientific research reveals hidden benefits of regular exercise") — mustaqil mashq (quyida rasm).
Practice 1–3 matnlari chop etilgan varaqlar (har o'quvchiga) — pastdagi Reading bo'limidan.
Taymer: Passage 3 uchun 20 daqiqa normasi doskaga yoziladi (14 savol).
Doskada uch ustun: "Y/N/NG → qaysi xatboshilar?", "Summary sarlavhasi → qaysi xatboshilar?", "MCQ → ism/raqam/line".

intro: Passage 3 — imtihondagi eng qiyin matn: uzunroq (700–900 so'z), akademik uslubda, ko'pincha muallifning fikri bilan yozilgan va 13 emas, 14 ta savol. 7.0 darajasida vazifa — uch xil savol turini bitta matnda 20 daqiqada, tartib va isbot bilan yechish.

Birinchi qadam — XARITA (2 daqiqa). Uchala savol guruhini ko'zdan kechiring: Y/N/NG ning kalit so'zlari (Merck, MK-869, Kaptchuk), summary SARLAVHASI ("Merck and MK-869" — faqat birinchi ikki xatboshi) va MCQ dagi ismlar (William Potter, Ted Kaptchuk) hamda "line 80". Shunda matn uch qismga bo'linadi va har qismni bir marta o'qiysiz.

YES / NO / NOT GIVEN — T/F/NG ning "fikr" versiyasi. Savol "Do the statements agree with the CLAIMS of the WRITER?" deydi: muallifning bahosi, xulosasi yoki ishonchi tekshiriladi. Signal so'zlar: not surprisingly, alarmingly, no doubt, it is hard to justify, in my view, the stakes could hardly be higher.

NO — muallif aksini da'vo qiladi ("MK-869 has not been the only..." ↔ "was unique"). NOT GIVEN — mavzu bor, lekin muallif aynan shu da'vo haqida hech narsa demaydi ("medical conditions" tilga olingan, lekin qaysi kasallik platseboga osonroq javob berishi yo'q). Qoida: NO uchun matnda qarshi gapni ko'rsata olishingiz SHART.

Summary with a box (A–I): 9 ta variant, 5 ta bo'shliq — 4 tasi ortiqcha. Avval bo'shliq atrofidagi so'zlarni o'qing va so'z turini aniqlang: "increasing ___ in the drugs industry" — ot; "MK-869 had some ___" — sanalmaydigan/ko'plikdagi ot, ijobiy ma'no. Keyin matndagi gapni topib, uning ma'nosiga mos variantni tanlang — matndagi so'z bilan bir xil so'z deyarli hech qachon bo'lmaydi.

Box tuzog'i: har bo'shliq uchun odatda 2–3 variant grammatik jihatdan mos keladi. Masalan, "increasing ___" ga prices, competition, criticism — hammasi to'g'ri keladi. Farqni faqat matn beradi: Merck raqobatchilardan orqada qolgani ("falling behind its rivals") — competition. "Prices" — tuzoq: matnda "cheaper generic products" bor, ya'ni narx o'smaydi, aksincha tushadi — "increasing prices" matnga zid.

MCQ (A–D): savoldagi ism/raqamni skaner qiling, keyin 3–5 gapni (yuqorisi va pasti) diqqat bilan o'qing. Har noto'g'ri variant uchun sabab toping: matnda yo'q (NG turi), qarama-qarshi (NO turi) yoki to'g'ri fakt, lekin savolga javob emas. "What does X refer to in line 80?" savolida iqtibosdan OLDINGI gapni o'qing — o'xshatish odatda oldingi fikrni tushuntiradi.

Tartib: Y/N/NG va MCQ javoblari matn tartibida keladi; summary esa bir necha xatboshidan olinishi mumkin (SB exam advice: "The answers may come from more than one part of the passage"), lekin summary ichidagi tartib ham odatda matn tartibiga mos.

Vaqt (20 daqiqa): xarita — 2, Y/N/NG — 6, summary — 5, MCQ — 5, tekshiruv va transfer — 2. Bitta savolga 2 daqiqadan ko'p sarflamang: belgilab o'ting, oxirida qayting. Summary javobi — faqat HARF (H, A, C), so'zning o'zi emas.
formulas: Uch guruhni ko'zdan kechirib, xarita tuzing
Y/N/NG → 3- va 9–11-xatboshilar (MK-869, Kaptchuk); summary → 1–2; MCQ → 5–10 (Potter, line 80, Kaptchuk)
unique, can ruin, to be expected
MCQ: ism/line → atrofdagi 3–5 gap → 3 tuzoqni rad eting
presentation: T/F/NG va Y/N/NG ning farqi nimada?
T/F/NG — matndagi FAKT (information); Y/N/NG — muallifning DA'VOSI va fikri (claims/views). Yondashuv bir xil, lekin Y/N/NG da baholovchi so'zlar (surprisingly, sadly, arguably) muhim.
Matnda "not surprisingly" bor. Bu nimani bildiradi?
Muallif natijani kutilgan deb hisoblaydi. SB 4-savol: "It was to be expected that the third group would do better" — YES.
Summary javobini matndagi so'z bilan yozsam bo'ladimi?
Yo'q. Box bo'lsa — faqat harf (A–I). Harf o'rniga so'z yozish yoki ro'yxatda yo'q so'z yozish — 0 ball.
Bitta harfni ikki marta ishlatsa bo'ladimi?
Odatda yo'q — har harf bir marta. Agar ikki bo'shliqqa bir xil harf chiqsa, bittasini qayta tekshiring.
MCQ da ikkita variant ham to'g'ridek ko'rinadi.
Savolning so'rog'ini qayta o'qing: "what significant DISCOVERY" — kashfiyot so'ralgan. B varianti (kutish ro'yxatida sog'ayish) — tadqiqotchilar oldindan bilgan narsa, kashfiyot emas.
"Line 80" ni qanday topaman?

Matn chetiga qarang: SB matnida har qator raqamlanmagan, faqat savolda so'ralgan qator belgilangan — 33-betda o'ng ustun chetidagi "line 80" yozuvi "a tight race" gapi yonida turadi. Iqtibosdan oldingi 1–2 gapni o'qing: o'xshatish nimani tushuntirayotgani o'sha yerda.

Har javobdan keyin uch savol bering: "isbot gap qaysi?", "savoldagi qaysi so'z matnda qanday aytilgan?", "qolgan variantlar nega xato?" — Band 7 o'quvchisi uchinchisiga ham javob bera olishi kerak.

class_ex.title: Fakt yoki fikr? — mini-matn
class_ex.instr: Ustoz doskaga yozadi yoki o'qiydi: "Hospitals increasingly rely on apps to remind patients to take their medicine. The idea is sensible, but the enthusiasm surrounding it is, in my view, exaggerated: reminders help people who forget, not people who have decided that a drug is not worth taking. Designers would do better to spend time explaining why a treatment matters." Har gap uchun javob va isbot so'z.
items: Hospitals are using reminder apps more and more.
Reminder apps are a completely useless idea.
Reminder apps are most popular with older patients.
Reminders cannot solve the problem of patients who doubt a drug's value.
why: "Increasingly rely on apps" = "more and more".
"The idea is sensible" — muallif g'oyani foydasiz demaydi, faqat ishtiyoqni "exaggerated" deydi. Qarshi gap bor — NO.
Yosh guruhlar haqida umuman gap yo'q — NOT GIVEN.
"Reminders help people who forget, not people who have decided that a drug is not worth taking".
class_ex.note: 2-gapda ko'p o'quvchi "exaggerated" ni ko'rib YES deydi. Farqni ko'rsating: "ishtiyoq oshirib yuborilgan" ≠ "g'oya foydasiz".

class_ex.title: Summary bo'shliqlari: so'z turi va eliminatsiya (SB, 5-mashq)
class_ex.instr: SB 34-betdagi "Merck and MK-869" summary'si. Matnni o'qimasdan: har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerak va box'dagi qaysi variantlar grammatik jihatdan umuman to'g'ri kelmaydi?
items: 6 — "concerns about increasing ___ in the drugs industry"
7 — "Merck decided to increase its ___ in the anti-depressant market"
8 — "Initially, MK-869 had some ___, but later trials revealed a different picture"
9 — "Although key ___ could be treated with the drug"
10 — "In the end, the ___ indicated that it was pointless continuing"
answers: ot, ijobiy ma'no; mumkin: success, activity
ko'plikdagi ot (davolanadigan narsa); mumkin: symptoms, diseases, patients
ko'plikdagi ot (natija ko'rsatadigan narsa); mumkin: tests, patients
why: "Increasing" dan keyin o'sadigan narsa. Keyin matn hal qiladi: "falling behind its rivals" → H competition.
"Increase its ___ in the market" — bozordagi ishtiroki: "expanding the company's reach" → A activity.
"Had some ___, but later..." — "but" ijobiydan salbiyga o'tishni ko'rsatadi: "tested extremely well early on" → C success.
"Could be treated" — davolanadigan narsa: patients "treated" bo'ladi, lekin "key" + "treated" → G symptoms ("hopelessness and anxiety lift").
"Indicated" — natija ko'rsatadi: "the trials crossed the futility boundary" → E tests.
class_ex.note: Mashqdan keyin SB 6-mashq: xatboshilarni o'qib, harflarni tanlash. Grammatik mos, lekin ma'nosi xato variantlarni (prices, criticism, diseases) ovoz chiqarib rad etish.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: YES / NO / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: YES — gap yozuvchining da'vosi/fikri bilan mos; NO — yozuvchi buning aksini da'vo qiladi; NOT GIVEN — yozuvchi bu haqda nima deb o'ylashini matndan aytib bo'lmaydi. Kalit so'zlar: Merck, MK-869, well-established company, medical conditions, Kaptchuk, combined treatments.
items: Merck's experience with MK-869 was unique.
These days, a small number of unsuccessful test results can ruin a well-established drugs company.
Some medical conditions are more easily treated by a placebo than others.
It was to be expected that the third group in Kaptchuk's trial would do better than the other two groups.
Kaptchuk's research highlights the fact that combined drug and placebo treatments should be avoided.
why: "MK-869 has not been the only much-awaited medical breakthrough to be undone in recent years by the placebo effect". "Unique" ↔ "not the only".
"In today's economy, the fate of a well-established company can hang on the outcome of a handful of tests". "A handful" = "a small number".
Kasalliklar tilga olinadi ("a common but painful medical condition"), lekin qaysi biri platseboga osonroq javob berishi taqqoslanmaydi.
"Not surprisingly, the health of those in the third group improved most". "Not surprisingly" = "it was to be expected" — bu muallifning bahosi.
"Studies like this open the door to hybrid treatment strategies" + Potter: "the best placebo response plus the best drug response". Muallif birgalikdagi davolashni qo'llab-quvvatlaydi.
tasks.note: 4-savol — Y/N/NG ning eng yaxshi namunasi: fakt (3-guruh eng ko'p yaxshilandi) T/F/NG ga, "not surprisingly" esa muallif fikriga tegishli. Kalit: SB 169-bet.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10 — Merck and MK-869
tasks.type: Complete the summary using the list of words, A–I, below.
tasks.instr: Sarlavha "Merck and MK-869" — faqat birinchi ikki xatboshi (Merck, Scolnick, MK-869). Javob — faqat harf.
items: 6 As a result of concerns about increasing (6) in the drugs industry, the pharmaceutical company Merck
7 decided to increase its (7) in the anti-depressant market. The development of the drug MK-869 was seen as the way forward.
8 Initially, MK-869 had some (8), but later trials revealed a different picture.
9 Although key (9) could be treated with the drug, a sugar pill was proving equally effective.
10 In the end, the (10) indicated that it was pointless continuing with the development of the drug.
why: "Merck ... was falling behind its rivals in sales ... cheaper generic products to flood the market". Rivals = competition. B prices — tuzoq: generic dorilar arzon, lekin narx o'sishi aytilmagan.
"Key to his strategy was expanding the company's reach into the anti-depressant market". Reach = activity. C success — tuzoq: bozorda muvaffaqiyat "oshirish" emas, ishtirokni kengaytirish.
"The drug tested extremely well early on, with minimal side effects". "But later" — "Behind the scenes, however, MK-869 was starting to unravel".
"Many test subjects treated with the medication felt their hopelessness and anxiety lift". Hopelessness, anxiety = symptoms. F diseases — depressiyaning o'zi davolanmagan, alomatlar yengillashgan.
"In the jargon of the industry, the trials crossed the 'futility boundary'". Trials = tests; futility = pointless.
tasks.note: 6-savolda B (prices) ni tanlaganlarga: "cheaper generic products" narxning TUSHISHI haqida, "increasing" ga zid. Kalit: SB 170-bet.

tasks.title: Questions 11–14
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D
tasks.instr: Ismlar bo'yicha skaner qiling: William Potter (5–7-xatboshi), "tight race" (line 80, 7-xatboshi), Ted Kaptchuk (9–10-xatboshi).
items: 11 Which of the following is true of William Potter's research? A) It was based on recently developed drugs that he had recommended. B) It included trial results from a range of drugs companies. C) Some of the trial results he investigated had not been made public. D) Some of his findings were not accepted by the drugs industry.

12 What did William Potter's research reveal about the location of drugs trials? A) The placebo effect was weakest in the US. B) Results were not consistent around the world. C) Results varied depending on the type of hospital. D) The FDA preferred drugs to be tested in different countries.
13 What does the 'tight race' refer to in line 80? A) the standard tests B) consistent results C) ratings by trial observers D) testing sites

14 What significant discovery was made by Ted Kaptchuk? A) The effects of a placebo can last longer than previously thought. B) Patients' health can improve while waiting to undergo a trial. C) Patients respond better to a placebo if they are treated by the same clinician throughout the trial. D) Those conducting a placebo trial need to know the subjects' disorder well.
why: "Potter combed through his company's database of published and unpublished trials — including those that had been kept secret". B — tuzoq: bitta kompaniya ("his company's"); A — dorilar yillar davomida yozilgan, yangi emas.

"Potter discovered, however, that geographic location alone could determine the outcome". A — tuzoq: Diazepam AQShda "likely to fail", Prozac esa AQShda yaxshiroq — umumiy xulosa yo'q; C — kasalxona turi aytilmagan.

Kalit izohi: tight race — standart testlar ("the standard tests used to gauge volunteers' improvement"); judges = trial observers, finish line = testlardagi baho. C — tuzoq: kuzatuvchilar "judges" ga o'xshatilgan, poyga emas.

"The benefits of their 'bogus' treatment persisted for weeks afterward, contrary to the belief ... that the placebo response is short-lived". B — tadqiqotchilar buni oldindan bilgan ("researchers know that..."), kashfiyot emas.
tasks.note: 13-savol eng qiyin: o'xshatishda uch element bor — race (testlar), judges (kuzatuvchilar), finish line (baholash mezoni). Doskada uchta ustun bilan chizing. Kalit: SB 170-bet.

B) Exercising for up to an hour a day can improve memory and learning for both young and old, scientists have found. C) Regular exercise benefits us all, whether young or old, but there are hidden dangers, scientists warn.

items: The possible impact of a sedentary lifestyle on the way children perform in the classroom is very worrying.
It is only recently that people have discovered exercise is more beneficial for you when you put more effort into it.

"His message to schools and parents is obvious" — keyin aniq tavsiya: "devise ways of increasing physical activity".
"For those who are sceptical about this, and no doubt there are many". Sceptical = disbelieve; no doubt = probably.
Shvetsiya tadqiqoti "perhaps even more revealing" deyiladi, lekin olimlar hayron bo'lgani haqida hech narsa yo'q.

7 Other researchers, such as Professor Art Kramer, think there is (7) that some parts of the brain become bigger,

9 Among other things, these scientific (9) could be used to benefit

items: 11 Which of the following is true, according to Professor Art Kramer? A) People become less active as they grow older. B) Exercising is an effective way of preventing diseases like diabetes. C) One particular type of exercise is more effective than others. D) When exercising, you should take short breaks during the exercise period.

why: "Aerobic exercise is best for this". A — tuzoq: "brain function decreases as we get older" va "people are ... living more sedentary lifestyles" — ikkisi alohida fikr; D — "continuous exercising" (aksi).

"Visual evidence to show that brain networks and structures actually change with exercise". C — hipokamp KATTALASHGAN, faolroq bo'lgani aytilmagan; D — "reversing brain ageing by one to two years" boshqa ma'no.
"Restricting people's diets to just 500 calories every other day" — kun ora kam yeyish. B — tuzoq: "a day" emas, "every other day"; C — oqsil ovqatda emas, organizmda ishlab chiqariladi.

readings.title: Practice 1: The ten-thousand-step question
readings.qtype: Yes / No / Not Given (1–5) + Summary with a box (6–10) + Multiple choice A–D (11–14)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 3 darajasi)
text: Few health targets are as widely known as the daily goal of 10,000 steps. It is built into fitness trackers and smartphone apps, and it is repeated by employers and gym instructors across the world. Yet the number did not come from a laboratory. It is usually traced to a pedometer sold in Japan in the mid-1960s, whose name translated roughly as 'ten-thousand-step meter'. The figure was chosen, it seems, because it was round, memorable and sounded ambitious. The device appeared at a time when interest in fitness was high in Japan, shortly after Tokyo had hosted the 1964 Olympic Games. That a marketing slogan should have become a global health standard is, to my mind, one of the stranger stories in modern health advice.

For decades, nobody tested the number properly. This was not because researchers were uninterested in walking; there is a vast literature linking physical activity to lower rates of heart disease, diabetes and early death. The difficulty was measurement. People are notoriously poor at estimating how much they move, and early studies relied on questionnaires in which volunteers simply described their own habits. Only when cheap, accurate step counters became available could scientists follow thousands of people and record what they actually did. Even then, many of the early devices were worn for only a week or two, which made it difficult to say anything about long-term health.

The results of these newer studies are more encouraging than the old slogan suggests. In several large projects, the risk of dying during the follow-up period fell steadily as daily steps rose from very low levels, but the benefit began to level off well before 10,000. For older adults, most of the gain appeared to be achieved at somewhere between 6,000 and 8,000 steps a day; for younger adults, the curve flattened a little later. In other words, the greatest improvement comes not from reaching an impressive total but from moving out of the least active group.

This matters because the traditional target may actually discourage the people who would benefit most. Someone who currently takes 3,000 steps a day may regard 10,000 as hopelessly out of reach and decide not to try at all. Health campaigns that present exercise as an all-or-nothing challenge risk sending exactly this message. It would be far more sensible, I would argue, to encourage gradual increases of an extra 1,000 or 2,000 steps a day, and to celebrate them as real progress rather than as a failure to reach the 'proper' figure.

Whether the speed of walking matters as much as the quantity is less clear. Walking speed is influenced by age, fitness and even the design of a town's streets, so it is not easy to study. Some researchers have found that people who walk briskly for at least part of the day do better than those who cover the same distance slowly, while others have found that the difference largely disappears once overall activity is taken into account. It is also hard to separate cause and effect: people who are already ill tend to walk both less and more slowly, which may make slow walking look more harmful than it really is.

None of this means that fitness trackers are useless. On the contrary, the evidence suggests that simply wearing a device that counts steps leads many people to walk more, at least in the first few months. The problem lies in the numbers the devices display. A target that is too high may cause users to lose interest, while one that is adjusted to their current level is more likely to keep them moving. Some manufacturers have begun to allow users to set personal goals, a change that deserves far wider attention than it has received.

The story of the 10,000-step target is, in the end, a useful reminder of how health advice spreads. A figure that is simple and easy to remember will often travel further than a complex but accurate one. Scientists who want their findings to change behaviour could learn something from the pedometer salesmen of the 1960s, provided that this time the simple message is firmly based on evidence.

tasks.instr: Sarlavha "newer studies" — 2-xatboshi oxiri, 3- va 4-xatboshilar. Har bo'shliq uchun avval so'z turini ayting.
items: 6 Newer studies were able to record people's actual (6) rather than relying on what they said.
7 They found that the risk of early death fell as daily steps increased, but that this (7) stopped increasing long before 10,000 steps.

why: "Scientists could follow thousands of people and record what they actually did" + "how much they move". G questionnaires — tuzoq: eski tadqiqotlar usuli.

"The benefit began to level off well before 10,000". Level off = stopped increasing (o'sishdan to'xtab, bir tekis bo'lib qoldi). Diqqat: foyda KAMAYMAGAN — faqat qo'shimcha qadamlar deyarli qo'shimcha foyda bermay qo'ygan.

why: "Is less clear. Some researchers have found ... while others have found that the difference largely disappears". A — faqat bir guruh tadqiqotchilarning fikri.

"A figure that is simple ... will often travel further" + "provided that this time the simple message is firmly based on evidence". B — "without question" shartga zid.

readings.title: Practice 2: The nocebo problem
readings.qtype: Yes / No / Not Given (1–5) + Summary with a box (6–10) + Multiple choice A–D (11–13)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 3 darajasi)
text: Most people have heard of the placebo effect: the tendency of some patients to feel better after taking a pill that contains no active ingredient. Far fewer have heard of its darker twin. The 'nocebo effect' occurs when negative expectations produce real symptoms, such as headaches, nausea, tiredness or pain, that cannot be explained by the treatment itself. The term, taken from the Latin for 'I shall harm', was introduced in the early 1960s, yet it has received only a fraction of the attention given to the placebo, and it is still rarely discussed with patients. In my view, this neglect is difficult to justify, because the nocebo effect may be doing considerable damage in ordinary medical practice.

The clearest evidence comes from clinical trials. Before volunteers join a trial, they must be told about the possible side effects of the drug being tested, and a proportion of those who receive the dummy pill go on to report exactly the side effects on the list. In some trials, the number of volunteers who drop out because of side effects is similar in the placebo group and in the group receiving the real drug. The pill, in these cases, is not responsible; the information is.

Everyday medicine provides further examples. Patients prescribed drugs to lower their cholesterol, for instance, frequently complain of muscle pain, and many stop taking the medication as a result. Muscle aches are, of course, common in the general population, especially among older adults. Yet when people in one small study took real tablets, dummy tablets and no tablets in alternating months, without knowing which was which, most of the discomfort they reported also appeared in the months when they were taking the dummy pills. For a number of the patients involved, simply seeing this pattern was enough to persuade them to return to the treatment.

Why should expectation have such power? Part of the answer lies in attention. A person who has been warned that a drug may cause headaches is more likely to notice the ordinary aches that everybody experiences and to blame them on the medicine. But there is also evidence of genuine physical change. Brain-imaging studies suggest that anxiety about pain can increase activity in the areas of the brain that process it, so the pain that is felt may be quite real even though its origin is psychological.

This creates an uncomfortable dilemma for doctors. Patients have a right to know about the risks of any treatment, and no responsible doctor would suggest hiding them. However, the way in which the information is presented appears to make a difference. Telling patients that nine out of ten people have no problems with a drug conveys the same facts as saying that one in ten suffers side effects, but it seems to produce fewer complaints. Some researchers have also proposed asking patients whether they would prefer not to hear about minor, harmless side effects, although this idea raises ethical questions of its own.

Not everyone is equally vulnerable. People who are anxious by nature, or who have had bad experiences with medicine in the past, seem to be more affected, as do those who have read alarming stories online. Doctors, of course, cannot control what their patients read. But they can control their own words, and it is here, I believe, that the most practical progress can be made. A few minutes spent explaining a treatment calmly and positively costs almost nothing, and it may prevent patients from abandoning medicines that would genuinely help them.

The placebo effect was once treated as a nuisance that got in the way of 'real' research, until scientists recognised that it could teach them something about the connection between mind and body. The nocebo effect deserves the same serious study. It is, after all, not a sign that patients are imagining things, but a reminder that what people are told about their health can shape what they feel. Understanding it better could make treatment both safer and cheaper, since patients who abandon useful medicines often need more expensive care later.

readings.title: Practice 3 (uyga): Sitting still — the case against the office chair
readings.qtype: Yes / No / Not Given (1–5) + Summary with a box (6–10) + Multiple choice A–D (11–14)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 3 darajasi), uy vazifasi
text: In the early 1950s, the British epidemiologist Jerry Morris noticed something curious about the men who worked on London's double-decker buses. The drivers, who sat for most of their shift, suffered heart attacks considerably more often than the conductors, who spent the day climbing up and down the stairs collecting fares. Morris's work is now regarded as one of the founding studies of exercise science, and it is hard to overstate its influence. Morris later found a similar pattern when he compared postmen, who delivered letters on foot, with clerks who worked at desks. Yet for decades its most important lesson was, I believe, misunderstood.

The conclusion most people drew from the bus study was that exercise protects the heart. That is true, but it is only half the story. The conductors were not athletes; they did not go to a gym or run marathons. Their advantage came from being on their feet and moving, gently but constantly, throughout the working day. The drivers' problem was not simply a lack of exercise but an excess of sitting, and for a long time these two things were treated as if they were the same.

They are not. Research over the past twenty years has shown that a person can meet the recommended amount of weekly exercise and still spend most waking hours seated. An office worker who jogs every morning, for example, may then sit at a desk for eight hours, sit in a car or bus on the way home and sit in front of a screen for the rest of the evening. Several large studies have linked long periods of sitting with a higher risk of heart disease and type 2 diabetes, and some have found that this risk is only partly reduced by regular exercise. Sitting, in other words, appears to be a health problem in its own right, not simply the absence of exercise.

Why should sitting be so harmful? One explanation concerns the large muscles of the legs. When they are inactive for long periods, the body appears to become less efficient at processing sugar and fats in the blood. Laboratory experiments in which volunteers interrupted their sitting every half hour with a few minutes of light walking have shown improvements in blood sugar levels after meals. The effect is modest, but it has encouraged the view that frequent short breaks may matter as much as the total amount of time spent sitting.

Employers have responded with enthusiasm, and the standing desk has become a familiar sight in many offices. Here, however, the evidence is less impressive than the advertising. Standing still is not the same as moving, and people who stand for very long periods can develop problems of their own, including back and leg pain. Moreover, studies suggest that many workers use their new desks eagerly for a few weeks and then return to sitting for most of the day. It would be a mistake, in my view, to see the standing desk as a solution in itself.

What seems to work better is a change in the way the working day is organised. Meetings held while walking, printers placed at the far end of the office and reminders to get up every half hour all encourage the kind of light, frequent movement that the bus conductors enjoyed. None of these measures is expensive, and together they may do more good than a single piece of new furniture. Some firms have even discouraged internal emails in favour of a short walk to a colleague's desk. The difficulty is that they depend on habits and workplace culture, which are far harder to change than equipment.

Morris is said to have stayed physically active well into his nineties, and he would perhaps have been amused to see his findings rediscovered by a generation of office workers. His bus study remains a useful reminder that the most important health decisions are often not the dramatic ones, such as joining a gym or entering a race, but the small, repeated choices that shape an ordinary day.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: YES / NO / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: YES — gap yozuvchining da'vosi/fikri bilan mos; NO — yozuvchi buning aksini da'vo qiladi; NOT GIVEN — yozuvchi bu haqda nima deb o'ylashini matndan aytib bo'lmaydi. 1–3-xatboshilar. 6 daqiqa.
items: The conductors in Morris's study were generally younger than the drivers.
Morris's bus study has had a very great influence on exercise science.
The conductors were healthier because they took part in sport outside work.
People who exercise regularly cannot be harmed by long periods of sitting.
Office workers spend more time sitting than any other group of employees.
why: Haydovchi va konduktorlarning yoshi haqida hech narsa aytilmagan.
"It is hard to overstate its influence" — ta'siri juda katta (muallif bahosi).
"The conductors were not athletes; they did not go to a gym or run marathons".
"This risk is only partly reduced by regular exercise ... a health problem in its own right".
Ofis xodimi misol sifatida keltirilgan, lekin boshqa kasblar bilan taqqoslanmagan.

tasks.type: Complete the summary using the list of words, A–I, below.
tasks.instr: Summary 4- va 5-xatboshilarga tegishli.
items: 6 One theory is that when the large leg muscles are (6) for a long time, the body deals less effectively with sugar and fats.
7 In experiments, short periods of light walking every thirty minutes led to (7) in blood sugar after meals.
8 Although the (8) was small, it suggests that regular breaks are important.
9 Standing desks have become (9) in offices, but the writer believes the evidence for them is weak.

why: "When they are inactive for long periods". B busy — teskari.
"Have shown improvements in blood sugar levels after meals". D damage — teskari.

tasks.title: Questions 11–14
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D
tasks.instr: 11–12 — 6-xatboshi, 13–14 — oxirgi xatboshi.
items: 11 What does the writer suggest in the sixth paragraph? A) Offices should buy more modern furniture. B) Changes to daily routines may be more effective than new equipment. C) Walking meetings are too expensive for most companies. D) Workers should exercise before they start work.

12 According to the writer, why are these measures difficult to introduce? A) They are costly. B) Most employees dislike them. C) They require changes in habits and culture. D) There is no evidence that they work.

13 What does the writer suggest about Morris in the final paragraph? A) He stayed active until late in life. B) He was disappointed that his work had been forgotten. C) He regretted not studying office workers. D) He disagreed with later research on sitting.

"They depend on habits and workplace culture, which are far harder to change than equipment". A — teskari.

homework_intro: Bugun Passage 3 da uch savol turini bitta xarita bilan yechdik: avval Y/N/NG (muallif fikri), keyin box'li summary (so'z turi + eliminatsiya), oxirida MCQ (ism/line + uchta tuzoqni rad etish).
Birinchi vazifa — Practice 3 "Sitting still": 20 daqiqa vaqt oling, 14 savolga javob bering. Har Y/N/NG javobi yoniga isbot gapni, har MCQ yoniga esa bitta rad etilgan variant sababini yozing.

Ikkinchi vazifa — lug'at: Student's Book 35-bet, Vocabulary 1–2-mashqlar (verb + noun collocations: promote (feelings of) well-being, gauge the effectiveness (of), overlook a factor, challenge an assumption, determine the outcome, yield results, devise a strategy, outline the causes) va Workbook 19-bet, Vocabulary 1–2-mashqlar. Javoblarni kalit bilan tekshiring (SB 170-bet, WB 63-bet).

Uchinchi vazifa — xatolar daftari: bugungi har xato javob — savol, to'g'ri javob va sabab ("fakt va fikrni aralashtirdim", "grammatik mos, lekin ma'nosi xato variant", "line reference'dan oldingi gapni o'qimadim").

kahoot.q: Y/N/NG questions check...
kahoot.explain: "Agree with the claims of the writer" — muallifning da'vosi va bahosi tekshiriladi. T/F/NG esa faktni tekshiradi.

kahoot.q: When is the answer NOT GIVEN?
options: The writer says nothing about this exact claim
The statement uses different words from the text
kahoot.explain: Mavzu bo'lishi mumkin, lekin aynan shu da'vo yo'q. Aksi aytilgan bo'lsa — NO.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Not surprisingly, group 3 improved most.' Statement: 'It was to be expected that group 3 would do best.'
kahoot.explain: "Not surprisingly" = "it was to be expected". Bu muallifning bahosi — YES.

kahoot.q: Text: 'MK-869 has not been the only breakthrough undone.' Statement: 'MK-869's failure was unique.'
kahoot.explain: "Not the only" ↔ "unique" — qarama-qarshi. Y/N/NG da javob NO (FALSE emas).

kahoot.q: What should you do FIRST with a summary that has a box A–I?
options: Read the title and find the right paragraphs
Write words from the passage into each of the gaps
kahoot.explain: Sarlavha qaysi xatboshilarni o'qish kerakligini ko'rsatadi: "Merck and MK-869" — birinchi ikki xatboshi.

kahoot.q: What do you write on the answer sheet for a summary with a box?
kahoot.explain: Box topshirig'ida faqat harf. So'z yozish — 0 ball bo'lishi mumkin.

kahoot.q: Gap: 'concerns about increasing ___ in the industry'. Which word could NOT fill the gap grammatically?
kahoot.explain: Bo'shliqqa ot kerak. "Treated" — fe'lning V3 shakli, bu joyga grammatik jihatdan tushmaydi. Qolgan uchtasi (competition, prices, criticism) mos — ular orasidan ma'no hal qiladi.

kahoot.q: Two box words both fit the grammar of a gap. How do you choose?
options: Find the sentence that proves the meaning
Choose the longer, more academic word
Choose the word that also appears in the text
Choose the first one that fits the grammar
kahoot.explain: Faqat matn tasdiqlagan ma'no to'g'ri. Matndagi so'z bilan aynan bir xil variant ko'pincha tuzoq.

kahoot.q: MCQ asks about 'tight race' in line 80. Where do you read most carefully?
kahoot.explain: O'xshatish odatda oldingi fikrni tushuntiradi: race = standart testlar, judges = kuzatuvchilar.

kahoot.q: An MCQ option is TRUE in the text but does not answer the question. It is...
kahoot.explain: SB 14: B (kutish ro'yxatida sog'ayish) — to'g'ri fakt, lekin "significant discovery" emas.

kahoot.q: Which question types in this passage usually follow the order of the text?
kahoot.explain: Y/N/NG va MCQ matn tartibida. Summary bir necha qismdan olinishi mumkin.

kahoot.q: Best time plan for Passage 3 (14 questions)?
options: About 20 minutes, max 2 minutes per hard question
About 10 minutes, reading only the questions
About 40 minutes, because it is the hardest passage
No fixed plan; read the whole passage twice
kahoot.explain: Xarita 2, Y/N/NG 6, summary 5, MCQ 5, tekshiruv 2 daqiqa. Qiyin savolni belgilab, keyin qayting.

kahoot.q: A placebo group helps to ___ the effectiveness of a drug.
kahoot.explain: Gauge the effectiveness — samaradorligini baholash.

kahoot.q: 'Potter thought a crucial factor had been overlooked.' Overlooked means...
kahoot.explain: Overlook — e'tibordan chetda qoldirmoq.

kahoot.q: 'His plan hinged on the success of MK-869.' The plan...
kahoot.explain: Hinge on — butunlay ...ga bog'liq bo'lmoq.

kahoot.q: The tests on children ___ some interesting results.
kahoot.explain: Yield results — natija bermoq.

kahoot.q: 'Merck was falling behind its rivals.' This means Merck was...
kahoot.explain: Fall behind — orqada qolmoq. Summary'da bu "increasing competition" bilan paraphrase qilingan.

kahoot.q: A person who sits most of the day has a ___ lifestyle.
kahoot.explain: Sedentary — kam harakatli. Vigorous — kuchli, jadal (faollik).

kahoot.q: 'The placebo response is short-lived.' It...
kahoot.explain: Short-lived — qisqa muddatli. Kaptchuk buning aksini ko'rsatdi: ta'sir haftalab davom etdi.

kahoot.q: The findings ___ a basic assumption of the drugs industry.
kahoot.explain: Challenge an assumption — taxminni shubha ostiga olmoq.

lessons.title: Unit 3 Listening — Section 3: Matching + Flow-chart completion
lessons.grammar_topic: Section 3 kombinatsiyasi: Matching (A–F / A–G ro'yxatdan) + Flow-chart completion (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS)
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 3 (A healthy life) — fizioterapiya, sport jarohatlari, og'riq qoldiruvchi dorilar tarixi
lessons.book_ref: Complete IELTS Bands 6.5–7.5: Student's Book, Unit 3, 31-bet (Listening Section 3, CD1 Track 13–14; skript 151–152-betlar, kalit 169-bet); Workbook, Unit 3, 18-bet (Listening Section 3, Track 5–6; skript 56-bet, kalit 63-bet).
objectives: Section 3 da ikki savol turi (matching + flow chart) kelganda tayyorlanish vaqtini bo'lish: matching variantlaridagi kalit g'oyalarni belgilash va flow chart bo'shliqlari turini aniqlash.
Matching'da variant "so'zini" emas, "g'oyasini" kutish: "most popular" = "it's what everyone asks for", "rarely used" = "we tend to avoid it".
Uch kishilik suhbatda (ikki talaba + mutaxassis) kim javob berayotganini kuzatish va talabaning taxminini mutaxassisning tuzatishidan ajratish.
Flow chart'da strelkalar bo'ylab ketma-ketlikni kuzatish va fe'l paraphrase'larini tanish: arrives at = turn up, evaluates = assess, supervises = oversee.
Javobni so'z chegarasi (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS), imlo va grammatik moslik (an + unli: an existing injury) bo'yicha tekshirib transfer qilish.
materials: Student's Book, Unit 3, 31-bet — savollar sahifasi (quyida rasm) va CD1 Track 13–14 audiosi.

intro: Section 3 — o'quv mavzusidagi suhbat: 2–3 kishi (talabalar va o'qituvchi yoki mutaxassis). Unda faktlar ham, fikrlar ham bor (SB exam information: "The questions may cover both factual information and opinions"). 7.0 darajasida Section 3 odatda ikki qismga bo'lingan: birinchi qismda matching, ikkinchisida flow chart, notes yoki sentence completion.

Tayyorlanish vaqtini ikkiga bo'ling. Matching uchun: A–F variantlaridagi kalit g'oyani tagiga chizing (strengthens / whole body, most popular, special sportswear, most effective, evening, rarely). Flow chart uchun: sarlavhani o'qing ("Example of patient route") va har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini yozing (an + unli bilan boshlanuvchi ot, jarohatga oid ot, odam turi).

Matching'da savollar (1–5) audio tartibida keladi, variantlar (A–F) esa aralash. Har savol uchun butun ro'yxatga qarash kerak — shuning uchun variantlarni tinglashdan oldin deyarli yod bilib olish foydali. Bitta variant bir marta ishlatiladi, bitta variant ortiqcha.

Matching tuzog'i — variantdagi SO'Z eshitiladi, lekin boshqa narsa haqida yoki inkor bilan. SB: "sports shoe" — C (special sportswear) emas, chunki "occasionally ... but not often" va bu biror davolash usuliga bog'lanmaydi. "This treatment can hurt sometimes" — salbiy detal, lekin javob D: "it gets results more quickly than anything else".

Uch kishilik suhbatda talaba ko'pincha TAXMIN aytadi, mutaxassis esa tasdiqlaydi yoki tuzatadi. Mike: "So it's for the back and neck?" — Steve buni tasdiqlamaydi; javobni Flo beradi: "it works on everything and gives you more power" va Steve: "we improve your overall form" → A (whole body). Kimning gapi yakuniy ekaniga quloq soling.

Flow chart — strelkalar = vaqt tartibi. Bo'shliq atrofidagi fe'llar audioda sinonim bilan keladi: arrives at → turn up; evaluates → assess; is prepared → design; check → monitor; supervises → oversee. Fe'lni eshitsangiz, javob darhol undan keyin keladi.

So'z chegarasi: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS. "An (6) ___" — artikl "an" javob unli bilan boshlanishini aytadi: existing injury. "Joint (9) ___" — "joint" allaqachon yozilgan, faqat "movement" yoziladi. Oxirida chartni boshdan-oxir o'qib, mantiqan to'g'ri ekanini tekshiring (SB exam advice).

WB dagi aspirin tarixi — flow chart'ning yana bir turi: yillar bo'yicha (2500 BCE → 1823 → 1838 → 1853 → 1893 → 1897 → 1899). Bu yerda raqamlar signal: yilni eshitsangiz, keyingi bo'shliq yaqin. Ism harflab aytilishi mumkin (S-A-L-I-C-I-N), lekin javob — atrofdagi ot (active ingredient).
formulas: an + unli ot / odam / ot birikmasi
presentation: Matching'da variant so'zi eshitildi. Uni yozaymi?
Shoshilmang. So'z bir xil bo'lishi — tuzoq belgisi. Gapning ma'nosi variant g'oyasiga mos kelishini kuting ("sports shoe" ≠ special sportswear).
Ikki talaba bir-biriga qarshi fikr aytsa-chi?
Savolni o'qing: "What comments do the SPEAKERS make" — mutaxassis yoki ikkala tomon kelishgan fikr javob bo'ladi. Faqat bitta talabaning taxmini odatda javob emas.
Bitta variantni ikki marta ishlatsa bo'ladimi?
Bu topshiriqda yo'q: 6 variant, 5 savol — har harf bir marta, bittasi ortiqcha.
Flow chart'da "an ___" bor. Bu nimaga yordam beradi?
Javob unli tovush bilan boshlanadi: an existing injury, an exercise plan. "A ___" bo'lsa — undosh: a personal trainer.
Javob uch so'z bo'lib qoldi: "the exercise plan".
Artiklni tashlang — "exercise plan". Chart'da bor so'zni (joint, clinic) takrorlamang.
Matching tugab, flow chart boshlanganini qanday bilaman?
SB da alohida track (13 → 14) va yangi savol: "So what happens when someone comes to your clinic?" Imtihonda ham qisqa pauza bo'ladi — shu paytda Q6–10 ga qayta qarang.
notes: Matching + flow chart juftligi 5.0 ning 27-darsida (Part 3) o'tilgan; 6.0 da Section 3 boshqa juftliklarda yechilgan (6-dars: Choose TWO letters + matching + short answer; 15-dars: MCQ + flow chart). 7.0 da urg'u — uch kishilik suhbatda fikr egasini kuzatish va fe'l paraphrase'larini avtomatik tanish.

Tekshiruvda SB 6-mashqni albatta bajaring: skriptda javob so'zlarini tagiga chizish va fe'l sinonimlarini yozish (turn up, assess, design, monitor, oversee). Bu keyingi darslar uchun eng foydali lug'at.
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: WB Track 5 ni variantlarga qaramasdan tinglab, har dori haqida bitta kalit fikrni yozish, keyin A–F bilan solishtirish.
mistakes: C — hech bir savolga to'g'ri kelmaydi
Mike'ning taxminini javob deb olish ("back and neck")
Aniq odam turi: "a personal trainer does that"

how: CORE — tibbiyot va sport jarohatlari haqidagi asosiy so'zlar; STRONG — Section 3 da paraphrase sifatida keladigan fe'llar (SB 6-mashq); SUPER — og'zaki nutqdagi iboralar.
Juftlikda: biri flow chart fe'lini aytadi (evaluates), sherigi audiodagi sinonimini (assess) va u bilan gap tuzadi.
core: The physiotherapist gave me exercises for my knee.
He is recovering from a sports injury.
I sprained my ankle playing basketball.
Manual therapy relieves stiffness in the joint.
My posture gets worse after hours on the laptop.
Noutbukda soatlab o'tirgandan keyin qaddim buziladi.
Don't take painkillers on an empty stomach.
Og'riq qoldiruvchi dorini och qoringa ichmang.
Morphine is available only on prescription.
Scientists extracted the active ingredient from the leaves.
Olimlar barglardan faol moddani ajratib oldi.
Ibuprofen reduces swelling around the ankle.
After treatment, patients move on to rehabilitation.
strong: First we assess the damage to the joint.
We monitor the movement in the joint each time.
Har safar bo'g'im harakatini kuzatib boramiz.
A personal trainer oversees the programme.
Massage helps to relieve stiffness and pain.
Bayer created a synthetic version of the acid.
super: An exercise plan only works if you stick to it.
Mashq rejasi faqat unga amal qilsangiz ishlaydi.
Video analysis outstrips all our other services.
Video tahlil boshqa barcha xizmatlarimizdan oshib ketadi.
Taking too many painkillers can be counter-productive.
Ko'p og'riq qoldiruvchi ichish teskari natija berishi mumkin.
I'm fed up with not doing any sport.

class_ex.title: Fe'l paraphrase zanjiri
class_ex.instr: Ustoz flow chart fe'lini aytadi, o'quvchilar Section 3 da uchraydigan sinonimini topadi va misol gap tuzadi.
items: arrive at (a clinic)
evaluate (the damage)
prepare (a plan)
check (progress)
supervise (activity)
relieve (pain)
why: SB Track 14: "so you turn up with what we call an 'existing injury'".
"So what we would do first is to assess the damage to the joint area".
"Plus we design an exercise plan for you".
"We monitor the movement in the joint each time".
"They oversee the programme for at least a couple of months".
WB Track 6: "what was in the leaves that helped to ease pain"; SB Unit 3 Starting off: "alleviate pain".
class_ex.note: Mashqdan keyin juftlikda: biri o'z jarohati haqida gapiradi (SB 7-mashq), sherigi shu 6 fe'lning kamida 3 tasini ishlatib savol beradi.

class_ex.title: "Qaysi variant?" — matching tuzog'i
class_ex.instr: Ustoz gapni o'qiydi. Variantlar: A It is the most popular. B It is rarely used. C It is best done in the evening. D It is the most effective. O'quvchi harfni va tuzoqni aytadi.
items: "People sometimes ask for it, but honestly we hardly ever recommend it these days."
"It isn't cheap, but nothing else gets people back on their feet so fast."
"Some clients come in the morning, but we find it works far better once the working day is over."
"It's not the most effective treatment, but it's the one that everybody wants."
why: "Hardly ever recommend" = rarely used. "People sometimes ask for it" — mashhurlik tuzog'i.
"Nothing else gets people back ... so fast" = most effective. "Isn't cheap" — ortiqcha ma'lumot.
"Works far better once the working day is over" = best in the evening. "Morning" — tuzoq.
"The one that everybody wants" = most popular. "Not the most effective" — D ni inkor qiladi.
class_ex.note: 4-gap — eng muhim namuna: variant so'zi ("the most effective") eshitiladi, lekin inkor bilan. Doskada "NOT" ni doiraga oling.

"Doctors and pharmacists advise that you avoid giving it to anyone under 12". Under 12 = children.

"Your doctor will need to see you on a regular basis to check you're getting the right dose". Tuzoq: "the after-effects can be extremely bad" — E dagi "slightly" ga zid.

"Italian scientists identified and extracted the active ingredient, salicin". Tuzoq: harflab aytilgan "S-A-L-I-C-I-N" — u qavs ichida allaqachon bor.

Germany, 1838: Salicin is also discovered in the meadowsweet flower.
France, 1853: Salicin is first produced in a (8) (called salicylic acid).
Germany, 1893: Acetyl is added to salicylic acid. Irritant qualities are reduced.
Germany, 1897: A (9) of acetyl salicylic acid is first produced by Bayer.
