listenings.title: Jony Academy mashqi: University sleep clinic (Q1–10)
intro: Ustoz skriptni bir marta, oddiy tezlikda o'qiydi (uch ovoz: DR HAYES — uyqu bo'yicha mutaxassis, LOLA va DANIYAR — psixologiya talabalari). Q1–5 dan keyin 20 soniya pauza qiling.
Avval 45 soniya: A–G dagi kalit g'oyalarni va flow chart bo'shliqlari turini belgilash. 7 variant, 5 savol — 2 tasi ortiqcha. Har savolda bitta tuzoq bor: talabaning taxmini, "used to" yoki inkor.
transcript: DR HAYES: Come in, both of you. You must be the psychology students.
LOLA: Yes, I'm Lola and this is Daniyar. Thank you for making time for us, Dr Hayes.
DANIYAR: We're giving a presentation on sleep problems next week, and our tutor said the clinic would be the best place to start.
DR HAYES: Happy to help. Where would you like to begin?
LOLA: Perhaps with the methods you use, both for measuring sleep and for treating problems.
DR HAYES: Fine. Well, almost everyone who comes here starts with a sleep diary. They write down when they went to bed, roughly when they fell asleep, how often they woke up, and so on.
DANIYAR: I'd have thought that was quite reliable. People know when they wake up.
DR HAYES: It's reasonably accurate, as long as people keep it up. The trouble is that most of them stop filling it in after four or five nights. They find it a chore.
LOLA: What about the wrist trackers? Half the people in our hall of residence wear one.

DR HAYES: Oh, they're very popular, and they're getting cheaper all the time. But I wouldn't trust the figures. They often record that you were asleep when you were actually lying still, reading or worrying about an exam.
DANIYAR: So they overestimate how much people sleep.

DR HAYES: Frequently, yes. Now, for the difficult cases we do an overnight study in our sleep laboratory. The patient sleeps here, connected to monitors that record brain activity, breathing and heart rate.
LOLA: That must cost a fortune.
DR HAYES: It's certainly the most expensive thing we offer. But nothing else comes close. If we want to know exactly what's happening during the night, that's the only way to be sure.
DANIYAR: And for treatment? I've read about light therapy.

DR HAYES: Yes, we use a lot of that. Patients sit in front of a special bright lamp. People tend to assume it's just for the winter months, or that it isn't safe for teenagers. Neither is true. The key thing is when you do it. It has to be first thing in the morning, within an hour of getting up, or it can actually make things worse.
LOLA: Interesting. And do you use relaxation recordings? I've got an app with some.
DR HAYES: We do. Honestly, on their own they don't achieve very much. But if patients use them alongside the diary and a regular bedtime, the results can be excellent.
LOLA: That's really helpful.
DANIYAR: Could you tell us what actually happens when a new patient comes to the clinic? We'd like to include a sort of patient journey in the presentation.
DR HAYES: Of course. Well, first of all, we don't accept people who contact us directly, even though quite a few try. Everyone has to be referred by their family doctor.
LOLA: Not by a hospital?

DR HAYES: Occasionally, but it's nearly always the family doctor. Then, at the first appointment, a nurse sees them. We used to weigh everyone, but we stopped doing that. Now the nurse measures their blood pressure and asks what medication they're taking.
DANIYAR: Why blood pressure?

DR HAYES: Some sleep problems are linked to heart health, so it's a useful early warning. After that, the patient goes home with a sleep diary. We used to ask for one week, but that wasn't enough to see a pattern, so now it's two weeks.
LOLA: And then the overnight study?

DR HAYES: Only if the diary suggests it's necessary. Either way, the results aren't discussed with the patient straight away. First the whole team goes through them at a team meeting, doctors, nurses and our psychologist, and we agree on the best approach.
DANIYAR: And what's the final stage?

DR HAYES: Most patients are invited to a group session, where they learn about sleep habits with other people who have similar problems. Individual sessions are only for the more serious cases. People are often nervous about the groups, but they usually enjoy them.
LOLA: That's brilliant. Thank you so much, Dr Hayes.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5 — Methods
tasks.type: What comment does Dr Hayes make about each method? Choose FIVE answers, A–G.
tasks.instr: Usullar suhbat tartibida. Talabalarning fikri (Daniyar, Lola) — tuzoq bo'lishi mumkin.
box: A It gives the most reliable results.
B Patients often give it up quickly.
C It must be used at a particular time of day.
E It is the cheapest option.
F It is not recommended for teenagers.
G It works best when combined with other methods.
items: 1 Sleep diary
2 Wrist tracker
3 Overnight laboratory study
4 Light therapy
5 Relaxation recordings
why: "Most of them stop filling it in after four or five nights". Tuzoq: Daniyar — "quite reliable" (A); doktor faqat "reasonably accurate" deydi.
"I wouldn't trust the figures. They often record that you were asleep when you were actually lying still". Tuzoq: "getting cheaper" (E) — eng arzon deyilmagan.
"Nothing else comes close ... that's the only way to be sure". Tuzoq: "the most expensive thing we offer" — E ning teskarisi.
"It has to be first thing in the morning, within an hour of getting up". Tuzoq: "isn't safe for teenagers ... Neither is true" (F).
"On their own they don't achieve very much. But if patients use them alongside the diary and a regular bedtime...".
tasks.note: E va F — ortiqcha variantlar, lekin ikkalasining so'zi audioda eshitiladi (cheaper, expensive, teenagers). Tekshiruvda o'quvchi har tuzoq gapni aytsin.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10 — A patient's route through the sleep clinic
tasks.type: Complete the flow chart below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
tasks.instr: Fe'l paraphrase'lari: is referred by, measures, keeps, are discussed at, attend. "Used to" — eski tartib, javob emas.
why: "Everyone has to be referred by their family doctor". Tuzoq: "Not by a hospital? — Occasionally"; bemorning o'zi murojaat qilishi qabul qilinmaydi.
"Now the nurse measures their blood pressure". Tuzoq: "We used to weigh everyone".
"We used to ask for one week ... so now it's two weeks". Tuzoq: one week (eski tartib).
"First the whole team goes through them at a team meeting". Tuzoq: "aren't discussed with the patient straight away".
"Most patients are invited to a group session". Tuzoq: "Individual sessions are only for the more serious cases".
tasks.note: Uchta "used to" / "not" tuzog'i (weigh, one week, individual) — Section 3 ning eng tipik tuzog'i. Tekshiruvda o'quvchi eski va yangi tartibni ajratib aytsin.
rows: Patient is referred to the clinic by their (6)
At the first appointment, a nurse measures the patient's (7) and asks about medication.
Patient keeps a sleep diary at home for (8)
If necessary, an overnight study is done. Results are discussed at a (9) before the patient is told.
Most patients attend a (10) to learn about sleep habits.

homework_intro: Bugun Section 3 da ikki savol turini ketma-ket yechdik: avval matching (variant g'oyasi, fikr egasi), keyin flow chart (strelka tartibi, fe'l paraphrase, so'z chegarasi).

Birinchi vazifa — shadowing: SB Track 14 ni (1 daqiqa 57 soniya) skript bilan birga 3 marta tinglang va Steve'ning gaplarini u bilan bir vaqtda takrorlang. Oxirgi urinishni ovozli xabar qilib guruhga yuboring.

Ikkinchi vazifa — Student's Book 31-bet, 6-mashq (skript 151–152-betlar): Q1–5 uchun javob bergan so'zlarni tagiga chizing; Q6–10 uchun tagiga chizilgan fe'llarning audiodagi sinonimlarini yozing. Keyin WB Track 6 ni qayta tinglab, 5 ta yil va har yilda nima bo'lganini xotiradan yozing (diktant).
Uchinchi vazifa — xatolar daftari: bugungi har xato javob — savol, to'g'ri javob va sabab (variant so'zi tuzog'i / talaba taxmini / "used to" / so'z chegarasi / imlo).

homework.title: Shadowing: SB Track 14
homework.instr: Skript bilan 3 marta; oxirgisi ovozli xabar sifatida guruhga.
homework.answers: Ustoz talaffuz va ritmni tekshiradi; fe'llar (turn up, assess, design, monitor, oversee) aniq eshitilishi kerak.

homework.title: SB 31-bet, 6-mashq + WB Track 6 diktanti
homework.instr: Skriptda javob so'zlari va fe'l sinonimlari; WB Track 6 dan 5 ta yil va voqea xotiradan.
homework.answers: Kalit — SB 6-mashq. Q1–5 javobni beradigan so'zlar: 1 (D) "it gets results more quickly than anything else"; 2 (A) "it works on everything" / "we improve your overall form"; 3 (F) "we tend to avoid it most of the time"; 4 (B) "it's what everyone asks for" / "it outstrips all our other services"; 5 (E) "come at the end of the day". Q6–10 fe'l sinonimlari: arrives at = turn up, evaluates = assess, is prepared = design, check = monitor, supervises = oversee. WB Track 6 diktanti (chart'dagi 7 ta yildan istalgan 5 tasi): taxminan 2500 BCE (Qadimgi Yunoniston) — tol daraxtining quritilgan barglaridan og'riq qoldiruvchi ichimlik (choy) tayyorlangan; 1823 (Italiya) — faol modda salicin aniqlanib, ajratib olingan; 1838 (Germaniya) — salicin meadowsweet gulida ham topilgan; 1853 (Fransiya) — salicin ilk bor suyuq shaklda olingan (salicylic acid); 1893 (Germaniya) — salicylic acid'ga acetyl qo'shilib, ta'sirlantiruvchi (oshqozonni og'rituvchi) xususiyati kamaygan; 1897 (Germaniya) — Bayer acetyl salicylic acid'ning sintetik versiyasini yaratgan; 1899 (Germaniya) — klinik sinovlardan keyin aspirin sotuvga chiqqan. Keyingi darsda 3 o'quvchi og'zaki aytadi.

homework.title: Xatolar daftari
homework.instr: Har xato: savol — to'g'ri javob — sabab.
homework.answers: Sababsiz qator qabul qilinmaydi.

kahoot.q: Section 3 of the IELTS Listening test is usually...
options: a conversation on a study-based topic
a monologue on a general topic
kahoot.explain: Section 3 — 2–3 kishi, o'quv mavzusi (talabalar + tutor/mutaxassis). Ma'ruza — Section 4.

kahoot.q: Before a matching task, what should you underline?
options: The key ideas in options A-F
kahoot.explain: SB 2-mashq: "Underline the key ideas in options A–F" — most popular, rarely, evening...

kahoot.q: In matching, the questions 1-5 are heard...
options: in order; the options A-F are mixed
kahoot.explain: Savollar audio tartibida; variantlar aralash — har safar butun ro'yxatga qaraysiz.

kahoot.q: Speaker: 'It's what everyone asks for.' Which option does this match?
kahoot.explain: Everyone asks for = most popular (video analysis, SB Q4).

kahoot.q: Speaker: 'We tend to avoid it most of the time.' Option?
options: It is best done in the evening.
kahoot.explain: Avoid most of the time = rarely used (electrotherapy, SB Q3).

kahoot.q: You hear 'sports shoe', and option C says 'special sportswear'. What should you do?
options: Check the meaning: the same word may be a trap
Write C at once, because you heard the word
Cross out C, because it has now been used
Write C and use it again for the next question too
kahoot.explain: Variant so'zi eshitilishi — tuzoq belgisi. SB da "a pad for a sports shoe, but not often" — C javob emas.

kahoot.q: A student guesses: 'So it's for the back and neck?' The expert does not agree. This guess is...
options: the answer to the next question
kahoot.explain: Talaba taxmini — tuzoq. Yakuniy fikrni kuting: "it works on everything" → A.

kahoot.q: Flow chart: 'Arrives at clinic with an ___'. The article 'an' tells you...
options: the answer begins with a vowel sound
the answer is a verb in the past tense
the answer must be a plural noun
the answer is a number or a date
kahoot.explain: An + unli: an existing injury, an exercise plan.

kahoot.q: Chart says 'evaluates'. Which word are you most likely to HEAR?
kahoot.explain: Evaluate = assess: "we assess the damage to the joint area".

kahoot.q: Chart: 'check joint ___'. You hear 'monitor the movement in the joint'. You write...
kahoot.explain: "Joint" chart'da bor. Faqat yangi so'z: movement.

kahoot.q: 'We used to ask for one week, but now it's two weeks.' The answer is...
kahoot.explain: "Used to" — eski tartib. Hozirgi holat javob bo'ladi.

kahoot.q: What should you do after completing a flow chart?
options: Read it through to check it makes sense
Add an extra word to each gap for clarity
Change each answer to a synonym you know
Move straight on to the next section
kahoot.explain: SB exam advice: chart'ni boshdan-oxir o'qib, mantiq va grammatikani tekshiring.

kahoot.q: A personal trainer ___ the programme and makes sure the patient carries it out.
kahoot.explain: Oversee = supervise, nazorat qilmoq.

kahoot.q: 'Video analysis outstrips all our other services.' It...
options: is more popular than all the others
costs less than all the others
is used less often than the others
will soon replace all the other services
kahoot.explain: Outstrip — ortda qoldirmoq, oshib ketmoq.

kahoot.q: 'I sprained my ankle.' This means I...
kahoot.explain: Sprain — bo'g'imni burab, lat yeyish (sinish emas).

kahoot.q: Codeine can cause ___: your body comes to rely on it.
kahoot.explain: Dependency — qaramlik (WB Track 5).

kahoot.q: An exercise plan only works if you ___ it.
kahoot.explain: Stick to — qat'iy amal qilmoq.

kahoot.q: Morphine is available only on ___, so you need a doctor.
kahoot.explain: Prescription — retsept. "Strictly prescription-only" (WB Track 5).

kahoot.q: Ibuprofen is anti-inflammatory: it reduces ___.
kahoot.explain: Swelling — shish. "It works by reducing swelling".

kahoot.q: 'So, a bit counter-productive then!' Something counter-productive...
options: has the opposite effect to the one intended
produces much better results than anyone expected
is cheap to produce in large amounts
works at once but only for a short time
kahoot.explain: Salitsil kislota og'riqni qoldirardi, lekin oshqozonni og'ritardi — teskari natija.

lessons.title: Unit 4 Reading — Passage 1: Table completion + Flow-chart completion + True / False / Not Given
lessons.grammar_topic: Uch savol turi bitta passage'da: Table completion + Flow-chart completion + TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN (Band 7 darajasi)
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 4 (Art and the artist) — plakat, bosma texnologiyalari, reklama fotografiyasi, san'at tarixi
lessons.book_ref: Complete IELTS Bands 6.5–7.5: Student's Book, Unit 4, 40–43-betlar (Reading Section 1: "The history of the poster"); Workbook, Unit 4, 24–26-betlar (Reading Section 1: "A brief history of photography in advertising"). Practice 1–3 — Jony Academy matnlari.
objectives: Xronologik (tarixiy) matnda uch savol guruhining "xaritasi"ni 1–2 daqiqada tuzish: jadval va flow chart sarlavhasidan kerakli xatboshilarni, T/F/NG dagi sana va ismlardan esa matndagi joyni topish.
Jadvalning ustun va qator nomlarini (Features / Problems, 1920s / 1930s) "manzil" sifatida ishlatib, javobni 2–3 xatbosh ichidan izlash.
Flow chart bo'shlig'i atrofidagi grammatikadan (another ___, both ___, a ___ of) so'z turi va sonini oldindan aniqlash.
Band 7 darajasidagi T/F/NG tuzoqlarini ajratish: darajani oshirish (as common as → more widely), kim g'oya bergani (support ≠ came up with), matnda umuman yo'q sabab.
Javobni matndan aynan, to'g'ri imlo va so'z chegarasi (NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS) bilan ko'chirish; ikki qismli javobni (colour AND design) to'liq yozish.
materials: Student's Book, Unit 4, 41–43-betlar ("The history of the poster") — sinfda birga ishlanadi (quyida rasm).
Workbook, Unit 4, 24–26-betlar ("A brief history of photography in advertising") — mustaqil mashq (quyida rasm).
Practice 1–3 matnlari chop etilgan varaqlar (har o'quvchiga) — pastdagi Reading bo'limidan.
Doskada uch ustun: "Jadval → qaysi xatboshilar?", "Flow chart → kim/qaysi davr?", "T/F/NG → sana, ism".
Taymer: Passage 1 uchun 17–18 daqiqa (Band 7 maqsadi) doskaga yoziladi.
timeline: Kirish

Isinish (kitob rasmi shart emas) — doskaga 3 savol: 1) Where do you usually see posters or adverts in your city? 2) What makes a poster catch your eye: the image, the colours or the words? 3) Do adverts today use more photographs or more drawn illustrations? Why? — 3–4 o'quvchi javob beradi.
Uch savol turi bitta passage'da
Ustoz doskada: xronologik matn xaritasi; jadval va flow chart qoidalari; T/F/NG ning Band 7 tuzoqlari; so'z chegarasi.
Sinf mashqi
"Nega bu javoblar noto'g'ri?" (SB 5-mashq asosida) va bo'shliq turini oldindan aytish.
Student's Book: The history of the poster
Q1–13 birga: jadval → flow chart → T/F/NG; har javob uchun isbot gap va paraphrase juftligi.
Workbook: Photography in advertising
17 daqiqa mustaqil, keyin javoblar izoh bilan tekshiriladi.
Practice 1
"Colour in a tube" — 16 daqiqa vaqt bilan, keyin tahlil.
Practice 2
"Behind the varnish" — 16 daqiqa, xatolar daftariga yoziladi.
Xulosa va vazifa
Practice 3 va SB/WB lug'at mashqlari uyga; xatolar daftari to'ldiriladi.

intro: Passage 1 da bu kombinatsiya juda tez-tez keladi: jadval (table), flow chart va TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN. Matn odatda TARIXIY — biror narsaning rivojlanishi yillar bo'yicha tasvirlanadi. Bu biz uchun sovg'a: sanalar va ismlar matndagi "manzil" vazifasini bajaradi.

Birinchi 1–2 daqiqa — XARITA. Uchala ko'rsatmani o'qing, so'z chegarasini doiraga oling va sarlavhalarga qarang: "Early Printing Methods" — matnning boshi (metal type, wood type, lithography); "Jules Cheret" — Cheret tilga olingan xatboshilar; T/F/NG dagi "1950s", "Typographic Style", "Weingart" — matnning ikkinchi yarmi.

Jadval — "mahalliy" savol: chap ustundagi toifalar (Metal type, Wood type, Lithography) matndagi xatboshilar tartibi bilan mos keladi. Qator nomi = qaysi xatbosh; ustun nomi (Features / Problems) = xatboshining qaysi gapi. Bo'shliq atrofidagi so'zlar ham yordam beradi: "cost, weight and ___ difficulties" — uchinchi muammo: cost, weight kabi ot kerak.

Flow chart — jarayon yoki vaqt chizig'i; javoblar deyarli har doim matn tartibida. Har qutidagi sana (1860s → 1870s → 1884–86 → 1890s) sizni keyingi xatboshiga olib boradi. Bo'shliq grammatikasini tahlil qiling: "combination of both ___" — IKKI narsa (words AND images); "another ___" — ikkala narsani qamraydigan birlikdagi umumiy ot (invention), aniq asbobning nomi (pantograph) emas.

T/F/NG — Band 7 da tuzoqlar nozikroq: 1) daraja o'zgaradi — "as common as" (teng) → "more widely seen" (ko'proq) = FALSE; 2) rol o'zgaradi — psixologlar strategiyani faqat "qo'llab-quvvatlagan", reklamachilar esa uni undan oldin sinab ko'rgan, ya'ni g'oyani psixologlar "o'ylab topmagan" = FALSE (bu gap bo'lmaganida "support" so'zining o'zi bilan NOT GIVEN bo'lardi); 3) sabab yoki manba matnda yo'q — Weingart g'oyalarini qayerdan olgani = NOT GIVEN.

Muhim: jadval va flow chart javoblari matndan AYNAN ko'chiriladi. Band 7 o'quvchisi ham imlo (greasy, not greesy), ko'plik -s va ikki qismli javobda ball yo'qotadi: "lacked both ___" — ikkala narsa kerak: colour and design.

Kitobdagi SB 5-mashq bu darsning kaliti: noto'g'ri javoblarning 5 xil sababi — grammatikaga mos emas, bo'shliqdagi so'z bilan birikmaydi (another pantograph — ma'no buziladi), javob to'liq emas, imlo xatosi, juda umumiy (paper ≠ transfer paper).

Vaqt: Band 7 maqsadi — Passage 1 ni 17–18 daqiqada tugatish, shunda Passage 3 ga 22–23 daqiqa qoladi. Jadval va flow chart'ga 9–10 daqiqa, T/F/NG ga 6–7 daqiqa, 1 daqiqa — transfer va imlo tekshiruvi.
formulas: Jadval sarlavhasi, qator va ustun nomlari
Early Printing Methods: Metal / Wood / Lithography
Qaysi xatboshi va qaysi gap — oldindan ma'lum
Flow chart qutilaridagi sana va ism
another ___ → birlik ot; both ___ → ikki narsa
greasy crayon, transfer paper, colour and design
presentation: Jadvalning qaysi ustunidan boshlayman?
Qator bo'yicha yuring: avval Metal type qatori (Features, keyin Problems), keyin Wood type. Matn ham shunday tuzilgan — har toifaga bitta xatbosh.
"Pantograph" matnda bor-ku, nega xato?
"another ___" dan keyin ikkala narsa uchun umumiy ot kerak: router bir ixtiro, pantograf — "another invention". "another pantograph" routerni ham pantograf deb aytadi — ma'no buziladi.
Ikki narsa so'ralganda bittasini yozsam-chi?
0 ball. "lacked both ___" — ikkala so'z ham kerak: colour and design (uch so'z — chegarada).
"As common as" va "more widely seen" farqi bormi?
Ha. Teng degani ko'proq degani emas. Matn tenglikni aytadi, savol ustunlikni — bu qarama-qarshilik, ya'ni FALSE.
T/F/NG javobi matnning oxirida bo'lishi mumkinmi?
Ha. Kitob maslahati: javoblar bir joyda yoki butun matn bo'ylab tarqalgan bo'lishi mumkin. NOT GIVEN bo'lsa ham, mavzu tilga olingan joyni topa olishingiz kerak.
"(greasy) crayon" — qavs nimani bildiradi?
Qavsdagi so'z ixtiyoriy: "crayon" ham, "greasy crayon" ham to'g'ri. Lekin "greesy" kabi imlo xatosi javobni butunlay noto'g'ri qiladi.
notes: 6.0 darsida (12-dars) chizma + T/F/NG + flow chart kombinatsiyasini ko'rgan edik. Endi darajani oshiramiz: matn akademikroq (lithography, typographic, pictorialist), jadval uch ustunli, T/F/NG tuzoqlari nozikroq.
Har javobdan keyin uch savol bering: "isbot qaysi gapda?", "savoldagi qaysi so'z matnda qanday aytilgan?" va "nega boshqa so'z (masalan pantograph, paper) mos emas?"
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: SB matnini o'qimasdan, faqat jadval, flow chart va T/F/NG sarlavhalariga qarab, har savol qaysi xatboshida ekanini 2 daqiqada taxmin qilish, keyin tekshirish.
mistakes: "another ___" — router ham, pantograf ham ixtiro: umumiy toifa so'zi kerak
Juda umumiy — maxsus qog'oz turi so'ralgan
Q10 da TRUE ("as common as" = "more widely")
Q13 da FALSE ("u o'zi o'ylab topgan" deb taxmin)
G'oyalari manbai haqida matnda hech narsa yo'q

how: CORE — san'at, bosma va reklama mavzusidagi asosiy so'zlar; STRONG — tasvir va baho beruvchi Band 7 sifatlari; SUPER — akademik iboralar (SB lug'at bo'limidagi make/take/do/have birikmalari bilan bog'lang).
Har so'z bilan o'quvchi o'zbek san'ati yoki shahrimizdagi reklama haqida gap tuzsin: "Uzbek suzani embroidery has exerted an influence on modern fashion."
core: The concert poster was designed by a local artist.
Early magazines relied on illustration rather than photography.
Ilk jurnallar fotosurat emas, qo'lda chizilgan rasmlarga tayangan.
The first exhibition of posters was held in 1884.
Ochre is one of the oldest pigments in the world.
Oxra dunyodagi eng qadimgi pigmentlardan biri.
Commercial photography grew with the advertising industry.
Tijoriy fotografiya reklama sanoati bilan birga o'sdi.
The paint tube was a simple but powerful innovation.
Bo'yoq tyubigi oddiy, lekin kuchli yangilik edi.
He earned a living by painting portraits.
She works for a major advertising agency.
Photography was then a relatively new medium.
O'sha paytda fotografiya nisbatan yangi vosita edi.
strong: The first posters were crudely produced.
Posters were the dominant means of communication.
His designs looked playful and spontaneous.
Uning dizaynlari quvnoq va erkin ko'rinardi.
Critics called the style cold and dogmatic.
Tanqidchilar bu uslubni sovuq va aqidaparast deyishdi.
ataylab bahs yoki kuchli reaksiya uyg'otuvchi, provokatsion
The advert was criticised as provocative.
Reklama provokatsion (ataylab bahs uyg'otuvchi) deb tanqid qilindi.
Good adverts make dreams seem attainable.
Yaxshi reklama orzularni erishsa bo'ladigandek ko'rsatadi.
super: The new style slowly took hold in other countries.
Yangi uslub boshqa mamlakatlarda asta-sekin ildiz otdi.
The style continues to exert an influence on designers.
Bu uslub dizaynerlarga hanuz ta'sir o'tkazmoqda.
By the 1950s, posters had begun to share the spotlight with radio.
1950-yillarga kelib plakatlar diqqat markazini radio bilan bo'lisha boshlagan edi.
His posters were chaotic, in stark contrast to earlier work.
Uning plakatlari avvalgi ishlardan keskin farqli ravishda tartibsiz edi.

class_ex.title: Nega bu javoblar noto'g'ri? (SB, 5-mashq asosida)
class_ex.instr: Jadvaldagi Q1–5 ga o'quvchi shunday javob yozgan. Har biri nega 0 ball olganini ayting va to'g'ri javobni matndan toping.
items: 1 cost, weight and not enough letters difficulties
2 used in connection with another pantograph
3 lacked both colour
4 design tool – a greesy crayon
5 had to use a mirror or paper
why: "not enough letters" — uch so'z, ya'ni so'z chegarasi ichida; xato sababi boshqa: bo'shliqdan keyin "difficulties" keladi, undan oldin aniqlovchi vazifasidagi OT kerak (storage difficulties). "not enough letters difficulties" grammatikaga mos emas. Matn: "required a large amount of storage space" → to'g'ri javob: storage (space).

"another ___" — ikkala narsani qamraydigan umumiy so'z kerak. Router bitta ixtiro, pantograf — boshqa ixtiro: "another invention". "another pantograph" esa routerni ham pantograf deb aytadi — ma'no noto'g'ri.
"both" ikki narsani talab qiladi. Matn: "they had little colour and design". Britancha "colour" ham, "color" ham qabul qilinadi.
Imlo xatosi: "greesy". Matnda "greasy crayon" — imlo noto'g'ri bo'lsa javob hisoblanmaydi.
"paper" juda umumiy — maxsus qog'oz turi: "traced on transfer paper".
class_ex.note: Doskada besh sababni yozib qo'ying: grammatika, birikma (collocation), to'liqlik, imlo, aniqlik. Dars oxirigacha har xato shu besh sababdan biriga yoziladi.

class_ex.title: Bo'shliq turini oldindan aytish (SB, Q6–9) va T/F/NG kalit so'zlari (Q10–13)
class_ex.instr: Matnni o'qimasdan: Q6–9 bo'shliqlariga qanday ma'lumot kerak? Q10–13 da qaysi so'zlarni tagiga chizasiz?
items: 6 — "combination of both ___ on coloured posters"
7 — "posters used for advertising and ___ in Europe"
8 — "Cheret's poster ___ and book on poster art"
9 — "posters represent ___ around the world"
10 — "By the 1950s, photographs were more widely seen than artists' illustrations on posters."
13 — "Weingart got many of his ideas from his students in Basel."
answers: Cheret plakatlar bilan qilgan ish (ot: tadbir yoki to'plam)
why: "both" — ikki narsa birga ishlatilgan; kalit bo'yicha: bir-biri bilan birga qo'yilgan ikki narsa.
"used for advertising and ___" — reklamadan tashqari yana bir maqsad; 1870s xatboshisi.
"poster ___ and book" — kitobdan oldingi voqea; 1884 sanasi matnda bor.
"around the world" — turli mamlakatlarda tasvirlangan narsalar; 1890s xatboshisi.
Sana joyni topadi, "more widely" esa darajani — aynan shu so'z javobni hal qiladi.
Ism va shahar joyni topadi; "ideas from his students" — tekshiriladigan da'vo.
class_ex.note: Kalit bo'yicha: 6 — birga ishlatilgan ikki narsa; 7 — plakat nimaga ishlatilgan; 8 — Cheret bilan bog'liq narsa; 9 — plakat nimani ifodalagan.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5 — Early Printing Methods
tasks.type: Complete the table below. Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage for each answer.
tasks.instr: Kalit bo'yicha: sarlavha javoblar matn boshida ekanini ko'rsatadi; chap ustundagi toifalar birinchi to'rt xatboshiga mos keladi.
answers: colour and design / design and colour
why: "It was expensive, required a large amount of storage space and was extremely heavy". Cost = expensive, weight = heavy, uchinchisi — storage.

"The router was used in combination with William Leavenworth's pantograph". Pantograf — boshqa ixtiro; matnda "the invention of a system for wood type production". "another ___" — router ham, pantograf ham ixtiro, shuning uchun ikkalasini qamraydigan umumiy toifa so'zi kerak: invention ("another pantograph" routerni ham pantograf deb aytadi).
"The first posters began to appear, but they had little colour and design". "Lacked both" = "had little"; ikkala so'z ham shart (color ham qabul qilinadi).
"The method involved drawing with a greasy crayon". "Design tool" = yozish/chizish vositasi.
"The images and lettering needed to be drawn backwards, often reflected in a mirror or traced on transfer paper".
tasks.note: Kalitdagi izoh: Q1 — "not enough letters" grammatikaga mos emas; Q2 — pantograph ixtironing nomi; "another ___" esa umumiy toifa so'zini (invention) talab qiladi.
head: Method
Features
Problems
rows: cost, weight and (1) difficulties ;; mixed styles
Darius's wood drill used in connection with another (2) ;; produced a range of letters
letters drawn by hand ;; design tool – a (4)
had to use a mirror or (5) to achieve correct image

tasks.title: Questions 6–9 — Jules Cheret
tasks.type: Complete the flow chart below. Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage for each answer.
tasks.instr: Sarlavha — Cheret: u tilga olingan xatboshilardan boshlang ("three-stone lithographic process"). Sanalar bo'yicha pastga yuring.
why: "The ability to mix words and images in such an attractive and economical format". "Combination" = "mix".
"Posters became the main vehicle for advertising ... and the dominant means of mass communication". Reklama qutida bor — ikkinchi vazifa kerak.
"Organised the first exhibition of posters in 1884 and two years later published the first book". 1884–86 = "two years later".
"Came to celebrate each society's unique cultural institutions". "Represent" = "celebrate"; "unique" — ixtiyoriy.
rows: combination of both (6) on coloured posters
1870s – posters used for advertising and (7) in Europe

readings.title: Practice 1: Colour in a tube
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 1 darajasi, Band 7 lug'ati)
text: For most of human history, painters could not simply buy their colours. Every pigment had to be found, dug up, crushed or cooked, and the range of colours available to an artist depended largely on geology, trade routes and chemistry. The story of how that range grew is, in many ways, a story of accident and commercial ambition as much as artistic vision. Colours were also closely linked to status: a painting that used rare pigments announced the wealth of whoever had paid for it.

The earliest pigments were earths. Ochres, which owe their yellow, red and brown tones to iron oxides, were used in cave paintings tens of thousands of years ago and are still sold today. They were cheap and stable, but their palette was narrow: bright blues and greens simply did not exist among the natural earth colours. The ancient Egyptians solved part of this problem by manufacturing what is often described as the first synthetic pigment, Egyptian blue, made by heating sand, copper and a mineral containing calcium. The recipe required careful control of temperature, and after the Roman period the knowledge of how to make it was largely lost. Remarkably, Egyptian blue glows under infrared light, a property that now helps researchers detect tiny traces of it on ancient objects.

In medieval and Renaissance Europe, the most prized blue was ultramarine, ground from the semi-precious stone lapis lazuli, which was mined in what is now Afghanistan and transported thousands of kilometres to Venice. Its colour was unmatched, but the cost was extraordinary: at times it was valued more highly than gold, and contracts between painters and their patrons sometimes specified exactly how much of it was to be used, usually for the robes of the Virgin Mary. Artists who could not afford it turned to azurite, a copper mineral that was cheaper but tended to turn greenish over time.

The first modern synthetic pigment appeared by chance. In Berlin in the early eighteenth century, a colour-maker attempting to produce a red accidentally created a deep blue, later named Prussian blue. It was inexpensive and intense, and within a few decades it had spread across Europe and eventually as far as Japan. A century later, in 1824, a French society offered a prize to anyone who could produce ultramarine artificially. The prize was claimed in 1828, and the price of the colour fell dramatically, putting it within reach of ordinary painters for the first time.

Yet the most significant change of the nineteenth century concerned not the colours themselves but the way they were stored. Before the 1840s, paint had to be prepared in the studio, usually by apprentices. Pigment was ground by hand on a stone slab and mixed with linseed oil to form a stiff paste. Because oil paint hardens when exposed to air, the paste was then sealed inside small bags made from pig's bladder and tied with string. To use it, the painter pierced the bag with a tack, squeezed out the amount required and plugged the hole again. The bags were fragile, frequently burst and could not easily be carried any distance.

In 1841 an American portrait painter living in London, John Goffe Rand, patented a collapsible tube made of tin and closed with a screw cap. The design kept paint fresh for far longer and could be slipped into a pocket. Colour-makers quickly adopted it, and within a few years ready-made paint in tubes was widely available. For the first time, artists could work outdoors for an entire day with a complete set of colours, and many art historians link this practical convenience to the rise of painting in the open air later in the century, a practice closely associated with the Impressionists.

Not every innovation was an improvement, however. Some of the new colours proved unstable: certain bright yellows darkened or faded when exposed to light, and a fashionable emerald green was made with arsenic, which made it poisonous to handle. Conservators examining nineteenth-century canvases frequently find that colours have shifted over time, which means that the paintings we admire today do not always look as their creators intended. Some of these problems were only understood decades later, when chemists began to analyse paint samples systematically.

readings.title: Practice 2: Behind the varnish
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 1 darajasi, Band 7 lug'ati)
text: Visitors to a museum rarely consider that the painting in front of them may have been cleaned, repaired and partly repainted several times since it left the artist's studio. Over the centuries, paintings suffer from dirt, smoke, changes in humidity and, not least, from earlier attempts to improve them. The modern profession of conservation aims to slow this decline and, where possible, to reverse it, while respecting a principle that previous generations often ignored: nothing should be done to a work of art that cannot later be undone. Because museums rarely display a painting while it is being treated, most of this work goes unseen.

Before any treatment begins, a painting is examined in detail, and much of this examination now relies on scientific imaging. X-radiography is particularly useful for older works because lead white, a pigment used widely until the twentieth century, blocks X-rays and therefore shows up clearly. The resulting images can reveal changes of composition, such as a hand that has been moved or a figure that has been painted out, which art historians call pentimenti. Infrared reflectography works differently: many paint layers are transparent to infrared radiation, whereas the carbon in charcoal or ink absorbs it, so the artist's preliminary drawing beneath the paint becomes visible. Ultraviolet light, meanwhile, is used mainly to study the surface. Aged natural varnish glows with a greenish fluorescence under UV, while later retouching tends to appear as dark patches, allowing conservators to map exactly where earlier restorers have worked.

The most visible stage of treatment is usually cleaning. Most old paintings were protected with a layer of natural resin varnish, which slowly yellows and darkens, so that a scene painted in bright daylight may appear to be set at dusk. Varnish that has been disturbed or poorly applied can also turn cloudy, a condition known as blooming. Removing it requires solvents strong enough to dissolve the varnish but not the paint below. Conservators therefore begin with tiny test areas, often no bigger than a fingernail, trying mixtures of increasing strength and examining the results under a microscope. Only when a safe solution has been identified is the whole surface cleaned, typically with small cotton swabs, a process that can take months for a large canvas.

Once the old varnish and dirt have gone, the damage they concealed becomes apparent. Areas where paint has flaked away, known as losses, are first filled with a putty-like material and shaped to match the texture of the surrounding surface. The next step, retouching, is where ethical questions become most pressing. Conservators apply colour only within the boundaries of each loss and never over original paint, and they use modern materials that remain soluble, so that a future conservator can remove the additions without difficulty. Finally, a fresh varnish is applied, both to protect the surface and to restore the depth of colour that the painter intended.

These rules were not always followed. In the nineteenth century, it was common for restorers to repaint large areas freely, sometimes 'improving' a composition to suit contemporary taste, and some used varnishes that later became almost impossible to remove. Another damaging practice was overcleaning, in which aggressive solvents removed not only the varnish but also the thin final layers of paint. A considerable part of the work carried out in conservation studios today consists of undoing such earlier interventions.

Cleaning in particular has provoked fierce public debate. When the Sistine Chapel ceiling was cleaned during the 1980s, critics argued that the vivid colours revealed could not be what Michelangelo had wanted, and that a final layer of shading applied by the artist himself had been removed along with the dirt. Supporters replied that the dark surface had consisted largely of candle smoke and grime, and that the bright palette was consistent with the artist's other work. Such arguments show that conservation, however scientific its methods, always involves an interpretation of what the artist originally intended. In recent decades, many museums have chosen to publish detailed reports of their treatments, partly in response to such controversies.

readings.title: Practice 3 (uyga): Pictures of the floating world
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 1 darajasi, Band 7 lug'ati), uy vazifasi
text: Few images are as widely reproduced today as Katsushika Hokusai's Under the Wave off Kanagawa, better known as The Great Wave. Yet when it was published around 1831, it was not regarded as a precious work of art. It was a commercial print, produced in large numbers and sold cheaply to ordinary city dwellers, in much the same way that posters would later be sold on the streets of Europe.

The print belonged to a genre called ukiyo-e, or 'pictures of the floating world', which developed in the city of Edo, now Tokyo, during the seventeenth century. The 'floating world' referred to the pleasure districts of the city, with their theatres, tea houses and entertainers. The name itself carried a sense of pleasure and impermanence, suggesting a life lived for the moment. Early prints were largely portraits of famous actors and fashionable beauties. Only in the nineteenth century did landscapes become a major subject, partly because travel within the country had become increasingly popular and a growing number of people wanted souvenirs of the places they had seen.

A print was never the work of a single person. The process was controlled by the publisher, who financed the project, chose the subject and sold the finished product. Publishers often commissioned a series of prints on a single theme, such as famous views of Mount Fuji, which encouraged customers to collect a complete set. Sales were often counted in thousands, and a successful series could keep a publishing house busy for years. The artist, or designer, supplied only the drawing. A carver transferred it to wood, and a printer produced the final sheets. Although the designer's name is the one remembered today, the carvers and printers were highly trained craftsmen, and the quality of a print depended as much on their skill as on the original drawing.

Production followed a fixed sequence. First, the designer made an ink drawing on thin, almost transparent paper. This was pasted face down onto a block of cherry wood, a hard, fine-grained timber that could hold extremely small details. The carver then cut away the wood around the lines, destroying the drawing in the process, to leave the outlines standing in relief; this became the key block. Proofs taken from the key block were returned to the designer, who marked on each one the areas to be printed in a particular colour, and a separate block was carved for every colour. To ensure that the colours lined up exactly, each block had two small guides cut into its edge, called kento: an L-shaped notch in one corner and a straight line along one side. The printer brushed water-based pigment onto the block, laid the damp paper on top using the guides, and pressed it by rubbing the back with a flat hand tool called a baren. A popular design might be printed thousands of times before the blocks wore out.

Colour technology altered the appearance of the prints. In the late 1820s, imported Prussian blue became available at an affordable price in Japan. Unlike the plant-based blues used earlier, it did not fade quickly, and artists exploited it to create deep skies and seas. The Great Wave, with its striking contrast of blues, is among the best-known examples. Within a few years, blue-dominated landscape prints had become so fashionable that some were printed almost entirely in shades of that single colour.

After Japan opened its ports to Western trade in the 1850s, prints began to reach Europe in large quantities, sometimes, according to a frequently repeated story, as wrapping paper for porcelain. Collectors in Europe soon paid high prices for sheets that had been considered cheap in Japan. Artists in Paris were fascinated by their flat areas of colour, bold outlines, unusual viewpoints and the way figures were cut off by the edge of the picture. Vincent van Gogh collected hundreds of them and painted copies of several, while Claude Monet hung prints throughout his house at Giverny. The enthusiasm for Japanese art became known as Japonisme, and its influence is evident in the posters of Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, whose simplified shapes owe a clear debt to the woodblock tradition.

kahoot.explain: Sarlavha va qator nomlari (Metal type, Wood type...) xatboshilar tartibiga mos keladi — butun matnni qayta o'qish shart emas.

kahoot.q: Gap: 'used in connection with another ___'. Which answer fits best?
kahoot.explain: 'another' + ikkala narsani qamraydigan umumiy ot: router ham, pantograf ham ixtiro. 'another pantograph' routerni ham pantograf deb aytadi (SB kaliti: pantograph — ixtironing nomi).

kahoot.q: Gap: 'lacked both ___'. The passage says 'little colour and design'. Correct answer?
kahoot.explain: 'both' — ikki narsa. Faqat bittasini yozish 0 ball.

kahoot.q: A student wrote 'greesy crayon'. Why is it marked wrong?
options: It is the wrong part of speech
It is from the wrong paragraph
kahoot.explain: Matnda 'greasy'. Imlo xatosi bo'lsa, ma'no to'g'ri bo'lsa ham ball berilmaydi.

kahoot.q: Why is 'paper' not accepted for 'had to use a mirror or ___'?
options: It should be in the plural
kahoot.explain: Matnda maxsus qog'oz turi — transfer paper. Umumiy so'z yetarli emas.

kahoot.q: Flow-chart answers usually appear...
options: in the same order as the passage
in no particular order in the text
in reverse order, from the end
kahoot.explain: Flow chart jarayon yoki vaqt chizig'i — javoblar deyarli har doim matn tartibida.

kahoot.q: Text: 'as common as illustration'. Statement: 'more widely seen than illustrations'. Answer?
kahoot.explain: Teng (as common as) ≠ ko'proq (more widely). Matn boshqa narsani aytadi — FALSE.

kahoot.q: Text: psychologists 'provided support for' a strategy advertisers had already tried. Statement: psychologists 'came up with the idea'. Answer?
kahoot.explain: G'oya avval reklamachilarda bo'lgan, psixologlar faqat qo'llab-quvvatlagan (WB Q10).

kahoot.q: Weingart is mentioned, but not where his ideas came from. 'He got ideas from his students' is...
options: FALSE, because he was a teacher
kahoot.explain: Ism va joy matnda bor, lekin da'vo yo'q. Isbot gap topilmasa — NOT GIVEN.

kahoot.q: According to the exam advice, when should you be able to find the part of the text for a T/F/NG item?
options: Always, even when the answer is NOT GIVEN
Only when the answer is TRUE or FALSE
Only when the statement has a date or name
Never, because you should just guess
kahoot.explain: Mavzu tilga olingan joyni har doim topasiz; NOT GIVEN — da'vo yo'q, mavzu esa bor.

kahoot.q: Limit: NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS. Which answer is NOT acceptable?
kahoot.explain: To'rt so'z — chegaradan oshgan. Qolganlari uch yoki ikki so'z.

kahoot.q: What is a good time target for Passage 1 at Band 7?
kahoot.explain: Passage 1 ni 17–18 daqiqada tugatsangiz, qiyin Passage 3 ga ko'proq vaqt qoladi.

kahoot.q: Cheret organised the first ___ of posters in 1884.
kahoot.explain: Exhibition — ko'rgazma. Plakatlar birinchi marta ko'rgazmada namoyish etilgan.

kahoot.q: The style 'continues to ___ its influence today'. Which verb fits?
kahoot.explain: Exert an influence (on) — ta'sir o'tkazmoq. Akademik birikma.

kahoot.q: The first posters were 'quickly and ___ produced' — without care or detail.
kahoot.explain: Crudely — qo'pol, ishlov berilmagan holda.

kahoot.q: Weingart's posters were chaotic, in ___ contrast to what had gone before.
kahoot.explain: In stark contrast to — keskin farqli ravishda. Tayyor ibora.

kahoot.q: Steichen made fantasies seem ___ — possible to achieve.
kahoot.explain: Attainable = achievable, erishsa bo'ladigan. WB flow chart Q9 dagi paraphrase.

kahoot.q: Adverts that try to shock people are called...
kahoot.explain: Provocative — ataylab bahs yoki kuchli reaksiya (hayrat, norozilik) uyg'otuvchi.

kahoot.q: By the 1950s posters had begun to share the ___ with radio and print.
kahoot.explain: Share the spotlight — diqqat markazini boshqa narsa bilan bo'lishmoq.

kahoot.q: Critics called the style 'cold, formal and ___' — following rigid rules.
kahoot.explain: Dogmatic — qat'iy qoidalarga bog'langan. Spontaneous va playful — uning aksi.

lessons.title: Unit 4 Listening — Section 4: Note completion
lessons.grammar_topic: Section 4 (akademik ma'ruza): Note completion — 10 bo'shliq, bitta ma'ruza, tanaffussiz
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 4 (Art and the artist) — qadimgi san'at, bo'yoqlar, tosh san'ati, zamonaviy rassomlik
lessons.book_ref: Complete IELTS Bands 6.5–7.5: Student's Book, Unit 4, 44–45-betlar (Listening Section 4, CD1 Track 19; skript — 153-bet); Workbook, Unit 4, 26–27-betlar (Listening Section 4, Track 7; skript — 57-bet).
objectives: Section 4 notes'ining tuzilmasini (sarlavha, bo'lim nomlari, strelkalar) 30–40 soniyada o'qib, ma'ruza rejasini oldindan bilish.
Har bo'shliq uchun ma'lumot turini aniqlash: san'at turi, modda, vaqt oralig'i, maqsad, buyum — va so'z turi (ot, ko'plik, raqam).
Ma'ruzachining bo'lim o'tish belgilarini (Let's move on to..., So, how have things changed?, OK, onto...) eshitib, notes'da adashmaslik.
Band 7 tuzoqlarini tanish: birinchi eshitilgan raqam (60,000 → 18,000), "nowadays" va "in the past" farqi, ma'ruzachi rad etgan nazariya.
Eshitilgan so'zni aynan yozish, NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER chegarasi va imloga rioya qilish.
materials: Student's Book, Unit 4, 44–45-betlar — kirish mashqlari va Q1–10 notes (quyida rasm), CD1 Track 19 audiosi.
Workbook, Unit 4, 26–27-betlar — Q1–10 notes (quyida rasm), Track 7 audiosi (imtihon rejimi, bir marta).

Recording script rasmlari — faqat ustozda; tekshiruvdan keyin ekranga chiqariladi. Uy vazifasi uchun kerakli parchalar (WB Track 7 — "Cave paintings" qismi; SB Track 19 — oxirgi 1 daqiqa) audio va skripti bilan dars oxirida guruh chatiga yuboriladi.
Kolonka yoki quloqchin; audio platformadan ochiladi (internetni oldindan tekshiring).
Jony Academy ma'ruzasi ("Stained glass") — ustoz o'qiydi; o'quvchilarga faqat notes varag'i beriladi.

intro: Section 4 — bitta so'zlovchining akademik ma'ruzasi (lecture). Tanaffus YO'Q: 10 savol boshidan oxirigacha bitta audioda. Til va mazmun eng qiyin, lekin tuzilma eng aniq — ma'ruzachi rejasini o'zi aytadi va har bo'limga o'tishini belgilaydi.

Note completion — Section 4 ning eng keng tarqalgan turi. Notes'ning o'zi ma'ruza XARITASI: sarlavha (Australian Aboriginal Art), katta bo'limlar (ANCIENT ART / MODERN ART), kichik bo'limlar (Cave art, Use of ochre, Preparation). Tayyorlanish vaqtida avval shu "skelet"ni o'qing.

Keyin har bo'shliq uchun ikki savol: 1) qanday MA'LUMOT kerak (san'at turi, modda, vaqt, maqsad, buyum)? 2) qanday SO'Z TURI (ot, ko'plik ot, raqam + birlik)? Masalan, "artist's palette found that is ___ old" — vaqt: raqam + years; "a range of ___" — ko'plikdagi ot.

Bo'lim o'tish iboralari — adashmaslik kaliti: "So let's start by...", "Let's move on to look at the materials", "So, how have things changed?", "OK, onto petroglyphs". Shu iborani eshitsangiz, ko'zingiz notes'ning keyingi sarlavhasiga o'tsin.

Paraphrase: notes'dagi so'z ma'ruzada boshqacha aytiladi. "protected from" = "sheltered, hasn't been destroyed by"; "main function" = "the key purpose"; "readily available" = "plentiful". Javob esa ko'pincha AYNAN eshitilgan so'z bo'ladi (weather, storytelling, powder).

Band 7 tuzoqlari: 1) birinchi raqam javob emas — ma'ruza "60,000 years" bilan boshlanadi, palitra esa "18,000 years"; 2) zamon farqi — "nowadays ... acrylic binder, but in the past ... tree sap, bush honey"; 3) ma'ruzachi nazariyani aytib, keyin rad etadi — notes "possibly" deydi, javob esa nazariyaning o'zi (magic qualities).

Kitob maslahati: eshitgan so'zingizni yozing. Javob so'zi deyarli har doim audioda aynan aytiladi; o'zingizning sinonimingiz faqat oxirgi chora (kalitda bo'lmasa, ball berilmaydi) — lekin bo'sh qoldirmang. Oxirida transfer: imlo (colours/colors), raqam (18,000), ko'plik -s va TWO WORDS chegarasi.
formulas: ANCIENT ART → Cave art → Use of ochre → MODERN ART
a ___ → birlik; a range of ___ → ko'plik
Let's move on to... / OK, onto...
Birinchi eshitilgan so'z har doim javob emas
presentation: Section 4 da tanaffus bormi?
Yo'q. Barcha 10 savol bitta ma'ruzada. Shuning uchun tayyorlanish vaqtida butun notes'ni ko'rib chiqing, faqat birinchi yarmini emas.
Bo'shliqni o'tkazib yubordim. Nima qilaman?
To'xtamang. Keyingi sarlavhani kuting va davom eting. Oxirida mantiqan taxmin qiling — bo'sh qoldirmang.
Notes'dagi so'z eshitilmadi-ku?
Section 4 da notes deyarli har doim paraphrase. "Main function" o'rniga "the key purpose" eshitasiz — ma'noni kuting.
"Body" yozsam bo'ladimi yoki "body art" kerakmi?
Kalitda "body (art)" — ikkalasi ham to'g'ri. Qavsdagi qism ixtiyoriy, lekin qo'shimcha so'z chegarani buzmasin.
Raqamni qanday yozaman?
Son bilan: 18,000 years yoki 18000 years. "Years" notes'da bo'lmasa, uni ham yozing — aks holda javob to'liq emas.
Ma'ruzachi nazariyani rad etsa, javob o'zgaradimi?
Yo'q, agar notes "Possibly believed to have..." desa — nazariya mazmuni yoziladi (magic qualities). Rad etish keyingi savolga o'tish signali.
notes: 6.0 da Section 4 ni sentence completion + flow chart bilan ishlagan edik. 7.0 da butun ma'ruza — note completion, ma'ruza uzunroq (5 daqiqa), til akademikroq (pigment, binder, petroglyph).
Tekshiruvda har javobdan keyin skriptdan aynan o'sha gapni ekranga chiqaring va tuzoq gapni boshqa rang bilan ko'rsating (60,000; acrylic binder; 12,000).
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: WB audiosini notes'siz tinglab, ma'ruzaning o'z notes'ini yozish (3 bo'lim × 3–4 qator), keyin kitobdagi notes bilan solishtirish.
mistakes: 60,000 — umuman Aboriginal san'at yoshi, palitra emas
Notes'da "tree sap or ___" — o'tmishdagi binder so'ralgan

how: CORE — ma'ruzadagi asosiy san'at va material so'zlari; STRONG — akademik tavsif so'zlari; SUPER — ma'ruza tilining iboralari (o'tish va baho). Takror (7-dars): pigment — yangi so'z sifatida sanalmaydi; oxra va bo'yoqlar haqida gapirganda qayta ishlating.
Har so'z bilan o'quvchi Samarqand yoki Buxorodagi qadimiy yodgorlik haqida bitta gap tuzsin: "The tiles have been preserved because they were sheltered from the weather."
core: Indigenous people have lived in Australia for thousands of years.
Tub aholi Avstraliyada ming yillardan beri yashaydi.
Ochre was ground into a fine powder.
In the nineteenth century, craftsmen began to revive the art of stained glass.
XIX asrda hunarmandlar vitraj san'atini qayta tiklay boshladi.
Tree sap was used as a binder.
Daraxt shirasi bog'lovchi modda sifatida ishlatilgan.
Modern artists began to paint on canvas.
The paintings were preserved inside caves.
The images were carved into rock surfaces.
Body art is important for ceremonial practice.
Wild animals are a common theme in cave art.
Yovvoyi hayvonlar g'or san'atida keng tarqalgan mavzu.
strong: Rock is more durable than bark.
Preparing the paint was time-consuming work.
Bo'yoq tayyorlash ko'p vaqt oladigan ish edi.
Abstract patterns are a recurring theme.
The carvings still have deep cultural significance.
O'ymakorliklar hanuz chuqur madaniy ahamiyatga ega.
super: Bu an'ana 60 000 yil oldinga borib taqaladi.
Dot painting has taken off internationally.
Nuqtali rassomlik xalqaro miqyosda birdan ommalashdi.
Selling paintings helps keep the culture alive.
Rasm sotish madaniyatni tirik saqlashga yordam beradi.
Some patterns seem hard-wired into the human brain.
Ba'zi naqshlar inson miyasiga tug'ma joylashganga o'xshaydi.

class_ex.title: Bo'shliq turini oldindan aytish (SB, 2-mashq)
class_ex.instr: Audio eshitishdan oldin: har bo'shliqqa qanday ma'lumot va qanday so'z turi kerak? Avval ma'ruza tuzilmasini ayting.
items: Ma'ruza qanday tuzilgan?
1 — ro'yxatda: rock and bark painting, sand drawings, ___, decorations on weapons
2 — "protected from ___"
3 — "dot paintings (e.g. arrows, water holes and ___)"
5 — "soil or rock contains ___"
6 — "artist's palette found that is ___ old"
10 — "paint and decorate pottery and a range of ___"
answers: ikki bo'lim: qadimgi san'at (g'or san'ati, oxra) va zamonaviy san'at
why: Kalit: birinchi qism — qadimgi san'at (g'or san'ati va oxra bo'yoq), ikkinchisi — zamonaviy san'at. Katta harfli sarlavhalar buni ko'rsatadi.
Ro'yxatning boshqa elementlari ham san'at turlari — bo'shliq ham shunday.
"protected from" — tabiat kuchi yoki xavf; kalit: "something that affects preservation".
"arrows, water holes and ___" — nuqtali rasmdagi belgilar ro'yxati; ko'plik.
"contains" — tarkibidagi modda; bu bo'lim bo'yoq ranglari haqida.
"that is ___ old" — yosh: son + years.
"a range of" dan keyin ko'plik ot — bezatiladigan narsalar.
class_ex.note: O'quvchilar javoblarini doskaga yozing va audiodan keyin solishtiring: ma'lumot turi to'g'ri taxmin qilingan bo'shliqlarda xato kamroq bo'ladi.

class_ex.title: O'tish iboralari: keyingi bo'lim qaysi?
class_ex.instr: Ustoz iborani o'qiydi. O'quvchilar notes'ning qaysi sarlavhasiga o'tish kerakligini aytadi (SB yoki WB notes'i).
items: "So let's start by having a look at some examples of ancient art."
"Let's move on to look at the materials."
"Preparing the ochre paints was time-consuming work. First, ..."
"So, how have things changed?"
"OK, onto petroglyphs."
"There has of course been much debate about why cave paintings were made."
why: "ancient art" — notes'dagi birinchi katta sarlavha.
"materials" = ochre; "Use of ochre → Reason" qismi boshlanadi.
"Preparing" = Preparation; "First" — strelkali ketma-ketlik boshlanishi.
"how have things changed" — o'tmishdan hozirga o'tish: MODERN ART.
"onto" — yangi bo'lim; WB notes'ining ikkinchi sarlavhasi.
"why ... were made" = purpose; javob (magic qualities) shu yerda.
class_ex.note: Bu iboralarni doskada qoldiring — WB audiosini tinglaganda o'quvchilar ularni eshitgan zahoti qo'l ko'taradi.

listenings.title: Student's Book, Track 19: Australian Aboriginal Art (Q1–10)
intro: Ma'ruzachi Avstraliya tub aholisining san'ati haqida gapiradi: qadimgi san'at turlari, g'or san'ati, oxra bo'yog'i va uni tayyorlash, zamonaviy san'at. Tinglashdan oldin 40 soniya: sarlavhalar va har bo'shliq turi (SB 2-mashq).

tasks.title: Questions 1–10 — Australian Aboriginal Art
tasks.type: Complete the notes below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
tasks.instr: Notes tartibi = ma'ruza tartibi. O'tish iboralarini kuting: "Let's move on to...", "So, how have things changed?"
why: "Then there's the whole area of body art, which is so important for ceremonial practice".
"It's been sheltered, hasn't been destroyed by the weather". "Protected from" = "sheltered".
"Here's a water hole, and these are animal tracks". "Arrows" va "water hole" notes'da bor.
"The key purpose of much of this rock art was storytelling". "Main function" = "key purpose".
"It's coloured by iron oxide, which is the mineral...". "Contains" — rangi shu moddadan.
"An artist's palette of ochres, dating back 18,000 years". Tuzoq: ma'ruza boshidagi "60,000 years" — umuman Aboriginal san'at haqida.
"The rock had to be broken up and ground into a powder".
"In the past, Aboriginal people used things like tree sap, or something similar like bush honey". Tuzoq: "nowadays ... professional artist's acrylic binder".
"Took up acrylic painting and began to paint on canvas". "Acrylic" notes'da bor.
"Aboriginal art can also be found on pottery and various musical instruments like didgeridoos". "A range of" = "various".

tasks.type: Qisqa javob

items: 1 Where might pictures A–E originate from?
2 Which of the art forms will you hear about, and in what order?
3 How is the lecture structured?
answers: A Peru (Nazca Desert); B France (Lascaux caves); C Ancient Egypt; D Ancient Rome (Pompeii); E the USA (Arizona)

tasks.title: Questions 1–10 — Prehistoric visual art
tasks.type: Complete the notes below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
tasks.instr: Uch bo'lim: Cave paintings → Petroglyphs → Geoglyphs. "OK, onto petroglyphs" — ikkinchi bo'lim signali.
why: "The Upper Paleolithic era, which is around 40,000 years ago". Tuzoq: "12,000 years" — petrogliflar haqida.
"Human hands also feature, and abstract patterns are a recurring theme".
"Probably chosen for their vivid colours". "Materials with ___" — ko'plik.
"Paintings made in this way are generally much better preserved than others". "Best ___" + sifatdosh.
"Images of animals were seen as possessing magic qualities". Ma'ruzachi "I would dispute this" deydi, lekin notes "Possibly believed" — nazariya mazmuni yoziladi.
"Images cut or carved into vertical or horizontal rock surfaces".
"Even now they have a deep cultural significance". "Still possess great" = "even now have a deep".
"A result of the genetically inherited structure of the human brain". "The way ___ is formed" = "structure".
"Size-wise, they're large, at least four metres across". "Minimum diameter" = "at least ... across".
"Consist of hundreds of individual figures representing creatures". "Many" = "hundreds of".

listenings.title: Jony Academy mashqi: Stained glass in medieval Europe (Q1–10)
intro: Ustoz ma'ruzani bir marta, tabiiy tezlikda, tanaffussiz va javob so'zlariga urg'u bermasdan o'qiydi. O'quvchilar avval 40 soniya notes'ni o'qiydi va har bo'shliq turini belgilaydi.
Har bo'limda bitta tuzoq bor: avval aytilgan raqam, "not ... but", bugungi va o'tmishdagi usul farqi. Tekshiruvda o'quvchi tuzoqni ham aytishi kerak.
transcript: LECTURER: Good morning, everyone. Today I'd like to look at one of the most remarkable art forms of the Middle Ages: the stained-glass window. I'll start with some background, then we'll look at one famous cathedral, after that at how a window was actually made, and finally at what happened to the craft later on.

LECTURER: Coloured glass itself is very old — the Romans used it in small quantities — but the great age of the stained-glass window in Europe began in the twelfth century, with the building of the large Gothic cathedrals. New building techniques meant that walls no longer had to carry the whole weight of the roof, so they could contain far larger openings, and those openings were filled with glass.

LECTURER: Why go to such expense? People sometimes assume the windows were mainly decoration, or a way for the Church to display its wealth, and there's some truth in both ideas. But their main purpose was to present Bible stories to people who couldn't read — and at that time, that was most of the population.

LECTURER: The best-known example is probably Chartres Cathedral in France. The cathedral had to be rebuilt after a fire in 1194, and of the windows made for the new building, more than 150 survive today — which is extraordinary. The glass at Chartres is famous for one particular shade: a deep, glowing colour known as 'Chartres blue'. Glassmakers have been trying to reproduce it for centuries, not always successfully.

LECTURER: So, how was a window made? We're fortunate here, because a monk who wrote under the name Theophilus left detailed instructions in the early twelfth century. The first step was the design. This was drawn at full size — not on paper, which was rare and expensive, but on a large wooden table that had been covered with whitewash.

LECTURER: The colour of the glass wasn't painted on. It came from metal oxides, which were added while the glass was still molten. Cobalt, for instance, gave a blue colour, while copper could produce red or green.

LECTURER: The glass then had to be cut into pieces to fit the design. Today, of course, we'd use a diamond or a steel wheel, but medieval craftsmen didn't have those. Instead, they drew a hot iron across the glass to make it crack along the line they wanted, and then shaped the edges with a tool called a grozing iron.

LECTURER: Next, details such as faces, hands and the folds of clothing were painted onto the glass with a dark paint made from ground glass and iron oxide. The pieces were then fired in a kiln, so that the paint fused permanently with the surface. Finally, the pieces were fitted together with strips of lead, the joints were soldered, and the complete panel was fixed into an iron frame in the window opening.

LECTURER: Now, what happened to these windows later? Many were destroyed in wars or replaced when tastes changed. Chartres was lucky. At the start of the Second World War, its windows were carefully removed and stored in a safe place, and they were put back once the war was over.

LECTURER: The craft itself declined for several centuries, but it was revived in the nineteenth century, and in the twentieth century some of the most famous painters of the age, including Marc Chagall and Henri Matisse, designed stained-glass windows. They didn't usually cut the glass themselves — that was done by specialist workshops — but the designs were entirely theirs. So an art form that began in the twelfth century is still very much alive.

tasks.title: Questions 1–10 — Stained glass in medieval Europe
tasks.type: Complete the notes below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
tasks.instr: Notes tartibi = ma'ruza tartibi. "So, how was a window made?" va "Now, what happened ... later?" — bo'lim signallari.
why: "Their main purpose was to present Bible stories to people who couldn't read". Tuzoq: "decoration", "display its wealth" — "there's some truth", lekin asosiy emas.
"More than 150 survive today". Tuzoq: "a fire in 1194" — yil, derazalar soni emas.
"A deep, glowing colour known as 'Chartres blue'". "Blue" yolg'iz — to'liq nom emas.
"Not on paper ... but on a large wooden table that had been covered with whitewash". Tuzoq: "paper".
"It came from metal oxides, which were added while the glass was still molten". "Cobalt" va "copper" — misollar.
"They drew a hot iron across the glass". Tuzoq: "a diamond or a steel wheel" — bugungi usul.
"The pieces were then fired in a kiln".
"The pieces were fitted together with strips of lead". "Iron frame" — butun panel uchun, tuzoq.
"Its windows were carefully removed and stored in a safe place".
"Some of the most famous painters of the age, including Marc Chagall and Henri Matisse, designed stained-glass windows". Tuzoq: "specialist workshops" — ular shishani kesgan, loyihalamagan.
tasks.note: Doskada tuzoqlar ro'yxati: 1194 (yil) ↔ 150 (son); paper ↔ whitewash; diamond ↔ hot iron; iron frame ↔ lead. Band 7 o'quvchisi har birini tushuntira olishi kerak.

homework_intro: Bugun Section 4 da note completion'ni ishladik: avval notes'ning "skeleti", keyin har bo'shliq turi, keyin o'tish iboralari va tuzoqlar. Eng ko'p ball uch joyda yo'qoladi — birinchi eshitilgan raqam, zamon farqi (nowadays / in the past) va imlo.

Birinchi vazifa — shadowing: Workbook Track 7 audiosini skript bilan (Workbook, 57-bet) oching va "Cave paintings" qismini (birinchi 1,5 daqiqa) ma'ruzachi bilan bir vaqtda, bir xil tezlikda 3 marta o'qing. Uchinchisini ovozli xabar qilib yuboring. Audio va skript parchasi guruh chatida (ustoz dars oxirida yuboradi).

Ikkinchi vazifa — qayta hikoya: Student's Book, 45-betdagi notes'ga (javoblaringiz bilan) qarab, Aboriginal san'at haqidagi ma'ruzani 1,5–2 daqiqada o'z so'zlaringiz bilan aytib bering. Kamida 3 ta o'tish iborasi ishlating (Let's move on to..., So, how have things changed?).

Uchinchi vazifa — xatolar daftari va diktant: bugungi xato javoblarni sababi bilan yozing (raqam / tuzoq / so'z turi / imlo), keyin SB Track 19 ning oxirgi 1 daqiqasini ("So, how have things changed?" dan) tinglab, diktant qiling va skript bilan (SB, 153-bet; parcha guruh chatida) o'zingiz tekshiring. Xatolar sonini diktant ostiga yozing.
