kahoot.q: Which is true of IELTS Listening Section 4?
options: One speaker gives an academic talk with no break
Two students and a tutor discuss a research project
There is a pause after Question 5
An example is given at the start
kahoot.explain: Section 4 — bitta so'zlovchi, akademik mavzu, tanaffussiz. Misol faqat Section 1 da beriladi.

kahoot.q: What should you read FIRST in the preparation time?
options: The title and headings of the notes
Only Question 1, then wait for the audio
The last question on the page
kahoot.explain: Sarlavha va bo'lim nomlari ma'ruza rejasini beradi — adashsangiz ham qayerga qaytishni bilasiz.

kahoot.q: Gap: 'artist's palette found that is ___ old'. What type of answer?
kahoot.explain: 'that is ___ old' — yosh: 18,000 years.

kahoot.q: Gap: 'a range of ___'. The answer will probably be...
kahoot.explain: 'a range of' dan keyin ko'plik ot keladi: (musical) instruments.

kahoot.q: The talk starts with '60,000 years'; later a palette 'dating back 18,000 years'. Q6 answer?
kahoot.explain: 60,000 — umuman Aboriginal san'at yoshi. Palitra haqida — 18,000.

kahoot.q: Notes: 'tree sap or ___ added'. You hear 'Nowadays ... acrylic binder, but in the past ... bush honey'.
kahoot.explain: Notes o'tmishdagi binderlar haqida (tree sap bilan birga) — bush honey.

kahoot.q: Which phrase signals that the lecturer is starting a NEW section?
options: Let's move on to look at the materials.
In fact, most of this work is inside caves.
kahoot.explain: 'Let's move on to...' — yangi bo'lim signali: notes'da keyingi sarlavhaga o'ting.

kahoot.q: Notes say 'main function: ___'. The lecturer is most likely to say...
options: the key purpose of this art was...
the main function of this art was...
the main problem with this art was...
kahoot.explain: Notes'dagi so'z odatda paraphrase qilinadi: main function = key purpose.

kahoot.q: The lecturer says 'I would dispute this' after a theory. For 'Possibly believed to have ___' you write...
options: nothing, because the lecturer rejects the theory
kahoot.explain: Notes nazariya mazmunini so'raydi. Rad etish — javobni o'zgartirmaydi, keyingi fikrga signal.

kahoot.q: Limit: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER. Which answer breaks it?
kahoot.explain: Uch so'z. Raqam + bir so'z (18,000 years) — ruxsat etilgan.

kahoot.q: You miss a gap during the lecture. Best strategy?
options: Move on and follow the next heading
Wait for the speaker to repeat the answer
kahoot.explain: Audio qaytarilmaydi. To'xtasangiz keyingi javoblar ham o'tib ketadi — oxirida mantiqan taxmin qiling.

kahoot.q: WB notes: 'Big: minimum diameter = ___'. You hear 'at least four metres across'. Answer?
kahoot.explain: 'minimum' = 'at least', 'diameter' = 'across'. Javob — o'lchov: four / 4 metres.

kahoot.q: Rock paintings survived because rock is more ___ than bark.
kahoot.explain: Durable — chidamli, uzoq saqlanadigan.

kahoot.q: Tree sap was used as a ___ to hold the powder together.
kahoot.explain: Binder — kukunni bog'lab bo'yoqqa aylantiruvchi suyuqlik.

kahoot.q: Aboriginal art 'dates ___ 60,000 years'.
kahoot.explain: Date back (to) — …ga borib taqalmoq.

kahoot.q: Dot painting has 'taken ___' and now sells on a big scale.
kahoot.explain: Take off — birdan ommalashmoq. 'Take up' — boshlamoq (took up acrylic painting).

kahoot.q: Preparing ochre paints was ___ work — it took a lot of time.
kahoot.explain: Time-consuming — ko'p vaqt oladigan.

kahoot.q: Petroglyphs still have deep cultural ___ for descendants.
kahoot.explain: Cultural significance — madaniy ahamiyat. WB Q7 javobi.

kahoot.q: Abstract patterns are a ___ theme: they appear again and again.
kahoot.explain: Recurring — takrorlanuvchi.

kahoot.q: People who have lived in a place from the earliest times are...
kahoot.explain: Indigenous — tub, mahalliy aholi.

lessons.title: Mock test 1: Unit 1–4 dan keyin — natijalar tahlili (imtihon alohida 150 daqiqalik sessiyada)
lessons.grammar_topic: Mockdan keyingi tahlil darsi: imtihonning o'zi dars sonidan tashqaridagi alohida 150 daqiqalik sessiyada (JonyOS → Imtihonlar → Mock testlar, qat'iy rejim, faqat kompyuter; Listening ~30, Reading 60, Writing 60 daqiqa); bu darsda Listening va Reading natijasi savol turlari bo'yicha Unit 1–4 ga bog'lab tahlil qilinadi, Writing AI izohi 4 mezon bo'yicha ko'rib chiqiladi (diagnostika) va ikki haftalik reja yoziladi
lessons.vocab_topic: Xom ball va band, olti xato sababi, savol turi bo'yicha naqsh, unitga qaytish, Writing mezonlari, ikki haftalik reja
lessons.book_ref: JonyOS mock bazasi: JonyOS → Imtihonlar → Mock testlar (qat'iy rejim, faqat kompyuter). Mock — dars sonidan tashqaridagi alohida 150 daqiqalik sessiya: Listening ~30, Reading 60, Writing 60 daqiqa; Listening yozuvi bo'lmasa, skriptni examiner ovoz chiqarib o'qiydi. Examiner javoblar varaqasi har savol bo'yicha o'quvchining javobi, to'g'ri javob va mavzu belgisini ko'rsatadi; Listening va Reading bandi rasmiy xom ball — band jadvali bo'yicha avtomatik qo'yiladi. Writing'ni JonyOS AI examiner 4 IELTS mezoni bo'yicha baholaydi; examiner 48 soat ichida tekshiradi yoki o'zgartiradi, keyin natija e'lon qilinadi.
objectives: Mock sessiyasini tartib bilan o'tkazish (alohida kun, JonyOS → Imtihonlar → Mock testlar; qat'iy rejim, faqat kompyuter): xona va ekran tayyorligi, qoidalar, Listening (yozuv bo'lmasa — skriptni examiner o'qiydi), tugatgan o'quvchi bilan ishlash.
Mock (Listening ~30 + Reading 60 + Writing 60 = 150 daqiqa) dars sonidan tashqaridagi alohida sessiya ekanini, bu 120 daqiqalik dars esa faqat natijalar tahlili ekanini bilish.
O'z natijasini o'qish: xom ball, band va qaysi bo'lim o'rtachani pastga tortgani.
Har xato javobni olti sababdan bittasiga ajratish.
Xatolarni savol turi bo'yicha guruhlab, Unit 1–4 dagi qaysi darsga qaytish kerakligini aniqlash.
Maqsad bilan solishtirish (Mock 1: kamida 6.5 — Listening 26+, Academic Reading 27+ (40 dan), Writing 6.5; kurs oxiridagi yakuniy maqsad — 7.0) va ikki haftalik aniq reja yozish.
Writing natijasini o'qish: AI examiner 4 mezon bo'yicha qo'ygan ballar, inglizcha izoh va xatolar ro'yxati; eng past mezonni topish, 5 ta xatoni tuzatish va har mezonga bitta keyingi qadam yozish.
materials: Mock sessiyasi uchun: chop etilgan ism ro'yxati — kim qaysi kompyuterda o'tirgani va kim tugatgani belgilanadi.
Mock sessiyasi uchun: Listening skripti (yozuv bo'lmasa o'qiladi) — faqat sessiyani o'tkazayotgan examiner ekranida, o'quvchiga ko'rsatilmaydi.
Mock sessiyasi uchun: har stolda zaxira qog'oz va qalam — Listening paytida ism, raqam va sanalar qoralama qilinadi.

Mock sessiyasi uchun: doskada xona qoidalari (telefon sumkada, imtihon to'liq ekranda, ekrandan chiqish tizimda sanaladi) va qolgan vaqt. Tahlil darsi uchun: doskada Listening va Reading xom ball — band jadvallari (9.0 gacha, 2-mashq).
Tahlil darsi: har o'quvchiga "Olti sabab" jadvali va "Savol turi → Unit" xaritasi (quyidagi 3-mashq jadvali) chop etilgan holda.
Tahlil darsi: har o'quvchiga "Ikki haftalik reja" varaqasi — 6 qator, oxirida ustoz imzosi uchun joy.

Tahlil darsi: har o'quvchi o'z examiner javoblar varaqasini o'z ekranida (kompyuterda) yoki chop etilgan shaxsiy nusxada ko'radi. Proyektorda faqat to'g'ri javoblar va guruh statistikasi (qaysi savolda nechta xato) ko'rsatiladi — shaxsiy natijalar proyektorga chiqarilmaydi.
Tahlil darsi: har o'quvchining examiner tasdiqlagan Writing natijasi — 4 mezon bo'yicha ball, inglizcha izoh va grammatika/lug'at xatolari ro'yxati (o'z ekranida yoki chop etilgan nusxada).
timeline: Kirish: bugun — tahlil darsi

Avval tekshiring: mock alohida 150 daqiqalik sessiyada o'tkazilganmi va natijalar (Writing — examiner tasdig'idan keyin) e'lon qilinganmi? Bo'lmasa, bu darsni natija chiqqandan keyinga ko'chiring. Bugun faqat natija va tahlil. Mock — o'lchov, jazo emas; ballar ovoz chiqarib aytilmaydi, har kim o'z varaqasi bilan ishlaydi.
Natijani ochish

Har o'quvchi Listening va Reading xom ball va bandini, Writing ballarini (4 mezon) daftariga yozadi va Mock 1 maqsadi bilan solishtiradi: kamida 6.5 — Listening 26+, Reading 27+ (40 dan), Writing 6.5. Speaking bo'lmasa, overall band hisoblanmaydi.
Xom ball — band jadvali
Doskada ikkala jadval (9.0 gacha); jadval chegarasida bitta savol yarim bandni o'zgartirishi ko'rsatiladi (2-mashq).
Olti sabab
Har sababga bitta tanish misol (1-mashq); sabablar jadvali tarqatiladi.
Javoblar varaqasi: Listening
Har kim o'z varaqasini savol-savol o'qiydi, har xatoga sabab raqami va Section turi yoziladi. Proyektorda faqat to'g'ri javoblar va guruh statistikasi (qaysi savolda nechta xato).
Javoblar varaqasi: Reading
Passage bo'yicha ketma-ket; har xatoga sabab raqami va savol turi yoziladi. Bir passage'dagi ikkinchi turga vaqt yetmagani (kombinatsiya xatosi) alohida belgilanadi.
Savol turi → Unit xaritasi
Har tur va har sabab necha marta chiqqani sanaladi; xatolar savol turi bo'yicha guruhlanadi va Unit 1–4 dagi qaysi darsga qaytish kerakligi topiladi (3-mashq).
Writing feedback

Examiner tasdiqlagan AI natijasi: 4 mezon bo'yicha ball, inglizcha izoh, grammatika va lug'at xatolari; eng past mezon, 5 ta tuzatish, har mezonga bitta keyingi qadam (4-mashq). Bu natija — diagnostika: 32-darsdagi Mock 2 bilan solishtiriladi.
Ikki haftalik reja
Har kim eng katta ikki naqsh bo'yicha 6 qatorli reja yozadi, ostiga 4-mashqdagi Writing odatini qo'shadi; juftlik o'qib tekshiradi.
Xulosa va vazifa
Reja ustozga ko'rsatiladi va imzolanadi; uyga: xatolar daftari, eng zaif tur, Writing xatboshisi. Task 2 essayi va AI izohi saqlanadi (26–27- va 32-darslar uchun).

intro: Bu — Mock 1 dan keyingi TAHLIL darsi. Imtihonning o'zi dars sonidan tashqaridagi alohida sessiyada o'tadi; bu 120 daqiqada natijalar savol-savol va savol turi bo'yicha tahlil qilinadi, Writing izohi 4 mezon bo'yicha ko'rib chiqiladi va ikki haftalik reja yoziladi. Yangi mavzu yo'q — Unit 1–4 da o'rganilgan savol turlari kombinatsiyalarining imtihon sharoitidagi natijasi tahlil qilinadi.

Mock sessiyasi (dars sonidan tashqarida, alohida kun): examiner JonyOS → Imtihonlar → Mock testlar bo'limidan guruh uchun mockni ochadi, o'quvchilar qat'iy rejimda (faqat kompyuter, to'liq ekran) ishlaydi: Listening ~30, Reading 60, Writing 60 daqiqa — jami 150 daqiqa, bitta o'tirishda. Speaking — filial imkon bersa, boshqa kuni examiner bilan: har o'quvchiga 11–14 daqiqa, 4 mezon bo'yicha (Fluency and Coherence, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy, Pronunciation); imkon bo'lmasa, bu mockda Speaking yo'q va overall band hisoblanmaydi.
Sessiyada Listening yozuvi bo'lmasa, skriptni EXAMINER ovoz chiqarib o'qiydi: bir marta, tabiiy va bir tekis tezlikda, javob so'zlariga urg'u bermasdan. Skript faqat examiner ekranida turadi.

Natija ikki raqam: XOM BALL (40 dan nechta) va BAND. Listening va Reading jadvallari bir xil emas: 26 ta to'g'ri javob Listeningda 6.5, Academic Readingda 6.0. Jadval chegarasida bitta savol yarim bandni o'zgartiradi (Reading 26 ta = 6.0, 27 ta = 6.5; Listening 29 ta = 6.5, 30 ta = 7.0) — bo'sh javob qoldirmang.

Olti sabab: 1) eshitmadim / topa olmadim; 2) eshitdim, lekin xato yozdim (imlo, ko'plik, raqam); 3) vaqt yetmadi; 4) savol turini noto'g'ri tushundim (so'z limiti, NOT GIVEN va FALSE farqi, TWO letters); 5) taxmin qildim; 6) bilardim, lekin javobni o'zgartirdim.

7.0 da tahlil savol turi, kombinatsiya va Writing mezoni bo'yicha olib boriladi. Har xatoning yonida savol turi yoziladi va "Savol turi → Unit" xaritasidan qaysi darsga qaytish kerakligi topiladi. Masalan, Matching headings da 3 ta xato — Unit 2 (3-dars) readinglari va Practice 1–3 qayta ishlanadi. Writing'da esa eng past mezon (TA/TR, CC, LR yoki GRA) topiladi va kursning Writing blokiga (Task 1 — 18–24-darslar, Task 2 — 25–31-darslar) bog'lanadi.
Kombinatsiya xatosini alohida belgilang: agar bir passage'da ikkinchi savol turiga vaqt yetmagan bo'lsa (3-sabab), muammo tur emas — xarita usuli va vaqt taqsimoti.

Maqsad (Mock 1): kamida 6.5 — Listening 26+, Academic Reading 27+ (40 dan), Writing 6.5: har task'da 4 mezon o'rtachasi kamida 6.5 (masalan 7, 7, 6, 6), birorta mezon 6 dan past emas. Kurs oxiridagi yakuniy maqsad (Mock 2, 32-dars): 7.0 — Listening 30+, Reading 30+, Writing 7.0. Maqsaddan past bo'lim — ikki haftalik rejaning birinchi qatori. Writing bloki kursda 18–31-darslarda o'tiladi, shuning uchun bugungi Writing natijasi — DIAGNOSTIKA: eng past mezon aniqlanadi va 32-darsdagi Mock 2 natijasi bilan solishtiriladi.

WRITING natijasi: JonyOS AI examiner Writing'ni 4 IELTS mezoni bo'yicha baholaydi — Task Achievement (Task 1) / Task Response (Task 2), Coherence and Cohesion, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy; Task 2 ikki barobar hisoblanadi. U inglizcha examiner izohi va grammatika/lug'at xatolari ro'yxatini beradi. Examiner (AI emas — maktab examineri) 48 soat ichida bahoni tekshiradi yoki o'zgartiradi, shundan keyin natija e'lon qilinadi. Har mezonga faqat butun ball qo'yiladi; .5 faqat o'rtachada — task va Writing bandida chiqadi.

Sessiya qoidasi: telefon sumkada, stolda emas. Qat'iy rejimda imtihon to'liq ekranda ishlanadi; ekrandan chiqib boshqa oynaga o'tish tizimda sanaladi va takrorlansa, o'quvchi imtihondan chetlatiladi. Savol bo'lsa qo'l ko'tariladi.
formulas: Bo'sh reja ishlamaydi; uyda 3 daqiqa zaxira bilan ishlanadi
Writing: eng past mezon + 5 ta tuzatish
Writing bandini ko'taradigan bitta aniq odat
presentation: To'liq mock bitta darsga sig'adimi?

Yo'q. Mock — dars sonidan tashqaridagi alohida 150 daqiqalik sessiya (JonyOS → Imtihonlar → Mock testlar; qat'iy rejim, faqat kompyuter): Listening ~30, Reading 60, Writing 60 daqiqa. Speaking — filial imkon bersa, boshqa kuni examiner bilan (har o'quvchiga 11–14 daqiqa, 4 mezon). Bu 120 daqiqalik dars — faqat natijalar tahlili.
Mock nega kerak, darslar yetmaydimi?
Darsda har tur alohida ishlanadi; mockda hammasi aralash va vaqt bilan. Kombinatsiya ko'nikmasi faqat shu yerda o'lchanadi.
Ballim past chiqdi. Nima qilaman?
Avval sabablarni sanang. Ko'pincha 2-sabab (imlo, raqam) — bu eng tez tuzaladigan xato.
Xatolarim har xil turlarda. Qayerdan boshlayman?
Eng ko'p xato bo'lgan ikki turdan. Xaritadan ularning darsini toping.
Listening skriptini keyin berasizmi?
Yo'q. Tahlil faqat javoblar varaqasi orqali, skript o'quvchiga berilmaydi.
Vaqt yetmadi — bu qaysi sabab?
3-sabab. Davosi — xarita usuli va har passage uchun 20 daqiqa qoidasi (Unit 1).
Writingni ham tahlil qilamizmi?

Ha, bugun 20 daqiqa (4-mashq). Writing'ni JonyOS AI examiner 4 IELTS mezoni bo'yicha baholaydi (TA/TR, CC, LR, GRA; Task 2 ikki barobar), inglizcha izoh va grammatika/lug'at xatolari ro'yxatini beradi; examiner 48 soat ichida tekshiradi yoki o'zgartiradi, keyin natija e'lon qilinadi. Writing bloki 18–31-darslarda — bugungi natija diagnostika, 32-darsdagi Mock 2 bilan solishtiriladi.
notes: Maktab qarori: mock imtihoni — dars sonidan tashqaridagi ALOHIDA 150 daqiqalik sessiya (JonyOS → Imtihonlar → Mock testlar; qat'iy rejim, faqat kompyuter): Listening ~30, Reading 60, Writing 60 daqiqa. Speaking — filial imkon bersa, boshqa kuni examiner bilan (har o'quvchiga 11–14 daqiqa, 4 mezon). Writing natijasi examiner tekshirgandan keyin (48 soat ichida) chiqadi, shuning uchun bu 120 daqiqalik tahlil darsini natijalar e'lon qilingandan KEYIN o'tkazing. Dars boshida belgilang: mock o'tkazilganmi? natijalar e'lon qilinganmi?
Natijalarni ochishdan oldin o'quvchilarga eslating: mock — o'lchov, jazo emas. Maqsad — keyingi ikki haftada qaysi darsga qaytishni bilish.
Tahlil qismida ustoz ham guruh bo'yicha umumiy naqshni yozib oladi: agar guruhning yarmi bitta turda xato qilgan bo'lsa, o'sha unit keyingi haftada sinfda qayta ko'riladi.
Bu kurs o'rtasidagi mock: natija Unit 5–8 ni boshlashdan oldin qaysi turlarni mustahkamlash kerakligini ko'rsatadi.

Sessiya kuni tartibi (dars timeline'iga kirmaydi): kompyuterlar tekshiriladi, mock JonyOS → Imtihonlar → Mock testlar bo'limidan ochiladi, ism ro'yxati va zaxira qog'oz tarqatiladi; telefon sumkaga, qat'iy rejim qoidalari ovoz chiqarib aytiladi. class_ex.title: 4-mashq: Writing — AI examiner izohi bo'yicha tahlil
class_ex.instr: Har o'quvchi examiner tasdiqlagan Writing natijasini ochadi: 4 mezon bo'yicha ball, inglizcha examiner izohi va grammatika/lug'at xatolari ro'yxati. Besh qadamni daftarda bajaring. O'ng ustunda namuna (Aziz) — ko'chirmang, o'z natijangiz bilan ishlang.
items: 1-qadam. Task 1 va Task 2 uchun 4 mezon bo'yicha ballaringizni yozing: Task Achievement (Task 1) / Task Response (Task 2), Coherence and Cohesion, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy. Har task o'rtachasini maqsad (6.5) bilan solishtiring.
2-qadam. Eng past mezonni belgilang. Task 2 ikki barobar hisoblanishini eslang: qaysi task'dagi past ball Writing bandini ko'proq tushirgan?
3-qadam. Inglizcha izohdan eng muhim BITTA gapni toping va o'zbekchaga o'giring: examiner nimani so'rayapti?
4-qadam. Xatolar ro'yxatidan 5 ta xatoni tanlang: to'g'ri shaklini yozing va turini belgilang (grammatika yoki lug'at).
5-qadam. Har mezon uchun bitta "keyingi qadam" yozing; eng past mezonga — eng aniq odat va Writing blokidagi mos dars.
answers: Aziz. Task 1: TA 6, CC 7, LR 7, GRA 6 (o'rtacha 6.5). Task 2: TR 5, CC 6, LR 7, GRA 6 (o'rtacha 6.0).

Eng past — Task 2 dagi TR 5. Task 2 ikki barobar og'ir, shuning uchun aynan shu mezon Writing bandini eng ko'p pastga tortgan. Task 1 maqsadda (6.5), Task 2 maqsaddan past (6.0). Writing bandi taxminan: (6.5 + 2 × 6.0) ÷ 3 ≈ 6.2 → 6.0 — maqsad (6.5) dan past.

"Your position is not consistent: you agree with the statement in the introduction but argue the opposite in the conclusion, and your main ideas are listed rather than developed." → Pozitsiyangiz izchil emas: kirishda fikrga qo'shilasiz, xulosada esa aksini yozasiz; asosiy g'oyalar rivojlantirilmagan, faqat sanab o'tilgan (TR).

"In 2010 the number of visitors has increased sharply" → "In 2010 the number of visitors increased sharply" (grammatika: aniq o'tgan vaqt — past simple); "people who lives in cities" → "people who live in cities" (grammatika: ega-kesim moslashuvi); "a negative affect on health" → "a negative effect on health" (lug'at: affect — fe'l, effect — ot); "scientists make research" → "scientists do (carry out) research" (lug'at: kollokatsiya); "This essay will discuss about both views" → "This essay will discuss both views" (grammatika: discuss dan keyin predlog kelmaydi).

TR: reja tuzishda pozitsiyamni bitta gap qilib yozaman va kirish, har body va xulosani shu gap bilan solishtiraman (25-, 28-, 30-darslar); har asosiy g'oyani sanab o'tmay, tushuntirish va misol bilan rivojlantiraman (27-, 29-darslar). CC: har xatboshida bitta markaziy g'oya (29-dars). LR: kuchli tomon — kollokatsiyalar daftarini davom ettiraman. GRA: topshirishdan oldin 3 daqiqa zamon va ega-kesim moslashuvini tekshiraman.
why: Har mezonga faqat BUTUN ball qo'yiladi (masalan 6 yoki 7); .5 faqat o'rtachada chiqadi: 6, 7, 7, 6 → 6.5.
Task 2 ikki barobar hisoblanadi: Task 2 dagi 1 ball farq Writing bandiga Task 1 dagiga qaraganda ko'proq ta'sir qiladi.
Izoh inglizcha — tushunmagan so'zni ustozdan so'rang. Izohdan bitta aniq harakat chiqishi kerak.
Tuzatilgan xato — keyingi ishda takrorlanmaydigan xato. Grammatika xatolari GRA ga; so'z tanlash, kollokatsiya va so'z yasalishi xatolari LR ga tegishli.

Odat kichik va aniq bo'lsin: "essayni yaxshilayman" emas, "pozitsiyamni bitta gapda yozib, uch joyda solishtiraman". Writing bloki (Task 1 — 18–24, Task 2 — 25–31-darslar) aynan shu mezonlarni o'rgatadi.
class_ex.note: Writing'ni JonyOS AI examiner 4 mezon bo'yicha baholaydi (Task 2 ikki barobar hisoblanadi), inglizcha izoh va xatolar ro'yxatini beradi; examiner 48 soat ichida tekshiradi yoki o'zgartiradi, natija shundan keyin e'lon qilinadi. Bu darsda faqat tasdiqlangan natija bilan ishlanadi. 7.0 da Writing bloki 18–31-darslarda o'tiladi, shuning uchun bu natija — DIAGNOSTIKA: 32-darsdagi Mock 2 bilan solishtiriladi. Task 2 essayi va AI izohi saqlanadi — 26–27-darslarda shu essay bilan ishlanadi. Ballni sinfda ovoz chiqarib aytmang.

homework_intro: Mock sessiyasida to'liq imtihonni topshirdingiz, bugun sinfda javoblar varaqasini savol-savol o'qidik va Writing izohini ko'rdik. Uyda xuddi shu ishni HAMMA xato bo'yicha oxirigacha qilasiz.

Birinchi vazifa — xatolar daftari: har xato uchun oltita ustun — savol raqami, sizning javobingiz, to'g'ri javob, savol turi, sabab raqami va qaytiladigan dars. Oxirida har sabab va har tur necha marta chiqqanini sanang.
Ikkinchi vazifa — ikki haftalik reja: eng katta ikki naqsh bo'yicha 6 qator; har qatorda qaysi dars, qancha mashq, qaysi kun va kim tekshiradi.

Uchinchi vazifa — eng zaif savol turining darsiga qayting. Reading turi bo'lsa — o'sha darsdagi Practice 1–3 ni vaqt bilan qayta ishlang, har javob yonida isbot gap bo'lsin. Listening turi bo'lsa — o'sha darsning Workbook treki va Jony Academy mashqini imtihon rejimida (audio BIR MARTA) qayta bajaring va har xatoga sabab raqamini yozing.

To'rtinchi vazifa — Writing: AI izohidagi eng past mezon bo'yicha Task 2 dan bitta body xatboshini qayta yozing; xatolar ro'yxatidan yana 5 ta xatoni tuzating. Task 2 essayingiz va AI izohini saqlang: 26–27-darslarda shu essay bilan ishlaysiz, 32-darsda Mock 2 natijasi bilan solishtiriladi.

intro: Band 7 darajasida Passage 2 odatda uch savol turini birlashtiradi. Bugungi kombinatsiya (SB va WB da bir xil): Matching information (1–5), Sentence completion (6–9) va Matching features (10–13). Har turning TARTIB qoidasi har xil — buni bilish 3–4 daqiqa tejaydi.

Matching information — "Which paragraph contains the following information?". Savollar matn tartibida EMAS, 7 xatboshidan faqat 5 tasi kerak bo'lishi mumkin (ba'zan bitta harf ikki marta — "NB You may use any letter more than once"). Bu sarlavha emas: xatboshining ASOSIY g'oyasi emas, uning ichidagi bitta gap yoki TAFSILOT so'raladi.

Savoldagi birinchi so'z — ma'lumot TURI: a comparison (solishtirish), a reference to / mention of (tilga olish), evidence for (dalil), a reason (sabab), an example (misol), a description (tasvir), an explanation (izoh). Masalan, SB 1-savol — "a comparison of a range of physical features": faqat jismoniy belgilar tilga olingan joy emas, IKKI tur SOLISHTIRILGAN joy kerak (D: "Neanderthals were particularly robust ... Homo sapiens, on the other hand, had longer forearms").

Sentence completion — gaplar DOIM matn tartibida. Kalit so'z (ism yoki ko'zga tashlanadigan aniq so'z: Petraglia, sewing, territorial, language and thought) bilan joyni topasiz, javobni aynan ko'chirasiz. NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS: "dating of the sediment layers" (5 so'z) — 0 ball. Eng xavfsiz yo'l — matndan uzluksiz bo'lak olish: "sediment layers" (gap grammatik to'g'ri davom etadi). Kitob kaliti "dating sediment layers" ni ham qabul qiladi, lekin so'zlarni o'rtadan tashlab ketishni odat qilmang.

Matching features — ismlar (tadqiqotchilar, usullar, joylar) matnda qutidagi TARTIBDA keladi, lekin gaplar (10–13) aralash. Bitta ism bir necha xatboshida uchrashi mumkin: Stringer SB da C, D, F, G xatboshilarida gapiradi. Shuning uchun HAR bir uchragan joyni belgilang. "None of the above" (WB, D) — gapni hech kim aytmagan bo'lsa tanlanadi; bu Band 7 ning sevimli tuzog'i.

Tavsiya etilgan tartib (7.0): 1) 1–2 daqiqa xarita: uchala guruhni ko'rib chiqing, ismlarni matnda tagiga chizing. 2) Sentence completion — tartib bilan, matnni birinchi marta o'qiyotganda. 3) Matching features — belgilangan ismlar atrofini o'qing. 4) Matching information — oxirida: endi siz matnni bilasiz va har xatbosh nima haqida ekanini eslaysiz. Kitob maslahati (A dan boshlab har xatboshini savollar bilan solishtirish) ham ishlaydi — lekin u sekinroq.

Vaqt: Passage 2 ga 20 daqiqa. Taxminan: xarita — 2, sentence completion — 5, features — 5, matching information — 6, tekshirish va transfer — 2 daqiqa. Matching information'da 2 daqiqadan ko'p qolib ketsangiz, taxmin yozib keyingi savolga o'ting.
formulas: Xarita: uch guruhni ko'rish, ismlarni matnda belgilash
Petraglia (B), Stringer (C, D, F, G), Spikins (F)
Matnni bir marta o'qib ikki ish
Features: ism atrofidagi iqtibosni gap bilan solishtirish
"no such division of labour" = no evidence ... allocated tasks
Kim aytgani muhim, kim haqida emas
Mavzu so'zi yetmaydi — tur ham mos bo'lsin
Harfni tanlashdan oldin isbot gapni topish
ill fortune → "in the wrong place at the wrong time" (G)
Mayda xatolar Band 7 ni olib qo'yadi
presentation: Matching information'ni nega oxirida qilamiz?
Chunki savollar tartibsiz va butun matnni qamraydi. Sentence completion va features'ni qilgach, siz matnni bilasiz — javob joyini eslash osonlashadi.
Savoldagi so'z xatboshida bor. Demak javobmi?
Shart emas. Ma'lumot TURI ham mos bo'lishi kerak: "reference to the FINAL location" — oxirgi boshpana (C: southern Iberia), A dagi umumiy yashash joylari emas.
Bitta xatboshi ikki savolga javob bo'la oladimi?
Ha, agar ko'rsatmada "NB You may use any letter more than once" bo'lsa. Bo'lmasa ham, ishlatilmagan xatboshilar bo'lishi normal.
Features'da ism ikki xatboshida chiqdi. Qaysi biri?
Ikkalasini ham o'qing. SB 13-savol: Stringer C da (refugia) va G da (climate fluctuation) gapiradi — gapga C dagi iqtibos mos.
"None of the above" ni qachon tanlayman?
Gapdagi da'voni hech bir olim aytmaganda. WB 11: Richmond "carry MORE at one time" deydi, "easier to carry HEAVY objects" emas — javob D.
NMT3W da "of the" ni tashlab yuborsam bo'ladimi?

Buni odat qilmang. Eng xavfsiz yo'l — matndan uzluksiz bo'lak olish: "sediment layers". "(dating) sediment layers" ham kitob kalitida qabul qilingan, lekin bu bitta istisno, qoida emas: so'zlarni o'rtadan tashlab ketmang, matn so'zlarini o'zgartirmang va yangi so'z qo'shmang.
notes: 6.0 kursida Matching information'ni ko'rgansiz (10-dars: Matching information + Matching features + Summary completion; 14-darsda esa Matching headings + Matching features + Sentence completion). Format o'sha: 7 xatbosh (A–G), 5 ta savol. 7.0 dagi farq — ma'lumot turi nozikroq (comparison, reference, mention, evidence for), paraphrase Band 7 darajasida va kombinatsiya yangi: Summary completion o'rniga Sentence completion (NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS). Headings bilan farqni doskada eslating: heading = butun xatboshining asosiy g'oyasi, information = bitta gap (tafsilot).
SB matnida har savoldan keyin so'rang: "Ma'lumot turi nima? Isbot gap qaysi?" — o'quvchi gapni ovoz chiqarib o'qisin. Kalitdagi izohlar (sb 175–176) aynan shu gaplarni beradi.

Kuchli o'quvchilarga: SB da ishlatilmagan xatboshilar (B, F) nega hech bir savolga mos emasligini isbotlash; WB da E xatboshi nega 4-savol emas (E — Lucy haqidagi shubhani yo'qotadi, D — vaqtni qayta ko'rib chiqishga majbur qiladi).

class_ex.title: Ma'lumot turi: savol nimani so'rayapti?
class_ex.instr: Ustoz qisqa parchani o'qiydi. O'quvchilar qaysi savol turiga mos kelishini aytadi: A a comparison, B a reason, C an example, D a reference to a future plan, E evidence for a claim. Har parcha — bitta javob.
items: "Their skulls were larger than ours, but their foreheads were lower and their chins far less pronounced."
"The villagers abandoned the site because the river had changed its course and the fields could no longer be irrigated."
"The team intends to return next spring with ground-penetrating radar to search the eastern slope."
"Burnt seeds found in the hearth show that the inhabitants were already growing barley."
"Many small objects travelled surprisingly far: a shell necklace from the Red Sea, for instance, was found in a cave 600 kilometres inland."
why: "larger than ours ... but ... lower ... far less" — ikki narsa solishtirilyapti (comparison). SB 1-savolga o'xshaydi.
"because" — sabab (reason). Mavzu so'zi (river, fields) emas, gapning VAZIFASI muhim.
"intends to return next spring" — kelajak rejasi. Bunday gaplar ko'pincha xatboshi oxirida keladi.
"show that" — dalil (evidence): topilma da'voni isbotlaydi. SB 3-savol ham "evidence for" turida.
"for instance" — misol (example). SB 2-savol: shell beads — savdo qilingan buyumlarga misol.
class_ex.note: Mashqdan keyin doskaga yozing: comparison — but / whereas / on the other hand; reason — because / due to / led to; evidence — show / suggest / indicate; example — for instance / such as. Bu signal so'zlar matching information'da joyni tez topishga yordam beradi.

class_ex.title: Inkor affikslari: matndagi so'zlar (SB Vocabulary, 57-bet asosida)
class_ex.instr: Qavsdagi so'zga prefiks yoki suffiks qo'shib gapni to'ldiring. Bu so'zlar SB va WB matnlarida uchraydi — o'qishda ularni tanish Band 7 uchun muhim.
items: 1 After the eruption, the simple tools gradually ___ from the record. (appear)
2 The desert was so ___ that no one could live there for long. (hospitable)
3 The team realised they had ___ their efforts on the wrong site. (direct)
4 During ___ periods, the climate changed from warm to cold very quickly. (stable)
5 Without a proper map, digging in random places proved ___. (practical)
6 The broken pots looked ___, but they told us a lot about daily life. (worth)
why: dis- + appear; o'tgan zamon -ed ("gradually" + fe'l). SB matnida: "eventually disappear completely".
in- + hospitable. "so ___ that" — sifat kerak. SB C xatboshida: "a cold, inhospitable, dry phase".
mis- (noto'g'ri) + direct + -ed: "They misdirected their energies" (SB, E xatbosh).
un- + stable. G xatboshida: "a phase of very unstable climate".
im- + practical (p harfidan oldin im-). "proved" dan keyin sifat.
-less suffiksi inkor ma'nosini beradi: worth → worthless. "but they told us a lot" — qarama-qarshilik.
class_ex.note: Doskada jadval: un- (unstable), in-/im-/il-/ir- (inhospitable, impractical, illogical, irreplaceable), dis- (disappear), mis- (misdirect), non- (non-existent), -less (worthless). Sentence completion'da matndagi shaklni AYNAN ko'chirish shart — affiks tushib qolsa, ma'no teskari bo'ladi.

readings.title: Practice 1: Reading the bones
readings.qtype: Matching information (1–5) + Sentence completion (6–9) + Matching features (10–13)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2 darajasi, Band 7)
text: How laboratory science has transformed what archaeologists can learn from a handful of ancient remains

A For most of its history, archaeology depended on what could be seen with the naked eye. A skeleton could reveal roughly how old a person had been at death, whether they had suffered serious injuries and perhaps whether they had done heavy physical work. Beyond that, researchers were largely reduced to educated guesswork. Over the past seventy years, however, a series of laboratory techniques has turned the bones and teeth of ancient people into remarkably detailed archives. Today, a single tooth can tell specialists when its owner lived, who their relatives were and even where they spent their childhood.

B The first of these revolutions came in the late 1940s, when the American chemist Willard Libby developed radiocarbon dating, work for which he later received a Nobel Prize. All living things absorb carbon from their environment, including a tiny amount of a radioactive form known as carbon-14. When an organism dies, it stops taking in carbon, and the carbon-14 it contains begins to decay at a steady, known rate: roughly half of it disappears every 5,700 years. By measuring how much remains, scientists can calculate how long ago the plant or animal died. Before this method existed, dates for prehistoric sites were often little more than informed estimates, and some later turned out to be wrong by thousands of years.

C The technique does, however, have its limits. After about 50,000 years, so little carbon-14 is left that it can no longer be measured reliably, which means that the method cannot be applied to the oldest human fossils. Early results were also distorted by the fact that the amount of carbon-14 in the atmosphere has not been constant over time. Researchers eventually overcame this problem by comparing radiocarbon results with the annual growth rings of very old trees, producing calibration curves that are still being refined today.

D A second revolution began in the 1980s, when scientists first managed to extract fragments of genetic material from ancient remains. Early attempts were frustrated by contamination: DNA from the researchers themselves, or from bacteria in the soil, could easily be mistaken for ancient material. It took decades of work in specially cleaned laboratories before reliable results emerged. In 2010, the Swedish geneticist Svante Pääbo and his colleagues published a draft of the Neanderthal genome, and in 2022 he was awarded the Nobel Prize for this work. One of the most striking findings was that many people living today carry a small proportion of Neanderthal DNA, evidence that the two populations had children together.

E Ancient DNA has also revealed populations that left almost no other trace. In the same year, genetic analysis of a tiny finger bone from Denisova Cave in Siberia showed that it belonged to a group of humans previously unknown to science, now called the Denisovans. Remarkably, this identification was made from genetic evidence alone, since the handful of bones recovered were far too small to tell researchers what these people had looked like.

F A third method, isotope analysis, examines different forms of chemical elements that become locked into bones and teeth. Because tooth enamel forms in childhood and does not change afterwards, the strontium it contains reflects the local rocks and water of the place where a person grew up. If these values do not match the area in which the person was buried, he or she almost certainly moved there later in life. Other isotopes, of carbon and nitrogen, reveal whether a person's diet was based mainly on plants, meat or seafood.

G Taken together, these techniques have changed the kind of questions archaeologists ask. Instead of focusing mainly on objects and buildings, many now investigate the movements, family relationships and diets of individual people. Some specialists warn, however, that laboratory results are only as good as the excavations that supply the samples, and that careful fieldwork remains essential. Others point out that most of these methods are expensive and involve destroying part of a precious bone, so museums must think carefully before deciding which remains can be tested.

readings.title: Practice 2: Digging with care
readings.qtype: Matching information (1–5) + Sentence completion (6–9) + Matching features (10–13)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2 darajasi, Band 7)
text: How archaeology learned that the way you dig matters as much as what you find

A Every excavation is, in a sense, an act of destruction. Once soil has been removed from a site, it can never be put back in exactly the same order, and any information that was not recorded at the time is lost for ever. Modern archaeologists therefore treat the layers of a site much as a historian treats the pages of a document. This careful attitude, however, developed only gradually, and the story of how it emerged is closely linked to a handful of remarkable individuals.

B In the early 1870s, the German businessman Heinrich Schliemann began digging at Hisarlik, a large mound in north-west Turkey that he was convinced was the site of Homer's Troy. Impatient to reach the city of legend, which he assumed lay near the bottom, he ordered his workers to cut an enormous trench straight through the mound. In doing so, he destroyed a great deal of evidence from the upper levels, including, as later scholars realised, parts of the very layers he was searching for.

C In 1873 Schliemann announced the discovery of a spectacular collection of gold and jewellery, which he named 'Priam's Treasure' after the king of Troy in Homer's poem. He smuggled the objects out of the Ottoman Empire, and photographs of his wife wearing some of the jewellery made him famous across Europe. Later research, however, showed that the treasure came from a level roughly a thousand years older than the period traditionally associated with the Trojan War. Nevertheless, his work proved that the ancient city was real, and his later seasons, carried out with the help of a trained architect, were considerably more careful.

D A very different approach was taken in England by Augustus Pitt-Rivers, a retired army general. As a young officer, he had studied the development of firearms and had become fascinated by the way designs changed gradually over time, an interest that led him to arrange ordinary objects in sequences. When he inherited a large estate in southern England in 1880, he spent almost twenty years excavating the sites on his land. He insisted that the exact position of every find be recorded, including broken pottery and animal bones, and he published detailed reports at his own expense. In 1882 he also became Britain's first Inspector of Ancient Monuments.

E In the twentieth century, Mortimer Wheeler developed these ideas further. At sites such as Maiden Castle in southern England, he divided the ground into a grid of square pits separated by narrow walls of undisturbed earth. These walls allowed diggers to see and draw the sequence of soil layers in section while the excavation continued around them. Between 1944 and 1948 Wheeler led archaeological work in India, where he trained a generation of local archaeologists in his methods. In the 1950s he also became a familiar face on British television, helping to make archaeology a popular subject.

F Meanwhile, in East Africa, Mary Leakey was demonstrating how patient excavation could transform our understanding of human origins. In 1959, at Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania, she found a skull around 1.75 million years old. Almost twenty years later, at Laetoli, her team uncovered a trail of footprints left by early humans some 3.6 million years ago. The prints had been made in wet volcanic ash, which hardened soon afterwards and was then buried, preserving them in extraordinary detail. They offered clear evidence that our ancestors walked upright long before their brains began to grow larger.

G Today, the lessons of these pioneers are built into professional practice. Many archaeologists now investigate sites without digging at all, using methods such as ground-penetrating radar. When excavation is necessary, it is common to leave part of a site untouched deliberately, on the assumption that future researchers will have techniques that are not yet available. In this sense, the most careful archaeologists are working not only for the present but also for generations who have not yet been born.

readings.title: Practice 3 (uyga): The land beneath the North Sea
readings.qtype: Matching information (1–5) + Sentence completion (6–9) + Matching features (10–13)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2 darajasi, Band 7), uy vazifasi
text: Fishermen, geophysicists and amateur collectors are slowly bringing a lost prehistoric landscape back to life

A Today the southern North Sea is a shallow, busy stretch of water crossed by ferries, fishing boats and cargo ships. Yet for thousands of years after the peak of the last Ice Age, much of it was dry land, connecting what is now Britain to the rest of Europe. In the late 1990s, the British archaeologist Bryony Coles gave this vanished territory a name: Doggerland, after the Dogger Bank, a large sandbank in the middle of the sea. The name caught on, and with it came a growing realisation that one of the most important landscapes of prehistoric Europe lies beneath the waves.

B The first clues came not from scientists but from fishing crews. For more than a century, trawlers working the North Sea have hauled up the bones and teeth of mammoths, woolly rhinoceroses and other animals in their nets. In 1931, the crew of one trawler brought up a lump of peat that, when broken open, contained a carefully shaped barbed point made of antler. At the time, few people could explain how a hunting weapon had ended up on the seabed, but it was later dated to the end of the last Ice Age, when the area was open land.

C The land disappeared gradually. At the height of the Ice Age, so much water was locked up in ice sheets that sea levels were far lower than today. As the climate warmed and the ice melted, the sea rose and slowly swallowed the lowest ground, turning hills into islands. By around 8,000 years ago, Britain had become an island. At about the same time, an enormous underwater landslide off the coast of Norway, known as the Storegga Slide, sent a tsunami across the region, and many researchers believe it may have struck what remained of Doggerland with devastating force.

D Studying a landscape buried under sediment and tens of metres of water might seem impossible, but researchers have found an ingenious solution. Oil and gas companies have spent decades carrying out seismic surveys of the North Sea, sending sound waves into the seabed to locate fuel reserves. Geophysicists realised that the same data could be reprocessed to reveal the ancient surface beneath. Using it, they have mapped a network of long-buried rivers, lakes, marshes and coastlines, allowing archaeologists to predict where people were most likely to have lived.

E Some of the most surprising finds, however, have been made on land. Along parts of the Dutch coast, huge quantities of sand have been dredged from the seabed to strengthen beaches and build new land for ports. Amateur collectors who search these artificial beaches regularly pick up worked flints, bone tools and animal remains that originally came from Doggerland. In 2009, researchers announced that a fragment of a Neanderthal skull had been recovered from such material, making it one of the few traces of that species ever found beneath the North Sea.

F From all this evidence, a picture of life in Doggerland is beginning to emerge. Far from being a simple bridge between two regions, it seems to have been a rich environment of wetlands, forests and estuaries. Its inhabitants survived by hunting deer and wild boar, catching fish and birds, and gathering wild plants. As the water crept inland generation after generation, however, these communities would have been forced to abandon their hunting grounds and move to higher ground, a process that may have taken place within the memory of a single lifetime in the lowest areas.

G Doggerland now faces a new and very modern challenge. The North Sea is one of the world's busiest areas for offshore wind farms, and building foundations and laying cables can damage buried archaeological layers. At the same time, companies are required to survey the seabed before construction begins, and these surveys are producing valuable new data for researchers. Many scientists also argue that the story of a landscape lost to rising seas has obvious lessons for coastal communities today.
glossary: trawler — trol kemasi (to'r bilan baliq ovlovchi kema)
barbed point — tishli (ilgakli) uch, nayza uchi
seismic survey — seysmik tadqiqot (tovush to'lqinlari bilan yer ostini o'rganish)
dredge — dengiz tubidan qum/loy qazib olmoq

forced to abandon their hunting grounds and move to higher ground
the origin of a name
gave this vanished territory a name: Doggerland, after the Dogger Bank
a sudden natural disaster
an enormous underwater landslide ... sent a tsunami

found by chance ... later dated
a lump of peat ... later dated to the end of the last Ice Age
collected for commercial purposes
Oil and gas companies ... to locate fuel reserves
a species other than Homo sapiens
a fragment of a Neanderthal skull

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Matching information — paragraphs A–G
tasks.instr: Which paragraph contains the following information? Avval har savoldagi MA'LUMOT TURINI (comparison, reference, mention, reason, example...) va mavzusini tagiga chizing. Savollar matn tartibida EMAS; ba'zi xatboshilar ishlatilmaydi. 7 daqiqa.
items: 1 reference to people being forced to leave the places where they lived
2 an explanation of where a name came from
3 mention of a sudden natural disaster
4 reference to an activity that both endangers and helps research
5 an example of an unexpected object that was later dated scientifically
why: "These communities would have been forced to abandon their hunting grounds and move to higher ground".
"Doggerland, after the Dogger Bank, a large sandbank in the middle of the sea".
"An enormous underwater landslide ... sent a tsunami across the region".
Shamol elektr stansiyalari: "can damage buried archaeological layers" + "surveys are producing valuable new data".
1931 yilgi antler nayza uchi: "few people could explain ... later dated to the end of the last Ice Age".
tasks.note: 3-savol tuzog'i: C boshidagi dengiz sathining ko'tarilishi — sekin jarayon ("gradually"), sudden emas. Sudden = landslide / tsunami.

tasks.title: Questions 6–9
tasks.type: Complete the sentences. Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage for each answer.
tasks.instr: Complete the sentences below. Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage for each answer. Gaplar matn tartibida; javobni aynan ko'chiring va gapga qo'yib qayta o'qing.
items: 6 During the Ice Age, sea levels were low because a great deal of water was held in ___.
7 Roughly 8,000 years ago, Britain became ___.
8 Reprocessed seismic data has shown ancient rivers, lakes, marshes and ___.
9 The people of Doggerland obtained food by hunting, fishing and ___.
why: "So much water was locked up in ice sheets that sea levels were far lower". held = locked up.
"By around 8,000 years ago, Britain had become an island". Artikl bilan 2 so'z.
"A network of long-buried rivers, lakes, marshes and coastlines".
"Hunting deer and wild boar, catching fish and birds, and gathering wild plants". 3 so'z.

tasks.title: Questions 10–13
tasks.type: Matching features — groups A–C (harf takrorlanishi mumkin)
tasks.instr: Match each statement with the correct option. Avval variantlarni (ism yoki usul) matnda topib, HAR BIR uchragan joyini tagiga chizing — ular matnda qutidagi tartibda keladi. Bitta harf bir necha marta ishlatilishi mumkin.
items: 10 Their finds include evidence of a human species other than our own.
11 Their work relies on information originally gathered for commercial reasons.
12 They have been recovering animal remains for over a hundred years.
13 The material they search was moved to protect the coast and create land.
why: Gollandiya sohilidagi material: "a fragment of a Neanderthal skull had been recovered from such material".
"Oil and gas companies have spent decades carrying out seismic surveys ... to locate fuel reserves" — tijoriy maqsad.
"For more than a century, trawlers ... have hauled up the bones and teeth of mammoths".
"Sand has been dredged from the seabed to strengthen beaches and build new land for ports".
tasks.note: C ikki marta ishlatiladi. 10-savol tuzog'i: A — baliqchilar ham ov qurolini topgan, lekin u qaysi tur odamniki ekani aytilmagan.

homework_intro: Bugun bitta passage'da uch savol turini yechdik: xarita → sentence completion → matching features → matching information. Uyda xuddi shu tartibda, soat bilan ishlaysiz.

Birinchi vazifa — Practice 3 "The land beneath the North Sea": 20 daqiqa, 13 savol. 1–5 savollarda har javob yoniga ma'lumot turini (reference, explanation, example...) va isbot gapni yozing. Ismlar/guruhlar (fishing crews, geophysicists, amateur collectors) uchragan HAMMA joyni tagiga chizing.

Ikkinchi vazifa — kitob mashqlari: Student's Book, 57-bet, Vocabulary 1–2-mashqlar (Word formation — negative affixes) va Workbook, 31-bet, Vocabulary 1–2-mashqlar (negative affixes + Key vocabulary). Javoblarni kitob oxiridagi kalit bilan tekshiring.

Uchinchi vazifa — xatolar daftari: bugungi xato javoblarni yozing — savol, to'g'ri javob va sabab ("ma'lumot turini tekshirmadim", "ismning ikkinchi joyini ko'rmadim", "4 so'z yozdim", "None of the above ni ko'rmadim" va h.k.).

kahoot.q: In Matching information questions (Which paragraph contains...?), the questions are...
options: in the order of the headings
kahoot.explain: Matching information savollari matn tartibida EMAS. Shuning uchun uni oxirida, matnni bilganingizda yechish qulay.

kahoot.q: Which question type in today's combination follows the order of the passage?
kahoot.explain: Sentence completion gaplari doim matn tartibida. Features'da esa gaplar aralash, faqat ismlar qutidagi tartibda.

kahoot.q: Matching features: the names in the box (A, B, C) usually appear in the passage...
options: in the same order as in the box
in the opposite order to the box
kahoot.explain: Kitob maslahati: variantlar matnda qutidagi tartibda keladi. Har bir uchragan joyini tagiga chizing.

kahoot.q: What is the recommended order for today's three question types?
kahoot.explain: Tartibli turlar avval: matnni bir o'qishda bilib olasiz. Tartibsiz matching information — oxirida.

kahoot.q: 'a comparison of a range of physical features' — what must the paragraph contain?
options: Two groups compared on several physical points
Any mention of bodies, bones or physical size
One strong physical feature described in detail
A detailed description of a single species
kahoot.explain: Ma'lumot TURI — comparison. SB D: Neanderthals robust ... Homo sapiens, on the other hand, longer forearms.

kahoot.q: Which phrase from the text matches 'ill fortune'?
options: in the wrong place at the wrong time
kahoot.explain: Stringer: Neanderthals were living in the wrong place at the wrong time — omadsizlik. Javob — G.

kahoot.q: 'allocated tasks to different members' is a paraphrase of...
kahoot.explain: Vazifalarni taqsimlash = division of labour. Spikins: bunday taqsimot bo'lmagan — 10-savol C.

kahoot.q: NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS. Text: 'dating of the sediment layers'. Which answer is acceptable?
options: the dating of the sediment layers
kahoot.explain: Eng xavfsiz yo'l — matndan uzluksiz bo'lak: 'sediment layers' (2 so'z). Qolgan variantlar 3 so'zdan oshadi. Kalit 'dating sediment layers' ni ham qabul qiladi, lekin so'zlarni o'rtadan tashlashni odat qilmang.

kahoot.q: A researcher's name appears in four paragraphs. What should you do?
options: Underline every mention and read around each
Use only the first mention and ignore the others
Use only the last mention and ignore the others
Skip that name and come back to it at the end
kahoot.explain: Stringer C, D, F, G da gapiradi. 13-savol javobi C dagi iqtibosda — hammasini tekshiring.

kahoot.q: When should you choose 'None of the above'?
options: When no listed person makes that claim
When two of the listed people agree
When the statement is about the whole passage
Never, because it is always a trap option
kahoot.explain: WB 11: Richmond 'carry more' deydi, 'easier to carry heavy objects' emas. Da'vo hech kimniki emas — D.

kahoot.q: The key word 'Neanderthals' appears in a paragraph. Is that enough to match it?
options: No — the type of information must match too
Yes — one key word is always enough to match
Yes, but only if the word appears more than once
Only if it is in the first sentence of the paragraph
kahoot.explain: Mavzu so'zi hamma joyda. Savoldagi tur (reason, reference, final location...) ham mos bo'lishi kerak.

kahoot.q: 'reference to the FINAL location of Neanderthals' — which is the best evidence?
options: their last known refuge being southern Iberia
In western Eurasia, the Neanderthals dominated
kahoot.explain: 'final' = last known refuge (C). A xatboshidagi Eurasia — umumiy joy, tuzoq.

kahoot.q: Their numbers ___ within a few thousand years. (fell very sharply)
kahoot.explain: plummet — keskin tushib ketmoq. SB C xatbosh: their numbers plummeted.

kahoot.q: The climate became cold, dry and ___ — very difficult to live in.
kahoot.explain: hospitable → in-hospitable. Affikslarni aynan bilish sentence completion imlosi uchun ham muhim.

kahoot.q: Better hunting technology may have given Homo sapiens ___.
kahoot.explain: give sb the edge — ustunlik bermoq. Petraglia iqtibosi, B xatbosh.

kahoot.q: Gibraltar was the Neanderthals' last known ___ — a safe place to hide.
kahoot.explain: refuge — boshpana. refugia (ko'plik) — yashash mumkin bo'lgan kichik hududlar.

kahoot.q: It took the team five years to ___ the skeleton carefully.
kahoot.explain: excavate — arxeologik qazish ishlari olib bormoq. evacuate — odamlarni ko'chirish, boshqa ma'no.

kahoot.q: Needles and other ancient ___ were found alongside the bones.
kahoot.explain: artefact — inson yasagan qadimiy buyum. ancestor — ajdod (odam).

kahoot.q: Neanderthals tended to keep themselves to themselves. This means they...
options: lived in small groups with little contact
shared ideas and knowledge widely with others
travelled long distances to find new resources
traded tools and food with other species
kahoot.explain: keep oneself to oneself — o'z holicha yashash. E xatbosh: small groups, faqat yaqin atrofdan resurs.

kahoot.q: Petraglia can only ___ about the role of the eruption — he has no proof.
kahoot.explain: speculate — dalilsiz taxmin qilmoq. 12-savol: 'is unclear to us' = Scientists cannot be sure.

lessons.title: Unit 5 Listening — Section 3: Multiple choice + Diagram labelling + Note completion
lessons.grammar_topic: Section 3 kombinatsiyasi: Multiple choice (A, B, C) + Labelling a diagram (jarayon) / Note completion (vaqt jadvali)
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 5 (Stepping back in time) — fosillar, arxeologiya, neolit davri; jarayon bosqichlari (sequencers)
lessons.book_ref: Complete IELTS Bands 6.5–7.5: Student's Book, Unit 5, 52–53-betlar (Listening Section 3, CD1 Track 26–27; recording script 154–155-betlar); Workbook, Unit 5, 30-bet (Listening Section 3, Track 8–9; recording script 58-bet). Jony Academy mashqi — yangi skript.
objectives: Section 3 da (ikki talaba suhbati) MCQ dan keyin diagram yoki notes kelganda tayyorlanish vaqtini bo'lish: MCQ — savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oya, diagram — bosqichlar va o'qlar, notes — sana/davr ustunlari.
MCQ tuzog'ini tanish: variantdagi so'z eshitiladi, lekin boshqa odam aytadi, rad etiladi yoki boshqa vaqt haqida (America — later; website — information, not booking).
Jarayon diagrammasida ketma-ketlik so'zlarini (as soon as, gradually, once, until, during that time, eventually, meanwhile) eshitib, qaysi bosqichda ekanini kuzatish.
Vaqt jadvali ko'rinishidagi notes'da raqamli davrlarni (9,000–8,000 years ago) signal sifatida ishlatish.
ONE WORD ONLY chegarasi: so'z turi (muddy — sifat, erosion — ot), ko'plik (minerals, tribes, stages) va imlo.
materials: Student's Book, Unit 5, 52–53-betlar — savollar sahifasi (quyida rasm) va CD1 Track 26, Track 27 audiolari.
Workbook, Unit 5, 30-bet — savollar sahifasi va Track 8, Track 9 audiolari (imtihon rejimi, bir marta).

Recording script rasmlari — faqat ustozda; tekshiruvdan keyin ekranga chiqariladi. Dars oxirida uy vazifasi uchun SB Track 27 va WB Track 9 audiosi hamda shu parchalarning skripti guruh chatiga yuboriladi.
Jony Academy mashqi skripti — ustoz ikki rolni tabiiy tezlikda, javob so'zlariga urg'u bermasdan o'qiydi (yoki kuchli o'quvchi bilan birga).
Doskada ikki ro'yxat uchun joy: "MCQ tuzoqlari" va "sequencers" — dars davomida to'ldiriladi.
timeline: Kirish

Isinish (kitob rasmi shart emas; kitob bo'lsa, SB Starting off rasmlarini ham ko'rsating) — doskaga 3 savol: 1) Have you ever seen a fossil or something very old in a museum? What was it? 2) How do you think a fish skeleton can turn into stone? 3) Which would you rather explore: ancient ruins or a sunken ship? Why? — 3–4 o'quvchi javob beradi.
Section 3 kombinatsiyasi
Ustoz doskada: MCQ + diagram / notes; tayyorlanish vaqtini bo'lish; tuzoqlar; sequencers.
Sinf mashqi
Sequencers ma'nosi (SB 6-mashq) va diagram bo'shliqlarini oldindan aytish (SB 4-mashq).
Student's Book: Track 26–27
Q1–5 (MCQ) → Q6–10 (diagram) → javoblar skriptdan isbot bilan.
Workbook: Track 8–9
Imtihon rejimi: 30 soniya tayyorlanish, audio BIR MARTA, 10 savol; keyin tekshirish.
Jony Academy mashqi
Ustoz skriptni o'qiydi: "Amber presentation" — 10 savol, bir marta.
Skript bilan tahlil
Xato savollar skriptda topiladi; tuzoq gap va signal ibora belgilanadi; SB 7-mashq (54-bet) og'zaki — o'quvchilarda kitob bo'lsa (kalit — "Sequencers" sinf mashqining izohida).
Xulosa va vazifa
Uyga: shadowing, diktant, sequencers mashqi (6 gap), amber jarayonini sequencers bilan gapirib berish. Ustoz SB Track 27 va WB Track 9 audiosini skript parchalari bilan guruh chatiga yuboradi.

intro: Section 3 — o'quv mavzusidagi suhbat: ikki talaba (ba'zan ustoz bilan) ma'ruza, loyiha yoki tadqiqotni muhokama qiladi. Band 7 uchun asosiy qiyinchilik — gapiruvchilar fikrini o'zgartiradi, bir-birini to'g'rilaydi va javobni to'g'ridan-to'g'ri emas, paraphrase bilan aytadi.

Bugungi Unit'da ikki kombinatsiya bor. SB: Multiple choice (1–5) + Labelling a diagram (6–10) — fosil hosil bo'lish JARAYONI. WB: Multiple choice (1–5) + Note completion (6–10) — neolit davri VAQT JADVALI. Ikkalasida ham 1–5 va 6–10 orasida qisqa pauza bor — o'sha paytda ikkinchi topshiriqni yana ko'zdan kechiring.

Tayyorlanish vaqtini ikkiga bo'ling. MCQ: savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyaning tagiga chizing ("WHY did Milton MISS", "what STARTED", "MOST enjoy", "MAIN thing", "AGREE to do") — variantlarga emas (SB 2-mashq). Diagram: sarlavhani o'qing (Formation of marine fossils), bosqichlar (Stage 1–3) va o'qlarni kuzating, har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini yozing (SB 4-mashq). Notes: davrlar (9,000–8,000 years ago...) — ular audioda signal bo'lib xizmat qiladi.

MCQ TUZOG'I (Exam advice): "Although you may hear the words in the options, the speaker may be expressing the opposite idea." SB 2-savol: America tilga olinadi, lekin "well before then" — qiziqish oldinroq, tasodifiy topilmadan boshlangan. SB 5-savol: website eshitiladi — lekin ma'lumot uchun, joy band qilish uchun emas (hunts are fully booked).

DIAGRAM LABELLING: jarayon bosqichma-bosqich tasvirlanadi, gapiruvchilar SEQUENCER'lar bilan o'tadi: "as soon as a fish dies", "gradually gets covered over", "once the fish gets buried" (1-bosqich); "until it becomes hard rock", "during that time ... replaced by minerals" (2-bosqich); "eventually be above sea level", "meanwhile ... wears away" (3-bosqich). Sequencer'ni eshitsangiz — diagrammadagi keyingi yorliqqa ko'z bilan o'ting.

NOTE COMPLETION (vaqt jadvali): raqamlar va davrlar signal: "about 8,000 years ago" → 7-bo'shliq. Ehtiyot bo'ling: "assumed / thought" bilan aytilgan gap — odatda eski, XATO fikr; to'g'ri fakt undan oldin yoki keyin aytiladi. WB 9 da Claudia avval faktni o'qiydi ("built in several different stages"), keyin qo'shadi: "I'd always assumed it all went up at once" — javob to'g'ri faktdan olinadi (stages).
Transfer: ONE WORD ONLY — "minerals" (ko'plik, "replace" fe'li -s siz — demak ot ko'plikda), "muddy" ("soft and ___" — sifat), "erosion" ("effects of ___" — ot). Artikl ham so'z hisoblanadi.
formulas: WHY miss / what STARTED / MAIN thing
Har bo'shliq uchun so'z turini yozing
soft and (6) → sifat; (9) replace → ko'plik ot
as soon as / once / until / eventually / meanwhile
Rad etilgan yoki boshqa odam aytgan variantni chiqaring
presentation: MCQ da uchala variant ham eshitildi. Qaysi biri?
Savol o'zagiga qayting: KIM haqida va NIMA so'ralyapti? SB 3: suratga tushish (B) ham, uyga olib ketish (C) ham eshitiladi, lekin bolalar "the best bit" deb aytgani — toshlarni urib ko'rish (A).
Diagrammada bo'shliqlar tartibdami?
Odatda ha — bosqichlar tartibida. Lekin bitta bosqich ichida (Stage 1: 6 va 7) yorliqlar chapdan o'ngga yoki yuqoridan pastga ketishi mumkin — ikkalasini birga kuzating.
Diagramma rasmi tushunarsiz bo'lsa-chi?
Yorliqlardagi so'zlarga tayaning: "sea floor", "layered sediment", "replace bones", "expose fossil" — ular audioda deyarli aynan eshitiladi va joyni ko'rsatadi.
Notes'da davrlar (years ago) nima uchun kerak?
Ular signal: "about 8,000 years ago, Britain became separated" — raqamni eshitganingizda javob yaqin. Raqamlar o'zi odatda javob emas, balki joy ko'rsatkichi.
Gapiruvchi "I'd always assumed..." dedi. Bu javobmi?

Yo'q. "assumed", "thought", "expected" — ko'pincha XATO (eski) fikr; to'g'risi uning yonida — oldin yoki keyin — aytiladi. WB 9 da to'g'ri fakt OLDIN keladi: "built in several different stages" → 9 stages.
"soft and ___" ga "mud" yozsam bo'ladimi?
Yo'q. "and" bilan "soft" (sifat) ga bog'langan — sifat kerak: muddy. Skriptda: "it's muddy as well".
notes: 6.0 kursida Section 3 da MCQ + flow chart (15-dars), diagram labelling esa Section 2 da (13-dars) bor edi. Bugungi farq — diagram labelling Section 3 da, MCQ bilan birga va JARAYON diagrammasida: flow chart'ga o'xshaydi, lekin rasm bilan va yorliqlar bosqich ichida turli joyda turadi.
Tekshiruvda har javobdan keyin skriptdan aynan o'sha gapni ekranga chiqaring (skript bloklari pastda). SB skriptida javob so'zlari (muddy, oxygen, minerals, erosion) tagiga chizilgan.
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: Track 27 dan keyin diagrammaga qarab fosil hosil bo'lishini 6 ta sequencer bilan og'zaki tushuntirib berish (1 daqiqa).
mistakes: A — get him to do an extra one
Sayt — ma'lumot uchun; hunts fully booked
C — during a period of change
2–3 ming yil — eski taxminiy DAVOMIYLIK, "ago" emas

how: CORE — fosil va arxeologiya so'zlari; STRONG — jarayon va davrni tasvirlash; SUPER — Section 3 dagi so'zlashuv iboralari. Takror (10-dars): remains — yangi so'z sifatida sanalmaydi; SB skriptida ("the remains of living organisms") eshitilganda eslating.
Har o'quvchi 4 ta sequencer (as soon as, gradually, eventually, meanwhile) bilan biror jarayonni tasvirlaydi: non yopish, choy damlash, uy qurish.
core: He found the most amazing fossil on a school visit.
U maktab sayohatida ajoyib fosil topdi.
Wood and leather decay quickly in the ground, so archaeologists rarely find them.
Yog'och va charm yer ostida tez chiriydi, shuning uchun arxeologlar ularni kamdan-kam topadi.
Layers of sediment slowly turn into rock.
The bone is gradually replaced by minerals.
Erosion wears away the rock over time.
Eroziya vaqt o'tishi bilan toshni yemiradi.
The fish lies there if no predator comes along.
Yirtqich kelmasa, baliq o'sha yerda yotaveradi.
The archaeologist presents programmes on TV.
The houses were permanent rather than temporary.
strong: Nomadic people wandered from place to place.
The skeleton was entombed in rock for millions of years.
Skelet millionlab yil tosh ichida ko'milib yotdi.
Within a few years they learnt to domesticate animals.
Bir necha yil ichida ular hayvonlarni xonakilashtirishni o'rgandi.
The fish lies undisturbed on the ocean bed.
Baliq okean tubida tegilmagan holda yotadi.
The fossils become prized possessions in their rooms.
Fosillar ularning xonasidagi eng qadrli buyumlarga aylanadi.
super: I had to catch up on some reading for my seminar.
Seminar uchun qolib ketgan o'qishni bajarishim kerak edi.
He got interested in fossils well before then.
U fosillarga undan ancha oldin qiziqqan.

Ular dehqonchilikka hayratlanarli darajada tez ko'nikishdi.

Odamlar bir joyda qola boshlagach, uy qurishdi.

class_ex.title: Sequencers: ma'nosini toping (SB 6-mashq)
class_ex.instr: Track 27 dagi ketma-ketlik so'zlarini ma'nosi bilan moslang: a slowly, over a period of time; b up to the time that; c from the moment when; d while something else is happening; e over that period; f in the end, especially after a long time; g immediately after. Bittasiga ikki ma'no mos keladi.
items: 1 ... as soon as a fish dies, ...
2 ... the fish gradually gets covered over ...
3 ... so once the fish gets buried ...
4 ... it gets heavier and heavier until it becomes hard rock ...
5 ... during that time, the bone in the skeleton is replaced ...
6 ... the rock may lift and eventually be above sea level.
7 Meanwhile, the surface of the rock wears away?
why: "as soon as" = from the moment when / immediately after — kitobda namuna sifatida berilgan.
"gradually" — asta-sekin, vaqt davomida.
"once" — ...gan zahoti, ...gan paytdan boshlab.
"until" — ...gunga qadar.
"during that time" — o'sha davr mobaynida (millionlab yil).
"eventually" — oxir-oqibat, uzoq vaqtdan keyin.
"meanwhile" — shu bilan bir vaqtda (tosh ko'tarilayotganda).
class_ex.note: Kalit: 1 c, g; 2 a; 3 c; 4 b; 5 e; 6 f; 7 d. Mashqdan keyin: har sequencer diagrammadagi qaysi bosqichga to'g'ri keladi? (1–3 → Stage 1, 4–5 → Stage 2, 6–7 → Stage 3). Tahlil bosqichidagi SB 7-mashq (og'zaki) kaliti: 1 Once 2 Whilst 3 Meanwhile 4 gradually 5 eventually 6 until.

items: 6 — "sea floor – soft and ___"
7 — "almost no light or ___"
8 — "layered sediment – turns into ___"
9 — "___ replace bones"
10 — "effects of ___ expose fossil"
answers: sifat: dengiz tubini tasvirlovchi yana bir so'z
ot: dengiz tubida kam bo'lgan narsa
ko'plikdagi ot: suyak o'rnini egallaydigan narsa
ot: harakatga o'xshash, fosilni ochib beradigan jarayon
why: "and" bilan "soft" (sifat) ga bog'langan — demak sifat.
"no light or ___" — yorug'lik kabi atrof-muhit sharti (havo, kislorod...).
"turns into" — yangi modda: tosh.
"replace" (-s siz) — ega ko'plikda: ... replace bones.
"effects of ___" — predlogdan keyin ot; tosh sirtini yo'qotadigan tabiiy jarayon.

"If we have enough people, we might be able to get him to do an extra one for us". B — ovlar to'la band, sayt faqat ma'lumot uchun; C — boshqa TALABALAR bilan guruh tuzish, ov qatnashchilari emas.

listenings.title: Workbook, Track 8: Dave and Claudia — Professor Jeffcott's talk (Q1–5)
intro: Dave arxeolog Professor Brian Jeffcott'ning neolit inshootlari haqidagi ma'ruzasini Claudia'ga aytib beradi. Avval Workbook 2-mashq: savollardagi kalit so'zlarni belgilang (30 soniya). Savollar sahifasi (1–10) quyida rasm sifatida.
Imtihondagidek: audio BIR MARTA. 1–5 dan keyin Track 9 (Q6–10) darhol keladi.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Dave har savolda bir nechta narsani aytadi — savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyaga mos kelganini tanlang.
items: 1 What does Dave think about Professor Jeffcott? A) He's a typical archaeology lecturer. B) He's very enthusiastic about archaeology. C) He's not as interesting as some archaeology lecturers.

2 What was the first part of Professor Jeffcott's talk about? A) How it's now possible to date Neolithic structures more accurately. B) Artefacts that have been discovered on Neolithic sites. C) What Neolithic structures were used for.

3 According to Professor Jeffcott, most Neolithic structures ... A) were built between two and three thousand years ago. B) were built by people before they moved from one place to another. C) were built during a period of change.
4 What fact about Neolithic people surprised the researchers? A) The kind of food they grew. B) The speed at which they developed new skills. C) The range of skills they had.
5 What is Dave going to do next? A) Study the way prehistoric buildings were built. B) Build a modern structure using prehistoric methods. C) Write an essay on prehistoric building methods.
why: "He's so passionate about his subject". A — teskari: "the complete opposite of how you imagine these archaeology types"; C — "I wish all lecturers were like that".
"New carbon-dating techniques and advanced computer programmes are allowing them to narrow that down to within ten or twenty years". B va C — inshootlar misol sifatida tilga olinadi, xolos.

Inshootlar ko'chmanchilikdan o'troq hayotga o'tish davrida qurilgan: "when people went from being nomadic ... to being more static". A — tuzoq: "two or three thousand years" — eski taxminiy DAVOMIYLIK; B — teskari: "People only really build when they're settled".
"What was news to them was how quickly Neolithic people took to other things". A — "the researchers knew that already" (cereals); C — ko'nikmalar sanaladi, lekin hayratlantirgani TEZLIK.
"My class is going on a field project to look at prehistoric construction methods". B — ularning QO'LLANILISHINI o'rganish, qurish emas; C — dissertatsiya keyinroq, "essay" emas.
tasks.note: Kalit: 1 B, 2 A, 3 C, 4 B, 5 A. 3-savol eng qiyin: "two or three thousand years" eshitiladi, lekin u "ago" emas, qurilish davomiyligi haqidagi eski taxmin.

Davrlar (9,000–8,000 years ago, 8,000 years ago...) — joy ko'rsatkichi: raqamni eshitsangiz, javob yaqin.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10 — The Neolithic period: major events
tasks.type: Complete the notes. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

"Britain became separated from mainland Europe when the sea covered low land between what is now England and France".
"They started building houses that were permanent rather than temporary". Tuzoq: "temporary" ham eshitiladi.
"It was built in several different stages over many hundreds of years". Tuzoq: "I'd always assumed it all went up at once".
"Tools made from stone for building and farming became more sophisticated". implements = tools.

Voqea

Stonehenge built in (9). ;; Pottery made and used for the first time. ;; Neolithic people start making (10) stone implements.

listenings.title: Workbook: recording script (Track 8–9) — ustoz uchun

listenings.title: Jony Academy mashqi: Amber presentation
listenings.qtype: Multiple choice (1–4) + Labelling a diagram (5–7) + Note completion (8–10) — Section 3
intro: Amira va Tom — geologiya talabalari — seminar taqdimotini rejalashtiradi: qahrabo (amber) ichida hasharot qanday saqlanib qoladi. Ustoz ikki rolni tabiiy tezlikda, javob so'zlariga urg'u bermasdan o'qiydi (yoki kuchli o'quvchi bilan). BIR MARTA.

1–4 dan keyin 20 soniya pauza qiling. Diagram (5–7): Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Notes (8–10): Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. Diagrammani (5–7) ekranga chiqaring (javoblar yopiq) yoki doskaga chizing: Stage 1 → Stage 2 → Stage 3.
transcript: AMIRA: Hi Tom, have you got a few minutes? We really need to decide what we're doing for Friday's seminar presentation.
TOM: Sure. Actually, I was going to suggest amber — you know, fossilised tree resin. Did you see the display in the geology museum last week?
AMIRA: I didn't, but I like the idea. Is that why you chose it?
TOM: Partly. But the main reason is that nobody else in the group has picked anything to do with fossils, and Dr Okafor told us she wanted a real range of topics.
AMIRA: Fair enough. Did she say anything else about the presentation itself?

TOM: Well, it can be up to ten minutes, but she said she isn't strict about that, and she doesn't mind if we use notes. What she really cares about is that we explain a process clearly, step by step, with some kind of visual.
AMIRA: So a diagram, then. I've found some great photos of insects in amber online, but I'm not sure we can use them.
TOM: Why not? Are they too small to show on the screen?

AMIRA: No, the quality's fine. The problem is that most of them are protected by copyright, so we'd need permission from the photographers. A couple of them actually show copal rather than real amber, but I could just leave those out.
TOM: Then let's draw our own diagram instead. To be honest, I'm probably better at drawing than you are.
AMIRA: That's true! OK, you do the diagram and I'll write the notes. Shall we practise the whole thing on Thursday evening?
TOM: I'm working on Thursday evening. But what about asking Dr Okafor if we could run through it in her office hour on Wednesday?
AMIRA: Even better — she can tell us what to fix before Friday. I'll email her this afternoon.
(Pause — 20 seconds)
AMIRA: Right, let's plan the diagram. Stage one — it all starts with the tree, doesn't it?
TOM: Yes. When a tree is damaged — say a branch breaks off, or beetles bore into the bark — it produces resin to seal the wound. And resin is incredibly sticky.
AMIRA: Which is how it catches the insect.

TOM: Exactly. An insect lands on the resin and gets stuck. Then, as more resin flows down the trunk, it covers the insect completely. That's the crucial point: once it's sealed in, no air can reach the body, so it doesn't decay the way it normally would.
AMIRA: OK, stage two. The resin can't just stay on the tree for millions of years.

TOM: No. Eventually the tree falls, often into a river or a lagoon, and the lumps of resin end up buried. A lot of books say they're buried in sand, but in fact it's usually fine sediment on the bottom — that's what protects them.
AMIRA: And stage three is when it actually turns into amber?

TOM: Right. Over millions of years, heat and pressure slowly drive out the chemicals that keep resin soft, and it gets harder and harder. First it becomes something called copal — that's C-O-P-A-L — which is a sort of halfway stage. Only much later does it become true amber.
AMIRA: Good. Now for my notes. How old is the amber in that museum display?
TOM: It's from the Baltic region. People often say it's fifty million years old, but the museum label said about forty, and that's the figure most geologists use.
AMIRA: Forty million, then. And I read that you can still find it on the beaches there.
TOM: Yes, because amber floats in salt water. It gets washed up on the Baltic coast, especially after storms. Collectors go out early the next morning with nets.
AMIRA: Great. And should we mention that film where scientists get dinosaur DNA from a mosquito in amber?
TOM: Only to say it's impossible. DNA is far too fragile to survive that long. We could end with that — people always enjoy a myth being destroyed.

tasks.title: Questions 1–4
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Uchala variant ham eshitiladi — savol o'zagiga mosini tanlang.
items: 1 Why did Tom suggest amber as a topic? A) He had seen a museum display about it. B) No one else had chosen a topic about fossils. C) Their tutor recommended it.
2 What does Dr Okafor consider most important in the presentation? A) keeping to ten minutes B) speaking without notes C) explaining a process clearly

"Most of them are protected by copyright, so we'd need permission". A — "the quality's fine"; C — faqat "a couple" copal, ularni olib tashlash mumkin.

tasks.title: Questions 5–7 — How an insect is preserved in amber
tasks.type: Label the diagram. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

"Once it's sealed in, no air can reach the body, so it doesn't decay".

Stage 1 (continued): more resin covers insect • no (6) reaches body → no decay

tasks.title: Questions 8–10 — Amira's notes
tasks.type: Complete the notes. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
tasks.instr: Raqamlar va sonlar tuzog'iga ehtiyot bo'ling: ikki raqam eshitiladi.
items: 8 Halfway stage between resin and amber: ___
9 Age of most Baltic amber: about ___ million years
10 Amber is washed up on Baltic beaches, especially after ___
