homework_intro: Bugun Section 3 da uch savol turini ko'rdik: multiple choice, diagram labelling va note completion. Eng ko'p ball uch joyda yo'qoladi: teskari fikr aytilgan variantni tanlashda, so'z turini tekshirmaslikda (mud/muddy) va rad etilgan birinchi so'zni yozishda.

Birinchi vazifa — shadowing: SB Track 27 ni ("So what did he talk about in the second part?" dan oxirigacha) 3 marta tinglang, keyin Juni'ning gaplarini u bilan bir vaqtda takrorlang. Oxirgi urinishni ovozli xabar qilib guruhga yuboring. Audio va skript parchasi guruh chatida (ustoz dars oxirida yuboradi).

Ikkinchi vazifa — diktant: WB Track 9 ni tinglang va Claudia'ning davrlar bilan boshlanadigan 5 ta gapini to'liq yozing ("about 8,000 years ago, Britain became separated..."). Diktantni yozib bo'lgach (oldin emas), guruh chatidagi skript parchasi bilan o'zingiz tekshiring, xatolarni qizil bilan belgilang va xatolar sonini diktant ostiga yozing.

Uchinchi vazifa — sequencers mashqi: tashlab ketilgan qadimiy shahar qanday qilib yer ostida qolib, keyin topilishi haqidagi 6 ta gapni to'ldiring (as soon as, gradually, until, during that time, meanwhile, eventually — har biri bir marta). Bu kitobdagi 7-mashq emas, yangi matn.
To'rtinchi vazifa — qahrabo (amber) hosil bo'lishini Jony mashqidagi uch bosqich bo'yicha 6 ta sequencer bilan 1 daqiqa og'zaki tushuntirib, ovozli xabar yuboring.

homework.title: Shadowing: SB Track 27
homework.instr: 3 marta tinglash, keyin Juni bilan bir vaqtda takrorlash; ovozli xabar guruhga.
homework.answers: Ustoz talaffuz va ritmni tekshiradi; sequencer'lar aniq eshitilishi kerak.

homework.title: Diktant: WB Track 9 (davrlar)
homework.instr: Claudia'ning 5 ta gapi to'liq yoziladi, skript bilan tekshiriladi.
homework.answers: Kalit — WB Track 9 skripti (rejadagi Workbook skript rasmi). O'quvchi diktantni skript bilan o'zi tekshiradi va xatolar sonini yozadi; ustoz tasodifiy 3 ta ishni qayta sanab ko'radi. Keyingi darsda ustoz 2 ta gapni tasodifiy so'raydi.

homework.title: Sequencers: qadimiy shahar qanday topiladi (6 bo'shliq)
homework.instr: Har bo'shliqqa qutidagi so'zlardan birini yozing, har biri bir marta: eventually • until • as soon as • meanwhile • during that time • gradually. Gap boshidagi so'zni bosh harf bilan yozing.
items: ___ the last families leave the town, wild animals start to move into the empty houses.
Wind blows dust and sand into the streets, and the ruins are ___ covered, a few centimetres at a time.
Above the ground, the last wooden roof suddenly collapses. ___, below the ground, the buried walls stay safe from wind and rain.
The town then stays hidden for more than two thousand years. ___, new villages are built on top of it, and people forget that it was ever there.
Nobody suspects anything ___ a farmer finds pieces of old pottery in his field.
After many seasons of careful digging, archaeologists ___ reach the main street of the ancient town.
why: "from the moment when / immediately after" — oilalar ketishi bilan darhol (SB 6: c, g). Gap boshida ikki gapni bog'laydigan bog'lovchi kerak.
"slowly, over a period of time" — "a few centimetres at a time" sekin jarayonni ko'rsatadi.

"while something else is happening" — yer ustida oxirgi tom qulaydi, shu paytda yer ostida devorlar butun qoladi (above / below — ikki joyda bir vaqtda). "During that time" mos emas: oldingi gapda davr yo'q, bir lahzalik voqea bor (suddenly collapses).
"over that period" — oldingi gapdagi aniq davr ("more than two thousand years") mobaynida.
"up to the time that" — dehqon topgunga qadar hech kim bilmaydi.
"in the end, especially after a long time" — "after many seasons": uzoq ishdan keyin nihoyat yetib boradi (reach — bir lahzalik voqea, gradually mos emas).
homework.note: SB 54-bet, 7-mashq (underwater archaeology) sinfda og'zaki qilinadi (kitob bo'lsa); bu — uy uchun yangi Jony matni, SB 6-mashqdagi ma'nolar bilan. Kalit: 1 As soon as 2 gradually 3 Meanwhile 4 During that time 5 until 6 eventually. 3 va 4 ma'nosi yaqin: 3 da oldingi gap bir lahzalik voqea (davr yo'q) va ikki joydagi holat bir vaqtda — faqat Meanwhile; 4 da oldingi gapda aniq davr bor ("more than two thousand years") — During that time (Meanwhile 3 da ishlatilgan).

homework.title: Amber jarayoni — ovozli xabar
homework.instr: Qahrabo (amber) hosil bo'lishini uch bosqichda, kamida 6 ta sequencer bilan 1 daqiqa gapirib bering (as soon as, once, gradually, until, during that time, meanwhile, eventually); ovozli xabar guruhga.
homework.answers: Namuna reja: Stage 1 — when a tree is damaged, it produces sticky resin; as soon as an insect lands on it, it gets stuck; once it is covered by more resin, no air can reach the body, so it does not decay. Stage 2 — eventually the tree falls into a river or lagoon, and the resin is gradually buried in fine sediment. Stage 3 — the resin stays buried for millions of years; during that time, heat and pressure slowly harden it until it becomes copal and, much later, true amber. (Ro'yxatdan 6 ta: as soon as, once, eventually, gradually, during that time, until.) Ustoz sequencer'lar soni va bosqichlar tartibini tekshiradi.

kahoot.q: Before a Section 3 MCQ, what should you underline first?
options: Key ideas in the question stem
Every word in each of the options
Only the letters A, B, C
kahoot.explain: SB 2-mashq: savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oya (WHY miss, MAIN thing). Variantlar hammasi eshitiladi — o'zak yo'l ko'rsatadi.

kahoot.q: You hear a word from option A, but the speaker says 'well before then'. What does it mean?
options: A happened later — probably not the answer
A is correct, because the word was heard
A happened earlier, so it is probably the answer
The speaker is not sure when A happened
kahoot.explain: SB 2: America tilga olinadi, lekin qiziqish 'well before then' — tasodifiy topilmadan boshlangan (B).

kahoot.q: SB Q5: 'I'll look on his website.' Why is 'book on the Internet' wrong?
options: The hunts are fully booked; the site is only for information
Juni has already booked places for both of them on the website
kahoot.explain: Kelishilgan narsa: guruh tuzib, Mr Brand'ga qo'shimcha ov o'tkazdirish (A). Sayt — faqat ma'lumot uchun.

kahoot.q: Diagram labelling: what should you read first?
options: The instructions of the next task
kahoot.explain: Exam advice: sarlavha nima haqida ekanini aytadi; bosqichlarni solishtiring va har bo'shliq uchun ma'lumot turini aniqlang.

kahoot.q: Label: 'sea floor – soft and ___'. What kind of word is needed?
kahoot.explain: 'and' ikki sifatni bog'laydi: soft and muddy. 'mud' yozilsa — so'z turi xato.

kahoot.q: Label: '___ replace bones'. The verb has no -s. So the answer is...
kahoot.explain: 'replace' (-s siz) — ega ko'plikda. Skript: replaced by minerals.

kahoot.q: Which sequencer means 'in the end, especially after a long time'?
kahoot.explain: SB 6-mashq: eventually = f. Meanwhile = shu bilan bir vaqtda; as soon as = ...gan zahoti.

kahoot.q: 'Meanwhile, the surface of the rock wears away.' 'Meanwhile' tells you...
options: two things happen at the same time
this is the first stage of the process
kahoot.explain: Meanwhile = while something else is happening. Tosh ko'tariladi va shu vaqtda eroziya uni yemiradi.

kahoot.q: ONE WORD ONLY. You hear 'until it becomes hard rock'. What do you write?
kahoot.explain: Faqat bitta so'z: rock. 'hard rock' — 2 so'z, 0 ball.

kahoot.q: Speaker: 'I'd always assumed it all went up at once.' This is usually...
options: a wrong belief — the correct fact is nearby
the correct answer, so write it down
an example that supports the main point
a summary of everything said up to this point
kahoot.explain: assumed / thought — ko'pincha eski, xato fikr; to'g'ri fakt uning yonida (oldin yoki keyin) aytiladi. WB 9 da u OLDIN keladi: built in several different stages → 9 stages.

kahoot.q: WB Q3: 'two or three thousand years' is heard. Why is option A wrong?
options: It was the old idea of how long building took, not 'ago'
The number in the audio is different from option A
Dave says he disagrees with the professor on this point
It refers to Stonehenge, not to most Neolithic structures
kahoot.explain: Eski taxmin: qurilish 2–3 ming yil DAVOM etgan. Javob C — ko'chmanchilikdan o'troqlikka o'tish davri.

kahoot.q: In a timeline note completion, the dates (e.g. '8,000 years ago') are mainly...
options: signposts that the answer is near
always the answer you need to write
kahoot.explain: Davrlar — joy ko'rsatkichi: 'about 8,000 years ago, Britain became separated' → 7 separated.

kahoot.q: The fish lies ___ on the ocean bed if no predator comes along.
kahoot.explain: undisturbed — tegilmagan, bezovta qilinmagan. Skript: 'Undisturbed.' — 'That's right.'

kahoot.q: Wind and water slowly wear away rock. This natural process is called...
kahoot.explain: erosion — yemirilish. Excavation — arxeologik qazish; extinction — yo'q bo'lib ketish.

kahoot.q: People who move from place to place and don't build permanent homes are...
kahoot.explain: nomadic — ko'chmanchi. Skript: 'from being nomadic ... to being more static'.

kahoot.q: Tools made from stone became more ___ — more advanced and complex.
kahoot.explain: sophisticated — murakkab, takomillashgan. WB 10-savol javobi.

kahoot.q: Milton missed the talk because he had to ___ some reading.
kahoot.explain: catch up on — qolib ketgan ishni bajarmoq. SB 1-savol: 'He had to catch up on some work' (B).

kahoot.q: Neolithic people ___ farming surprisingly quickly. (started doing it easily)
kahoot.explain: take to sth — tez ko'nikmoq. WB: 'how quickly Neolithic people took to other things' → 4 B.

kahoot.q: The fish skeleton was ___ in rock for millions of years.
kahoot.explain: entombed — ko'milgan, qamalib qolgan. Exposed — aksincha, ochilib qolgan (Stage 3).

kahoot.q: They started building houses that were ___ rather than temporary.
kahoot.explain: permanent — doimiy. 'rather than temporary' — qarama-qarshi juftlik; WB 8-savol javobi.

lessons.title: Unit 6 Reading — Passage 3: Multiple choice + Yes/No/Not Given + Sentence endings
lessons.grammar_topic: Passage 3 kombinatsiyasi: Multiple choice (A–D) + Yes/No/Not Given + Matching sentence endings
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 6 (IT society) — ta'limdagi texnologiya, aqlli shahar, raqamli hayot
lessons.book_ref: Complete IELTS Bands 6.5–7.5: Student's Book, Unit 6, 63–66-betlar (Reading Section 3: "The new way to be a fifth-grader"); Workbook, Unit 6, 36–38-betlar ("How Green is your PlanIT Valley?"). Practice 1–3 — Jony Academy matnlari.
objectives: Passage 3 dagi uch savol turini bitta tartibda yechish: MCQ (1–5) → Y/N/NG (6–10) → sentence endings (11–14), har guruhga vaqt ajratib.
MCQ da savol o'zagini ("What does the writer say about...", "What does this reversal refer to") aniq tushunish va variantdagi "to'g'ri, lekin savolga javob emas" tuzog'ini tanish.
Y/N/NG da yozuvchining DA'VOSINI iqtibos keltirilgan odamlarning fikridan ajratish; NOT GIVEN ni "mavzu bor, da'vo yo'q" bilan isbotlash.
Sentence endings da ism/kalit so'z bilan joyni topish va tugash grammatik hamda mazmunan mos kelishini tekshirish.
Reference so'zlarni (it, this, such, doing so, among them) matndagi aniq g'oyaga bog'lash — MCQ va butun passage uchun.
materials: Student's Book, Unit 6, 63–66-betlar ("The new way to be a fifth-grader") — sinfda birga ishlanadi (pastda rasm).
Workbook, Unit 6, 36–38-betlar ("How Green is your PlanIT Valley?") — mustaqil mashq: 18 daqiqa ishlash + 2 daqiqa tekshirish (20 daqiqalik bosqich).
Practice 1–3 matnlari chop etilgan varaqlar (har o'quvchiga) — pastdagi Reading bo'limidan.
Uch rangli qalam: MCQ kalit g'oyasi — bir rang, Y/N/NG kalit so'zlari — ikkinchi, sentence endings dagi ismlar — uchinchi rang.
Doskada uch ustun: "MCQ — o'zak", "Y/N/NG — kimning fikri?", "Endings — ism → joy → tugash".
timeline: Kirish
SB 1–2-mashq: "Maktabda matematika yoqardimi? Sarlavhadan nima kutasiz?" — 3–4 o'quvchi javob beradi.
Uch savol turi birga
Ustoz doskada: xarita, ishlash tartibi, har tur qoidasi, yozuvchi va iqtibos farqi, 20 daqiqa taqsimoti.
Sinf mashqi
Reference so'zlar (SB 4-mashq) va "Kimning fikri?" mashqi.
Student's Book: The new way to be a fifth-grader
Skimming (SB 3-mashq) → Q1–14 birga: har javob uchun isbot gap va tuzoq varianti.
Workbook: How Green is your PlanIT Valley?
18 daqiqa mustaqil, keyin javoblar izoh bilan tekshiriladi.
Practice 1
"Do we still need to remember?" — 17 daqiqa vaqt bilan, keyin tahlil.
Practice 2
"Working from anywhere" — 17 daqiqa, xatolar daftariga yoziladi.
Xulosa va vazifa
Practice 3 (+ 8 ta reference so'z), WB Referencing mashqi uyga; xatolar daftari to'ldiriladi.

intro: Passage 3 — imtihonning eng uzun va eng qiyin matni: ko'pincha bahsli maqola, unda yozuvchining o'z fikri va boshqa odamlarning (olimlar, tanqidchilar, homiylar) fikrlari aralash keladi. Bugungi kombinatsiya: Multiple choice (1–5), Yes/No/Not Given (6–10) va Matching sentence endings (11–14).

Multiple choice (A–D) — savollar matn tartibida. Uch xil savol bo'ladi: tafsilot ("What do you learn about the student..."), yozuvchi fikri ("What does the writer say about...") va reference/lug'at ("What does this reversal refer to in line 40?"). Reference savolida javob so'zdan OLDIN ham, KEYIN ham bo'lishi mumkin — atrofdagi 2–3 gapni o'qing.

MCQ tuzog'i: noto'g'ri variantlar ko'pincha matnda so'zma-so'z uchraydi, lekin boshqa odam, boshqa vaqt haqida yoki teskari ma'noda. Masalan, SB 4-savolda "Advanced students get bored" bor — lekin D variantdagi "students in this category" (o'rta guruh) haqida emas.

Yes/No/Not Given — faktni emas, YOZUVCHINING DA'VOSINI tekshiradi ("agree with the claims of the writer"). NO — matnda teskari da'vo bor; NOT GIVEN — mavzu tilga olingan bo'lishi mumkin, lekin shu gap haqida yozuvchi hech narsa demaydi. Isbot gapni barmoq bilan ko'rsata olmasangiz — YES ham, NO ham emas.

Sentence endings — boshlanishlar (11–14) odatda ismlar yoki aniq kalit so'zlar bilan beriladi va matn tartibida keladi. Tugashlar (A–G) aralash, uchtasi ortiqcha. Ortiqcha tugashlar ko'pincha matnda BOR, lekin boshqa odamga tegishli (SB da A — yozuvchining o'z fikri, hech qaysi ismga tegishli emas).

Tartib va vaqt: 1 daqiqa — xarita (uch guruhni ko'rib chiqing, 11–14 dagi ismlarni matnda doiraga oling). Keyin matnni boshidan o'qing va savollarni tartib bilan yeching: MCQ va Y/N/NG bir xil tartibda yuradi, ismlar esa sizga 11–14 uchun joy belgilab beradi. Taxminiy vaqt (jami 20 daqiqa): xarita — 1, MCQ — 7, Y/N/NG — 6, endings — 5, tekshirish va transfer — 1 daqiqa.

Band 7 uchun: parafrazni kutib o'qing. Savolda "did not immediately know how to solve" — matnda "It took a while for me to work it out"; savolda "omitted in class" — matnda "teachers often gloss over". Bir xil so'zni qidirish bu darajada deyarli ishlamaydi.
formulas: Xarita: uch guruh + 11–14 dagi ismlarni doiraga olish
MCQ: o'zakdagi kalit g'oyaning tagiga chizish
What does the WRITER say about the CONTENT...
this reversal → lectures at home, homework at school
Y/N/NG: kimning fikri? yozuvchimi yoki iqtibosmi?
NOT GIVEN isboti: mavzu bor, da'vo yo'q
Endings: gapni to'liq o'qib, grammatika va ma'noni tekshirish
Ben Kamens has been told that KA could cause...
presentation: MCQ da ikkita variant matnda bor. Qaysi biri?
Savol o'zagiga qayting: KIM haqida, QAYSI jihat (content, reason, problem)? Ikkinchi variant odatda boshqa odam yoki boshqa jihat haqida.
Reference savoli — javob doim oldingi gapdami?
Ko'pincha shunday, lekin har doim emas. "this reversal" dan oldin "invert the normal rhythms of school" bor — va aynan shu joyda ma'no ochiladi.
Matnda iqtibos bor: "Schools have become joyless test-prep factories". Bu yozuvchining fikrimi?
Yo'q — bu Gary Stager'ning so'zi. Y/N/NG da yozuvchi fikri so'raladi; ismli iqtiboslar esa ko'pincha sentence endings uchun ishlatiladi.
NO va NOT GIVEN ni qanday ajrataman?
NO — matnda teskari gapni ko'rsata olasiz ("at an even pace" ↔ "at different rates"). NOT GIVEN — ko'rsatadigan gap yo'q, faqat mavzu so'zi bor.
Sentence endings da tugash matnda to'g'ri gap. Demak javobmi?
Shart emas. U aynan SHU odam haqida bo'lishi kerak. SB da A ("only suited to subjects where questions have exact answers") matnda bor, lekin hech qaysi ism aytmagan — tuzoq.
Vaqt yetmasa, qaysi guruhni oxiriga qoldiraman?
Endings eng tez yechiladi, chunki ismlar joyni ko'rsatadi. Qiyin MCQ ni belgilab o'tib keting, oxirida qayting — bo'sh qoldirmang.
notes: 7.0 guruhi aynan shu kombinatsiyani (MCQ + Y/N/NG + sentence endings) 6.0 ning 16-darsida ishlagan; bugun daraja oshadi: matn uzunroq, fikrlar ko'p ovozli, tuzoqlar nozikroq. Asosiy ko'nikma — Passage 3 dagi "ko'p ovozli" matnda kim nima deyayotganini kuzatish. SB matnini o'qiyotganda har iqtibos yoniga chetga ism bosh harfini yozdiring (G, S, M, K).
SB 5-mashqdagi "suggested underlining" ni doskada ko'rsating: 2 content / videos; 3 this reversal / line 40; 4 teaching / 'middle' / class; 5 Students praise / because.

Kuchli o'quvchilarga: ishlatilmagan C va F tugashlari nega matnga mos kelmasligini isbotlash; WB 12-savol (kalitda A) bo'yicha bahs — "yangi texnologiya yaratish" emas, "hamma texnologiya mavjud yoki texnik jihatdan mumkin".
mistakes: 1-savolga B ("did not expect his answer to be correct")
D — did not immediately know how to solve it
"sheepishly" — vaqt ketgani uchun, javobga ishonmagani uchun emas
B — technology has not until now provided a solution
"moving along together at an even pace" — "different rates" ga teskari
Direktorlar faqat maosh haqida — taklif qilish haqida gap yo'q
D — only prepares students to pass exams

how: CORE — ta'lim va texnologiya haqidagi asosiy akademik so'zlar; STRONG — Passage 3 ga xos kuchli fe'l va iboralar; SUPER — Band 7+ idiomatik birikmalar. Takror (11-dars): sophisticated — yangi so'z sifatida sanalmaydi; SB matnida ("sophisticated classroom technology", "anything but sophisticated") uchraganda eslating.
Har o'quvchi o'z maktab tajribasi haqida 3 gap tuzadi va kamida ikkita STRONG/SUPER birikma ishlatadi: "Our teacher often glossed over the difficult steps."
core: Online videos are a useful supplement to classroom teaching.
Onlayn videolar sinfdagi ta'limga foydali qo'shimcha.
The national curriculum was revised last year.
Milliy o'quv dasturi o'tgan yili qayta ko'rib chiqildi.
Each student can learn at his or her own pace.
Har bir o'quvchi o'z sur'atida o'rganishi mumkin.
The software offers exercises tailored to each learner.
Dastur har bir o'quvchiga moslashtirilgan mashqlar beradi.
Online lessons are a viable option for pupils who live far from school.
Onlayn darslar maktabdan uzoqda yashaydigan o'quvchilar uchun amalga oshirish mumkin bo'lgan yo'l.
The city is testing an innovative approach to recycling.
Shahar qayta ishlashga yangicha yondashuvni sinab ko'ryapti.
Many critics call rote learning an outdated technique.
Ko'plab tanqidchilar yodlashni eskirgan usul deb ataydi.
She is a strong advocate of online learning.
The plan became more credible once investors joined.
Many residents are sceptical about the new smart city.
Ko'p aholi yangi aqlli shaharga shubha bilan qaraydi.
strong: The government plans to overhaul the exam system.
Hukumat imtihon tizimini tubdan qayta qurmoqchi.
One-to-one tutoring is prohibitively expensive for most families.
Yakkama-yakka repetitorlik ko'p oilalar uchun haddan tashqari qimmat.
The textbook glosses over the most difficult steps.
Darslik eng qiyin bosqichlardan yuzaki o'tib ketadi.
Students grapple with a subject when they do homework.
O'quvchilar uy vazifasini qilganda mavzu ustida bosh qotiradi.
Teaching to the middle can lead to mediocrity.
O'rtachaga qarab o'qitish o'rtamiyonalikka olib kelishi mumkin.
Most social networks cater to young people.
super: He stumbled onto a solution while helping his cousin.
U jiyaniga yordam berayotib tasodifan yechim topdi.
All our attempts to fix the old computer were in vain.
Eski kompyuterni tuzatishga urinishlarimiz bekorga ketdi.
The videos are anything but sophisticated.
They plan to build a whole city from scratch.

class_ex.title: Reference so'zlar: nimaga ishora qiladi? (SB, 4-mashq)
class_ex.instr: SB matnidagi kursiv so'zlar nimaga ishora qilishini ayting. Javobni so'zdan oldingi va keyingi gaplardan qidiring.
items: 1 work it out
2 on which students (can watch)
3 the next one
4 more than that
5 such a luxury
6 plan for doing so
7 among them
8 this dismal trend
9 grasp it better
why: Kitobda namuna sifatida berilgan: bola yechayotgan "trigonometry problem".
"It is an educational website on which students can watch some 2,400 videos".
"Once you've mastered a video, you can move on to the next one" — keyingi video.
Kalitda: Thordarson's normal instruction. U avval saytni "merely a helpful supplement" deb o'ylagan, keyin u undan ancha ko'proq bo'lib chiqqan.
"The one-to-one instruction it requires is ... prohibitively expensive" — keyingi gapdagi hashamat shu.
"never intended to overhaul the school curricula ... a plan for doing so".
"some of his fans believe ... Most notable among them is Bill Gates".
Oldingi gap: "Schools have become joyless test-prep factories".
"if they can't understand the lecture in a classroom, they're not going to grasp it better".
class_ex.note: 3-savol (MCQ) ham reference savoli: "this reversal". Mashqdan keyin doskaga yozing: reference → oldingi 2 gap + keyingi 1 gap.

class_ex.title: Kimning fikri? Yozuvchi, iqtibos yoki hech kim
class_ex.instr: Ustoz Passage 3 uslubidagi qisqa parchani o'qiydi. O'quvchilar bold qilingan fikr KIMga tegishli ekanini aytadi: W — yozuvchi, P — iqtibos keltirilgan odam, N — matnda yo'q.
items: "Critics say the app turns learning into a game. In my view, that is exactly why it works." — Fikr: the app works because it is like a game.
"According to one teacher, pupils now arrive at lessons better prepared." — Fikr: pupils are better prepared.
"The company claims its software can replace textbooks, a promise that seems premature." — Fikr: the software cannot yet replace textbooks.
"Several schools in the region have adopted the platform." — Fikr: the platform is the most popular in the country.
"Some parents fear screen time; the evidence for this fear is weak." — Fikr: parents' fear is not well supported.
why: "In my view" — yozuvchining fikri. "Critics say" qismi esa boshqalarniki; Y/N/NG uchun faqat ikkinchi qism hisoblanadi.
Bu o'qituvchining fikri. Y/N/NG da so'ralsa — yozuvchi bu haqda o'z fikrini aytmagan (NG bo'lishi mumkin); sentence endings da esa "one teacher" ga tegishli.
Da'vo kompaniyaniki, lekin "a promise that seems premature" — yozuvchining bahosi: hali erta.
Matnda faqat "several schools in the region" — butun mamlakat bo'yicha eng mashhurligi haqida hech narsa yo'q.
"The evidence for this fear is weak" — yozuvchi ota-onalar fikriga baho bermoqda.
class_ex.note: SB matnida xuddi shunday: Stager, Martinez va Gates fikrlari — sentence endings; "Khan never intended...", "The very concept of grade levels implies..." — yozuvchi da'volari, Y/N/NG.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
tasks.instr: Avval savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyaning tagiga chizing (variantlarga emas), keyin matndan joyni topib, o'sha qismni diqqat bilan o'qing. Savollar matn tartibida.
items: 1 What do you learn about the student in the first paragraph? A) He has not used the maths software before. B) He did not expect his answer to the problem to be correct. C) He was not initially doing the right maths problem. D) He did not immediately know how to solve the maths problem.

2 What does the writer say about the content of the Khan Academy videos? A) They have been produced in a professional manner. B) They include a mix of verbal and visual features. C) Some of the maths problems are too easy. D) Some of the explanations are too brief.

3 What does this reversal refer to in line 40? A) going back to spending fewer hours in school B) students being asked to explain answers to teachers C) swapping the activities done in the class and at home D) the sudden improvement in students' maths performance

4 What does the writer say about teaching to the 'middle' of the class? A) Teachers become too concerned about weaker students. B) Technology has not until now provided a solution to the problem. C) Educators have been unwilling to deal with the issues. D) Students in this category quickly become bored.

5 Students praise Khan's videos because they A) show the extent of his mathematical knowledge. B) deal with a huge range of maths problems. C) provide teaching at different ability levels. D) cover details that are often omitted in class.
why: "It took a while for me to work it out," he admits sheepishly. B — tuzoq: "sheepishly" uyalganini bildiradi, lekin sabab — vaqt ketgani; A va C haqida matnda hech narsa yo'q.

Videolar — ovoz ("a voiceover ... chattily describing") + ekrandagi qo'lda chizilgan formula va diagrammalar. A — teskari: "anything but sophisticated"; C va D — matnda yo'q (7–14 daqiqa — uzunlik, qisqa tushuntirish emas).

readings.title: Practice 1: Do we still need to remember?
readings.qtype: Multiple choice (1–5) + Yes/No/Not Given (6–10) + Matching sentence endings (11–14)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 3 darajasi)
text: Ask a group of teenagers for the phone number of their closest friend and most will reach, almost without thinking, for the device in their pocket. Ask their grandparents the same question and many will recite a string of digits they learned decades ago. It is tempting to conclude from this contrast that the younger generation has weaker memories, but that conclusion is almost certainly mistaken. What has changed is not the capacity of the human brain, which has remained essentially the same for tens of thousands of years, but the decisions it makes about what is worth storing.

Psychologists call this habit 'cognitive offloading': the practice of placing information in the outside world so that the mind does not have to hold it. Offloading is nothing new. Shopping lists, diaries and calendars, and before them knotted cords and notches carved in wood, all served the same purpose. What is new is the scale and speed of the process. A smartphone can hold every address, appointment and photograph a person is likely to need, and a search engine can retrieve almost any fact in seconds. Under these conditions, it would be strange if the brain did not adjust.

Experiments have begun to reveal how that adjustment works. In one widely reported series of studies, participants typed short trivia statements into a computer. Half were told that their typing would be saved; the rest were told that it would be deleted. Those who expected the information to be saved remembered noticeably less of it, although they were often able to recall where it had been stored. The researchers concluded that people treat the internet rather like a well-informed friend: there is little point in memorising what a reliable partner already knows, as long as you know how to ask.

A related effect has been observed in museums. Visitors who were asked to photograph objects later recalled fewer details about them than visitors who were simply asked to look. The act of taking the picture seemed to signal to the brain that the job of remembering had been handed over to the camera. Interestingly, when participants were asked to zoom in on one particular feature of an object, their memory for that feature improved, which suggests that it is attention, rather than the camera itself, that makes the difference.

Critics of digital technology see such findings as evidence of decline. If students can look up the date of any battle, the argument runs, they will stop learning history altogether, and a society that remembers nothing will be easy to mislead. This view seems to me exaggerated. Knowing a date has never been the same as understanding an event, and the time saved by not memorising lists could, in principle, be spent on the harder work of interpretation. The real danger is not that we forget facts but that we lose the habit of connecting them.

That habit depends on knowledge that is held in the head. Experts in any field are distinguished less by the number of facts they can recall than by the way those facts are organised, so that one idea immediately calls up others. A search engine can supply a missing detail, but it cannot tell a beginner which details matter or how they fit together. Some educators therefore argue that a solid base of memorised knowledge is more important in the age of the internet, not less, because without it learners cannot judge the reliability of what they find online.

The sensible response is neither to reject digital memory nor to surrender to it, but to use it deliberately. Offloading appointments and phone numbers frees mental resources for other tasks, and there is no reason to feel guilty about it. The core ideas of a subject, on the other hand, are worth the effort of learning by heart, because they are the framework on which everything else hangs. The question is not whether we should remember less, but what we should choose to remember.

readings.title: Practice 2: Working from anywhere
readings.qtype: Multiple choice (1–5) + Yes/No/Not Given (6–10) + Matching sentence endings (11–14)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 3 darajasi)
text: For most of the twentieth century, going to work meant going somewhere. Offices were designed on the assumption that supervision required physical presence: managers needed to see their staff, and staff needed to be seen. In the early 2020s that assumption was tested on a scale no one had planned for, when millions of office employees were sent home and asked to carry on as normal using laptops, video calls and shared documents. To the surprise of many managers, a large share of the work carried on.

The technology that made this possible was not new. Video conferencing had existed for decades, and online file sharing had been widely available for years. What had held remote work back was not engineering but habit and trust. Many managers believed, often without evidence, that employees who could not be seen would not work. The sudden, enforced experiment removed the choice, and in doing so it revealed how much of office life had depended on custom rather than necessity.

The results for productivity have been mixed, and much depends on the kind of work involved. Tasks that require long periods of concentration, such as writing reports or analysing data, often benefit from the absence of office interruptions. By contrast, tasks that rely on quick exchanges of information, or on training new staff, tend to suffer. Junior employees in particular appear to lose out, because much of what they learn at work comes not from formal instruction but from overhearing how experienced colleagues handle problems, something that is difficult to reproduce on a screen. Measuring productivity is itself far from simple. Output that can be counted, such as the number of sales calls made, is easy to compare, but much office work produces nothing that can be measured so neatly, which is one reason why studies of remote work have reached such different conclusions.

For employees, the most obvious gain is time. A worker who once spent an hour each way travelling to an office may recover ten hours a week, and surveys consistently show that avoiding the commute is the benefit remote workers value most. Yet the boundary between work and home can easily disappear. When the laptop is always on the kitchen table, the working day has no clear end, and some people report working longer hours than before, not fewer. Others miss the informal conversations that once made the working day sociable, and loneliness is a common complaint among remote workers who live alone.

Employers, meanwhile, have discovered advantages of their own. Firms that allow remote work can recruit from a far wider area, and some have reduced their spending on office space. However, a number of large companies have since asked staff to return to the office for most of the week, arguing that creativity and company culture depend on face-to-face contact. It is striking that these announcements have rarely been accompanied by data showing that remote teams performed worse. The effects have also spread beyond individual firms: in many city centres, cafés and sandwich shops that depended on office workers have lost customers, while similar businesses in residential suburbs have gained them.

The most common outcome has been a compromise: the hybrid model, in which staff spend some days in the office and some at home. In theory, this combines the best of both arrangements. In practice, it raises new difficulties. If team members choose their office days independently, a worker may travel for an hour to sit in a half-empty building and spend the day on video calls. Hybrid work succeeds only when it is organised around the purpose of each day, with collaboration in the office and concentration at home, rather than around individual preference.

It would be a mistake to treat remote work as either a revolution or a passing fashion. For many occupations, such as nursing, construction or retail, it was never an option, and the debate means little to millions of workers. For office staff, however, the experiment has permanently changed expectations. The question facing employers is no longer whether people can work away from the office, but how to decide which work belongs where.

tasks.instr: YES — yozuvchining fikriga mos; NO — yozuvchining fikriga zid; NOT GIVEN — yozuvchi bu haqda fikr bildirmagan. Savollar matn tartibida.
items: 6 The technology needed for remote work was developed during the early 2020s.
7 Tasks requiring deep concentration are often done better away from the office.
8 Remote workers generally earn less than their office-based colleagues.
9 The hybrid model is effective whatever way it is organised.
10 Most people who work in retail would prefer to work from home.
why: "The technology that made this possible was not new. Video conferencing had existed for decades".
"Tasks that require long periods of concentration ... often benefit from the absence of office interruptions".
Maosh (earnings, pay) haqida matnda hech narsa yo'q.
"Hybrid work succeeds only when it is organised around the purpose of each day" — "only" shartni bildiradi, "whatever way" ga zid.
Chakana savdo haqida faqat: "it was never an option". Ular nimani afzal ko'rishi aytilmagan.
tasks.note: 10-savol — "retail" so'zi bor, lekin istak (prefer) haqida da'vo yo'q. 9-savol — "only when" kabi shartli iboralar ko'pincha NO ning isboti.

items: 11 Tasks that depend on the rapid sharing of information
12 Firms that allow their staff to work remotely

"Firms that allow remote work can recruit from a far wider area".

readings.title: Practice 3 (uyga): The office that never went paperless
readings.qtype: Multiple choice (1–5) + Yes/No/Not Given (6–10) + Matching sentence endings (11–14)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 3 darajasi), uy vazifasi
text: In the mid-1970s, a business magazine confidently predicted that computers would soon make paper in offices unnecessary. Documents would be written, stored and sent electronically; filing cabinets would disappear, and the printed page would become a curiosity. The idea of the 'paperless office' proved so attractive that it was repeated, with small variations, for the next thirty years. Yet for most of that period, offices in developed countries used more paper, not less.

The explanation lies partly in the technology itself. The same personal computers that were supposed to replace paper made it far easier to produce. Before word processors, correcting a typed letter often meant retyping the whole page, so drafts were few. Once text could be edited on screen and printed in seconds, people printed drafts to check them, printed again after each correction, and printed copies for colleagues. Laser printers and cheap photocopiers made each extra page seem free. Email, rather than reducing paper, often generated more of it, as many workers printed important messages in order to read or file them. Filing systems grew as well, because a document that existed only on a computer disk felt less secure than one kept in a folder, and many organisations printed and stored copies of electronic files simply as a precaution.

There were also good reasons, rather than mere habit, for paper's survival. Researchers who observed office workers found that people used paper in ways that the screens of the time could not easily copy. Readers spread documents across a desk to compare them, wrote comments in the margins, and moved quickly back and forth between pages. Paper was also portable, required no power and could be read in almost any light. For tasks such as reviewing a long report, it was simply the better tool.

Change, when it came, was gradual and driven by several developments at once. Screens became larger and sharper, and many workers began to use two of them side by side, which recreated some of the advantages of a desk covered in documents. Software allowed several people to comment on the same file, removing the need to circulate printed copies. Laws in many countries began to accept electronic signatures, so contracts no longer had to be printed and signed by hand. Digital storage also became steadily cheaper, so keeping an electronic archive cost far less than renting space for rows of filing cabinets. Above all, the arrival of tablets and smartphones meant that a document could be read anywhere without being printed.

As a result, office paper consumption in many developed economies appears to have peaked in the early years of this century and has declined since. The decline, however, has been slow and uneven. Organisations that deal with the public, such as hospitals and local government offices, have often found it harder to abandon paper than private companies, partly because some of the people they serve do not use digital services. Much of the fall has come from paper that was never necessary, such as printed emails, rather than from documents that people genuinely prefer to read on the page.

Some studies also suggest that readers understand long, complex texts slightly better on paper than on screen, particularly when they are working under time pressure. One possible explanation is that paper gives readers a physical sense of where information is located and how much of the text remains, which may help them to build a mental map of an argument. The difference seems to be small, and it may shrink as people gain more experience of reading digitally. Nevertheless, it is a reminder that the choice between paper and screen is not only a matter of cost or convenience.

The history of the paperless office offers a useful lesson about predictions of technological change. Forecasters tend to assume that a new technology will simply replace an old one. More often, the two exist side by side for a long time, while people discover what each does best. Paper did not disappear from the office; it lost the jobs it did badly and kept, for the moment, some of the jobs it does well.
paraphrases: repeated for decades
repeated, with small variations, for the next thirty years
easy to print many versions
printed drafts ... printed again after each correction
suited certain tasks better than screens
For tasks such as reviewing a long report, it was simply the better tool
the most important factor
Above all
exist side by side
old and new technologies coexist
seem to cost nothing
seem free

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
tasks.instr: Avval savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyaning tagiga chizing (variantlarga emas), keyin matndan joyni topib, o'sha qismni diqqat bilan o'qing. Savollar matn tartibida. 7 daqiqa.
items: 1 What does the writer say about the prediction made in the 1970s? A) It was quickly forgotten. B) It was based on careful research. C) It continued to be made although the opposite was happening. D) It was made by computer manufacturers.

2 According to the second paragraph, word processors increased paper use because they A) were difficult for office workers to use. B) made it easy to print many versions of a document. C) could not store documents safely. D) were cheaper than typewriters.

3 What did researchers find about office workers' use of paper? A) It was mainly the result of habit. B) It was used mostly for printing emails. C) Workers rarely wrote on printed documents. D) It suited certain tasks better than screens did.

4 What does 'The decline' refer to in the fifth paragraph? A) the fall in the number of printers sold B) the reduction in the amount of paper used in offices C) the decrease in public services offered on paper D) the drop in the quality of reading on screen

5 What is the writer's main point in the final paragraph? A) New technologies usually replace old ones quickly. B) Forecasters are usually right in the long term. C) Old and new technologies often exist together for a long time. D) Paper will soon disappear from offices completely.
why: "it was repeated ... for the next thirty years. Yet for most of that period, offices ... used more paper, not less".
"people printed drafts to check them, printed again after each correction, and printed copies for colleagues".
"There were also good reasons, rather than mere habit" va "For tasks such as reviewing a long report, it was simply the better tool". A — teskari; C — aksincha, hoshiyaga izoh yozishgan.
Oldingi gap: "office paper consumption ... has declined since". "The decline" = shu kamayish.
"More often, the two exist side by side for a long time". D — teskari: "Paper did not disappear".

tasks.title: Questions 6–10
tasks.type: Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer? Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.
tasks.instr: YES — yozuvchining fikriga mos; NO — yozuvchining fikriga zid; NOT GIVEN — yozuvchi bu haqda fikr bildirmagan. Savollar matn tartibida. 6 daqiqa.
items: 6 Before word processors, office workers produced relatively few drafts of documents.
7 Electronic signatures are now accepted in every country.
8 Tablets and smartphones did more than anything else to reduce office printing.
9 The difference in understanding between reading on paper and on screen is large.
10 Hospitals have tried harder than private companies to stop using paper.
why: "correcting a typed letter often meant retyping the whole page, so drafts were few".
Matnda: "Laws in many countries began to accept electronic signatures". "Every country" haqida da'vo yo'q — "many" "every" ni inkor ham, tasdiq ham qilmaydi.
"Above all, the arrival of tablets and smartphones" — "above all" = eng muhim omil.
"The difference seems to be small".
Matnda: kasalxonalarga qog'ozdan voz kechish QIYINROQ bo'lgan. Ular ko'proq HARAKAT qilgani aytilmagan.
tasks.note: 7 va 10 — Band 7 NOT GIVEN tuzoqlari: "many" → "every" va "found it harder" → "tried harder". Bu NO emas, chunki matn teskarisini ham aytmaydi.

tasks.title: Questions 11–14
tasks.type: Complete each sentence with the correct ending, A–G.
tasks.instr: Har gapni A–G dan to'g'ri tugash bilan yakunlang. Avval tugashlardagi kalit g'oyalarni belgilang, keyin savoldagi ism yoki kalit so'z bilan matndan joyni toping. Uchta tugash ortiqcha. 5 daqiqa.
items: 11 Laser printers and cheap photocopiers
12 Software allowing several people to comment on one file
13 Hospitals have found it hard to abandon paper partly because some of the people they serve
14 Some studies suggest that readers working under time pressure
why: "Laser printers and cheap photocopiers made each extra page seem free".
"Software allowed several people to comment on the same file, removing the need to circulate printed copies".
"partly because some of the people they serve do not use digital services".
"readers understand long, complex texts slightly better on paper ... particularly when they are working under time pressure".
tasks.note: Ortiqcha tugashlar: F — qog'ozning xususiyati ("required no power"), printerlar haqida emas; D — elektron imzo aksincha chop etishni kamaytirgan; B — matnda yo'q.
box: A removed the need to circulate printed copies.
B prefer to read all documents on screen.
C may understand complex texts slightly better on paper.
D made contracts easier to print and sign.
E made each extra page seem to cost nothing.
F required no power and could be read in any light.
G do not use digital services.

homework_intro: Bugun Passage 3 da uch savol turini birga yechdik: MCQ → Y/N/NG → sentence endings. Eng ko'p ball uch joyda yo'qoladi: iqtibos keltirilgan odam fikrini yozuvchi fikri deb olish, "so'z bor — demak NO" deb o'ylash va ortiqcha tugashni tanlash.

Birinchi vazifa — Practice 3 "The office that never went paperless": 20 daqiqa vaqt oling, 14 savolga javob bering. Har Y/N/NG javobi yoniga isbot gapning birinchi 3 so'zini yozing; NOT GIVEN uchun esa "matnda nima bor, nima yo'q" ni bir gapda o'zbekcha yozing.

Ikkinchi vazifa — Workbook, 40-bet, Grammar: Referencing (18 ta bo'shliq, box'dagi so'zlar bilan) va Practice 3 matnidan 8 ta reference so'z: ular nimaga ishora qilishini yozing. SB 4-mashqni sinfda og'zaki qildik — endi xuddi shu ko'nikmani yangi matnda mustaqil tekshiring. WB javoblarini WB 67-bet kaliti bilan solishtiring; reference so'zlarni ustoz keyingi darsda tekshiradi.

Uchinchi vazifa — xatolar daftari: bugungi xato javoblarni yozing — savol, to'g'ri javob va sabab ("iqtibosni yozuvchi fikri deb oldim", "many ni every deb o'qidim", "tugash boshqa odamga tegishli edi" va h.k.).

homework.title: Practice 3: "The office that never went paperless"
homework.instr: 20 daqiqada 14 savol; har Y/N/NG yoniga isbot gap, NG uchun izoh.
homework.answers: Javoblar Reading bo'limida izoh bilan.

homework.title: WB 40-bet: Grammar — Referencing
homework.instr: 18 ta bo'shliqni box'dagi so'zlar bilan to'ldiring.
homework.answers: WB 67-bet kaliti bilan tekshiriladi; ustoz 3 tasini og'zaki so'raydi.

homework.title: Practice 3: reference so'zlar (8 ta)
homework.instr: Practice 3 ni tugatgandan keyin: har banddagi reference so'z (it, that, them, one, which) nimaga ishora qilishini yozing. Javobni so'zdan oldingi va keyingi gaplardan qidiring (sinfdagi SB 4-mashq kabi, lekin endi yangi matnda).
items: 1 it was repeated (1-xatboshi)
2 for most of that period (1-xatboshi)
3 made it far easier to produce (2-xatboshi)
4 printed drafts to check them (2-xatboshi)
5 generated more of it (2-xatboshi)
6 one kept in a folder (2-xatboshi)
7 use two of them side by side (4-xatboshi)
8 which recreated some of the advantages (4-xatboshi)
answers: the thirty years after the prediction (from the mid-1970s)
using two screens side by side
why: "The idea of the 'paperless office' proved so attractive that it was repeated" — it = shu g'oya.
"...repeated, with small variations, for the next thirty years. Yet for most of that period" — that period = o'sha o'ttiz yil.
"The same personal computers that were supposed to replace paper made it far easier to produce" — it = paper.
"people printed drafts to check them" — them = drafts (ko'plik).
"Email, rather than reducing paper, often generated more of it" — it = paper.
"a document that existed only on a computer disk felt less secure than one kept in a folder" — one = a document (qog'ozdagi nusxa).
"Screens became larger and sharper, and many workers began to use two of them side by side" — them = screens.

"many workers began to use two of them side by side, which recreated some of the advantages of a desk covered in documents" — "which" bitta otga emas, oldingi butun qismga qaytadi: ikki ekranni yonma-yon ishlatish.
homework.note: 8-misol eng qiyini: "which" bitta otga emas, butun gap qismiga ishora qiladi (Band 7 darajasidagi reference). Tekshirish: ustoz keyingi darsda 3 tasini og'zaki so'raydi.

homework.title: Xatolar daftari
homework.instr: Bugungi xato javoblar: savol — to'g'ri javob — xato sababi.
homework.answers: Sababsiz qator qabul qilinmaydi.

kahoot.q: In a Yes/No/Not Given task, what do you check each statement against?
kahoot.explain: Y/N/NG yozuvchining da'vosi va fikrini tekshiradi. O'z bilimingiz yoki umumiy fikr hisobga olinmaydi.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Khan never intended to overhaul the school curricula.' Statement: 'Khan wanted to change school courses completely.'
kahoot.explain: overhaul = completely change; "never intended" teskari da'vo. Demak NO.

kahoot.q: 'Principals' appears in the passage, but only in connection with pay. Statement: 'Principals invited Khan to their schools.'
options: YES, because the word is there
kahoot.explain: Mavzu so'zi bor, lekin taklif haqida da'vo yo'q. So'z bor = javob bor degani emas — NOT GIVEN.

kahoot.q: Text: 'grade levels imply students moving along together at an even pace'. Statement: '...progressing at different rates.'
options: YES, the topic is the same
kahoot.explain: "even pace" (bir xil sur'at) ↔ "different rates" (turli sur'at) — teskari ma'no, NO.

kahoot.q: A quotation says: 'Schools have become joyless test-prep factories.' Whose view is this?
options: Khan, the founder of the website
Bill Gates, one of Khan's fans
kahoot.explain: Iqtibos — Stager'niki. Bunday fikrlar odatda sentence endings uchun ishlatiladi, Y/N/NG uchun emas.

kahoot.q: MCQ reference question: 'What does this reversal refer to?' Where is the answer usually found?
options: In the nearby sentences, often just before it
Only in the first paragraph of the whole passage
In the title and subheading of the article
In the last sentence of the whole passage
kahoot.explain: Reference so'z atrofidagi 2–3 gapni o'qing: "invert the normal rhythms of school" — shu joyda ma'no ochiladi.

kahoot.q: In Multiple choice (A–D), which should you underline FIRST?
options: The key idea in the question stem
Every word in each of the four options
Only the names in the options
kahoot.explain: O'zakdagi kalit g'oya (what PROBLEM, what does the WRITER say about CONTENT) nimani qidirishni aytadi; variantlar chalg'itadi.

kahoot.q: An MCQ option repeats words from the passage exactly. What does this often mean?
options: It may be a trap about another person or idea
It is always the right answer, so you can choose it
It is always wrong and should be ignored
kahoot.explain: So'zma-so'z takror ko'pincha tuzoq: "Advanced students get bored" bor, lekin savol o'rta guruh haqida.

kahoot.q: Matching sentence endings: compared with the sentence beginnings, how many endings are there usually?
kahoot.explain: SB da 4 ta boshlanish va 7 ta tugash — uchtasi ortiqcha. Ortiqchalari ko'pincha matnda bor, lekin boshqa odamga tegishli.

kahoot.q: What is the quickest way to locate sentence beginnings like '12 According to Gary Stager...'?
options: Circle the names in the passage before reading
Read all seven endings first and guess the order
Start from the last paragraph and work back
kahoot.explain: Ismlar joyni ko'rsatadi va matn tartibida keladi. Xarita bosqichida ularni doiraga oling.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Many universities now accept online applications.' Statement: 'Online applications are accepted by every university.'
kahoot.explain: many ≠ every, lekin matn "hamma universitet emas" ham demaydi. Da'vo yo'q — NOT GIVEN.

kahoot.q: Passage 3 has 14 questions. What is a realistic time plan?
options: About 35 minutes, since it is the hardest
No plan; spend as long as needed
kahoot.explain: 60 daqiqa / 3 passage = 20 daqiqa. Passage 3 rejasi: xarita 1, MCQ 7, Y/N/NG 6, endings 5, tekshirish va transfer 1 — jami 20 daqiqa.

kahoot.q: Teachers often ___ the small, hidden steps in a maths problem.
kahoot.explain: gloss over — yuzaki o'tib ketmoq. Khan aynan shu qadamlarni tushuntiradi.

kahoot.q: One-to-one instruction is ___ expensive, so few countries can afford it.
kahoot.explain: prohibitively expensive — imkonsiz darajada qimmat.

kahoot.q: Schools spent millions on technology, but the effort was ___.
kahoot.explain: in vain — bekorga, natijasiz.

kahoot.q: Khan never intended to ___ the school curricula.
kahoot.explain: overhaul — tubdan qayta qurmoq (completely change).

kahoot.q: At first she saw the site as a helpful ___ to her normal teaching.
kahoot.explain: supplement — qo'shimcha, to'ldiruvchi vosita.

kahoot.q: Many parents are ___ about the new learning app and doubt that it will really help their children.
kahoot.explain: sceptical (about) — shubha bilan qaraydigan; gapdagi "doubt" shu ma'noni tasdiqlaydi.

kahoot.q: Living PlanIT plans to build a smart city ___ in northern Portugal.
kahoot.explain: from scratch — noldan, hech narsasiz joydan boshlab.

kahoot.q: Once several serious investors joined, the plan suddenly looked far more ___.
kahoot.explain: credible — ishonarli: jiddiy investorlar qo'shilgach, rejaga ishonch ortadi.

intro: Section 4 — akademik ma'ruza yoki taqdimot: bitta gapiruvchi, 10 savol, o'rtada PAUZA YO'Q. Shuning uchun tayyorlanish vaqtida butun notes'ni (1–10) ko'rib chiqish kerak — keyin qaytishga vaqt bo'lmaydi.

Notes tuzilmasi — sizning xaritangiz. SB da uch daraja yordam bor: 1) qalin sarlavhalar (History, Pixar Animation Studios, Future developments) — mavzu almashishini bildiradi; 2) chap ustundagi ismlar va so'zlar (Thomas Edison, Émile Cohl, Earnings, Famous films) — ma'ruzachi aynan shularni aytadi; 3) bo'shliq atrofidagi so'zlar — javob turini beradi.

So'z turini bashorat qiling: "used many ___ of faces" — ko'plikdagi ot; "used ___ slides" — sifat; "Over $___" — raqam (pul); "a ___" — birlikdagi sanaladigan ot; "As many as ___ of bank customers" — foiz. Bashorat noto'g'ri javobni darrov chiqarib tashlaydi.

Signal iboralar notes'dagi bandlarni ochadi: "Well, firstly..." → a, "A second aspect..." → b, "A further challenge..." → c, "And lastly..." → d. Signalni eshitsangiz, ko'zingiz keyingi bandga o'tsin.

Section 4 distraktorlari: 1) raqamlar — ikki raqam aytiladi, biri boshqa narsa haqida ("invested 10 million dollars" — investitsiya, "earnings of over 6.3 billion" — daromad); 2) yaqin so'z — natija va usul ("realistic-looking water" — natija, "digital lighting" — usul); 3) notes'da BOR so'z — "skin and ___": skin allaqachon yozilgan, javob — ikkinchi narsa (facial movement).

So'z chegarasi: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER. "6.3 billion" — raqam + so'z, ruxsat. "hand-painted" — defisli so'z bitta so'z. "more detailed facial movement" — uch so'z, 0 ball. Qavsdagi so'z ixtiyoriy: (animal) fur — "fur" ham to'g'ri.

Band 7 uchun: Section 4 da parafraz ko'p. Notes: "believable simulations of people and ___" — audio: "credible human characters and advances in the simulation of crowds". Notes: "a move from ___ to new concepts" — audio: "reality has been the goal ... now ... other concepts". Ma'noni tinglang, so'zni emas.
formulas: Har bo'shliq uchun so'z turini yozing
Transfer: so'z soni, defis, imlo, ko'plik
presentation: Section 4 da pauza bo'lmasa, qachon o'qiyman?
Faqat boshidagi tayyorlanish vaqtida. Shuning uchun 1–10 ni birdaniga ko'rib chiqing va har bo'shliq yoniga so'z turini qisqa yozing (n, pl, adj, №).
Bitta bo'shliqni o'tkazib yubordim. Nima qilaman?
To'xtamang — keyingi sarlavha yoki ismni kuting. Oxirida bashorat qilgan so'z turingiz bo'yicha eng mantiqli javobni yozing, bo'sh qoldirmang.
"6.3 billion" ni qanday yozaman?
Raqam + so'z: "6.3 billion". "$" va "dollars" notes'da bor — takrorlamang. Raqamlar bilan yozish so'z bilan yozishdan xavfsizroq.
"hand-painted" ikki so'zmi?
Yo'q, defisli so'z bitta so'z hisoblanadi. Kalitda "hand painted" ham qabul qilingan.
Ma'ruzachi "water" ham, "digital lighting" ham dedi. Qaysi biri?
Notes: "new techniques in ___" — texnika (usul) kerak. "Water" — texnika bilan yaratilgan natija.
Katta harf muhimmi?
Yo'q, Listening'da katta-kichik harf ball olib qo'ymaydi. Lekin imlo — ha: "lightning" (chaqmoq) ≠ "lighting" (yoritish).
notes: 7.0 guruhi note completion'ni 6.0 da (11-dars, Section 1) va shu kursning 8-darsida (Section 4) ishlagan. Bugungi urg'u — raqam distraktorlari (pul, foiz, yil) va xronologik notes (WB: 1980s → 1990s → 2000+). Asosiy ko'nikma — uzun ma'ruzada (6 daqiqa) diqqatni yo'qotmaslik va parafrazni tanish. SB audiosi ~6 daqiqa, WB — 4,5 daqiqa, 12 savol.
SB audiosi boshida "Unit 6, Listening, Exercise 3" e'loni bor (kitob sarlavhasi kesilgan). E'londan keyin 1 daqiqa tayyorlanish vaqtini bering, keyin davom ettiring.

Tekshiruvda har javobdan keyin skriptdan aynan o'sha gapni ekranga chiqaring; signal iborani bir rang, distraktorni boshqa rang bilan ko'rsating. Kuchli o'quvchilarga: SB Vocabulary 1-mashqidagi 7 ta kollokatsiyani skriptdan topish.
mistakes: 10 million — Steve Jobs investitsiyasi, daromad emas
8-savolga "skin and facial movement" yoki "more detailed facial movement"
skin notes'da bor; uch so'z — 0 ball
62 — AQSh va Britaniya; "in one country" — Shvetsiya, 90

how: CORE — texnologiya va bank sohasidagi asosiy so'zlar; STRONG — ma'ruza uslubidagi fe'l va sifatlar; SUPER — tarixiy o'zgarishni tasvirlovchi idiomalar. Takror (8-dars): take off — yangi so'z sifatida sanalmaydi; WB Track 10 tekshiruvidan keyin skriptdagi "when the Internet took off" gapida eslating (audio imtihon rejimida to'xtatilmaydi).
Har o'quvchi o'zi biladigan bitta texnologiya (smartfon, onlayn-do'kon, o'yin) tarixi haqida 3 gap aytadi va kamida ikkita SUPER ibora ishlatadi: "Online shopping really took off in the 2010s."

Kompyuter animatsiyasi qo'lda chizilgan filmlarni siqib chiqardi.

class_ex.title: Bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerak? (SB, 2-mashq)
class_ex.instr: Tinglashdan oldin SB 67-betdagi 1–10 bo'shliqlarga qarang. Har biri uchun so'z turini va qanday ma'lumot kerakligini ayting.
items: 1 — "used many ___ of faces"
2 — "cut-outs made of ___"
3 — "used ___ slides"
4 — "Over $___ worldwide"
5 — "included ___ as a new animation feature"
6 — "new techniques in ___"
7 — "believable simulations of people and ___"
8 — "focusing particularly on skin and ___"
9 — "companies producing ___ will help"
10 — "a move from ___ to new concepts"
answers: ot — Monsters, Inc. dagi yangi element
ot — ekranda ishonarli bo'lishi kerak narsa
ot (birlik yoki ko'plik) — boshqa turdagi kompaniya mahsuloti
why: "many ___ of faces" — "many" dan keyin ko'plik. Kalit: plural noun, something to do with faces.
"made of" dan keyin material nomi keladi.
Ot (slides) oldida — sifat yoki sifatdosh.
"$" belgisi va "Over" — pul miqdori, raqam.
"included ___ as a new feature" — ot.
"techniques in ___" — soha yoki texnika nomi, ot.
"people and ___" — "people" ga o'xshash ot (ko'plik bo'lishi mumkin).
"skin and ___" — teri kabi insonning yana bir jihati.
"companies producing ___" — mahsulot nomi.
"a move from ___ to new concepts" — "new concepts" ga qarama-qarshi uslub.
class_ex.note: SB 2-mashqning 1–2-savollarini ham so'rang: ma'ruza qaysi uch mavzuni qamraydi (tarix, Pixar, kelajak) va notes tuzilmasi qanday yordam beradi (sarlavhalar, chap ustun, bo'shliq atrofidagi so'zlar).

class_ex.title: Qaysi raqam javob?
class_ex.instr: Ustoz qisqa ma'ruza parchasini o'qiydi, o'quvchilar notes'dagi bo'shliqqa to'g'ri raqamni aytadi va qolgan raqam(lar) nega tuzoq ekanini tushuntiradi.
items: "The company was bought for 20 million dollars; today its products earn over 4 billion a year." — Notes: Annual earnings: over $___
"The first model weighed 30 kilograms. The second, launched two years later, weighed just 12." — Notes: Weight of second model: ___ kg
"Tickets originally cost 5 pounds, and today they cost 9 — sorry, I mean 8 pounds." — Notes: Current ticket price: £___
"We expected about 200 participants — in the end, 340 people came." — Notes: Actual number of participants: ___
"About a third of users are teenagers, although in Japan the figure is closer to half." — Notes: In one country, almost ___ of users are teenagers
why: 20 million — sotib olish narxi, daromad emas. SB 4-savol xuddi shunday: 10 million (investitsiya) ↔ 6.3 billion (daromad).
30 kg — birinchi model. "The second" — kalit so'z.

5 — eski narx ("originally"); 9 — adashib aytilgan raqam, ma'ruzachi uni darrov tuzatdi ("sorry, I mean"). IELTS'da javob raqami aynan aytiladi, hisoblash talab qilinmaydi. Tuzatish signallarini kuting: "sorry, I mean / or rather / actually" — javob tuzatishdan KEYINGI raqam.
200 — kutilgan son. "In the end" — haqiqiy natija signali.
"In one country" — Yaponiya; a third — umumiy. WB 8-savolda xuddi shu tuzilma bor.
class_ex.note: Doskadagi "Distraktorlar" ustuniga yozing: bought for / expected / originally / the first / tuzatishdan oldingi raqam ("sorry, I mean ...") → odatda javob EMAS.

listenings.title: Jony Academy mashqi: Barcodes and QR codes
listenings.qtype: Note completion — Section 4 (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER)
intro: "Everyday technology" ma'ruzalar seriyasidan: shtrix-kod va QR-kod tarixi. Ustoz ma'ruzachi sifatida tabiiy tezlikda, javob so'zlariga urg'u bermasdan o'qiydi, BIR MARTA. Boshida 45 soniya tayyorlanish vaqti bering.
Notes'ni o'quvchilarga oldindan tarqating (yoki doskaga yozing). Ma'ruza o'rtasida to'xtamang — Section 4 dagidek.
transcript: LECTURER: Good afternoon, everyone. In this series on everyday technology, we're looking at inventions that most of us use several times a day without ever noticing them. Today's subject is the barcode, and its younger relative, the QR code. I'll start with where the idea came from, then look at how barcodes changed shopping, and finish with QR codes.

LECTURER: The story begins in 1948 in Philadelphia. A graduate student called Bernard Silver overheard the president of a local food chain asking a university dean for help. The businessman wanted a system that would record product information automatically at the checkout. The dean wasn't interested, but Silver mentioned the conversation to a friend, Norman Joseph Woodland, and the two of them began working on the problem.

LECTURER: Woodland's key idea came to him, so the story goes, while he was sitting on a beach in Florida. Now, you might expect an engineer to take his inspiration from something technical, like a telegraph machine or a punched card. In fact, it came from something he had learned as a Boy Scout: Morse code. He drew its dots and dashes in the sand with his fingers, and when he pulled his fingers down towards him, the dots and dashes became thin and thick lines. That, essentially, is a barcode: information stored in lines of different widths.

LECTURER: Interestingly, the first design didn't use straight lines at all. Woodland and Silver bent the lines into a series of circles, one inside another, so it looked rather like the target you'd see in archery. The advantage was that it could be read from any direction. They applied for a patent in 1949, and it was finally granted in 1952.

LECTURER: But there was a serious problem. To read the code, you needed a very bright, narrow beam of light, and a computer to make sense of the result. Neither was cheap. One early experiment used an enormous light bulb, which got so hot that it was hardly practical. It wasn't until lasers became available, and gradually more affordable, that a scanner at a supermarket checkout made any sense. So the idea waited for about twenty years.

LECTURER: Moving on to the Universal Product Code. In 1973, a committee representing the American grocery industry chose a single standard. Several companies submitted designs, including a circular one, but the committee picked a rectangular design produced by an engineer at IBM. One reason was a practical one: circular codes tended to smudge when they were printed at high speed, because the ink spread in the direction the paper was moving, and a smudged code couldn't be read.

LECTURER: The first product ever scanned at a real checkout was in a supermarket in Ohio in June 1974. People often assume it must have been something important, perhaps a bottle of milk or a loaf of bread. In fact, it was a ten-pack of chewing gum, which is now kept in a museum.

LECTURER: Now, what did shops gain from all this? Most people would say faster checkouts, and yes, queues did move a little more quickly. But the real benefit for retailers was something customers never saw: much more accurate stock control. For the first time, a shop knew exactly what had been sold and when, so it could reorder goods before the shelves were empty. Not everyone was happy, though. Consumer groups worried that if prices were no longer marked on each item, shoppers would be overcharged.

LECTURER: Finally, QR codes. QR stands for 'quick response', and the code was developed in Japan in 1994 by a company that supplied the motor industry. Its original purpose was to track car parts as they moved through the factory. Workers had been scanning several ordinary barcodes on every box, because a barcode can hold only around twenty characters, and the company wanted a code that held far more information and could be read quickly.

LECTURER: The engineer who designed it has said that the idea for the pattern came to him while he was playing the board game Go, which uses black and white stones on a grid. Some people assume the black and white squares come from chess, but that isn't the case. Three large squares in the corners tell the scanner where the code is, so it can be read from any angle.

LECTURER: Crucially, the company decided not to charge anyone for using the code, so anyone could create one free of charge. Even so, for many years QR codes were popular mainly in Japan. Elsewhere, people had to download a special app to scan them, and most didn't bother. That changed once smartphone cameras could read the codes without any special app. Today you'll find them on restaurant menus, concert tickets and even shop windows.
LECTURER: Right, next week we'll look at another invention that changed shopping: the credit card.

tasks.title: Questions 1–10 — Barcodes and QR codes
tasks.type: Complete the notes below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
tasks.instr: Sarlavhalar: Origins → The Universal Product Code → QR codes. Distraktorlarni kuting: "you might expect...", "people often assume...", "most people would say...".
why: "In fact, it came from something he had learned as a Boy Scout: Morse code". Tuzoq: "a telegraph machine or a punched card" — kutilgan, lekin rad etilgan.
"so it looked rather like the target you'd see in archery".
"They applied for a patent in 1949, and it was finally granted in 1952". 1949 — ariza yili, tuzoq.
"It wasn't until lasers became available ... that a scanner ... made any sense". Tuzoq: "light bulb" — amaliy bo'lmagan.
"circular codes tended to smudge when they were printed at high speed". Notes: "tended to ___" — fe'l kerak.
"In fact, it was a ten-pack of chewing gum". Tuzoq: "a bottle of milk or a loaf of bread" — odamlar taxmini.
"But the real benefit for retailers was ... much more accurate stock control". Tuzoq: "faster checkouts".
"Its original purpose was to track car parts as they moved through the factory".
"while he was playing the board game Go". Tuzoq: chess — rad etilgan.
"That changed once smartphone cameras could read the codes without any special app".
tasks.note: Bu mashqdagi distraktorlarning hammasi bitta shaklda: avval kutilgan yoki odatiy fikr ("you might expect", "people often assume", "most people would say"), keyin "In fact / But the real..." bilan haqiqiy javob. Doskadagi "Signal iboralar" ustuniga qo'shing.
head: Bo'lim
Eslatma (notes)
rows: 1948: a food-chain president wanted product information recorded automatically at the checkout ;; Woodland's inspiration: (1) code, drawn in the sand on a beach ;; First design: a set of circles, like an archery (2) ;; Patent granted: (3) ;; No practical way to read codes until (4) became available and affordable

1973: grocery industry chose a rectangular design from IBM ;; Circular codes rejected because they tended to (5) when printed at speed ;; June 1974: first item scanned — a pack of (6) ;; Main benefit for shops: much more accurate (7)
1994: developed in Japan to track (8) in factories ;; Square pattern inspired by the board game (9) ;; Free to use, but spread worldwide only when (10) could read them without a special app

homework_intro: Bugun Section 4 ma'ruzasida note completion'ni ishladik: notes tuzilmasi bo'yicha reja tuzish, so'z turini bashorat qilish, signal iboralar va raqam distraktorlari. Eng ko'p ball uch joyda yo'qoladi: ikkinchi raqamni yozish, natijani usul o'rniga yozish va notes'dagi so'zni takrorlab so'z chegarasini buzish.

Birinchi vazifa — kollokatsiyalar: Student's Book, 68-bet, Vocabulary 2-mashq (1-mashqdagi kollokatsiyalar bilan 5 gap) va Workbook, 39-bet, Vocabulary 1-mashq (film sharhi, 5 bo'shliq). Javoblarni SB 177-bet va WB 67-bet kalitlari bilan tekshiring.

Ikkinchi vazifa — diktant: WB Track 10 ning birinchi qismini ("Now, believe it or not..." dan "...most of those were businesses" gacha) tinglang va to'liq yozing. Audio va skript parchasi guruh chatida (ustoz dars oxirida yuboradi). Skriptni faqat diktantni yozib bo'lgach oching. Skript bilan o'zingiz tekshiring, xatolarni qizil bilan belgilang va xatolar sonini diktant ostiga yozing.

Uchinchi vazifa — shadowing: SB CD2 Track 1 ning oxirgi qismini ("So how do companies like Pixar plan to meet the challenges of the future?" dan oxirigacha; audio parcha guruh chatida) 3 marta tinglang, keyin ma'ruzachi bilan bir vaqtda takrorlang. Signal iboralar (firstly, a second aspect, a further challenge, lastly) aniq eshitilsin. Oxirgi urinishni ovozli xabar qilib guruhga yuboring.

homework.title: SB 68-bet Vocabulary 2-mashq + WB 39-bet Vocabulary 1-mashq

A phone call to book a service
A tour guide talks to tourists
kahoot.explain: Section 4 — bitta gapiruvchi, akademik ma'ruza. Section 3 — o'quv suhbati, Section 1 — kundalik dialog, Section 2 — umumiy monolog.

kahoot.q: Is there usually a pause in the middle of Section 4?
options: No, so read all the notes before it starts
Yes, a short pause after every heading
Only if the talk is longer than five minutes
kahoot.explain: Section 4 da o'rtada pauza yo'q. Tayyorlanish vaqtida 1–10 ni birdaniga ko'rib, so'z turini belgilang.

kahoot.q: Notes: 'Earnings: Over $___ worldwide'. You hear: 'earnings of over 6.3 billion dollars'. What do you write?
kahoot.explain: "Over" va "$" notes'da bor. Faqat "6.3 billion" — raqam + bir so'z, chegaraga mos.

kahoot.q: 'Steve Jobs invested 10 million dollars... earnings of over 6.3 billion.' Why is '10 million' wrong for 'Earnings'?
options: It is an investment, not earnings
It is too small to be true
It is not a round number
The lecturer corrects this figure later
kahoot.explain: Ikki raqam — ikki xil narsa. Notes'dagi so'z (Earnings) qaysi raqamga tegishli ekanini tinglang.

kahoot.q: Limit: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER. Which answer is NOT acceptable?
kahoot.explain: Uch so'z — 0 ball. Defisli so'z (hand-painted) bitta so'z; "6.3 billion" — raqam + so'z.

kahoot.q: Notes: 'focusing particularly on skin and ___'. You hear: 'realistic human skin and more detailed facial movement'.
kahoot.explain: "skin" notes'da bor — takrorlanmaydi. "detailed" qo'shilsa, ma'no to'g'ri, lekin chegara buziladi.

kahoot.q: Notes: 'Finding Nemo – new techniques in ___'. You hear 'digital lighting' and 'realistic-looking water'.
kahoot.explain: "techniques in ___" — usul so'raladi. Digital lighting — usul, water — shu usul bilan yaratilgan natija.

kahoot.q: The lecturer says 'A second aspect that Pixar hope to improve on is...'. What does this tell you?
options: Move to the next point (b) in the notes
The lecturer is about to summarise the talk
Go back to the History section
kahoot.explain: Firstly → a, A second aspect → b, A further challenge → c, And lastly → d. Signal ko'zingizni keyingi bandga olib o'tadi.

kahoot.q: Notes: 'Early banking required a computer, a monitor and a ___'. What type of answer do you expect?
options: A number such as a year
A verb in the past simple tense
kahoot.explain: "a" artikli — birlikdagi sanaladigan ot. Javob: phone line.

kahoot.q: Notes: 'As many as ___ of bank customers banking online in one country'. You hear 62% (US/UK) and 90% (Sweden).
kahoot.explain: "In one country" — Shvetsiya: up to 90 percent. 62 percent — ikki davlat bo'yicha umumiy raqam.

kahoot.q: Which spelling of the answer to SB question 6 is correct?
kahoot.explain: lighting — yoritish; lightning — chaqmoq. Imlo xatosi javobni butunlay noto'g'ri qiladi.

kahoot.q: Do capital letters matter in IELTS Listening answers?
options: Yes — every answer must be written in capitals
Only the first word of each answer needs a capital
Only numbers and dates need a special format
kahoot.explain: Katta-kichik harf ball olib qo'ymaydi; ko'pchilik barcha javobni bosh harflarda yozadi — bu xavfsiz.

kahoot.q: Finding Nemo ___ new techniques in digital lighting.
kahoot.explain: pioneer — birinchi bo'lib joriy qilmoq.

kahoot.q: The on-screen fur helped to ___ the appeal of one of the central characters.
kahoot.explain: enhance the appeal — jozibasini oshirmoq.

kahoot.q: Studios hope to create ___ digital actors that audiences like.
kahoot.explain: convincing — ishonarli; "robotic" ning teskarisi.

kahoot.q: Online banking first appeared in the USA, and the idea soon ___ in other countries.
kahoot.explain: catch on — ommalashmoq, keng tarqalmoq.

kahoot.q: The Internet really ___ in the 1990s, when more people bought computers.
kahoot.explain: take off — keskin o'sib, muvaffaqiyat qozonmoq.

kahoot.q: Many consumers were ___ to carry out financial transactions online.
kahoot.explain: reluctant = hesitant — istamaydigan, ikkilanadigan.

kahoot.q: Three million payments were worth ___ one billion dollars.
kahoot.explain: in excess of — ...dan ortiq (more than). WB notes'dagi ibora.

kahoot.q: Pixar now wants to ___ and create films that don't look real.
kahoot.explain: break new ground — yangi yo'l ochmoq, avval qilinmagan narsani qilmoq.

lessons.title: Unit 7 Reading — Passage 2: Matching headings + Sentence completion + Multiple choice (TWO letters)
lessons.grammar_topic: Uch savol turi bitta passage'da: Matching headings (7 bo'lim) + Sentence completion (NMT3W) + Choose TWO letters
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 7 (Our relationship with nature) — changlatuvchilar, ekotizim, keystone species, yirtqich va o'lja
lessons.book_ref: Complete IELTS Bands 6.5–7.5: Student's Book, Unit 7, 77–79-betlar (Reading Section 2: "Gold dusters"); Workbook, Unit 7, 44–46-betlar (Reading Section 2: "Keystone species"). Practice 1–3 — Jony Academy matnlari.
objectives: Passage 2 da uch savol turi kelganda vaqtni rejalash: headings ~10 daqiqa, sentence completion ~4, TWO letters ~4, tekshirish ~2 daqiqa.

Matching headings'da 7 bo'limning asosiy g'oyasini tafsilotdan ajratish; Band 7 darajasidagi abstrakt sarlavhalarni ("An unexpected setback", "The undesirable alternative") matndagi misollarga bog'lash.
Sentence completion'da NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS qoidasini aniq bajarish: ko'plik -s, qo'sh harf, yetishmagan so'z va gapdagi paraphrase qilingan so'zni takrorlamaslik.
Choose TWO letters savolida javoblar matnning ikki xil joyida bo'lishi mumkinligini hisobga olib, headings xaritasidan foydalanish.
Ekologiya mavzusidagi Band 7 lug'atini (pollinator, keystone species, decline, thrive, far-reaching) passage ichida tanish va ishlatish.
materials: Student's Book, Unit 7, 77–79-betlar ("Gold dusters" by Jennifer S. Holland) — sinfda birga ishlanadi (quyida rasm).
Workbook, Unit 7, 44–46-betlar ("Keystone species") — mustaqil mashq (quyida rasm).
Practice 1–3 matnlari chop etilgan varaqlar (har o'quvchiga) — pastdagi Reading bo'limidan.
Rangli qalamlar: sarlavha kalit so'zlari — bir rang, sentence completion kalit g'oyasi — ikkinchi rang.
Doskada jadval: "Bo'lim → asosiy g'oya (3–4 so'z) → sarlavha" — xarita uchun; yonida "10 + 4 + 4 + 2 daqiqa" rejasi.

Uch savol turi birga
