intro: Band 6.5–7.5 darajasidagi Passage 2 da uch savol turi ketma-ket keladi: Matching headings (1–7), Sentence completion (8–11) va Choose TWO letters (12–13). Kitob kaliti tavsiya qilgan vaqt: headings — 10 daqiqa, sentence completion — 4, pick from a list — 4 daqiqa. Qolgan 2 daqiqa — tekshirish va transfer.

TARTIB: bo'limlarni o'z tartibida yeching (SB 1-mashq: "Do the tasks in the order they occur"). Headings topshirig'i sizni butun matnni bo'limma-bo'lim o'qishga majbur qiladi — shu o'qish paytida har bo'lim chetiga 3–4 so'zlik asosiy g'oyani yozing. Bu XARITA keyingi ikki topshiriqda joyni 10 soniyada topishga yordam beradi.

HEADINGS 7.0 da: sarlavhalar abstrakt va matndagi so'zlarni takrorlamaydi. "An unexpected setback" (kutilmagan zarba) — matnda "in 2006 came an extreme blow"; "The undesirable alternative" — matnda "our lives would be dictated by the wind". Sarlavha misollarni UMUMLASHTIRADI — shuning uchun avval "Bu bo'lim nima haqida?" savoliga o'z so'zingiz bilan javob bering, keyin ro'yxatga qarang.

Ro'yxatda 10 sarlavha, 7 bo'lim — 3 tasi ortiqcha. Ortiqcha sarlavhalar ko'pincha bo'limdagi bitta TAFSILOTga mos keladi ("Discovering a new bee species" — B da 20 000 tur tilga olinadi, lekin yangi tur kashfiyoti haqida gap yo'q) yoki matnda umuman yo'q g'oyani beradi ("Blaming the beekeepers").

SENTENCE COMPLETION (NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS): gaplar matn tartibida. Javob matndan AYNAN ko'chiriladi. SB 5-mashqi (REASONS FOR LOSING MARKS) 5 ta ball yo'qotish sababini beradi: a) ko'plik o'rniga birlik (coat — coats), b) qo'sh harfni tushirib qoldirish (fury — furry), c) ikki javobdan birini yozmaslik (flies — flies and beetles), d) gapdagi paraphrase so'zni takrorlash (travel longer distances — gapda "travel" bor), e) muhim so'zni tashlab ketish (bees — worker bees).

CHOOSE TWO LETTERS: javoblar matnning bir yoki bir necha joyida bo'lishi mumkin (SB: 12 — F bo'lim, 13 — G bo'lim). Headings xaritasidan foydalaning: savol "methods of combating the problems" haqida — demak yechimlar bo'limi (F) va xulosa (G). Har variantni to'rt toifaga ajrating: BOR, TESKARI (D — farmlarni kattalashtirish — aksincha, muammo sababi), AYTILMAGAN (A, B), SAVOLGA TEGISHLI EMAS.

Band 7 uchun muhim: matndagi kuchli paraphrase'lar — "bolster populations" = ko'paytirmoq, "ease the burden on managed bees" = asalarilarga kamroq tayanmoq (E), "a menace to" = xavf. Bu so'zlarni tanimasangiz, to'g'ri joyni topsangiz ham javobni tanlay olmaysiz.
formulas: Bo'lim → o'z so'zingiz bilan asosiy g'oya → sarlavha
Sentence completion: kalit g'oya + so'z turi
flies and beetles / furry coats / worker bees
C — BOR, E — BOR, D — TESKARI
presentation: Sarlavhadagi so'z bo'limda yo'q. Qanday topaman?
Band 7 da bu normal. Bo'limning vazifasini aniqlang: muammo? yechim? misollar ro'yxati? tarix? Keyin shu vazifaga mos sarlavhani izlang.
Ikkita sarlavha bitta bo'limga mos keladi. Nima qilaman?
Ikkalasini qalam bilan yozib qo'ying va keyingi bo'limlarga o'ting. Oxirida qolgan sarlavhalar orasidan eng umumiysini tanlang — bittasi odatda boshqa bo'limga aniqroq mos keladi.
NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS — bitta so'z yozsam bo'ladimi?
Ha, 1, 2 yoki 3 so'z. Lekin muhim so'zni tashlab ketmang: "bees" emas, "worker bees".
"(furry) coats" — qavs nimani bildiradi?
Kalitda qavsdagi so'z ixtiyoriy: "coats" ham, "furry coats" ham to'g'ri. Lekin "coat" (birlik) — 0 ball.
TWO letters javoblari bitta bo'limdami?
Shart emas. SB da 12 — F, 13 — G bo'limda. Shuning uchun headings xaritasi juda foydali.
Qiyin savolda javob topolmadim. Bo'sh qoldiraymi?
Yo'q — taxmin qiling. Noto'g'ri javob uchun ball olib tashlanmaydi (SB 1-mashq, 5).
notes: 6.0 da headings + TWO letters va headings + sentence completion juftliklarini alohida ishlagan edik. 7.0 da uchalasi birga, passage uzunroq (≈900 so'z) va sarlavhalar abstrakt — asosiy ko'nikma vaqtni boshqarish.
SB matnini ishlashda har bo'limdan keyin to'xtab so'rang: "Bu bo'lim nima QILADI — muammo, sabab, yechim yoki misol beradimi?" Band 7 sarlavhalari ko'pincha shu funksiyani nomlaydi.
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: ishlatilmagan sarlavhalar (ii, iv, vii) nega mos kelmasligini matndan isbotlash.
Sinf mashqidagi 5 sabab (a–e) — SB 5-mashqidagi aniq ro'yxat (REASONS FOR LOSING MARKS). Uni doskada qoldiring va Practice'larni tekshirishda har xatoga harf qo'ying.
mistakes: B bo'limga iv ("Discovering a new bee species")
viii Some obvious and less obvious pollen carriers
20 000 tur — tafsilot; bo'lim changlatuvchilar xilma-xilligi haqida
Kimya, virus, zamburug' — sabab izlanadi; asalarichilar ayblanmaydi
Ko'plik -s va qo'sh r (a, b sabablari)
12–13 ga D ("increasing the size of many farms")
Katta monokultura farmlari — muammo sababi, yechim emas

how: CORE — tabiat va ekologiya mavzusidagi asosiy so'zlar; STRONG — passage'lardagi ilmiy so'zlar; SUPER — Band 7 iboralari.
Har o'quvchi o'z hududidagi bitta hayvon yoki o'simlik haqida 3 gap tuzadi va kamida 3 ta yangi so'z ishlatadi: "Bees are vital pollinators, but their numbers are in decline."
core: Bees are the best-known pollinators, but flies and beetles also do the job.
Asalarilar eng mashhur changlatuvchilar, lekin pashsha va qo'ng'izlar ham bu ishni qiladi.
Habitat loss is a greater threat to bees than disease.
Yashash muhitining yo'qolishi asalarilar uchun kasallikdan ham kattaroq xavf.
Scientists have identified about 20,000 species of bee.
Olimlar asalarining 20 mingga yaqin turini aniqlagan.
Removing one species can change the whole ecosystem.
Bitta turni yo'q qilish butun ekotizimni o'zgartirishi mumkin.
Paine observed a dramatic decline in species diversity.
Paine turlar xilma-xilligining keskin kamayishini kuzatdi.
The sea otter is a keystone predator in the North Pacific.
Dengiz qunduzi Shimoliy Tinch okeanidagi asosiy yirtqichdir.
Tiny organisms play a huge role in protecting biodiversity.
Mayda organizmlar biologik xilma-xillikni himoya qilishda katta rol o'ynaydi.
By the end of the 17th century, the dodo was extinct.
XVII asr oxiriga kelib dodo qushi yo'qolib ketgan edi.
Wolves were reintroduced to the park in the 1990s.
At least a hundred crops rely on managed honeybees.
Kamida yuzta ekin boqiladigan asalarilarga tayanadi.
strong: The starfish turned out to be a keystone species.
Dengiz yulduzi ekotizimning tayanch turi bo'lib chiqdi.
Viral and fungal pathogens may work together.
Virus va zamburug' qo'zg'atuvchilar birgalikda ta'sir qilishi mumkin.
Geckos carry pollen on their feet as they forage.
Gekkonlar oziq izlaganda changni oyoqlarida tashiydi.
Pioneer trees thrive in full sunlight.
Kashshof daraxtlar to'liq quyosh nurida yaxshi o'sadi.
Wildflower havens would bolster insect populations.
Yovvoyi gul maskanlari hasharotlar sonini ko'paytiradi.
Ravens feed on the carcasses that wolves leave behind.
Qarg'alar bo'rilar qoldirgan o'liklar bilan oziqlanadi.
super: It's hard to tease apart the factors behind CCD.
CCD ortidagi omillarni bir-biridan ajratish qiyin.
Poor nutrition might wear down a bee's immunity.
Yomon oziqlanish asalarining immunitetini asta-sekin zaiflashtirishi mumkin.
The loss of one species can have far-reaching consequences.
Bitta turning yo'qolishi keng ko'lamli oqibatlarga olib kelishi mumkin.
A species may seem unimportant in isolation.
Alohida olganda tur ahamiyatsiz ko'rinishi mumkin.

class_ex.title: Reading test bo'yicha maslahatlar (SB, Reading 1-mashq)
class_ex.instr: Har gapda to'g'ri variantni ayting va nega shunday ekanini bir gapda tushuntiring.
items: 1 Do the sections in the order in which they come / of your choice.
2 Spend a maximum of / more than 20 minutes on each of the first two sections.
3 Leave any tasks you do not like until last. / Do the tasks in the order they occur.
4 Answers that consist of letters should also / need not be written out in full.
5 If a question is too difficult, leave a blank / guess the answer.
6 You must / need not use correct spelling.
answers: Do the tasks in the order they occur.
why: Passage'lar qiyinlik bo'yicha tartiblangan — oson matndan boshlash foydali.
Butun test 60 daqiqa; birinchi ikki bo'limda vaqtni cheklasangiz, eng qiyin Section 3 ga to'liq 20 daqiqa qoladi.
Har savolni matn yodingizda turganda yeching; keyinroq qaytishga vaqt bo'lmaydi.
Faqat completion javoblari to'liq yoziladi; harflar va T/F/NG yetarli — to'liq yozish vaqt yo'qotadi.
Noto'g'ri javob uchun ball olinmaydi — taxmin qilsangiz, to'g'ri chiqishi mumkin.
Imlo xatosi bo'lgan javob 0 ball.
class_ex.note: Kitob kaliti bo'yicha. 2-bandni bugungi darsning vaqt rejasi bilan bog'lang: 20 daqiqa = 10 + 4 + 4 + 2.

class_ex.title: Nega 0 ball? (SB, Reading 5-mashq asosida)
class_ex.instr: Bu javoblar SB 8–11-savollarga yozilgan. Har biri uchun ball yo'qotish sababini tanlang: a) birlik o'rniga ko'plik kerak; b) qo'sh harf tushib qolgan; c) ikki javobdan biri yo'q; d) gapdagi paraphrase so'z takrorlangan; e) muhim so'z tashlab ketilgan.
items: 8 Both ___ were the first creatures to pollinate the world's plants. — flies
9 Monkeys transport pollen on their ___ . — coat
9 Monkeys transport pollen on their ___ . — fury coats
10 Honeybees ... partly because they travel ___ . — travel longer distances
11 A feature of CCD is often the loss of all the ___ . — bees
11 A feature of CCD is often the loss of all the ___ . — worker bee
why: "Both" — ikki xil jonzot: "Flies and beetles are the original pollinators". To'g'ri: flies and beetles.
"their" — maymunlar ko'p, demak "furry coats to which pollen sticks" — ko'plik: (furry) coats.
Matnda "furry" — ikki r. Bitta harf xatosi — 0 ball.

"travel" gapda allaqachon bor; javob faqat (longer) distances. "travel longer distances" — 3 so'z, chegaraga sig'adi; xato sababi — takror (d). Matndagi "cover longer distances" yozilsa ham xuddi shu d xatosi: gapda "cover" "travel" bilan paraphrase qilingan.
Matnda "the worker bees gone" — "worker" so'zisiz javob to'liq emas: qirolicha ham asalari.
"all the ___" — ko'plik kerak: worker bees.
class_ex.note: Bu mashqning kaliti (bandlar tartibida): flies — c; coat — a; fury coats — b; travel longer distances — d; bees — e; worker bee — a. Ma'lumot uchun: kitobdagi 5-mashq boshqa savol beradi — "8–11-savollarga qaysi sabablar tegishli bo'lishi mumkin?"; uning kaliti sabab → savol raqamlari: a — 8, 9, 10, 11; b — 8, 9, 11; c — 8; d — 10; e — 9, 11 (bu yuqoridagi bandlarning javobi emas). Mashqdan keyin shu 5 sababni doskada qoldiring — Practice'larni tekshirishda ishlatiladi.

readings.title: Student's Book: Gold dusters
readings.qtype: Matching headings (1–7) + Sentence completion (8–11) + Choose TWO letters (12–13)
readings.source: Complete IELTS 6.5–7.5, Student's Book, Unit 7 — sinfda tushuntirish
readings.book_ref: Student's Book, 77–79-betlar (Reading Section 2). Kitob sahifalari quyida rasm sifatida; ro'yxatda 10 sarlavha — 3 tasi ortiqcha.
paraphrases: An impossible task for any human
Growers have tried numerous ways ... But natural means seem to work better
some obvious and less obvious pollen carriers
bees ... Even non-flying mammals ... Most surprising, some lizards
the preferred pollinator
a hundred commercial crops rely almost entirely on managed honeybees
an unexpected setback
in 2006 came an extreme blow
looking for clues
It's hard to tease apart factors and outcomes
a more troublesome issue
even more of a menace to pollinators than pathogens
the undesirable alternative
our lives would be dictated by the wind
cultivating a wide range of flowering plants
hedgerows and patches of native flowers ... multiple plant species
placing less reliance on honeybees
ease the burden on managed bees by letting native animals do their part

tasks.title: 2-mashq: skimming va vaqt
tasks.type: Choose A, B or C
tasks.instr: 2–3 daqiqada matnni ko'zdan kechiring: qaysi variant asosiy mavzuni eng yaxshi beradi?
items: Main topic: A) where pollinators are most widely used  B) how honeybee losses have affected plant growth  C) why we need to encourage a wider range of pollinators
why: A va B matnda tilga olinadi, lekin asosiy g'oya emas; oxirgi bo'lim: "It's vital that we give pollinators more of what they need ... letting native animals do their part". Kalit bo'yicha vaqt: headings 10, sentences 4, pick from a list 4 daqiqa.

tasks.title: Questions 1–7
tasks.type: Matching headings — uchta sarlavha ortiqcha
tasks.instr: Avval sarlavhalar ro'yxatidagi kalit g'oyalarning tagiga chizing. Keyin har bo'limni o'qib, uning ASOSIY g'oyasini o'zbekcha bir gapda ayting va mos sarlavhani tanlang. Ro'yxatda uchta ortiqcha sarlavha bor.
items: 1 Section A
2 Section B
3 Section C
4 Section D
5 Section E
6 Section F
7 Section G
answers: v An impossible task for any human
viii Some obvious and less obvious pollen carriers
iii Solutions to a more troublesome issue
why: Pomidor guli juda kuchli silkinishni talab qiladi; odamlar "shaking tables, air blowers and blasts of sound" ishlatgan, lekin "natural means seem to work better" — inson uddalay olmaydigan ish.

"What's astonishing is the array of workers": pashsha, qo'ng'iz, asalari (obvious), keyin opossum, maymun va "Most surprising, some lizards" (less obvious). iv tuzog'i: 20 000 tur — yangi tur kashfiyoti emas.
"A hundred commercial crops rely almost entirely on managed honeybees"; boshqa asalarilar samaraliroq bo'lsa ham, asalari katta koloniya, uzoq masofa va boshqaruvga chidamli.
"In 2006 came an extreme blow" — asalarilar qishda ommaviy yo'qolgan (CCD). Kutilmagan zarba = setback.
Sabab izlanadi: pestitsid, oziqlanish, fungitsid, virus va zamburug'. "It's hard to tease apart factors and outcomes". ii tuzog'i: asalarichilar ayblanmaydi — ayb kimyoviy moddalarga qo'yilgan.
"Habitat loss ... even more of a menace to pollinators than pathogens" (troublesome issue) va yechimlar: to'siq-butalar, mahalliy gullar, pestitsidsiz maskanlar.
Xilma-xillik yo'qolsa, faqat shamol changlatadigan ekinlar qoladi: "our lives would be dictated by the wind" — istalmagan muqobil.
tasks.note: Ishlatilmagan sarlavhalar: ii Blaming the beekeepers (matnda asalarichilar ayblanmaydi), iv Discovering a new bee species (tur kashfiyoti yo'q), vii Plant features designed to suit the pollinator (A da pomidor gulining xususiyati bor, lekin bo'lim inson urinishlari haqida). Kalit: 1 v, 2 viii, 3 vi, 4 x, 5 i, 6 iii, 7 ix.
box: iii Solutions to a more troublesome issue
iv Discovering a new bee species
v An impossible task for any human
vii Plant features designed to suit the pollinator
viii Some obvious and less obvious pollen carriers

tasks.title: Questions 8–11
tasks.type: Complete the sentences. Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage for each answer.
tasks.instr: Gaplar matn tartibida keladi. Kalit g'oya bilan joyni toping, javobni matndan AYNAN ko'chiring (NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS), keyin to'ldirilgan gapni grammatika bo'yicha qayta o'qing. 8–9 → B, 10 → C, 11 → D bo'lim.
items: 8 Both ___ were the first creatures to pollinate the world's plants.
9 Monkeys transport pollen on their ___ .
10 Honeybees are favoured pollinators among bee species partly because they travel ___ .
11 A feature of CCD is often the loss of all the ___ .
why: "Flies and beetles are the original pollinators". "First" = "original"; "Both" — ikkala jonzot yoziladi.
"Nimble hands that tear open flower stalks and furry coats to which pollen sticks". Ko'plik -s va qo'sh r.

readings.title: Practice 1: The return of the wolf
readings.qtype: Matching headings (1–7) + Sentence completion (8–11) + Choose TWO letters (12–13)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2 darajasi, Band 6.5–7.5)
text: A For most of the twentieth century, Yellowstone National Park had no wolves. The last known pack inside the park was killed in the 1920s, at a time when predators were seen as a threat to livestock and to the deer and elk that visitors came to see. Without wolves, the elk population grew rapidly. Large herds spent the winter in the river valleys, where they fed heavily on young willow and aspen. Along many streams, few young trees survived long enough to grow taller than an elk could reach, and some areas that had once been thick with shrubs were reduced to open grass. For decades, park staff tried to control the problem by shooting or removing elk, a policy that was finally abandoned in the late 1960s.

B Returning wolves to the park was debated for many years. Supporters argued that a national park should contain its full set of native species; opponents, especially ranchers on the land surrounding the park, feared that wolves would leave its boundaries and kill cattle and sheep. After long legal battles, 31 wolves were captured in Canada and released in the park in 1995 and 1996. They were first kept for several weeks in large fenced pens so that they would become used to their new surroundings rather than trying to return home. To reduce opposition, a conservation group agreed to pay ranchers for any animals lost to wolves.

C What happened next has become one of the best-known stories in ecology. As wolf numbers grew, elk numbers fell, and the elk that remained appeared to change their behaviour, spending less time in places where they could easily be trapped, such as narrow valleys. In some of these areas, young willows and aspens began to grow again. The returning trees provided food and building material for beavers, whose dams created ponds that in turn supported fish, frogs and insects. Birds that nest in riverside shrubs became more common. Scientists call this kind of chain reaction, in which a change at the top of a food chain spreads down through the levels below it, a 'trophic cascade'.

D Wolves also changed life for many animals that never hunt large prey at all. A wolf pack rarely eats an entire elk at once, and the carcasses they leave behind are visited by ravens, magpies, eagles and bears. Because wolves kill throughout the year, these animals have a more reliable supply of food. At the same time, wolves killed or drove away many coyotes, which had become the park's main predator in their absence. With fewer coyotes, some small mammals and the young of the pronghorn, a deer-like animal, appear to have had a better chance of survival.

E However, not all scientists accept the most dramatic version of this story. Some point out that the recovery of trees has been patchy: in many places willows are still short, and in others they recovered for reasons unrelated to wolves. Bears, which also eat young elk, increased during the same period, and hunting outside the park, as well as a series of dry years, also reduced elk numbers. Along some streams, the long absence of beavers had allowed the water to cut deep channels, and the resulting lower water table meant that willows could not return even when elk were few. For these researchers, the lesson is that removing a predator may cause damage that is not easily reversed simply by bringing it back.

F Outside the park, the relationship between wolves and people remains difficult. The total number of cattle and sheep killed by wolves is small compared with losses from disease or bad weather, but for an individual family farm the loss of several animals can be serious. Ranchers and conservationists have therefore experimented with ways of keeping the two apart. Large guard dogs are kept with flocks of sheep, and lines of brightly coloured flags, which wolves are reluctant to cross, are hung along fences. In some areas, riders on horseback patrol grazing land to watch over herds. Meanwhile, wolf-watching has brought visitors to the region, although the money they spend rarely reaches the ranchers who bear the costs.

G Yellowstone's experience is now studied by people planning to restore large predators elsewhere. In Europe, wolves have returned to countries such as Germany and France largely without human help, spreading from populations in the east and south, and in Britain there are debates about bringing back the lynx. The main lesson from Yellowstone may be that a predator is not a switch that restores a damaged ecosystem overnight. Its effects depend on local conditions, on other species and on the attitudes of the people who share the land with it, and they can only be understood through many years of careful monitoring.

readings.title: Practice 2: The forest gardeners
readings.qtype: Matching headings (1–7) + Sentence completion (8–11) + Choose TWO letters (12–13)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2 darajasi, Band 6.5–7.5)
text: A A tree cannot walk, yet its seeds need to travel. A seed that falls directly beneath its parent must compete with it for light, water and nutrients, and it is more likely to be found by insects and fungi that specialise in attacking that particular species. Plants have therefore developed many ways of sending their seeds away. Some produce seeds light enough to be carried by the wind, and others rely on rivers or ocean currents. In tropical rainforests, however, where the air near the ground is often still, most tree species depend on animals, offering sweet fruit as a reward for carrying their seeds to a new place.

B Among the most effective of these carriers are forest elephants in Central Africa. An elephant can eat large quantities of fruit in a day and may walk several kilometres before the seeds pass through its body. They are then deposited in a pile of dung that provides moisture and nutrients for the young plant. Researchers who have followed elephants have found that they carry seeds much further than most other animals, and some tree species produce fruit so large and hard that few other creatures can swallow it. Where elephants have been removed by hunting, these trees produce fewer young plants, and those that do grow tend to cluster around the parent.

C In the forests of Africa and Asia, hornbills play a similar role high in the canopy. These large birds swallow fruit whole, digest the soft flesh and later bring up or pass the seeds, often far from where they were eaten. Their unusually wide beaks allow them to handle fruits that smaller birds cannot manage, and because they fly long distances between feeding trees, they can move seeds across valleys and between separate patches of forest. In South America, toucans do comparable work. Because a single hornbill may feed from dozens of tree species, the disappearance of these birds from a forest can affect many plants at once.

D Some of the most important gardeners are far less impressive in size. In the Amazon, the Brazil nut tree produces its seeds inside a woody capsule as hard as a coconut shell. Few animals have teeth strong enough to open it, but the agouti, a rodent about the size of a rabbit, can gnaw through the capsule. It eats some of the nuts immediately and buries others in scattered hiding places to eat later. Many of these stores are never recovered, either because the agouti forgets them or because it is killed by a predator, and the forgotten nuts are then able to germinate. Without agoutis, very few new Brazil nut trees would grow.

E Fruit bats, meanwhile, are especially valuable for the recovery of damaged land. Many fruit-eating birds avoid open ground, where they are exposed to hawks, but bats fly at night and cross cleared areas without hesitation. As they fly, they drop seeds, often of fast-growing pioneer trees that thrive in full sunlight. Studies of abandoned farmland in the tropics have found that a large share of the first trees to appear had been spread by bats, which makes them some of the most important agents in the natural regrowth of forest.

F In many tropical regions, these relationships are breaking down. Large fruit-eating animals are often the first to be hunted, and a forest can keep its trees while losing most of its birds and mammals, a condition some ecologists call 'empty forest syndrome'. From the air, such a forest looks perfectly healthy. Over time, however, trees with large seeds, which depend on large animals, fail to replace themselves, while small-seeded species spread by the wind or by small birds take their place. Because many large-seeded trees have dense, heavy wood, computer models suggest that forests which lose their seed dispersers may eventually store less carbon, adding to the problem of climate change.

G Protecting the gardeners is therefore also a way of protecting forests. The most obvious step is to control hunting, but the design of protected areas matters as well. Where forests have been divided into fragments, corridors of trees along rivers or across farmland can allow birds and mammals to move between them. On cleared land, restoration projects have placed simple wooden perches in open fields; birds stop to rest on them and leave seeds below, speeding up the return of the forest. Breeding endangered birds in zoos is sometimes proposed as well, but experts point out that this cannot replace the work of wild populations in their natural habitat.

readings.title: Practice 3 (uyga): Losing the dark
readings.qtype: Matching headings (1–7) + Sentence completion (8–11) + Choose TWO letters (12–13)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2 darajasi, Band 6.5–7.5), uy vazifasi
text: A For almost all of human history, a clear night sky was full of stars. Today, most people never see one. According to a world atlas of artificial sky brightness published in 2016, more than 80 per cent of the world's population lives under skies polluted by light, and the Milky Way is hidden from more than a third of humanity. The problem is growing: measurements made by volunteers around the world suggest that the night sky has been getting brighter every year. Astronomers were the first to complain, but biologists now argue that the loss of darkness matters far more to other species than it does to people with telescopes.

B Insects are among the most obvious victims. Anyone who has looked up at a streetlight on a summer night has seen the cloud of moths and other insects that gather around it. Many of them will circle the lamp until they die of exhaustion or are caught by bats and birds that have learned to hunt there. Scientists are still debating exactly why insects are drawn to lights, but the consequences are becoming clearer. Moths are important night-time pollinators, and experiments in which streetlights were placed in fields have found that flowers near the lamps received noticeably fewer visits from insects after dark.

C On beaches, the effects can be even more dramatic. Sea turtles lay their eggs in the sand, and when the young hatch, usually at night, they find their way to the sea by moving towards the brightest horizon, which on a natural beach is the open water reflecting the light of the moon and stars. Lights from hotels, roads and houses behind the beach can send them in the wrong direction. Hatchlings that head inland may be killed by traffic or predators, or simply dry out in the morning sun. For this reason, many coastal towns in nesting areas now have rules that require lights near the beach to be switched off, shielded or replaced during the nesting season.

D Birds that migrate at night face a different danger. Many songbirds travel thousands of kilometres between their summer and winter homes, partly using the stars to find their way. Brightly lit buildings and towers, especially in cloudy or foggy weather, can draw them off course. Confused birds may circle a lit building for hours, wasting energy they need for their journey, and many die after flying into windows. In response, several North American cities run 'Lights Out' programmes, in which the owners of tall buildings agree to switch off unnecessary lights during the spring and autumn migration seasons.

E Humans are not immune either. Our bodies follow a daily rhythm controlled by an internal clock, which relies on the change from daylight to darkness. Light in the evening, particularly light that is rich in blue wavelengths, reduces the production of melatonin, a hormone that helps to prepare the body for sleep. Researchers are still investigating how much outdoor lighting, as opposed to screens and indoor lamps, affects our health, but many doctors advise keeping bedrooms as dark as possible.

F Fortunately, light pollution is one of the easiest environmental problems to solve. Unlike chemical pollution, it disappears the moment a light is switched off. Much of the light that brightens the sky is simply wasted: it shines sideways or upwards rather than onto the ground where it is needed. Fitting a simple shield to a lamp ensures that its light points only at the ground, and timers and motion sensors mean that lights are on only when someone is present. The spread of LED lamps has brought mixed results. Because LEDs are cheap to run, many councils have installed more lights than before, and many early models gave out a harsh, blue-rich light. On the other hand, LEDs can easily be dimmed and are now available in warmer colours that are less harmful to wildlife.

G Some communities have gone further and made darkness something to be proud of. An international organisation now certifies parks, reserves and whole towns where lighting is carefully controlled, and more than two hundred such places have been recognised around the world. Some of them attract visitors who come specifically to see the stars, bringing income to rural areas during the quieter months. Their experience suggests that, once people see what a truly dark sky looks like, they are often surprisingly willing to change their own lighting habits.

tasks.title: Questions 8–11
tasks.type: Complete the sentences. Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage for each answer.
tasks.instr: Gaplar matn tartibida keladi. Kalit g'oya bilan joyni toping, javobni matndan AYNAN ko'chiring (NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS), keyin to'ldirilgan gapni grammatika bo'yicha qayta o'qing.
items: 8 Insects attracted to a lamp may keep circling it until they die of ___ .
9 Newly hatched turtles normally move towards the ___ .
10 Some cities ask building owners to switch off lights as part of ___ programmes.
11 A ___ fitted to a lamp keeps its light pointing at the ground.
why: "Circle the lamp until they die of exhaustion" (B).
"By moving towards the brightest horizon" (C). "horizon" yolg'iz — muhim so'z yetishmaydi.
"Several North American cities run 'Lights Out' programmes" (D).
"Fitting a simple shield to a lamp ensures that its light points only at the ground" (F).

tasks.title: Questions 12–13
tasks.type: Choose TWO letters, A–E
tasks.instr: Ikkita javob; tartib ahamiyatsiz ("A, C" = "C, A"), imtihonda har harf alohida 1 ball. Har variantni tekshiring: matnda BOR / TESKARI / AYTILMAGAN / savolga tegishli EMAS.
items: 12–13 Which TWO disadvantages of LED lighting does the writer mention? A) higher running costs B) the installation of more lights C) a short working life D) light that is rich in blue wavelengths E) difficulty in dimming
why: B — "many councils have installed more lights than before". D — "many early models gave out a harsh, blue-rich light". Tuzoqlar: A — teskari ("cheap to run"); E — teskari ("can easily be dimmed"); C — aytilmagan.

homework_intro: Bugun Passage 2 da uch savol turini birga yechdik: headings xaritasi → sentence completion (NMT3W) → TWO letters. Eng ko'p ball uch joyda yo'qoladi: tafsilotga qarab sarlavha tanlash, javob shaklidagi mayda xatolar (ko'plik, imlo, yetishmagan so'z) va matnda TESKARI aytilgan variantni tanlash.

Birinchi vazifa — Practice 3 "Losing the dark": 20 daqiqa vaqt oling (10 + 4 + 4 + 2). Har bo'lim chetiga asosiy g'oyani 3–4 so'zda yozing; TWO letters savolida har variant yoniga BOR / TESKARI / AYTILMAGAN belgisini qo'ying.

Ikkinchi vazifa — Workbook, 43-bet, Key vocabulary 2-mashq (bolster, cloning, forage, numerous, stunning, tempt, thrive, toxic, viral — 1–9-gaplar + 10-so'z: uni qalin harflardan tuzasiz). Ulardan oltitasi (bolster, forage, numerous, thrive, toxic, viral) bugungi SB matnida uchradi. To'qqizta so'zning har biri bilan tabiat mavzusida o'z gapingizni ham yozing.
Uchinchi vazifa — xatolar daftari: bugungi xato javoblarni yozing — savol, to'g'ri javob va sinf mashqidagi sabab harfi (a–e) yoki "tafsilot tuzog'i" / "teskari variant".

kahoot.q: Passage 2 has 7 heading questions, 4 sentence gaps and 2 TWO-letter answers. What time plan does the book suggest?
options: Headings 10, sentences 4, pick from a list 4 minutes
Headings 4, sentences 10, pick from a list 4 minutes
Read everything carefully for 15 minutes, then answer
kahoot.explain: Kitob kaliti: headings 10, sentence completion 4, pick from a list 4 daqiqa; qolgan 2 daqiqa — tekshirish va transfer.

kahoot.q: Which is the best order for this combination of tasks?
options: Do the tasks in the order they occur
Do the task you like best first
kahoot.explain: SB maslahati: vazifalarni tartib bilan bajaring. Headings butun matnni o'qitadi va xarita beradi.

kahoot.q: Section D says: 'in 2006 came an extreme blow'. Which heading does this match?
kahoot.explain: Setback = zarba, orqaga ketish. Band 7 sarlavhasi matn so'zini takrorlamaydi — ma'noni umumlashtiradi.

kahoot.q: A heading matches one sentence in a section, but not the rest. What is it probably?
kahoot.explain: Sarlavha butun bo'limning asosiy g'oyasini beradi. Bitta gapga mos sarlavha — odatda tuzoq.

kahoot.q: 'Both ___ were the first creatures to pollinate.' A student writes 'flies'. Why 0 marks?
options: One of two answers is missing
It repeats a word in the question
kahoot.explain: "Both" — ikki javob: flies and beetles. Kitobdagi c sababi.

kahoot.q: 'Monkeys transport pollen on their ___.' Which answer is correct?
kahoot.explain: Matnda "furry coats": ko'plik -s va qo'sh r. "coats" yolg'iz ham qabul qilinadi.

kahoot.q: 'Honeybees ... partly because they travel ___.' Why is 'travel longer distances' wrong?
options: It breaks the NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS rule
It is not in the passage
kahoot.explain: Gapdagi so'zni qayta yozmang: "travel" gapda allaqachon bor (u matndagi "cover" ning paraphrase'i). "travel longer distances" — 3 so'z, chegaraga sig'adi; xato so'z sonida emas, takrorda. Javob: (longer) distances.

kahoot.q: NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS. Which answer is NOT allowed?
kahoot.explain: "the flies and beetles" — 4 so'z. Artikl ham so'z hisoblanadi.

kahoot.q: Choose TWO letters: an option says the opposite of the passage. How do you mark it?
options: It counts as half a mark
kahoot.explain: Har variant: BOR / TESKARI / AYTILMAGAN / tegishli emas. Faqat BOR ikkitasi javob.

kahoot.q: In SB Q12–13, where are the two answers found?
options: In two different sections (F and G)
Always next to each other in one paragraph
kahoot.explain: Kitob maslahati: javoblar bir yoki bir necha joyda bo'lishi mumkin. 12 — F, 13 — G.

kahoot.q: Sentence completion questions in this task usually follow...
options: the order of the headings list
kahoot.explain: Sentence completion gaplari matn tartibida keladi — 8 dan 11 gacha oldinga skanerlang.

kahoot.q: WB Q12–13: 'Their eggs were eaten by European settlers.' Why is B wrong?
options: The passage says nothing about eggs
kahoot.explain: "introduced dogs, cats and rats, which raided their nests" — tuxumni hayvonlar yegan. Javob C, ko'chmanchilar emas.

kahoot.q: Bees, flies and even lizards can be ___ — they carry pollen from flower to flower.
kahoot.explain: Pollinator — changlatuvchi. Predator — yirtqich, pathogen — kasallik qo'zg'atuvchi, insectivore — hasharotxo'r.

kahoot.q: When Paine removed the starfish, species diversity in the bay saw a dramatic ___.
kahoot.explain: Decline — kamayish. 15 turdan 8 tasi qolgan.

kahoot.q: A species whose loss can change a whole ecosystem is called a ___.
kahoot.explain: Keystone species — tayanch tur. Flagship species — e'tibor tortadigan mashhur tur (kit, yo'lbars).

kahoot.q: Wildflower havens would ___ populations of useful insects.
kahoot.explain: Bolster — mustahkamlamoq, ko'paytirmoq.

kahoot.q: It's hard to ___ the different factors that cause CCD.
kahoot.explain: Tease apart — bir-biridan ajratib tahlil qilmoq.

kahoot.q: Geckos carry pollen on their feet as they ___ for nectar.
kahoot.explain: Forage — oziq izlab yurmoq.

kahoot.q: A species may seem unimportant ___, but it can be part of a much larger system.
kahoot.explain: In isolation — alohida olganda.

kahoot.q: The disappearance of one species could have ___ consequences.
kahoot.explain: Far-reaching — keng ko'lamli. Far-fetched — aqlga sig'maydigan.

intro: Section 3 — o'quv mavzusidagi suhbat: odatda tutor va bir-ikki talaba topshiriq yoki safarni rejalashtiradi. Band 7 darajasida qiyinchilik — fikrlar tez almashadi, talabalar taxmin qiladi va tutor ularni TUZATADI. Javob ko'pincha tuzatishdan keyin keladi.

Bugungi kombinatsiya (SB va WB da ham): Plan/map labelling (harflar), Short-answer questions (ONE WORD ONLY) va Sentence completion (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS). Har tur uchun tayyorlanish boshqacha — vaqtni bo'lib ishlating.

PLAN LABELLING: tinglashdan oldin xaritani o'z so'zingiz bilan tasvirlang (SB 2-mashq): kompas qayerda? ko'l qanday shaklda? o'rmonlar nechta va qaysi biri katta? Har harf yoniga 2–3 so'zlik tavsif yozing (C — ko'llar qo'shilgan joy; F — katta o'rmon va daryo orasi). Audio shu tavsiflarga o'xshash iboralar ishlatadi: "where the two lochs meet", "the largest area of forest ... in the corner", "the larger of the two on that side".

XARITA TUZOG'I: talaba bir joyni taklif qiladi, tutor rad etadi. SB: "perhaps this south side of Loch Affric" — "Not right on the edge, though ... but in this slightly bigger patch of woodland behind it" (B emas, A). WB: "There are two hides there, and Goose hide is the one on the far side". Rad etish signallari: not ... though, used to be, the other one, no — ...

SHORT ANSWER: savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyani belgilang ("What can CAUSE someone to MISS a good photograph?", "What PERSONAL QUALITY...?"). Javob so'zi audioda aynan eshitiladi, lekin savol so'zlari paraphrase qilinadi: miss a photograph = lose the moment; personal quality = one of the most important qualities. ONE WORD ONLY — "my hesitation" emas, "hesitation".

SENTENCE COMPLETION: kitob maslahati — audio savoldagi so'zlarning SINONIMlarini ishlatadi (bad weather → mist, driving rain; take advantage of → make the most of / profit from; avoid → prevents), lekin bo'shliq so'zini aynan eshitasiz. Har bo'shliq uchun ma'lumot turini oldindan yozing ("something linked to water", "people who help produce ideas").

Transfer: to'ldirilgan gapni qayta o'qing — grammatik va mantiqan to'g'rimi? So'z chegarasi, ko'plik va imlo (WB 5-mashq cheklisti). Qavsdagi so'z ixtiyoriy: (neck) pain — "pain" ham, "neck pain" ham to'g'ri.
formulas: C — where the lochs meet; F — big forest + river
entrance in the south; sea to the north

miss a photograph → lose the moment
take advantage of = make the most of → reflections

presentation: Xarita harflari tartib bilan eshitiladimi?
Yo'q — SAVOLLAR tartib bilan keladi (1, 2, 3), harflar esa xaritaning istalgan joyida. Har savol nomini (Oldest Scots pine trees, Red deer) eshitishni kuting.
Talaba bir joyni aytdi, tutor "Yes, they're OK, but..." dedi. Qaysi biri?
"but" dan keyingi joy — javob. SB 1-savol: katta o'rmon (E) "OK", lekin eng qari qarag'aylar ko'llar qo'shilgan joyda — C.
Short answer'da javob ikki so'z bo'lib qoldi. Nima qilaman?
ONE WORD ONLY — faqat asosiy so'z: "hesitation" ("my hesitation" emas). Kalitda hesitating / waiting ham qabul qilingan.
Sentence completion'da audioda boshqa so'z eshitildi. Xatomi?
Yo'q, bu normal: savol paraphrase qilingan. Faqat bo'shliqqa tushadigan so'z aynan eshitiladi (landscape, reflections, designers).
"reflection" yoki "reflections"?
Kalit ikkalasini ham qabul qiladi: (a/the) reflection(s). Lekin har doim gapga qo'yib tekshiring.
WB da "Camouflage yourself" — bu ikki so'z-ku?
Ha, NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS — ruxsat. Gap katta harf bilan boshlanadi: "___ if you can" — fe'l kerak.

Yaxshi dala mahorati — sekin va jim harakat qilish.
Think like a hunter and stalk the birds carefully.
Ovchidek o'ylang va qushlarni ehtiyotkorlik bilan poylang.
My problem is hesitation — I wait too long.
Mening muammom — ikkilanish, juda uzoq kutaman.
Your photos may reveal conservation problems.
Suratlaringiz tabiatni muhofaza qilish muammolarini ochib berishi mumkin.
super: If you frighten the deer, just put it down to experience.
Bug'uni cho'chitib yuborsangiz, buni tajriba deb qabul qiling.
Suddenly something will take your breath away.
In the long run, you'll still get your pictures.
I want to make the most of the reflections in the water.

class_ex.title: Tinglashdan oldin: xaritani tasvirlash (SB, 2-mashq)
class_ex.instr: SB 75-betdagi Loch Affric xaritasiga qarab savollarga javob bering. Keyin juftlikda har harf qayerda ekanini tasvirlang.
items: 1 What does the map show?
2 How many woodland areas are there, where are they, and how do they compare in size?
3 What shape are the lochs? Where are they on the map?
4 How many rivers are there, and where are they?
5 Take turns to explain where each letter (A–F) is situated.
answers: An area of Scotland with lochs (lakes), wooded and non-wooded ground.
Five: the largest in the south-east; three smaller areas on either side of the lochs and where the lochs meet; the smallest on the south shore of one loch.
Long and thin; they run across the map from south-west to north-east.
Three; all in the non-wooded areas — two in the south and one in the north.
Masalan: C — where the two lochs meet / where it narrows in the centre; F — between the largest forest and the river.
why: Kalit (SB) javobi. "Loch" — Shotlandcha "ko'l" (skriptda ham tushuntiriladi).
Kalit javobi. O'lcham so'zlari (the largest, a slightly bigger patch) 1–3-savollarda aynan ishlatiladi.
Kalit javobi. "Where the two lochs meet" — 1-savol javobining kaliti.
Kalit javobi. 2-savolda tutor "between the woodland and the river" deydi.
Ochiq javob — o'quvchilar joylashuv iboralarini mashq qiladi: on the south shore, in the corner, next to, between ... and ..., behind.
class_ex.note: Bu mashqni o'tkazib yubormang: 1–3-savollarda eshitiladigan iboralarning yarmini o'quvchilar shu yerda o'zi aytadi.

class_ex.title: Idiomatik iboralar (SB, Vocabulary 1–2-mashqlar)
class_ex.instr: Track 9–10 skriptidagi iboralarni qutidagi so'zlar bilan to'ldiring: account, bear, breath, experience, most, run, time. Keyin har ibora ma'nosini ayting.
items: 1 It's like anything, you have to put it down to ___ .
2 But suddenly something will take your ___ away.
3 I wouldn't worry — in the long ___ , you'll still get your pictures.
4 You need to take the landscape into ___ .
5 I want to make the ___ of all the stunning reflections.
6 Just take your ___ , and you might capture an amazing reflection.
7 It's just something to ___ in mind.
why: put it down to experience — xafa bo'lmay, tajriba deb qabul qilish.
take your breath away — hayratda qoldirmoq.
in the long run — oxir-oqibat.
take into account — hisobga olmoq (bear in mind bilan sinonim).
make the most of — maksimal foydalanmoq (profit from).
take your time — shoshilmaslik, sabr qilish.
bear in mind — yodda tutmoq, hisobga olmoq.
class_ex.note: Kalit (SB): 1 experience 2 breath 3 run 4 account 5 most 6 time 7 bear. 2-mashq: 1 make the most of, 2 put it down to experience, 3 take your time, 4 in the long run, 5 take your breath away, 6 take into account / bear in mind. Bu iboralarni Speaking Part 2 da ishlatishni talab qiling.

listenings.title: Student's Book, Track 9: Glen Affric photography trip (Q1–5)
intro: Ikki talaba (Brett va Mica) tutor bilan Shotlandiyadagi Glen Affric'ga suratga olish safarini muhokama qiladi. Tinglashdan oldin: 2-mashq (xarita tavsifi) va 3-mashq — 4–5-savollardagi kalit g'oyaning tagiga chizish (What / cause / miss / photograph; quality / photographers / need).
Rasmda SB 75–76-betlar: 1–5-savollar birinchi sahifada, 6–10 — ikkinchisida (Track 10 uchun).

tasks.title: Questions 1–3
tasks.type: Label the plan. Write the correct letter, A–F
tasks.instr: Tinglashdan oldin: kompas, start nuqtasi va har harf atrofidagi belgilarni (ko'l, o'rmon, daryo, yo'l) o'z so'zingiz bilan tasvirlang. Javoblar savollar tartibida keladi; gapiruvchi aytgan yo'nalishni qalam bilan kuzating.
items: 1 Oldest Scots pine trees
2 Red deer
3 Red squirrels
why: Mica katta o'rmonni (E) ko'rsatadi, tutor: "Yes, they're OK, but if you look at where the two lochs meet" — Brett: "where it narrows in the centre of the map?" — "You'll find some of the oldest pines there". Tuzoq: E.

"This largest area of forest — here, in the corner of the map? — Yes — they also need water, so between the woodland and the river — I'd try that spot" — F. Tuzoq: E (o'rmonning o'zi) va "non-wooded areas".
"Perhaps this south side of Loch Affric. — Not right on the edge, though — that's where you'd look for birds — but in this slightly bigger patch of woodland behind it" — A. Tuzoq: B (qirg'oqda).
tasks.note: Kalit: 1 C, 2 F, 3 A. Uchala savolda ham talaba birinchi taklif qilgan joy — tuzoq; tutorning "but" / "Not ... though" dan keyingi gapi — javob.

tasks.title: Questions 4–5
tasks.type: Answer the questions. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.
tasks.instr: Savol o'zagini paraphrase qiling: miss a good photograph = lose the moment; personal quality = one of the most important qualities.
items: 4 What can cause someone to miss a good photograph?
5 What personal quality do wildlife photographers particularly need?
why: Brett: "My problem's hesitation — I wait too long! — You lose the moment." Kalit hesitating va waiting ni ham qabul qiladi.
"Sometimes you've got to have patience. — That's one of the most important qualities if you're a wildlife photographer."
tasks.note: 4-savolda "experience" tuzog'i: "put it down to experience" — bu cho'chitib yuborilgan hayvon haqida, suratni o'tkazib yuborish sababi emas.

listenings.title: Student's Book, Track 10: advice for the trip (Q6–10)
intro: Savollar yuqoridagi rasmda (SB 76-bet). Avval 5-mashq: kalit g'oyalarning tagiga chizing va har bo'shliq uchun ma'lumot turini ayting. Kitob misoli: bad weather → mist / driving rain.
Kitob maslahati: audio savoldagi so'zlarning sinonimlarini ishlatadi, lekin bo'shliq so'zini AYNAN eshitasiz. NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.

tasks.title: 5-mashq: qanday ma'lumot kerak?
tasks.type: Og'zaki bashorat
tasks.instr: Tinglashdan oldin har gapda kalit g'oyaning tagiga chizing va bo'shliq uchun ma'lumot turini ayting.
items: 6 In bad weather, think more carefully about the ___ .
7 Take advantage of ___ when photographing near water.
8 Use a piece of equipment called an 'angle finder' to avoid ___ .
9 Use the work of both artists and ___ to generate ideas.
10 Think about ___ issues when deciding on what to photograph.
answers: a problem that an angle finder helps you avoid
a type or area of issue (a topic word)
why: Kalit (SB): bad weather / think more carefully — ob-havo ta'sir qiladigan narsa.
Take advantage / near water — suv bilan bog'liq narsa.
equipment / 'angle finder' / avoid — asbob oldini oladigan narsa (ot).
work / artists / ideas — "artists and ___" — odamlar (ko'plik).
Think about / issues / deciding — "___ issues" — soha nomi (sifat vazifasidagi ot).

tasks.title: Questions 6–10
tasks.type: Complete the sentences. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
tasks.instr: Sinonimlarni kuting: take advantage of = make the most of / profit from; avoid = prevents; generate ideas = get ideas.
items: 6 In bad weather, think more carefully about the ___ .
7 Take advantage of ___ when photographing near water.
8 Use a piece of equipment called an 'angle finder' to avoid ___ .
9 Use the work of both artists and ___ to generate ideas.
10 Think about ___ issues when deciding on what to photograph.
why: "What about driving rain? — ... it does mean that you need to take the landscape into account. Perhaps to a greater degree than you would normally." "shadow" — tuzoq: "you get shadow in good weather".
"I want to make the most of all the stunning reflections in the water. — ... you really should profit from this with the water around you."
"What's great about it is that it prevents neck pain". avoid = prevents.
"Wildlife paintings by Scottish artists ... — Some designers can be helpful, too ... they can help give you ideas".
"We should consider matters related to conservation when we choose a scene to photograph".
tasks.note: Kalit: 6 landscape, 7 (a/the) reflection(s), 8 (neck) pain, 9 designers, 10 conservation. 6-savolda "weather" va "mist" ham eshitiladi — ular savoldagi "bad weather" ning o'zi.

listenings.title: Student's Book: recording script (CD2 Track 9–10) — ustoz uchun
intro: Tekshiruvdan keyin ekranga chiqaring. Har javob gapini, rad etilgan joyni ("Not right on the edge, though") va idiomatik iboralarni alohida rang bilan ko'rsating. Track 9 — chap ustun va o'ng ustun tepasi; Track 10 — o'ng ustun va pastki qism.

listenings.title: Workbook, Track 11: bird-watching tips (Q1–5)
intro: Talaba Ewan qo'riqxonada qush kuzatishdan oldin Professor Blake'dan maslahat so'raydi. Avval WB 1–2-mashqlar (1 daqiqa): qaysi javoblarni oldindan taxmin qilsa bo'ladi?
Keyin imtihondagidek: tayyorlanish, audio BIR MARTA. Rasmda WB 42–43-betlar: 1–5 va 6–8 (xarita) 42-betda, 9–10 — 43-bet tepasida.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Complete the sentences. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
tasks.instr: Tutor maslahatlari tartib bilan keladi: durbin → fieldcraft → qushni tanish (ovoz, ko'rinish, harakat, oziqlanish).
items: 1 Choose binoculars that are comfortable to carry and have excellent ___ .
2 Follow the birds the way a ___ would follow them.
3 ___ if you can, so the birds don't see you.
4 Listen to the noises the bird makes, and observe what it looks like (its ___ , shape, markings and other characteristics).
5 Observe movement and flight patterns, ___ and habitat.
why: "They should be as light as possible ... and their optical quality should be very good". "light" — tuzoq: bu "comfortable to carry" qismi.
"You need to think like a hunter and stalk the birds carefully".
"You should also try to camouflage yourself against the background ... to avoid being seen by the birds". Gap fe'l bilan boshlanadi.
"What is the approximate size of the bird?" "size" yolg'iz ham mantiqli, lekin kalit — approximate size.
"Then try to determine its feeding habits". Kalit "eating habits" ni ham qabul qiladi.
tasks.note: Kalit (WB): 1 optical quality 2 hunter 3 Camouflage yourself 4 approximate size 5 feeding/eating habits.

listenings.title: Workbook, Track 12: hides at the Wychwood reserve (Q6–10)
listenings.qtype: Plan labelling (6–8) + Short answer (9–10) — Section 3, imtihon rejimi
intro: Savollar yuqoridagi rasmda. Tinglashdan oldin xaritada toping: entrance (janubda), sea (shimolda), o'ngdagi ko'l, g'arbdagi ikki o'rmon, soy ustidagi ko'prik, yo'l ayrilgan joy.
Audio BIR MARTA. 9–10: ONE WORD ONLY.

tasks.title: Questions 6–8
tasks.type: Label the plan. Write the correct letter, A–G
tasks.instr: Tinglashdan oldin: kompas, start nuqtasi va har harf atrofidagi belgilarni (ko'l, o'rmon, daryo, yo'l) o'z so'zingiz bilan tasvirlang. Javoblar savollar tartibida keladi; gapiruvchi aytgan yo'nalishni qalam bilan kuzating.
items: 6 Goose hide
7 Eagle hide
8 Cuckoo hide
why: "A lake on the right, beyond the woods by the entrance ... There are two hides there, and Goose hide is the one on the far side ... hard up against the hill behind it" — E. Tuzoq: G — ko'l yonidagi ikkinchi hide ("the other one by the lake").
"Around the north side of the lake, but turn left where the path forks, shortly before the bridge over the stream. Then head towards the sea. You'll find Eagle hide where two paths meet" — C.
"See the wood in the west of the reserve? The larger of the two on that side? — That's where you'll find Cuckoo hide" — B. Tuzoq: F — kichikroq o'rmon.
tasks.note: Kalit (WB): 6 E 7 C 8 B. 7-savol eng qiyin — yo'nalishni qalam bilan chizib boring: kirish → ko'lning shimoli → ayrilishda chapga → dengiz tomon.

tasks.title: Questions 9–10
tasks.type: Answer the questions. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.
tasks.instr: Savol o'zagi: WHAT makes bird-watching ENJOYABLE? / APART FROM binoculars, what to TAKE?
items: 9 What, according to the tutor, helps to make bird-watching especially enjoyable?
10 Apart from binoculars, what should the student take with him?
why: "It's much more fun when you've got company". "friend" — tuzoq: bu Ewan'ning gapi; tutor umumiy fikr sifatida "company" deydi.
"It might be a good idea to pack something to eat in your bag alongside your binoculars ... Sandwiches, or something like that". "weather forecast" — tekshirish kerak, olib yurish emas.

listenings.title: Workbook: recording script (Track 11–12) — ustoz uchun
intro: Skriptda kitob javoblarning tagiga chizilgan. Qayta tinglashda o'quvchilar yo'nalish iboralarini (on the far side, turn left where the path forks, the larger of the two) topib, doskadagi "Joylashuv iboralari" ustuniga yozadi.

listenings.title: Jony Academy mashqi: Hollins Marsh wildlife survey
listenings.qtype: Plan labelling (1–4) + Short answer (5–6) + Sentence completion (7–10) — Section 3
intro: Tutor Dr Okafor va talabalar Lena va Tom tabiat bog'ida yovvoyi hayvonlarni hisoblash tadqiqotini rejalashtiradi. Ustoz uch rolni o'qiydi (yoki ikki kuchli o'quvchi bilan). BIR MARTA, tabiiy tezlikda; rollarni ovoz ohangi bilan farqlang, javob so'zlarini urg'u yoki pauza bilan ajratib ko'rsatmang.
Avval xarita jadvalini doskaga chizing (shimol tepada). 1–6 va 7–10 orasida 20 soniya pauza qiling.
transcript: DR OKAFOR: Come in, both of you. So, you're doing your wildlife survey at Hollins Marsh Nature Park next month. Have you got the plan of the park I sent you?
TOM: Yes, it's here. The visitor centre's right in the middle, isn't it?

DR OKAFOR: That's right, and the main entrance and the car park are directly south of it. The lake takes up the top of the map, and the boardwalk runs from west to east across the reed beds, between the lake and the visitor centre.
LENA: OK. The first thing we need to find is the bat boxes. I read on the website that they're on the old barn — that's just east of the visitor centre, isn't it?

DR OKAFOR: They used to be. But when the barn roof was repaired last year, the boxes were taken down. The new ones have been fixed to the oak trees in the north-east corner, on the opposite side of the lake from the bird hide.
TOM: So not the barn. North-east corner — got it. And where's the bird hide?
DR OKAFOR: In the north-west corner, on the lake shore. You won't need it for this project, but don't confuse it with the pond-dipping platform.
LENA: Oh, I assumed the platform would be on the lake itself.
DR OKAFOR: No — the lake is far too deep, and it's mainly children who use the platform. It's on the small pond at the western end of the boardwalk, just below the bird hide.
TOM: West end of the boardwalk. Right. Now, we have to count bees in the wildflower meadow. Is that the field by the entrance?

DR OKAFOR: There are two fields by the entrance. The one on the west side is grazed by sheep, so there aren't many flowers. The meadow is the other one, in the south-east corner, right next to the car park.
LENA: And the moth trap? It needs electricity, doesn't it?

DR OKAFOR: It does, and it also needs to be sheltered from the wind. The area at the eastern end of the boardwalk is very open, so that's no good. The warden suggested the walled garden on the west side of the visitor centre — there's a power socket on the outside wall.
LENA: Perfect.

DR OKAFOR: Now, a couple of rules. When you watch the bats leave the boxes in the evening, whatever you do, don't use a torch. The light may stop them coming out at all. The department has headlamps with red filters — use those instead. Cameras are fine, as long as you switch the flash off.
TOM: OK. Do we need to tell the park office when we're coming?
DR OKAFOR: The office closes at five, so there's no point. You must phone the warden before every visit — he needs to know who is on site after dark.
(Pause — 20 seconds)
LENA: Can we go through the methods now? For the moths, we set the trap at dusk and leave it on overnight?
DR OKAFOR: Yes, but you need to get there early. Birds soon learn that moths settle around the trap, so empty it before sunrise, not after breakfast.
TOM: That's early! And for the bees — I suppose we should choose sunny days?
DR OKAFOR: Sunshine helps, but the key thing is that the day is calm. Bees don't fly much when it's windy, so you'd get misleading results. Warm and calm — that's what you want.
LENA: And what should we write down at the start of each count? The time?
DR OKAFOR: If you use the app, the time is recorded automatically. What you must note yourselves is the air temperature, because it affects how active the insects are.
TOM: OK. And in the report, can we compare our results with earlier surveys?

DR OKAFOR: The park did a big survey about five years ago, but it used different methods, so the figures aren't really comparable. What you can use is last summer's count by volunteers from the local wildlife trust. They followed exactly the same method as you.
LENA: Great. We'll ask the warden for a copy.
DR OKAFOR: Good. And one last thing — take your time with identification. It's better to write 'unknown' than to guess.

tasks.title: Questions 1–4 — Hollins Marsh Nature Park (plan)
tasks.type: Label the plan. Write the correct letter, A–H
tasks.instr: Jadval — xarita: shimol tepada, g'arb chapda. Markazda tashrif markazi. Har joy uchun harf yozing.
items: 1 Bat boxes
2 Pond-dipping platform
3 Wildflower meadow
4 Moth trap
why: "The new ones have been fixed to the oak trees in the north-east corner" — B. Tuzoq: F — eski ombor ("They used to be").
"On the small pond at the western end of the boardwalk, just below the bird hide" — C. Tuzoq: A — qushlarni kuzatish kulbasi; ko'lning o'zi — "far too deep".
"The meadow is the other one, in the south-east corner, right next to the car park" — H. Tuzoq: G — qo'y boqiladigan dala.
"The walled garden on the west side of the visitor centre" — E. Tuzoq: D — "very open, so that's no good".
tasks.note: Ishlatilmagan harflar: A (bird hide), D, F, G — har biri skriptda rad etilgan joy. SB va WB dagi kabi: talaba taklifi — tuzoq, tutor tuzatishi — javob.
head: West
Centre
East

tasks.title: Questions 5–6
tasks.type: Answer the questions. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.
tasks.instr: Savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyani belgilang: NOT use / WHO / phone.
items: 5 What must the students not use when they watch the bats?
6 Who must the students phone before every visit?
why: "Whatever you do, don't use a torch". Tuzoqlar: headlamps — ruxsat etilgan; cameras — "fine", faqat flash o'chiriladi.
"You must phone the warden before every visit". Tuzoq: park office — "closes at five, so there's no point".

tasks.title: Questions 7–10
tasks.type: Complete the sentences. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
tasks.instr: Signal va tuzatishlarni kuting: "not after breakfast", "Sunshine helps, but...", "aren't really comparable".
items: 7 Empty the moth trap before ___ .
8 Count bees on days that are warm and ___ .
9 At the start of each count, write down the ___ .
10 Results can be compared with last summer's count by the local ___ .
why: "Empty it before sunrise, not after breakfast".
"Sunshine helps, but the key thing is that the day is calm ... Warm and calm". "sunny" — tuzoq.
"What you must note yourselves is the air temperature". "temperature" yolg'iz ham to'g'ri (air — ixtiyoriy). "the time" — tuzoq: ilova uni o'zi yozadi.
"Last summer's count by volunteers from the local wildlife trust". Tuzoq: besh yil oldingi park tadqiqoti — "not really comparable".
tasks.note: Barcha 10 savolda tuzoq bor — tekshiruvdan keyin o'quvchilardan har tuzoqni skriptdan topishni so'rang (skriptni ekranga chiqarishingiz mumkin).

homework_intro: Bugun Section 3 da uch savol turini ketma-ket yechdik: xarita, qisqa javob va gap to'ldirish. Eng ko'p ball ikki joyda yo'qoladi — talaba taklif qilgan (keyin rad etilgan) joyni yozishda va so'z chegarasi/ko'plik xatolarida.

Birinchi vazifa — shadowing: SB Track 9 ning oxirgi qismini ("What if you frighten your subject off?" dan boshlab) va Track 10 ni skript bilan 3 marta tinglang, keyin gapiruvchilar bilan bir vaqtda takrorlang. 7 ta idiomatik iborani aniq talaffuz qiling (2 tasi Track 9 oxirida, 5 tasi Track 10 da). Audio va skript parchasi guruh chatida (ustoz dars oxirida yuboradi). Oxirgi urinishni ovozli xabar qilib guruhga yuboring.

Ikkinchi vazifa — Workbook, 43-bet, Vocabulary 1-mashq (Idiomatic expressions): qush kuzatish haqidagi matndagi 12 bo'shliqni to'ldiring. Keyin shu iboralardan 4 tasini ishlatib o'zingiz yoqtirgan tabiat maskani haqida 5–6 gap yozing.

Uchinchi vazifa — diktant: WB Track 12 ning xarita qismini (Goose, Eagle, Cuckoo hide) tinglang va tutorning yo'nalish gaplarini to'liq yozing. Audio va skript parchasi guruh chatida. Skript bilan o'zingiz tekshiring, xatolar sonini diktant ostiga yozing va yo'lni WB xaritasida qalam bilan chizing.

homework.title: Shadowing: SB Track 9 (oxiri) + Track 10
homework.instr: 3 marta skript bilan tinglash, keyin gapiruvchilar bilan bir vaqtda takrorlash; ovozli xabar guruhga. Audio va skript parchasi guruh chatida.
homework.answers: Ustoz 7 ta idiomaning talaffuzi va urg'usini tekshiradi.

homework.title: Workbook, 43-bet: Vocabulary 1-mashq
homework.instr: 12 bo'shliq + 4 ibora bilan 5–6 gaplik matn.
homework.answers: Kalit (WB): 1 bear 2 in mind 3 take 4 into account 5 make 6 the most of 7 take 8 your breath away 9 in the 10 long run 11 put it down 12 to experience (1–2 va 3–4 o'rnida bear in mind / take into account almashishi mumkin).

homework.title: Diktant: WB Track 12 (xarita qismi)
homework.instr: Uch hide'ga yo'l ko'rsatish gaplarini to'liq yozish, skript bilan tekshirish, xaritada chizish.
homework.answers: O'quvchi diktantni skript bilan o'zi tekshiradi va xatolar sonini yozadi; ustoz tasodifiy 3 ta ishni qayta sanab ko'radi. Keyingi darsda ustoz bitta hide'ga yo'lni og'zaki so'raydi.

normativ: 12 dan 10 tasi to'g'ri; yo'nalish gaplari 1 xatogacha

kahoot.q: Plan labelling in Section 3: in what order do the answers come?
options: In the order of the questions
kahoot.explain: Savollar tartib bilan keladi (1, 2, 3); harflar esa xaritaning istalgan joyida bo'lishi mumkin.

kahoot.q: What should you do with the map BEFORE you listen?
options: Describe where each letter is in your own words
Write a guess next to every question number
Count the letters and ignore everything else
Read the recording script before the audio starts
kahoot.explain: SB 2-mashq: har harfni tasvirlang (where the lochs meet, the largest forest) — audio shunga o'xshash iboralar ishlatadi.

kahoot.q: Student: 'Perhaps this south side of the loch.' Tutor: 'Not right on the edge, though...' The south side is...
options: a trap — the answer comes next
the correct answer to the question
a place that is not on the map
the best place to look for deer
kahoot.explain: "Not ... though" — rad etish signali. Javob: "the slightly bigger patch of woodland behind it" (A).

kahoot.q: Tutor: 'Yes, they're OK, but if you look at where the two lochs meet...' Which is the answer?
kahoot.explain: "but" dan keyingi joy — javob (C). Birinchi taklif (katta o'rmon) — tuzoq.

kahoot.q: Short answer, ONE WORD ONLY: 'What can cause someone to miss a good photograph?' Which answer loses the mark?
kahoot.explain: "my hesitation" — ikki so'z. Kalit hesitation / hesitating / waiting ni qabul qiladi.

kahoot.q: 'miss a good photograph' is paraphrased in the recording as...
kahoot.explain: Brett: "I wait too long!" — Mica: "You lose the moment." Savol so'zlari audioda sinonim bilan keladi.

kahoot.q: Sentence completion: the book says you will hear...
options: the exact word(s) for the gap
the whole question read aloud first
kahoot.explain: Savol paraphrase qilinadi, lekin bo'shliq so'zi aynan eshitiladi: landscape, reflections, designers.

kahoot.q: 'Use an angle finder to avoid ___.' Which word in the recording signals the answer?
kahoot.explain: "It prevents neck pain" — avoid = prevent. Javob: (neck) pain.

kahoot.q: 'Think about ___ issues when deciding what to photograph.' What type of word is needed?
options: the name of a person in the recording
kahoot.explain: "___ issues" — soha nomi, sifat vazifasida: conservation issues.

kahoot.q: WB: 'Goose hide is the one on the far side.' What does this tell you?
options: Choose the hide further away across the lake
Choose the hide nearest to you on the path
Goose hide is the one closest to the entrance
Either of the two hides by the lake is correct
kahoot.explain: "There are two hides there" — "the one on the far side" (E); yaqinidagi ikkinchi hide — tuzoq.

kahoot.q: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS. Which answer is NOT allowed?
kahoot.explain: "the approximate size" — uch so'z. Artikl ham so'z; gapda "its" allaqachon bor.

kahoot.q: Section 3 differs from Section 1 because...
options: speakers suggest, disagree and correct each other
there is only one speaker, as in a lecture
the answers are always numbers, dates or names
the recording is played twice, so you can check
kahoot.explain: Section 3 — tutor va talabalar bahsi: taklif, rad etish, tuzatish. Audio bir marta eshitiladi.

kahoot.q: If you frighten the animal away, don't get upset — just ___ experience.
kahoot.explain: Put it down to experience — tajriba deb qabul qilish, xafa bo'lmaslik.

kahoot.q: In driving rain, you need to take the landscape into ___.
kahoot.explain: Take into account = bear in mind — hisobga olmoq. "take into attention" deyilmaydi (to'g'risi: pay attention to).

kahoot.q: Don't worry about the mist — in the long ___, you'll still get your pictures.
kahoot.explain: In the long run — oxir-oqibat.

kahoot.q: Suddenly something will take your ___ away and it will all be worth it.
kahoot.explain: Take your breath away — hayratda qoldirmoq.

kahoot.q: Wildlife photographers need ___: they may sit for hours waiting.
kahoot.explain: Patience — sabr. Hesitation — ikkilanish (bu muammo, fazilat emas).

kahoot.q: Don't wear bright clothes, and try to ___ yourself against the background.
kahoot.explain: Camouflage yourself — fonga moslab niqoblanmoq. Distinguish yourself esa aksincha — ajralib, ko'zga tashlanib turish.

kahoot.q: Birds are watched from a small wooden shelter called a ___.
kahoot.explain: Hide — qushlarni ko'rinmay kuzatish uchun kulba.

kahoot.q: I want to make the ___ of the stunning reflections in the water.
kahoot.explain: Make the most of — maksimal foydalanmoq (profit from).

lessons.grammar_topic: Passage 3 (Reading Section 3) kombinatsiyasi: YES / NO / NOT GIVEN (yozuvchi fikri) + Multiple choice A–D (shu jumladan "writer's purpose") + Summary completion (A–I so'zlar qutisi)
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 8 (Across the universe) — koinotni tadqiq qilish, xalqaro hamkorlik, Marsni o'zlashtirish, akademik fe'l + predlog

intro: Passage 3 — imtihondagi eng uzun va eng mavhum matn: bu yerda yozuvchi faqat ma'lumot bermaydi, balki BAHOLAYDI va TUSHUNTIRADI. Bugungi kombinatsiya — YES / NO / NOT GIVEN (1–5), Multiple choice A–D (6–9) va Summary + A–I qutisi (10–14). Bu kombinatsiyani 3-unitda (5-dars) ishlaganmiz, YNNG va MCQ ni 6-unitda (12-dars) ham ishlaganmiz; bugun — Band 7 tezligi (uch tur 20 daqiqada) va yangi savol: writer's purpose.

XARITA (2 daqiqa). SB 2-mashqdagidek: savol guruhlarini ko'zdan kechiring va har guruh matnning qaysi qismiga tegishli ekanini belgilang. SB da YNNG 1–5 — matnning boshi (ikki jamoa, Fondning tashkil topishi), MCQ 6–8 — misollar (Guatemala, Suriya, mukofotlar), 9 — butun matn, summary sarlavhasi "Field research: Applying the Earth's environment to the settlement of space" — faqat g'orlar va Arktika krateri haqidagi ikki xatbosh. Xarita tufayli matnni bir marta o'qiysiz.

YES / NO / NOT GIVEN — yozuvchining fikri. Band 7 da qiyinlik shundaki, gaplarning ko'pi "yarim to'g'ri": kalit so'zlar matnda bor, lekin da'vo boshqa. SB 2-savol: "It is unclear why..." — matnda sabab ANIQ aytilgan ("chiefly historical"), demak NO. SB 3-savol: hukumatlar va pul matnda bor, lekin qaysi sohaga KO'PROQ pul berilishi solishtirilmagan — NOT GIVEN. Qoida: har gapdagi baholovchi yoki taqqoslovchi so'zni (unclear, more ... than, unfortunately, later than) toping va aynan shu so'zni tekshiring.

MCQ: ikki xil savol bor. Faktik savol (7: "GPS and satellite imagery were used ... to") — joyni topib, isbot gap bilan solishtirasiz. Tahliliy savol (6: "significance of the novel approach", 8: "one of the purposes of the awards", 9: "the writer's purpose") — xatboshining yoki matnning VAZIFASI so'raladi. Bunday savollarda isbot xatboshining topic gapida ham, xulosa gapida ham bo'lishi mumkin — shuning uchun butun xatboshini o'qing. SB da ikkalasi ham xulosa gapida ("This novel approach is now making the protection of the forests a sensible economic decision", "they provide longevity for the objectives"), lekin bu qoida emas.

"Writer's purpose" savolini (9) oxirida ishlang: butun matnni o'qib bo'lgach, ohangni aniqlaysiz. Variantlarni ohang bo'yicha tekshiring: persuade (iltimos, chaqiruv bormi?), show how views have changed (vaqt bo'yicha o'zgarish bormi?), reject criticisms (tanqidga javob bormi?), explain (tushuntirish, misollar). SB matni — tushuntiruvchi: to'g'ri javob B.

Summary + quti: javob — faqat HARF. 5 bo'shliq, 9 variant, ya'ni 4 tasi ortiqcha. Ishlash tartibi: 1) summary sarlavhasidan matndagi joyni toping; 2) har bo'shliq uchun so'z turini yozing ("in 10 ___ situations" → sifat; "the 13 ___ place" → sifat, artikl bilan); 3) qutini so'z turi bo'yicha qisqartiring; 4) qolgan 2–3 variantni matndagi paraphrase bilan tanlang: harsh environments → extreme, long-term isolation → extended, an excellent replica → ideal.

Summary tuzog'i: bo'shliq atrofidagi so'zlar boshqa variantga ishora qiladi. SB 11: "tolerate ___ periods on their own" — "on their own" I (individual) ni tanlashga undaydi, lekin "periods" ga mos sifat — extended (long-term isolation). WB 12–14 da esa quti fe'llardan iborat: hit, create, increase, rise — "rise" o'timsiz fe'l, "___ the planet's temperature" dan keyin to'ldiruvchi bor, demak o'timli "increase" kerak. Grammatika Band 7 da variantlarni ajratishning eng tez yo'li.

Vaqt: Passage 3 ga 20 daqiqa. Tavsiya: xarita 2, YNNG 5, MCQ 6–8 — 5, summary 5, writer's purpose + tekshirish 3 daqiqa. SB 4-mashq savoli ("How long should you spend on each of them?") ga o'quvchilar o'zi javob bersin, keyin shu reja bilan solishtiring.
formulas: 1–5 boshi, 6–8 misollar, 9 butun matn, 10–14 sarlavha bo'yicha
unclear / more than / unfortunately / later than
Isbot topic yoki xulosa gapida — butun xatboshini o'qing
presentation: YNNG da matnda "governments" va "money" bor. Demak YES yoki NO emasmi?
Yo'q. So'zlar borligi yetarli emas — gapdagi TAQQOSLASH (more money to X than Y) matnda bormi? Yo'q bo'lsa — NOT GIVEN (SB 3).
"Unfortunately" so'zi YNNG gapida nimani bildiradi?
Bu yozuvchining bahosi. Yozuvchi shu vaziyatni afsuslanarli deb hisoblaydimi va vaziyatning o'zi rostmi — ikkalasini tekshiring. SB 4 da vaziyat teskari: jamoalar bir-biriga resurs bera oladi — NO.
"Significance" va "purpose" savollarining farqi bormi?
Ikkalasi ham "nega bu muhim / nima uchun kerak" deb so'raydi. Isbot — natijani ko'rsatadigan gap (making ... a sensible economic decision; provide longevity).
Summary da qutidagi so'z matnda aynan bor. Shunisi to'g'rimi?
Ehtimoli past. SB da "scientific" (G) matnda bor va 14 ga to'g'ri keladi, lekin ko'pincha to'g'ri javob paraphrase bo'ladi (harsh → extreme). Har doim ma'noni tekshiring.
Summary variantini ikki bo'shliqqa qo'ysa bo'ladimi?
Odatda har harf bir marta ishlatiladi. Agar bitta variant ikki joyga mos kelsa, qaysi biriga aniqroq mos kelishini matn bilan tekshiring.
"Writer's purpose" savolida ikkita variant o'xshash ko'rinsa-chi?
Matnda isboti bo'lmagan so'zlarni qidiring: "persuade" — chaqiriq yo'q; "changed" — vaqt bo'yicha o'zgarish yo'q; "criticisms" — tanqid yo'q. Qolgani — "explain".
notes: SB 6-mashq (referencing) darsning yashirin kaliti: "both fields of interest" → Q1, "this dichotomous existence" → Q2, "both communities" → Q4, "These collections" → Q7, "Together, they demonstrate" → Q8. Har javobni tekshirganda o'quvchidan "bu olmosh nimaga ishora qiladi?" deb so'rang.
7.0 darajasida o'quvchilar ko'pincha YNNG da NO va NOT GIVEN ni adashtiradi. Qoida: matnda gapga ZID ma'lumot bormi (NO) yoki umuman ma'lumot yo'qmi (NOT GIVEN)? Isbot gapni doskaga yozdiring.
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: SB summary dagi 4 ta ortiqcha variant (C, E, F, I) nega mos kelmasligini bir gapda tushuntirish.
WB matnida summary fe'llardan iborat — o'quvchilarga fe'l grammatikasini (o'timli/o'timsiz, to + infinitive) eslating.
mistakes: Qaysi sohaga ko'proq pul berilishi solishtirilmagan
SB 11 ga I (individual) — "on their own" tufayli
"rise" o'timsiz; "___ the planet's temperature" — o'timli fe'l kerak
WB 1 ga YES ("Mars may be more promising")

how: CORE — koinot va tadqiqot mavzusidagi Band 7 so'zlari; STRONG — akademik matn tili (Passage 3); SUPER — yozuvchi fikrini bildiruvchi iboralar (YNNG uchun juda muhim).
Har so'z bilan o'quvchi koinot yoki fan haqida o'z fikrini bildiruvchi gap tuzsin: "International collaboration fosters links between scientists who would otherwise compete."
core: Space exploration has produced technologies we use every day.
Koinotni tadqiq qilish biz har kuni ishlatadigan texnologiyalarni berdi.
The project was an international collaboration between five agencies.
Loyiha besh agentlik o'rtasidagi xalqaro hamkorlik edi.
Satellites monitor changes in the polar ice caps.
Sun'iy yo'ldoshlar qutb muzliklaridagi o'zgarishlarni kuzatib boradi.
The observatory is located in a remote part of Chile.
Rasadxona Chilining borish qiyin hududida joylashgan.
Astronauts must cope with months of isolation.
Astronavtlar oylab davom etadigan yolg'izlikka bardosh berishi kerak.
Scientists are searching for habitable planets.
Mars has a very thin atmosphere.
The Arctic crater is a good replica of conditions on Mars.
Arktikadagi krater Marsdagi sharoitning yaxshi nusxasi.
Permanent settlement on Mars is still decades away.
Marsda doimiy o'rnashishga hali o'nlab yillar bor.
A base on the Moon must be sustainable for years.
Oydagi baza yillar davomida barqaror bo'lishi kerak.
strong: There is a false dichotomy between protecting Earth and exploring space.
Yerni himoya qilish va koinotni o'rganish o'rtasida soxta qarama-qarshilik bor.
The charity was set up to foster links between scientists.
Xayriya tashkiloti olimlar o'rtasidagi aloqalarni rivojlantirish uchun tuzilgan.
Forests have an intrinsic value beyond their economic use.
O'rmonlarning iqtisodiy foydasidan tashqari o'z qiymati bor.
Could extraterrestrial life exist beneath the ice?
Muz ostida Yerdan tashqari hayot bo'lishi mumkinmi?
The awards provide longevity for the Foundation's aims.
Mukofotlar Fond maqsadlarining uzoq davom etishini ta'minlaydi.
Terraforming would stretch human ingenuity to its limits.
super: Both fields stem from the same human curiosity.
Ikkala soha ham insonning bir xil qiziquvchanligidan kelib chiqadi.
The mission is fraught with technical challenges.
it comes as no surprise that
It comes as no surprise that Mars attracts so much attention.
Mars shunchalik e'tibor tortishi ajablanarli emas.
ɪt kʌmz əz nəʊ səˈpraɪz ðæt
The importance of water on the Moon cannot be overstated.
Oydagi suvning ahamiyatini qanchalik aytsak ham kam.

class_ex.title: Bu ibora nimaga ishora qiladi? (SB, 6-mashq)
class_ex.instr: SB matnidan quyidagi beshta iborani toping. Har biri nimaga ishora qiladi va qaysi savolga javob berishga yordam beradi?
items: 1 both fields of interest
2 this dichotomous existence
3 both communities
4 These collections
5 Together, they demonstrate
answers: space exploration + study/protection of the Earth's environment — Q1
artefacts and remnants of early civilisations — Q7
Mars va undan keyingi ekspeditsiyalar uchun mukofotlar — Q8
why: Birinchi gap: "The community that focuses ... on the exploration of space ... from the community focused on the study and protection of the Earth's environment". Ikkalasi ham "scientific exploration" — Q1 YES.
"Dichotomous" = ikkiga bo'lingan. Keyingi gap uning sababini aytadi: "chiefly historical" — shuning uchun Q2 ("It is unclear why") NO.
Ikkinchi xatbosh oxiri: kosmos jamoasi sun'iy yo'ldosh bera oladi, ekologlar esa ekstremal muhitdagi hayot haqida ma'lumot — Q4 NO.
"Mounds, or 'tels', containing artefacts and remnants" → these collections. Q7: GPS topilmalarni topish uchun ishlatilgan — A.
"They" = Mars awards + keyingi mukofotlar; "provide longevity for the objectives" — Q8 D.
class_ex.note: Mashqdan keyin qoida: Passage 3 da javob ko'pincha ikki gap o'rtasida — olmosh (this, these, both, they) oldingi gapdagi ma'lumotni keyingi gapdagi baho bilan bog'laydi.

class_ex.title: Summary qutisini qisqartirish (SB, Questions 10–14)
class_ex.instr: Matnni o'qishdan OLDIN har bo'shliq uchun qutidagi (A comparable, B extreme, C connected, D ideal, E unexpected, F beneficial, G scientific, H extended, I individual) qaysi 2–3 variant grammatik va kollokatsiya jihatidan mos kelishini ayting.
items: 10 how humans function in ___ situations
11 who tolerate ___ periods on their own
12 environments on Earth that are ___ to those on Mars
13 the ___ place to test the technologies
14 gather other relevant ___ information
why: "___ situations" — vaziyatni tasvirlaydigan sifat. Matnda "harsh environments" → B extreme.
"___ periods" — davomiylik. Matnda "long-term isolation" → H extended. I — tuzoq: "on their own" allaqachon "individual" ma'nosini beradi.
"___ to those on Mars" — faqat "to" bilan ishlaydigan sifat: comparable to, connected to. Matnda "space-like environments" → A comparable.
"the ___ place to test" — superlativga yaqin baho: ideal. Matnda "an excellent replica".
"relevant ___ information" — ma'lumot turi. Matnda "biological potential" va "scientific research" → G scientific.
class_ex.note: Maqsad — 9 variant bilan emas, 2–3 variant bilan matnga kirish. Keyin SB blokida yakuniy javoblar isbot gap bilan tekshiriladi (10 B, 11 H, 12 A, 13 D, 14 G).
